Attack into the Dreaming Tree battlefield with your unit

Target your attacking unit with Cleave (or another spell)

If this is the first time this turn you've chosen a friendly unit there with a spell, draw 1 card

Nuances:

The card was errataed to change "you" to "a player" to clarify that any player can trigger the effect when targeting their own units at the battlefield, regardless of who controls it

This interaction is consistent with how other battlefields work (e.g., Trifarian War Camp providing +1 might to units there regardless of battlefield control)

question: Does Lux's ability trigger when a spell is countered or when its target becomes invalid?
answer:
Ruling: Lux's ability triggers when you play a spell, regardless of whether the target becomes invalid. However, if the spell is countered, Lux will not trigger.

Sequence:

When a spell's targets become illegal, the spell still resolves (ignoring impossible instructions), and Lux triggers

When a spell is countered, the spell does not resolve, and Lux does not trigger

Nuances:

A spell with invalid targets due to effects like Retreat still counts as resolving, just with some instructions ignored

Countering a spell (like with Wind Wall) prevents resolution entirely, which prevents Lux from triggering

question: If Teemo, Scout is played from hidden, can you Gust him before he gets the might gain?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can Gust Teemo before his might gain resolves. When Teemo enters play, his trigger goes on the chain, and you can React with Gust before his trigger resolves.

Sequence:

Teemo enters play

His trigger goes on the chain

You can React with Gust

Gust resolves before Teemo's trigger resolves

question: If Player A initiates a showdown at battlefield 1, Player B plays Ride the Wind to go to battlefield 2, then Player B plays another Ride the Wind to return to battlefield 1 and wins, does Player B score one point or two points that turn?
answer:
Ruling: Player B scores only one point. When Player B plays Ride the Wind to battlefield 2 while the first showdown at battlefield 1 has not yet resolved, the showdown at battlefield 2 never happens because the existing showdown must fully resolve first.

Sequence:

Player A initiates showdown at battlefield 1

Player B plays Ride the Wind to battlefield 2, staging a second showdown

The first showdown at battlefield 1 must fully resolve before the second showdown can begin

Player B plays Ride the Wind back to battlefield 1 before the first showdown resolves

Since Player B returned to battlefield 1 before the first showdown resolved, the showdown at battlefield 2 never happens

Player B wins at battlefield 1 and scores one point

Nuances:

A showdown fully resolves when both players pass on an empty chain with focus

Playing Ride the Wind into an ongoing showdown at the same battlefield is called a "surprise defence"

question: Can Ezreal's Legend ability be used in response to targeting the same enemy unit twice, before those spells resolve?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Ezreal's Legend ability can be used immediately after choosing/targeting the same enemy unit twice, without waiting for those spells to resolve.

Nuances:

"Choose" is equivalent to "Target" for the purposes of this ability

The targeting action itself triggers the ability condition, not the resolution of the spells doing the targeting

question: Does recalling a unit exhaust it?
answer:
Ruling: Recalls do not inherently exhaust units. A unit only exhausts if the specific effect text says to exhaust it.

Nuances:

A recall only happens when an effect specifically uses the word "recall" - moving units back to your base is not automatically a recall

Many recall effects do say to recall the unit exhausted, but that's part of the effect text, not an inherent property of recalls

Some cards have errata that affect recall effects, so check for updated card text rather than relying on printed text

question: If Orange Lee Sin dies from combat damage and was buffing a Clockwork Keeper that also took damage, does the Clockwork Keeper die when it loses Lee Sin's buff?
answer:
Ruling: The Clockwork Keeper does not die. After combat damage is assigned and units are killed, they are immediately healed before any other game state checks and before any abilities are able to enter the chain.

Sequence:

Combat damage is assigned to all units simultaneously

Units that received lethal damage are killed

All units are immediately healed

Game state checks and abilities occur after healing

Nuances:

You cannot assign over-damage to a unit; once lethal damage is assigned to a unit, you must assign remaining damage to the next unit

The written rules initially suggested the Clockwork would die, but the FAQ clarified that healing occurs before the buff is removed, so the Clockwork survives

question: When conquering Zaun Warrens as the first battlefield with 7 points already, what order do the replacement draw (for the 8th point) and Zaun Warrens' discard draw trigger occur?
answer:
Ruling: The question was answered in a different thread and not resolved in this thread.

Sequence: N/A

Nuances: N/A

question: Does Ezreal's discount apply to the energy cost paid for Hard Bargain's effect?
answer:
Ruling: No, Ezreal cannot discount Hard Bargain's energy cost. Hard Bargain's cost is paid to get an effect separate from the spell (to not counter your spell), not as part of the spell's cost itself.

Nuances:

Hard Bargain's payment is a cost for an effect that is separate from the spell being cast

Ezreal's discount only applies to spell costs, not to costs for separate effects

question: Can cards that say 'return a unit in the trash to your hand' target champion units?
answer: Ruling: Yes, champion units can be targeted by effects that return units from the trash to your hand, because all champion units are units.

question: If you cast a spell (like Hextech Ray) targeting an opponent's unit with Deflect, but cannot pay the Deflect cost, are you forced to retarget your own unit, or does the spell get fully rewound back to your hand?
answer:
Ruling: At high OPL, if you place a spell on the chain as pending but select an illegal target (one requiring a Deflect cost you cannot pay), the judge will typically rewind only to the targeting step and require you to select a legal target (your own unit). At low OPL, a full rewind back to hand is expected.

Sequence:

The card is placed on the chain as "pending" (this is a valid action)

Targets are selected during the finalization process

If an illegal target is selected, only that targeting action is rewound

You must then select a legal target to proceed with the spell

The spell does not return to hand if a legal target exists

Nuances:

Whether a full rewind occurs depends heavily on whether information was gained (opponent's reaction, hand movements, etc.). If the judge is certain no information was gained, a full rewind may be allowed even at high OPL

Both players can mutually agree to a full rewind at any OPL level

Rule 355.3 states that if an illegal choice is made during the play process, actions are undone - but there is debate about whether "this process" means the entire spell or just the illegal step

Current precedent from Chinese regionals supports rewinding only to the targeting step when a legal target exists

The card exists on the chain as "pending" before costs and targets are finalized, which is a valid game state that can be rewound to

question: How does Icathian Rain work - do you choose targets when you cast it or when it resolves?
answer:
Ruling: Icathian Rain uses a reflexive trigger (indicated by "do this:" text). You choose targets when it resolves, not when you cast it. When it resolves, it creates 6 separate triggered abilities on the chain, each dealing 2 damage to a targeted unit.

Sequence:

Play Icathian Rain

Players can react

Icathian Rain resolves, putting 6 reflexive triggers on the chain

Choose targets for the 6 reflexive triggers

Pay additional costs for each trigger targeting an enemy unit with deflect

Players can react between each trigger

Each trigger resolves separately, dealing 2 damage

Nuances:

Any card with "do this:" text creates a reflexive trigger that goes on the chain upon resolution

This applies to other cards like Falling Star and Twisted Fate's attack ability

The design creates more opportunities for counterplay - opponents can respond between each damage instance, and deflect costs apply to each trigger separately

If ability-countering cards are released, having separate triggers makes the spell less vulnerable to being fully countered

question: Can you use Retreat on a unit that is in your base, or only on units at battlefields?
answer: Ruling: You can use Retreat on a unit in your base. There is no restriction on the card text that limits it to units at battlefields only.

question: If a unit with 5 might takes 4 damage from Voidseeker, then has its might reduced by Stupefy on a new chain, does the unit die or stay at 1 hp?
answer:
Ruling: The unit would die. After Stupefy resolves, a cleanup happens and the game checks if the unit's damage meets or exceeds its (now reduced) might.

Sequence:

Voidseeker resolves, dealing 4 damage to the unit with 5 might

On a new chain, Stupefy is cast and resolves, reducing the unit's might

A cleanup happens and checks the damage against the new might value

The unit dies because the damage now meets or exceeds its reduced might

question: What happens after a showdown when two players have units at the battlefield and neither can defeat the other?
answer:
Ruling: When units controlled by different players remain at a battlefield at the end of combat, the attackers are recalled to base.

Sequence:

Combat resolves at the showdown

If units from different players remain at the battlefield

The attacking units are recalled to base

question: Does the Vision keyword stack, and if so, how does it work?
answer:
Ruling: If something has multiple instances of Vision, they trigger separately.

Sequence:

First Vision triggers: look at 1 card, choose to keep on top or put on bottom

Second Vision triggers: look at 1 card, choose to keep on top or put on bottom

Third Vision triggers: look at 1 card, choose to keep on top or put on bottom

(Continue for each instance)

Nuances:

If you choose to keep a card on top during the first Vision, you can forgo looking at the remaining Visions since you already know what card you want on top

question: Do two Leona Zealot -8 effects stack?
answer: Ruling: Yes, two Leona Zealot -8 effects stack.

question: When a card effect ignores energy cost (like Harrowing), does it also ignore the additional cost from Accelerate?
answer: Ruling: No, ignoring energy cost only applies to base costs. Any additional costs, including the extra cost from Accelerate, must be paid as normal.

question: Can you play a spell (like Gust) without any valid targets on the battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot play any spell that doesn't have a legal target to begin with.

Nuances:

This applies to all spells requiring targets, not just Gust specifically

question: When Baited Hook recycles multiple cards, can you choose which order to recycle them, or is it random?
answer:
Ruling: When you recycle more than one card at once, it must be done in a random order.

Nuances:

This applies to Baited Hook and any other effect that recycles multiple cards simultaneously

You cannot choose the order yourself

question: If I use Ride the Wind to move a unit to a battlefield during my opponent's turn in response to them triggering a showdown, and I win that showdown, do I gain a point for conquering or just for holding?
answer:
Ruling: You gain a point for conquering because you establish control of a battlefield you have not yet scored that turn.

Sequence:

Opponent moves a unit to an open battlefield, triggering showdown

You use Ride the Wind (an Action) to move Volibear to that battlefield during the showdown

After the showdown resolves, if your units remain at the battlefield and you don't already control it, you establish control

Since you have not yet scored that battlefield this turn (it's your opponent's turn), this counts as a Conquer

Nuances:

This works because Ride the Wind is an Action, so it can be played during your opponent's turn

You become the Defender in the showdown even though you didn't have units there at the start

The key rule is that establishing control results in a Conquer if you haven't scored that battlefield yet this turn

question: How does scoring work in Riftbound, particularly regarding holding and conquering battlefields?
answer:
Ruling: You gain points in two ways: (1) beginning your turn with control of a battlefield gives you a "Hold" point for each battlefield controlled, or (2) ending a showdown with a unit present at a battlefield you do not control (and haven't scored at this turn) gives you a "Conquer" point. Each battlefield can only be scored once per turn.

Sequence:

Hold points are awarded at the start of your turn for each battlefield you control

Conquer points are awarded when you end a showdown with a unit at an opponent's battlefield (that you haven't scored at yet)

You can score multiple points in one turn by holding one battlefield and conquering another

Nuances:

The final game point (8th point in 1v1) has special rules: if you conquer at 7 points and have scored at every battlefield this turn, you get the victory point; otherwise you score a draw from your main deck

Battlefield effects apply to both players regardless of who chose the battlefield

question: Does the blue seal (Sapphire Seal) provide energy or just power, and how can a player use it to pay for Teemo after channeling runes?
answer:
Ruling: The Sapphire Seal only provides power, not energy. The player was able to pay for Teemo by floating energy from a rune they recycled earlier to pay for the Seal, then using that floated energy along with the Seal's power.

Sequence:

Player channels two runes (adding energy to their rune pool)

Player plays Sapphire Seal for one power, exhausting one rune (the energy from this rune goes into the rune pool)

Player plays Teemo using the floated energy from the rune pool plus the power from the Seal and the remaining physical rune

Nuances:

The rune pool (where energy floats) and physical runes are separate concepts

Energy from recycled/exhausted runes remains available in the rune pool even after the physical rune is used

question: Can a unit with 2 Might in showdown assign 1 damage to 2 different units to trigger Emperor's Decree?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot split damage from a single unit across multiple targets for Emperor's Decree. You must assign damage equal to the unit's full Might to one target before moving to the next target.

Sequence:

Assign all damage equal to the attacking unit's Might to one target

Only after all damage is dealt does Emperor's Decree trigger

Then you may move to the next target

question: Does Ravenbloom Student get +1 when you play a spell from hidden?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Ravenbloom Student gets +1 when you play a spell from hidden. Playing a card from hidden still counts as playing it.

Nuances:

Hiding a spell is a separate action from playing it and does not count as playing the spell

Hiding does not open a chain or pass priority

Playing a card from hidden works like playing from other zones (CC zone, Hand, or Banishment during aurora)

Revealing a unit from hidden does not trigger Ravenbloom Student since it is not a spell

question: If I cast Gust targeting a 2 Might unit in response to a Quickdraw trigger (before Sterak's attaches and would make it 5 Might), is Gust legal and does it resolve?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Gust is legal and resolves. When you cast Gust in response to the Quickdraw trigger, Gust resolves first before Sterak's attaches, so the unit is still 2 Might when Gust checks its target validity.

Sequence:

Sterak's is played from hand

Quickdraw trigger goes on the stack

Gust is cast in response to the Quickdraw trigger

Gust resolves while unit is still 2 Might

Quickdraw trigger resolves and Sterak's attaches

Nuances:

You cannot react to Sterak's being played itself, but you can react to the Quickdraw trigger

question: Can opponent burn out give you the winning point at 7 points?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, burn out can give you the winning point. Only points earned from Conquer or Hold have restrictions on the final point.

Nuances:

Conquering for the final point has a restriction: you must have scored every other battlefield that turn, otherwise you draw instead of getting the last point

Points from sources other than Conquer or Hold (like burn out) are not subject to these restrictions

question: Is there timing before a Showdown starts where reactions can be played, and do abilities like Assault, Shield, or 'When I attack/defend' triggers open chains that can be reacted to?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot react to a unit moving into the battlefield before the showdown starts. Assault and Shield are passive abilities that don't go onto the chain, but 'When I attack/defend' triggers do go onto an initial chain once the showdown has already begun.

Sequence:

Unit moves to battlefield with another unit present

If the moving unit has 'when you move me' triggers, those must be fully resolved before the showdown begins

Showdown begins

'When I attack/defend' triggers go onto the initial chain (already within combat steps)

Nuances:

The only exception for pre-showdown timing is 'when you move me' triggers (like Travelling Merchant), which must be fully resolved before the staged combat/showdown begins

If moving to the battlefield triggers no abilities or printed text, there are no pre-combat chain opportunities to react

question: If I steal control of a repeat spell with Mystic Reversal, do I get both instances of the repeat effect if my opponent paid for both?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you get all instances of the repeat effect that were paid for. When you gain control of a repeat spell, the repeated spell effects are part of the original spell which has been finalized and paid for, so gaining control doesn't change the fact that the repeat cost has been paid.

Sequence:

The original spell is cast and repeat costs are paid

The spell (with repeat effects) is finalized

Control of the spell is stolen

The spell performs its effects the number of times corresponding to how many repeat costs were paid

Nuances:

Repeat effects don't go on the chain separately; they're essentially appended to the text of the original spell

You get 1 spell that performs its effects multiple times (twice if one repeat cost was paid, three times if two repeat costs were paid, etc.)

question: When using Bellows Breath with Repeat, can you target a separate battlefield/location for the repeated effect?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, when you pay the Repeat cost for Bellows Breath, you can target a different battlefield for each instance of the effect. The two sets of damage are chosen separately.

Sequence:

First instance: Deal 1 to up to three units at the same battlefield

Second instance: Deal 1 to up to three units at the same battlefield (can be a different battlefield than the first)

Nuances:

Bellows Breath can target units at a base (bases count as valid locations)

Each instance of the effect requires all targets within that instance to be at the same battlefield, but the two instances can target different battlefields

question: Do Miss Fortune's Legend ability (giving Ganking to a unit) and Captain ability (choosing to ready a unit) trigger Spirit Wheel?
answer:
Ruling: Both Miss Fortune abilities trigger Spirit Wheel because they target/choose a unit.

Sequence:

Miss Fortune Legend ability targets a unit to give Ganking, so Spirit Wheel triggers as chain link 2

Miss Fortune Captain ability chooses a unit to ready, which also counts as targeting for Spirit Wheel

question: If you conquer a battlefield, then retreat and return to conquer that same battlefield again on the same turn, do you get the point again and do field abilities (like Candlelit Sanctum) trigger?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot score a battlefield more than once per turn. When you close the second showdown after moving back to a previously scored battlefield, you will not score a point and thus will not conquer. No conquer effects will trigger.

Nuances:

Conquering is a type of scoring, not a separate step that happens after scoring

If you conquer but cannot get a point (like when you're at 7 points), you still get conquer effects

If you take control of a battlefield you've already scored that turn, you don't conquer at all, so no effects trigger

You can still win on your 8th point via conquering, as long as you've scored every other battlefield that turn

question: How does priority work when reactions are stacked in a showdown, and who can react as the chain resolves?
answer:
Ruling: As each item on the chain resolves, there is another round of priority for players to react. The player who controls the next item on the chain after an item resolves gets priority first, then they can play a reaction or pass priority to the next player in turn order. When all players pass in succession, the topmost item resolves and the process repeats.

Sequence:

Player 1 (with Focus) stacks reactions 1, 2, 3 and passes priority

Player 2 can respond to any item on the chain (e.g., Defy targeting reaction 2)

When all players pass, the topmost item begins to resolve

As each item resolves, the player controlling the next item on the chain gets priority first

Players can add new items to the chain at each pause

When all players choose not to respond, the topmost item resolves

This repeats until the chain is empty

Nuances:

Focus is specifically for playing cards/activating abilities during a showdown when nothing is on the chain; it doesn't affect priority or the chain itself directly

Focus swaps when the chain fully resolves in a showdown, or when a player chooses to pass focus rather than start a new chain

Defy can target any item on the chain when it's being finalized except for itself

question: In a 4-player game, if players A and B are in showdown on a battlefield, can player C use a reaction to assign additional damage to one of the units?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, player C can interact with a reaction during the showdown between players A and B.

Sequence:

Priority goes around to all players, not just the attacker and defender

Every player gets a window of focus (the ability to start chains)

Each player gets a chance to add items to each chain, regardless of whether they are an attacker, defender, or neither

Nuances:

The "inviting" system (where you had to use priority to invite a player to act) was removed from the core rules in the NA release version in October

question: Does Ravenbloom trigger when revealing Teemo from hidden?
answer:
Ruling: No, Ravenbloom does not trigger when revealing Teemo from hidden because Teemo is a unit, not a spell.

Nuances:

A card is only considered a spell if it says "spell" in the type line of the card

Playing a hidden unit does not count as playing a spell

question: If an opponent uses Fight or Flight to leave combat, then you use Ride the Wind to return to the battlefield, does the opponent still score?
answer:
Ruling: No, the opponent does not score. When Fight or Flight resolves, the combat showdown does not end - it only ends once both players pass with focus on an empty chain.

Sequence:

Fight or Flight resolves, leaving the opponent as the only unit on the battlefield

You use Ride the Wind to return to the battlefield

The combat continues as the same showdown with the same attacker/defender designations

Since you returned to defend, the opponent does not score

question: What does "choose" a friendly unit mean in Riftbound? Does it mean the same as targeting?
answer:
Ruling: "Choose" means "Target" in Riftbound.

Nuances:

This clarification applies when evaluating whether cards are "choosing" units

question: In a closed state, can a reaction be played after the last card/ability in the chain resolves?
answer:
Ruling: The chain ends once the last card resolves. A reaction card drawn during the resolution of the last card in the chain cannot be played within that same chain.

Sequence:

The last card/ability in the chain resolves completely

If the chain is now empty, play proceeds in an open state

If there is currently a showdown, focus is passed to the opponent where they have the opportunity to start a new chain

Nuances:

Even if a player draws a reaction card as part of the resolution of the last card in the chain (e.g., drawing 2 cards from Hidden Blade killing a unit), they cannot play that reaction within the same chain

question: Can Zaun Warrens trigger if you have no cards in hand?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Zaun Warrens can trigger even if you have no cards in hand. You do as much as you can, following the instructions in order.

Sequence:

Attempt to discard a card (if you have no cards, you can't discard)

Draw a card

Nuances:

This principle applies to similar effects: if an effect instructs you to discard then draw, you'll discard as many cards as you can and then draw the specified number of cards

question: If I use Aurora to play a unit onto an open battlefield at 7 points (after having already scored from the other battlefield this turn), do I score the second point and win immediately?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you score and win immediately. If you conquered one battlefield and the second one is open, conquering it triggers scoring and victory.

Nuances:

It doesn't matter that it's not end of turn; what matters is whether both conquests happened in the same turn

question: Does Spirit Wheel trigger its draw ability when you choose to move a unit back to base and exhaust it using Spirit Wheel's own effect?
answer:
Ruling: No, Spirit Wheel does not trigger its draw ability from its own movement effect. The unit must be targeted by a spell or effect (specifically targeted, not just chosen by you) to trigger the draw.

Nuances:

The distinction is between you choosing to move a unit versus a spell or effect targeting the unit

The card requires the unit to be specifically targeted, not just affected by your choice

question: For Jinx (red), is the 'discard two' effect a cost that must be paid, or a normal 'when you play' triggered effect?
answer:
Ruling: The discard two is a triggered ability, not a cost. It triggers after Jinx has been played, and you do as much of it as you can based on your hand size.

Sequence:

Play Jinx

The 'when you play' trigger occurs

Discard up to 2 cards (discard 1 if you only have 1 card in hand, discard 0 if you have no cards)

Nuances:

If it were a cost, the card would say "as an additional cost to play me, discard a card"

The "when you play me" wording indicates it's a trigger that happens after the unit has been played

question: When conquering Zaun Warrens with Kai'Sa, do you have to discard for Zaun Warrens before drawing for Kai'Sa's conquer ability, or can you draw first then discard?
answer:
Ruling: You get to choose in which order you resolve these abilities since they trigger at the same time.

Sequence:

Both abilities trigger simultaneously when you conquer

You choose the order to resolve them

You may draw from Kai'Sa first, then discard for Zaun Warrens, or vice versa

question: Can you conquer and score a battlefield on your opponent's turn if you controlled it at the start of their turn but lost control during their turn?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can conquer and score a battlefield on your opponent's turn if you lost control of it during that turn, as long as you haven't already scored it that turn. You must lose control before you can conquer again.

Sequence:

You control a battlefield at the start of opponent's turn

You lose control of that battlefield during opponent's turn

You regain control of that battlefield during opponent's turn (via effects like Ride the Wind)

You conquer and score the battlefield

Nuances:

You cannot score a battlefield you've already scored that turn

Successfully defending a battlefield (opponent contests but fails) does not count as conquering - you must actually lose and regain control to score again

This is different from 2v2 rules regarding teammate-controlled units

question: Can you win the game on your opponent's turn, and does the 'score both battlefronts' rule still apply in that scenario?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, it is possible to win the game on your opponent's turn, and the requirement to score both battlefronts still applies.

Sequence:

Opponent attacks and you lose control of battlefront A

Opponent attacks battlefront B

During showdown at B, you use Ride The Wind to move a unit to A and conquer it

You also use Ride The Wind to move a unit to B and conquer/defend it

You win by controlling both battlefronts on opponent's turn

Nuances:

This strategy is commonly used by Annie decks

Yasuo, Windrider can also achieve this by moving 3 times on opponent's turn when at 7 points

question: Does Svellsongur create a separate instance of Azir Ascendant's Action ability, allowing you to use each instance once per turn?
answer: Ruling: Yes, Svellsongur creates a separate instance of Azir's Action ability, meaning you can use each instance once per turn.

question: Can you pay the repeat cost of Called Shot multiple times or just once?
answer: Ruling: You can only pay the repeat cost of Called Shot once.

question: Does Ahri, Nine-Tailed Fox (Legend) give -1 might to every unit attacking a battlefield or just one? Does Ahri, Inquisitive work the same way?
answer:
Ruling: Ahri, Nine-Tailed Fox (Legend) gives -1 might to all units attacking her battlefield. Ahri, Inquisitive only targets one unit.

Sequence:

When an opponent's unit is assigned as an attacker to Ahri Legend's battlefield, her trigger goes on the initial chain (before players can play actions)

The -1 might applies to all attacking units at that time

If a new unit joins combat later (e.g., via Ride the Wind after the initial chain resolves), Ahri Legend triggers again for that new unit

The new trigger starts a new chain that players can respond to with reactions

Nuances:

Ahri Legend can trigger multiple times in one combat if new attackers are assigned after the initial chain

Ahri, Inquisitive only triggers once per combat

Ahri Legend's trigger occurs during the initial chain, but once on the chain, players can respond with reactions

When a unit joins combat via an action like Ride the Wind, it doesn't gain the attacker designation until that action resolves, so Ahri's trigger starts a new chain afterward

question: If you use Hidden Blade on your own unit and save it with Sett's legend ability, do you still draw 2 cards?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you still draw 2 cards. Hidden Blade's kill effect and draw effect are separate from each other, so the draw happens regardless of whether the unit actually dies.

Nuances:

If the targeted unit leaves the battlefield before Hidden Blade resolves (bounced, banished, recycled, or killed by another card), the target becomes illegal and nobody draws cards because the controller can no longer be determined

The unit must still be at a battlefield when Hidden Blade resolves for the draw to happen

If the unit moves to a board-zone (base), its controller can still be determined and draws two

If the unit moves to a non-board-zone (hand, deck, trash, banish), there is no controller to determine and nobody draws

question: Does Mask of Foresight trigger when you attack an open battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: No, Mask of Foresight does not trigger when moving to an open battlefield because there is no combat and you are not attacking.

Nuances:

Moving to an open battlefield does not count as attacking

question: Can you play Shen after a Deathknell trigger during combat cleanup to maintain control of the battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can play Shen after a Deathknell trigger during combat cleanup. The Special Cleanup (which triggers Deathknell) occurs before clearing the Contested status from the battlefield, allowing you to respond with Shen while still controlling the battlefield.

Sequence:

Combat cleanup begins with Special Cleanup being invoked

Deathknell triggers during Special Cleanup and goes on the Chain

A new cleanup occurs after Deathknell becomes a Legal Item on the Chain

After this cleanup completes, the game is in a Closed state and the defending player gets priority

The defending player can play Shen at this point

Only after this does the battlefield's Contested status get cleared

Nuances:

This ruling is based on Chinese FAQ clarification that Special Cleanup and clearing Contested status are separate sequential steps, not simultaneous

The validity of this ruling was questioned as the Chinese FAQ may predate the 1.1 English CRD update, leaving the final answer uncertain

This interaction could make battlefields effectively unconquerable with recurrable reaction speed units like Teemo via Swift Scout

question: If a unit has 5 damage on it and 6 might, does it die if Stupefy is used on it (reducing might)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the unit dies. If a unit has damage markers on it equal to or greater than its might, it dies.

Sequence:

Unit has 5 damage and 6 might

Stupefy reduces might (presumably to 5 or below)

Damage markers (5) now equal or exceed might

Unit dies

question: Does Ravenbloom Student trigger when a spell is placed on the chain, or only when it resolves?
answer:
Ruling: Ravenbloom Student triggers when a spell resolves (is played successfully), not when it is placed on the chain.

Sequence:

Spell resolves

Ravenbloom triggers and is put on the chain

Trigger resolves

Nuances:

Placing a spell on the chain has no effect on Ravenbloom

A card is not considered "played" until it resolves and is removed from the chain

question: If Strategist Teemo is defending and triggers to find Nocturne, can Nocturne be played directly to the battlefield being defended?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can play Nocturne directly to the battlefield you're defending because you're still controlling it until combat ends.

Nuances:

If you're defending with Teemo via surprise defense and don't actually control the battlefield, then you cannot play Nocturne to that battlefield.

question: When playing Ride the Wind during an opponent's attack to move a unit to another occupied battlefield, what happens with combat timing and attacker designation?
answer:
Ruling: The new showdown is put in pending status, and the original combat resolves first. Since you are contesting the new battlefield, you are designated as the attacker in that showdown.

Sequence:

Original combat (where opponent attacked you) resolves completely first

New showdown (at the battlefield your unit moved to) is placed in pending

In the new showdown, you become the attacker because you are the one contesting

question: When a unit with Hidden is un-hidden on a later turn, must it be played to the same battlefield where it was hidden, or can it be played to a different battlefield or base?
answer:
Ruling: When a card is played from Hidden, it must be played to the same location where it was hidden. An additional restriction of "Here" is added to the card when played from Hidden.

Nuances:

The battlefield itself is not a target, but the play location is restricted to where the card was hidden

This restriction applies whether the hidden card is a unit or has other targeting requirements

question: Does 'board' include the trash pile, or is it just the base and battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: The board does not include the trash pile. It consists only of the base and battlefield zone.

Nuances:

According to the comprehensive rules, the board specifically consists of: Base, Battlefield Zone (which includes Facedown Zone and Legend Zone)

Trash is a separate public zone that is not part of the board

question: Can you play Primal Strength on Carnivorous Snapvine after playing it so it fights with additional power?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot play Primal Strength on Carnivorous Snapvine after playing it because Primal Strength is Action speed, not Reaction speed. Only Reaction speed cards can be used in response to Snapvine's effect.

Nuances:

Reaction speed cards like Discipline can be used with Snapvine's effect

Primal Strength is still useful for combat in other situations

question: When can spells be played based on their timing keywords (no timing keyword, Action, Reaction)?
answer:
Ruling: Spells with no timing keyword are used in neutral open state (nothing on chain, no showdown). Action speed can be used in neutral open and showdown open states. Reaction speed can be used in all states including when the chain is closed.

Sequence:

Base speed (no timing keyword): Anytime on your turn when there is no active showdown or chain

Action Speed: Anytime you can play Base speed, plus anytime you have priority in a showdown with no chain (state is open)

Reaction Speed: Anytime you could play Action, plus anytime you have priority in a showdown regardless of whether there is a chain

Nuances:

Each speed inherits from those below it, so anytime you can play base speed you can also play action/reaction

You must have priority to use them

In neutral open state, you can only cast spells on your turn

When it's not your turn, you can only use abilities if there is a chain and you get priority to react, or there is a showdown and you get focus/priority to play on an empty chain

question: Does Trinity Force score twice (for 3 points total) when both Trinity Force and Skyfall of Areion are attached to a unit on Reckoner's Arena?
answer: Ruling: Yes, you score twice from Trinity Force when both Trinity Force and Skyfall of Areion are attached to a unit on Reckoner's Arena, for 3 points total.

question: Can you play a hidden card if it has no legal targets available?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot play a card from hidden if you cannot choose all legal targets. Cards need all legal targets to be played.

Sequence:

Choosing targets is part of playing a card

If you can't choose targets, you can't play the card

This applies even when playing from hidden

question: Are the 'Sample' cards from the Gencon decks legal for tournament play?
answer:
Ruling: No, the Sample cards from the Gencon decks are not legal for tournament play.

Nuances:

The cards have the word "SAMPLE" printed on them, which disqualifies them from tournament use

The cards do have proper set numbers and the same text and art as regular versions

The card stock may be different from regular cards

This is distinct from alters, which are legal

question: Can you include a 4th copy of a card in your deck for a modified starter deck event if you pull it from packs?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot have more than 3 copies of a card in your deck even if you pull a 4th copy from additional packs. However, since release events are not riot sanctioned, the specific rules may vary by LGS.

Nuances:

Release events are not riot sanctioned, so individual stores may have different rules

Most stores are enforcing the 3-copy limit despite extra pulls

question: Do equipment keywords become a unit's keywords (specifically regarding Kato and items like Doran's Shield with Tank)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, equipment keywords become the equipped unit's keywords.

Nuances:

This information comes from Riot devs, with final confirmation pending official rules documentation

question: Does Grabber require all three conditions (recycle 3, tapping the card, and paying 1 energy) to activate its effect?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, all three requirements must be met to activate the ability. Everything to the left of the semicolon represents the cost that must be paid.

Sequence:

Recycle 3 cards from your trash

Pay 1 energy

Exhaust the Grabber

Draw 1 card

Nuances:

If you don't have 3 cards in your trash or 1 energy to spend, you cannot use the ability

The ability can be used when you first summon Grabber

question: When Thousand Tail Watcher reduces might to a minimum of 1, and Sett gains might from other units, how is Sett's total might calculated when all units have buffs?
answer:
Ruling: Sett becomes 6 might total. The calculation is: 5 (base) + 1 (buff) + 3 (from his effect counting other units) - 3 (Watcher reduction) = 6. The other small units become 1 might each.

Nuances:

Limitations like "minimum of 1" are applied at the moment the effect is applied and the reduction amount is remembered as a static number

If units lose buffs after Watcher's effect is applied, they can go to 0 might because the Watcher reduction remembers a static decrease but doesn't remember the "minimum of 1" limitation

If Watcher comes into play before units get buffed, those units will have higher might because Watcher remembers a smaller reduction amount to apply to them

question: When playing Imperial Decree with a 3 might unit attacking 3 units with 10 might each at a battlefield, can you choose to deal 1 damage to each unit to kill them all?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot deal 1 damage to each unit. Imperial Decree does not modify the concept of Lethal Damage, so you must still assign enough damage to kill a unit via normal means before assigning damage to another unit.

Sequence:

Assign lethal damage (enough to kill) to the first defending unit

Only after assigning lethal damage to the first unit can you assign damage to the next unit

Continue until all damage is assigned

Nuances:

Imperial Decree works best when attacking with low Might units, as only 1 damage is enough to kill even a 10 Might unit

The effect works both ways (affects both players)

Sending in units one at a time could be a good strategy when using Imperial Decree

question: If a 3 might creature is targeted by 4 of 6 Icathian Rain darts and the opponent responds with Zhonya's Hourglass, what happens and why?
answer:
Ruling: The unit dies twice during the resolution of the four darts. After the second dart deals lethal damage, the unit dies but Zhonya's Hourglass replaces that death (resetting damage to 0). The remaining two darts still hit the same unit, dealing lethal damage again, causing it to die a second time.

Sequence:

First dart deals 2 damage (2 damage on unit)

Second dart deals 2 damage (4 total damage, lethal to 3 might unit)

Cleanup occurs, lethal damage is checked, unit dies

Death is replaced by Zhonya's Hourglass, unit returns with 0 damage

Third dart deals 2 damage to the same unit (still valid target)

Fourth dart deals 2 damage (4 total damage, lethal again)

Cleanup occurs, unit dies

Nuances:

Each Icathian Rain dart is an individual ability on the chain, not part of the spell's resolution

The Icathian Rain spell itself has already resolved when the darts are created

Cleanup (including lethal damage checks) happens after each dart resolves

The unit remains the original valid target for all darts even after Zhonya's Hourglass replaces its death

question: If Stupefy's target becomes invalid before resolution (e.g., due to Hidden Blade), does Stupefy still draw a card?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you still draw a card from Stupefy. You do as much as you can on resolution, so as long as the target was valid when you played the card, you draw even if the target becomes invalid before resolution.

Nuances:

This works for Stupefy specifically because the target being valid is not a condition for the draw

Other cards like Hidden Blade cannot draw if their target becomes invalid before resolution (e.g., if the target is moved off the battlefield)

question: Where do I apply for the judge program?
answer: Ruling: You can apply for the judge program at https://locator.riftbound.uvsgames.com/settings/account-management

question: If Teemo Strategist is hidden and played during a showdown, does his ability trigger twice (once for playing from hidden and once for being declared defender)?
answer:
Ruling: With the original printed text and current core rules, the ability would trigger twice - once when played from hidden and once when declared as a defender.

Nuances:

The card has received errata that changes this interaction

The printed text does not explicitly say "or when I'm played from hidden"

Under current official play, the errata'd version should be used, which would only trigger once when defending

question: Does Ezreal's cost reduction work on Draven's ability that has a 'may pay' cost when attacking or defending?
answer:
Ruling: Ezreal's cost reduction does not work on Draven's ability. Ezreal only discounts cards that have "as an additional cost" and "may" wording together, which are optional additional costs paid when playing a card. Draven's ability is a triggered ability with its own cost, not an additional cost to cast.

Nuances:

The "may" wording on Draven refers to whether you want to pay the cost for the triggered ability to resolve, not an optional additional cost to cast

Optional additional costs are only paid when you play the card itself, not when using triggered abilities

Ezreal works with effects like Accelerate that have "as an additional cost" wording

question: If you control two Zhonyas Hourglass and two units die simultaneously, can both Zhonyas save one unit each?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, if two units die simultaneously and you control two Zhonyas Hourglass, each Zhonyas can save one unit. X Zhonyas can save X units, even if they die simultaneously.

Sequence:

When two units die simultaneously, each Zhonyas sees both death events

The controller picks which death event each Zhonyas will replace

Each Zhonyas replaces one of the deaths and is killed instead

Both units are saved

Nuances:

If only one unit dies with two Zhonyas in play, the controller chooses which Zhonyas replaces the death. The second Zhonyas does nothing because the death has already been replaced by the first Zhonyas.

When multiple replacement effects would replace the same event, the owner of the object being acted on determines the order the replacement effects apply.

The second replacement effect cannot replace a death that has already been replaced.

question: When Darius is played as the second card for turn, does his ability go on the chain and give the opponent priority to activate reactions?
answer: Ruling: Yes, Darius's ability goes on the chain when he is played as the second card for turn, and the opponent can play a reaction in response after priority is passed.

question: When Zhonya's triggers to save a unit that was about to be killed by damage, does the unit return with damage on it or does it heal? Also, do debuffs like Stupidify remain on the unit?
answer:
Ruling: When Zhonya's triggers, the unit is recalled and healed (damage is cleared). However, other effects like might reductions from Stupidify remain on the unit.

Nuances:

Only damage is cleared when the unit is saved

All other effects stay the same (debuffs, stat modifications, etc.)

Passive effects that only apply on battlefield or similar location-specific effects would not apply while recalled

Cards like Zhonya's received errata to specifically heal the unit they save

question: Does Tideturner's ability count as moving its target unit for the purpose of Kayn's ability that requires moving twice?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Tideturner's ability moves the targeted unit (Kayn), so if Kayn is moved by Tideturner and then moved again, his passive ability activates and he doesn't take damage.

Nuances:

The word "move" is implied in Tideturner's text even though it only explicitly states "move me to its location and it to my original location" - the second "move" is understood to apply to the target as well.

question: Can an opponent activate a hidden card in response to moving a unit to a battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: No, an opponent cannot activate a hidden card in response to moving a unit. Moving does not use the Chain and cannot be reacted to.

Nuances:

Movement can only be responded to if there is a trigger effect like "when I move, do something"

question: When a Sprite token dies, does Viktor create a token since Sprites are 'fae' (non-recruit units)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Viktor can create a token when a Sprite dies because Sprite tokens are not recruits.

Nuances:

Sprites count as non-recruit units due to their 'fae' unit type

question: When attacking with Crackshot Corsair (deals 1 damage to an enemy unit when I attack) and Warwick (kills all damaged units here when I attack), can I choose which trigger resolves first?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, when abilities you control simultaneously trigger, you get to choose the order they resolve.

Sequence:

Both "when I attack" triggers happen simultaneously

You choose which trigger resolves first

You can choose to have Crackshot Corsair deal 1 damage first, then Warwick kills all damaged units

question: When Udyr's ability refers to 'one you've not chosen this turn,' does this memory persist across multiple copies of Udyr or when Udyr changes zones?
answer:
Ruling: Each Udyr is a separate entity with its own memory of choices. If Udyr leaves play and re-enters, it becomes a new entity and does not remember previous choices.

Sequence:

Multiple Udyrs on the battlefield track their choices independently

When Udyr changes zones (bounced and replayed), all temporary modifications cease to be tracked

The returned Udyr is treated as a new entity with no memory of prior choices

Nuances:

The comprehensive rules lack specific rules about modal abilities in general, so this interpretation is based on the zone change rules that clear temporary tracking

question: Does Ravenbloom Student get +1 might when a spell resolves but has no effect (like Gust targeting a unit that became 4+ might)?
answer:
Ruling: Riftbound does not have fizzling. Gust will resolve with no effect and Ravenbloom Student will still get +1 might.

Nuances:

Spells resolve even when their conditions are no longer met

The spell resolving (even with no effect) is sufficient to trigger Ravenbloom Student's ability

question: Can a player respond with a reaction after an opponent's action spell or regular spell resolves outside of a showdown, when the chain becomes empty?
answer: Ruling: No, you cannot respond with a reaction after the chain empties outside of a showdown. When a chain ends outside of a showdown, it returns to the active player's open neutral state without another pass of priority.

question: Can you use Reinforce to pull another unit and then use Nocturne's ability?
answer: The thread does not contain a clear answer. The user references another Discord thread for the answer rather than providing it directly in this conversation.

question: Where in the Comprehensive Rules is it defined that action spells cannot be played in response to something and must be played on an empty chain?
answer:
Ruling: Action spells can only be played during closed states, not in response to other effects. This means they must be played when the chain is empty.

Nuances:

The relevant timing rule is found in the Reaction timing section of the rules, which specifies that reactions can be played during closed states (implying actions have different timing restrictions).

question: Can Ride the Wind move one of your units from battlefield A to battlefield B mid-showdown (during opponent's turn)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Ride the Wind can move one of your units from one battlefield to another mid-showdown during your opponent's turn, similar to how Charm works.

Nuances:

This can allow you to conquer a field during your opponent's turn

If you manage to do this twice in one turn and conquer both battlefields, you can win on your opponent's turn (if you're at 6 points)

When you move a unit into a battlefield where your opponent already has a unit, your opponent's unit becomes the attacker (they applied contested status first) and your unit becomes the defender

question: Does Mask of Foresight trigger when a unit with Challenge initiates a fight, or only during combat in showdowns?
answer:
Ruling: Mask of Foresight only activates during combat, which occurs when units from 2 players become present at a battlefield. Challenge does not create a combat, so Mask of Foresight does not trigger from Challenge fights.

Nuances:

Mask of Foresight will not activate during an open showdown (when you move to a battlefield without any units)

question: Does Blue Ahri (Ahri, Inquisitive) trigger Deflect, and if so, must you pay the Deflect cost?
answer:
Ruling: Ahri, Inquisitive's triggered ability does target and will trigger Deflect, but you may choose not to pay the Deflect cost. When you decline to pay, the triggered ability will not go on the chain.

Nuances:

Deflect is a mandatory cost for spells and activated abilities, but for triggered abilities you can opt not to pay

Ahri, Nine-tailed Fox (the legend) does not target, so this ruling does not apply to that card

question: If Foxfire targets a unit on the battlefield (chain 1), then the opponent moves that unit back to base (chain 2), does the damage still resolve, fizzle, or does the caster choose a new target?
answer:
Ruling: The spell will still resolve, but nothing will happen because Foxfire specifically requires the unit to be at a battlefield.

Nuances:

The spell does not fizzle completely, it just has no effect

No new target is chosen

question: If Thousand Tailed Watcher is played and moved to a battlefield, does a unit that is revealed from hidden at that battlefield come into play with -3 might?
answer:
Ruling: No, the hidden unit does not come into play with -3 might.

Nuances:

Thousand Tailed Watcher only affects units that are present at the battlefield when it is played

Units revealed from hidden after Watcher is already in play are not affected by its ability

question: If you pay the deflect cost to target a unit with deflect, and then the spell gets countered, do you get the rune back?
answer:
Ruling: No, you do not get the rune back. Countering a spell does not refund any costs paid for that spell, including the mandatory additional cost from deflect.

Sequence:

You pay the deflect cost (mandatory additional cost) when targeting a unit with deflect

If the spell is then countered, it does not resolve

The costs paid (including the deflect cost) are not refunded

Nuances:

This is similar to how you don't get energy back if a spell is countered - costs are paid regardless of whether the spell resolves

The deflect cost is a mandatory additional cost for targeting, not a cost that depends on resolution

question: What does 'unrecognizable' mean for card alter rules in Riftbound?
answer:
Ruling: Card alters should be limited to border extensions to avoid making the card unrecognizable. The head judge will make the final determination.

Nuances:

Even if the altered art depicts the same character, it can cause confusion since multiple cards may feature that same character

Completely different artwork is problematic even when showing the same character

question: When multiple units die simultaneously from Bullet Time, does the player choose which unit is saved by Zhonya's?
answer: Ruling: Yes, when multiple units die simultaneously from Bullet Time, you get to choose which unit Zhonya's saves.

question: Can you use Seals to pay for themselves?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot use a Seal you are trying to play to pay for itself, because you pay costs before the card enters play. However, you can use a Seal already in play to pay for a second Seal, as long as it matches the correct domain (color).

Sequence:

Pay costs for the card (including using Seals already in play)

The card enters play

Nuances:

A Seal already in play can pay for another Seal being played if it's the correct domain

A Seal cannot pay for its own cost since it's not in play yet when costs are paid

question: Does Forge of the Fluft allow you to attach an already attached equipment to a different unit?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Forge of the Fluft allows you to attach an equipment that is already attached to one unit to a different unit.

Sequence:

When you attach a card, it automatically detaches from any card it is currently attached to

The equipment then attaches to the new target

question: Can Sett the Boss's legend ability be used during the opponent's turn?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Sett's legend ability is a replacement effect that is active at all times, including during your opponent's turn.

Nuances:

The ability is a replacement effect, not a triggered ability

It does not require an action or reaction to use

It resolves whenever a unit is about to die, regardless of whose turn it is

question: After initial attack/defend triggers resolve, does the attacker retain focus?
answer:
Ruling: The attacker retains focus after the initial attack/defend trigger chain resolves. The attacker always gets to play an action first in showdown.

Sequence:

Attacker has focus during the initial chain

After initial chain resolves, attacker still has focus

Attacker plays first action in showdown

Nuances:

This is a known oversight in the rules that will be fixed in updated rules

Focus is the ability to start a chain with activated abilities and spells; starting a chain with a triggered ability does not cause you to lose focus after that chain resolves

question: Does selecting your own units for Divine Judgement count as targeting for Not so Fast to counter?
answer:
Ruling: No, Divine Judgement does not target. The spell itself doesn't target anything - players choose units as part of resolution.

Nuances:

Sets of objects chosen by multiple players (as in Divine Judgement) are not considered targets

This is similar to how Cull works - the choosing happens during resolution, not as targeting

When a single player chooses a set of objects (like Back to Back choosing "two friendly units"), those are still considered targets

The rule about sets not being targets only applies when multiple players are choosing

question: Can floated runes be combined with newly exhausted runes to pay for a unit's energy cost?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, floated energy can be combined with newly exhausted runes to pay for a unit's total energy cost.

Sequence:

Float energy from runes (e.g., 2 energy)

Spend other resources if needed (e.g., power for abilities)

Exhaust additional runes to combine with floated energy to meet the total cost (e.g., 2 floated + 2 newly exhausted = 4 total energy for a 4-cost unit)

question: When Green Yasuo deals 6 ability damage to Orange Master Yi (who has +2 might from defending alone), then Yasuo is moved to base with Flash during the showdown, does Master Yi die? When does the +2 might passive end?
answer:
Ruling: Orange Master Yi survives. Flash does not cause the combat showdown to end, and the combat continues to full resolution including cleanup.

Sequence:

Green Yasuo deals 6 ability damage to Orange Master Yi during the showdown

Green Yasuo is moved to base with Flash

Orange Master Yi remains at 8 might (6 base + 2 from defending alone) with 6 damage marked

Combat showdown continues to completion

During cleanup, damage is healed before "defender" status is cleared

Master Yi heals to full while still at 8 might

After healing completes, defender status ends and Master Yi returns to 6 might with no damage

Nuances:

Once a combat showdown starts, it doesn't end until fully resolved, even if one player no longer has units at that battlefield

Passive effects like the +2 might from defending alone (and Shield) remain applied until after the combat has fully resolved and units lose defender status

Damage is healed before defender status is cleared during combat showdown cleanup

question: How does the repeat mechanic work with counterspell effects? Are they two separate spells that must be countered separately, or does a single counterspell counter both?
answer:
Ruling: A single counterspell will counter both the original spell and the repeat effect, as they are treated as the same spell.

Nuances:

If a repeat spell has the original spell not target an enemy unit/gear, but the repeat effect does target an enemy unit/gear, cards like Not So Fast can likely be cast on it to counter (because the spell will have a matching unit as a target overall), but this needs confirmation from the new rules.

question: Does charming a unit to an open battlefield cause them to conquer it?
answer: Ruling: Yes, charming a unit to an open battlefield causes them to conquer it and score a point.

question: Does Ezreal's 'I don't deal combat damage' ability mean his might is added to the sum during showdowns but deals 0 damage, or does he not contribute his might to the sum at all (like a stunned unit)?
answer:
Ruling: Ezreal does not contribute his might to the sum during showdowns, similar to how stunned units work.

Nuances:

The text "I don't deal combat damage" appears to function synonymously with the stun modifier for combat purposes

Stunned units don't contribute their might to the sum (per CR 411.1.b)

The alternative interpretation (adding might to sum but dealing 0 damage) would create unusual assignment scenarios but is considered unlikely to be the intended design

question: If I buff my Fiora to give her Deflect after my opponent has already cast a spell targeting her, does my opponent have to pay the Deflect cost?
answer:
Ruling: No. When a spell is finalized (targets chosen and costs paid), those choices are locked in and cannot be changed. Giving Fiora Deflect after a spell targeting her has already been played does not retroactively add a Deflect cost to that spell.

Sequence:

Opponent plays spell targeting Fiora (without Deflect)

Opponent finalizes the spell by choosing targets and paying costs (no Deflect cost at this time)

Spell is now on the chain with locked targets and costs

You respond by buffing Fiora to give her Deflect

The original spell resolves without requiring Deflect payment

Any NEW spells cast after Fiora gains Deflect would require the Deflect cost to be paid

Nuances:

If you buff Fiora to 5 might (giving Deflect) and opponent casts two Stupefys simultaneously before either resolves, they pay Deflect twice

If the first Stupefy resolves (removing Deflect), the second Stupefy would not require Deflect payment

Reflexive trigger spells like Falling Star work differently - they create targeting effects on resolution, so buffing Fiora before the Star resolves (but after it's played) can force Deflect payment on the triggers

question: When a Draven at battlefield 1 moves to battlefield 2 with Ride the Wind, and an opponent's Sivir at battlefield 2 moves to battlefield 1 with Ride the Wind after combat is created, can the Draven player resolve the combat showdown (and draw a card with Draven's legend ability) before the new showdown at battlefield 1 starts?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the combat showdown at battlefield 2 must fully resolve before the staged showdown at battlefield 1 can start. Draven will draw a card from his legend ability because this was a combat showdown, even though no enemy units remain at that battlefield.

Sequence:

The combat showdown at battlefield 2 continues until both players pass focus on it

Draven triggers his draw 1 ability as this was a combat showdown

After the combat showdown fully resolves, the staged showdown at battlefield 1 begins

Nuances:

Even though no enemy units remain at the battlefield where combat was created, it still counts as a combat showdown for triggered abilities

A staged showdown cannot start until the current showdown fully resolves

question: When Stormbringer moves a unit to Kog'maw's battlefield and kills Kog'maw, does the moved unit take damage from Kog'maw's Deathknell trigger?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the unit moves to the battlefield first via Stormbringer, then Kog'maw's Deathknell trigger resolves and deals damage to the moved unit.

Sequence:

Stormbringer resolves completely, moving the unit to Kog'maw's battlefield

Kog'maw dies and its Deathknell trigger goes into a pending state

After the initial chain completes, Kog'maw's trigger goes on the chain

The Deathknell damage resolves, affecting the unit that was moved there

Nuances:

Deathknell triggers go into a pending state when the unit dies and trigger after the initial chain that caused the death completes

Stormbringer is not broken up into separate effects like Falling Star

question: Can Bard move himself when he's played?
answer: Ruling: Yes, Bard can move himself when played. The ability says "any number" of units, not "any number of other units," so Bard can include himself in the units he moves.

question: When an opponent plays Rebuke on an equipped unit in the battlefield, what happens to the attached gear?
answer:
Ruling: When a unit with attached gear is affected by Rebuke (or dies, is banished, or recycled), the attached cards detach and gear is recalled to base if not already in base.

Sequence:

The unit is affected by Rebuke

Attached cards detach from the unit

Gear cards are recalled to base (if they are not already in base)

question: When playing a hidden card with Viktor Blue in play, does Viktor's 'when you play a card' ability trigger when the hidden card is placed on the battlefield or when it is revealed?
answer:
Ruling: Viktor's ability triggers when the card fully resolves (completes the play process), not when it is initially revealed or placed.

Sequence:

Hidden card is revealed (Pending state)

All choices are made and costs paid (Finalized state)

Card effect is implemented and removed from chain (Resolved state)

Viktor's "when you play a card" ability triggers after the card is fully resolved

Nuances:

If the hidden card is countered (e.g., by Defy), it never fully resolves, so Viktor's ability would not trigger and no token would be created

question: If I use Ravenborn Tome and play Hextech Ray, then my opponent uses Mystic Reversal to gain control of Hextech Ray, how much damage does the spell do?
answer:
Ruling: When your opponent takes control of Hextech Ray with Mystic Reversal, they become the controller and are considered to be playing the spell. Since they don't control Ravenborn Tome, the spell does regular damage (not the boosted damage from Tome).

Nuances:

"Playing" a spell means properly resolving it without it being countered

The "you" in Ravenborn Tome refers to the controller of the Tome

When a spell changes control, the new controller is the one "playing" it for the purposes of card effects

question: How many warnings does a player need to receive a game loss in Summoner Skirmish?
answer:
Ruling: 3 warnings of the same category results in a game loss.

Nuances:

Examples of things that could result in warnings include general errors and violations of the Rules of Riftbound

The tournament rules document contains detailed guidance on warning categories and penalties

question: Does the layers update change how Thousand-Tailed Watcher's -3 power effect works? Specifically, is the effect retroactive or does it snapshot?
answer:
Ruling: Thousand-Tailed Watcher's -3 power effect is a snapshot that only applies to units in play when it resolves. It does not continuously check or apply to units that enter play afterward.

Sequence:

Watcher's effect resolves and reduces the power of all current units by 3 (to a minimum of 1)

The effect stops checking after it resolves

Units that enter play after Watcher resolves are not affected

If an affected unit is later buffed, it simply adds to its current power (no retroactive recalculation)

Nuances:

Hidden units are not affected because they are not in play when the effect resolves

The layers update does not change this snapshot behavior; it only addresses issues where later layers affect earlier layers (like Fiora's might reduction affecting her traits)

Other similar effects like Grand Strategem work the same way (snapshot, not continuous)

question: Can a player react to Watchful Sentry's deathknell trigger by playing a hidden Teemo that was face-down on the battlefield, and how does this resolve?
answer:
Ruling: You can technically play Teemo in reaction to the deathknell trigger, but Teemo becomes essentially a vanilla unit in this situation because he can only be played after players and units have had attacker and defender designations removed.

Nuances:

This is a weird edge case situation that may have rules clarifications in the future

The interaction becomes even more complex with Teemo Strategist

Players should check with their head judge when this situation arises

question: Can you attack with a unit and play Shen as a reaction to add him to the attack?
answer: Ruling: No, you cannot play Shen as a reaction to add him to an attack. You can only play units to battlefields you control.

question: If a defender moves away from a location during combat, does the attacker lose its attacker designation, and would cards that buff 'while it's an attacker' still work?
answer:
Ruling: The attacking unit retains its attacker designation even if the defender moves away from the location during combat. Cards that buff a unit "while it's an attacker" (like Cleave) will still apply.

Nuances:

The attacker designation persists through the combat even when there is no longer a defender present at the location.

question: Can Baited Hook be used during a showdown to play Noxus Hopeful into a contested battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Baited Hook cannot be used during a showdown because it is base speed, not action speed. Additionally, units can only be played into a battlefield you control, not a contested one.

Sequence:

Baited Hook must be used at base speed (outside of showdowns)

Units can only be played to battlefields you control

During a showdown, neither base speed abilities nor playing units into contested battlefields is allowed

Nuances:

The illegal play attempted to combine multiple rule violations: using a base speed ability during a showdown and playing a unit into a contested battlefield

question: Can you write down the enemy's hand in your notepad while looking at it with Sabotage?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you are allowed to write down the opponent's hand in your notepad while using an effect that lets you look at their hand.

Nuances:

This applies to any effect that allows you to look at the opponent's hand, not just Sabotage specifically.

question: If I move Traveling Merchant, do I have an option to not use his ability?
answer:
Ruling: You must use triggered abilities unless they say "may". For Traveling Merchant, there is no "may", so you have to use the ability every time it moves.

Nuances:

The trigger will still go on the chain even if it says "may"

You decide whether or not to do the effect when it resolves (for "may" abilities)

question: Are combat cleanup and end of turn cleanup subject to the effects of 'Cleanup' (such as chain items not resolving, legal items not executing, priority and focus not passing), or are they only cleanups when a special cleanup is invoked?
answer:
Ruling: Combat cleanup and end of turn cleanup are NOT Cleanups (capital C) as defined by the cleanup rules. Only the special cleanup steps (like 440.1.a) that are explicitly numbered as cleanup steps count as actual Cleanups.

Nuances:

The fact that the section heading contains the word "cleanup" does not make all steps within it subject to Cleanup rules

Steps that are Cleanups are clearly identified by having cleanup step numbers

This creates some edge case problems in the rulebook that may need future clarification or errata

Until official clarification, tournament rulings on related edge cases are up to the head judge

question: Can you use a Seal to play another Seal by using it as the power cost?
answer: Ruling: Yes, you can use a Seal to pay the power cost for playing another Seal.

question: Does Void Hatchling's ability (which triggers on revealed cards) work with Stacked Deck (which makes you look at cards instead of revealing them)?
answer:
Ruling: No, Void Hatchling's ability does not work with Stacked Deck because "look" and "reveal" are distinct actions. Void Hatchling only triggers when cards are revealed, not when you look at them.

Nuances:

Nocturne received errata to include both "reveal" and "look" in its effect, but this was a specific exception

Cards like Void Hatchling are designed for archetypes that specifically work with revealing cards, so the limitation is intentional

question: If Watcher sends a unit from 2 might to 1 might, then that unit is buffed by 1 might, does it go back to 2 might or stay at 1 might?
answer:
Ruling: The unit goes back to 2 might. Watcher's effect is continuous, so when the unit's might is increased, Watcher reapplies its effect based on the new total.

Sequence:

Watcher is played and reduces a 2-might unit to 1 might

The unit receives a +1 might buff

Watcher's continuous effect reapplies, reducing the unit back to 2 might total

question: How do buffs and debuffs interact when calculating a unit's might, specifically when Smokescreen (-4 might) is applied to a unit with base 1 might and a +1 might buff?
answer:
Ruling: Buffs and debuffs are applied in layers - increases first, then decreases. Smokescreen snapshots its debuff value when it resolves (calculating the reduction to a minimum of 1 might), then continuously applies that snapshotted value for the rest of the turn.

Sequence:

Start with base might and apply all increases (buffs)

When Smokescreen resolves, it calculates its debuff based on the current might value, reducing to a minimum of 1

Smokescreen snapshots this debuff amount and applies it continuously

Any subsequent buffs applied that turn are added to the calculation alongside the snapshotted debuff

Nuances:

In the example of 1 base might + 1 buff = 2 might, Smokescreen would snapshot to -1 might (since 2 - 4 = -2, but minimum 1, so the reduction is only -1), resulting in final 1 might

If you buff a Smokescreened unit in the same turn, you calculate from the current value (1 might), not from a negative value

If En Garde resolves before Smokescreen on a 1 might unit: 1 + 2 = 3, then Smokescreen snapshots to -2 (3 - 4 = -1 minimum, so -2 reduction), then if another En Garde resolves it becomes 1 + 2 + 2 - 2 = 3 total

question: Does Sett Brawler's ability require both playing AND conquering to get a buff, or does it trigger separately on each event?
answer:
Ruling: Sett Brawler's ability triggers separately - once when played and once when it conquers. Each trigger grants a buff independently.

Nuances:

If the ability required both conditions, it would only say "When I conquer" since every card with that condition must be played first anyway

question: Does Iron Ballista count as ability damage for interactions with Unyielding Spirit and Deflect?
answer:
Ruling: Iron Ballista counts as ability damage, so Unyielding Spirit prevents it. If you target a unit with Deflect, you must pay its power cost because you are choosing to select that unit.

Nuances:

Iron Ballista is both ability damage and gear damage (though nothing currently cares about the gear damage distinction)

question: Can you cast Retreat before an opponent gains a hold to win the game?
answer: Ruling: You cannot react to an opponent scoring a hold point. You must play Retreat earlier, either during your own turn or in response to a "at the beginning of your turn" ability if one goes on the chain, as those happen before scoring.

question: Can Jinx Rebel be readied more than once per turn, and does she still get +1 if already ready when you discard?
answer:
Ruling: Jinx Rebel can be readied multiple times per turn, with each discard trigger activating her ability separately. If she is already ready when you discard, she still gets +1 (do what you can).

Nuances:

You must actually discard a card for the ability to trigger; if you have no cards to discard, the ability does not activate.

question: Does Ravenbloom Student gain +1 Might after every spell cast, allowing it to potentially gain +12 Might from casting 12 one-cost spells?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Ravenbloom Student gains +1 Might until end of turn after each spell you cast, so casting 12 one-cost spells would result in +12 Might total.

Sequence:

Cast a spell

Ravenbloom Student gains +1 Might until end of turn

Repeat for each spell cast

All Might bonuses stack and last until end of turn

question: If a player is at 7 points with no units on the battlefield, and they conquer a battlefield choosing to draw 1 card instead of gaining a point, does that count as scoring and allow them to conquer a second battlefield to win?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, drawing 1 card instead of gaining a point due to final point restrictions still counts as both Conquering and Scoring, allowing you to conquer a second battlefield and win the game.

Sequence:

Conquer first battlefield at 7 points, choosing to draw 1 card

This counts as Scoring even though no point was gained

Conquer second battlefield

Win the game

question: If an opponent controls both battlefields at the start of my turn, and I kill their unit on one battlefield, then they move their unit from the other battlefield during my attack, do they still score a point even though they controlled that battlefield at the start of my turn?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, they score a point. You can only score a battlefield once per turn, and since they haven't scored it during your turn yet, they can score it when they gain control at the end of the resulting showdown.

Sequence:

Opponent controls both battlefields at start of your turn

You kill their unit on battlefield A

You attack battlefield B (where they have a unit)

Opponent moves their unit from battlefield B to battlefield A

A showdown occurs at battlefield A after your current combat ends

If opponent is the only player controlling units at battlefield A at the end of that showdown, they score a point

Nuances:

To score a battlefield, you must not have scored it that turn AND you must gain control of it at the end of the showdown

Moving to a battlefield you already control does not open a showdown

The showdown only takes place after the current combat ends

question: If I use Void Seeker to deal 4 damage to a 7 might unit, then use Smoke Screen to reduce it by 4 might, does the unit die?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the unit will die during the next cleanup when the game checks if damage marked on it is greater than or equal to its might.

Sequence:

Apply Void Seeker (4 damage) and Smoke Screen (-4 might) in either order

During the next cleanup, the game checks if damage ≥ might

The unit dies (4 damage ≥ 3 might)

Nuances:

The order of applying damage and might reduction generally doesn't matter, as long as damage isn't healed between application and cleanup

Order only matters for "when you kill with a spell" triggers: Smoke Screen first then damage counts as a spell kill, but damage first then Smoke Screen does not count as a spell kill

question: Does Janna's healing ability remove the -3M debuff from Watcher, or does healing only work against marked damage?
answer:
Ruling: Healing clears marked damage from units. Healing does not negate effects like Watcher's that lower might.

Nuances:

If you want Janna to heal units after they take damage from an action spell, you need to play Janna on a new chain after the damage spell resolves

If Janna is played in response to an action spell like Wages of Pain, Janna's ability resolves first before the spell deals damage
