Riftbound rechecks spells and abilities at resolution, so location-dependent effects like "here" must be valid when the ability resolves, not just when it triggers

question: If a player starts their turn at 6 points without holding any battlefield, can they win by conquering both battlefields in the same turn?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, if you start your turn at 6 points with no hold, you can win by conquering both battlefields in the same turn.

Sequence:

Start turn at 6 points with no battlefield held

Conquer first battlefield (score 7th point)

Conquer second battlefield (score 8th point and win)

Nuances:

The final point restriction only applies if you would score a point by conquering and haven't scored at the other battlefield(s) this turn (either by conquering or holding) - in that case you draw a card instead

Since you're conquering both battlefields in the same turn, the restriction doesn't prevent the win

question: Can you activate card effects when you can't fully complete all parts of the effect, such as discarding fewer cards than specified?
answer:
Ruling: You do as much as you can when activating card effects. You can activate an effect even if you cannot fully complete all parts of it.

Sequence:

Perform each part of the effect in order

If you cannot fully complete a part (like discarding 2 cards when you only have 1), you do as much as possible for that part

Then proceed to the next part of the effect (like drawing cards)

Nuances:

The parts of an effect are independent unless explicitly linked with conditional language like "discard 2 to draw 2"

This applies even with an empty hand - you would discard nothing and then proceed to draw cards

If an effect uses "to" to link actions (e.g., "discard 2 to draw 2"), then you must fully complete the first action to perform the second

question: Can a player cut their own deck after their opponent has shuffled it during deck presentation?
answer:
Ruling: No, once your opponent has shuffled your deck after presentation, you cannot shuffle or cut it again. The deck presentation procedure is complete at that point.

Nuances:

A cut is considered a form of shuffle in Riftbound rules

If you are suspicious about how your opponent shuffled your deck, you should call a judge rather than cutting it yourself

question: If Stacked Deck reveals Nocturne, does it trigger Nocturne's ability to play him for 1 power?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, revealing Nocturne with Stacked Deck triggers his ability and allows you to play him for 1 power.

Nuances:

Nocturne's text "if you don't draw" refers to not drawing Nocturne itself, not other cards

Drawing is different from revealing or looking at cards

The card must be banished to use the ability

question: If I use Charm to move an opponent's unit into a battlefield where my Deadbloom is alone, does this trigger Master Yi's 'defend alone' ability?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, this triggers Master Yi's defend alone ability. The charmed unit is considered the attacker because it is the unit applying contested status to the battlefield.

Sequence:

You charm the opponent's unit into the battlefield

The moved unit applies contested status

Since the moved unit's controller is your opponent and they are applying contested, they are the attacker

Your unit (Deadbloom/Master Yi) is defending alone

Nuances:

This works the same way for any forced movement effect (Ahri passive, Blitzcrank pull, etc.) - the unit being moved is always the one applying contested status and is therefore the attacker, regardless of how they got there

question: What happens when an ability requires you to discard cards but you have no cards in hand (e.g., Red Jinx's 'when you play me, discard 2' or Zaun battlefield's 'when you conquer discard one, draw one')?
answer:
Ruling: When an ability requires you to discard but you have no cards in hand, the ability still resolves but you do as much as you can (DAMAYC). For Jinx, nothing happens. For Zaun's trigger, you don't discard but still draw 1 card.

Sequence:

The ability goes on the stack and creates a reaction window for both players

When it resolves, you perform as much of the effect as possible

Any parts you cannot do (discarding with no cards) are skipped

Any parts you can do (drawing) still happen

Nuances:

The ability still finalizes and creates a reaction window even if you cannot fully perform its effects

"Do as much as you can" (DAMAYC) principle applies - you perform the parts of the ability that are possible

question: When Tideturner's ability is put on the chain, does it store the destination location at that time, or does it determine the destination on resolution?
answer:
Ruling: Tideturner's ability does not choose or store a location when activated. It targets a unit at a different location, and on resolution, Tideturner moves to whatever location that unit is currently at (as long as it's different from Tideturner's location).

Sequence:

Tideturner hidden on battlefield A is played and targets a unit at battlefield B

Flash is chained targeting Tideturner (Flash always moves to base, no choice)

Flash resolves: Tideturner moves to base

Tideturner's ability resolves: The unit moves from B to base (where Tideturner currently is), then Tideturner moves from base to B (where the unit was)

Nuances:

The destination is determined on resolution based on current game state, not locked in when the ability is activated

Even though Flash and Tideturner have fixed/restricted destinations, this doesn't mean the destination is "stored" when put on the chain

question: If I hide Sprite Call, can I place the token on another battlefield or in base when I cast the spell?
answer:
Ruling: When you play a hidden Sprite Call, you must place the sprite token on the same battlefield where the spell was hidden. You cannot choose a different battlefield or your base.

Nuances:

Hidden cards have an additional restriction requiring you to choose the hidden location when determining where to play the card itself

This restriction applies even though Sprite Call doesn't target - it still chooses where to play the unit

You can alternatively play Sprite Call from your hand by paying its energy cost, which would allow normal placement choices

question: If I use Cleave on my Traveling Merchant in my base, then move it to a contested battlefield, but my opponent uses Flash on their unit in response to the on-move trigger, does the Traveling Merchant's Assault trigger? What type of showdown occurs?
answer:
Ruling: The Flash resolves before combat starts, so the battlefield becomes uncontested. A non-combat showdown begins instead of a combat showdown. The Traveling Merchant's Assault will not trigger because no combat is initiated.

Sequence:

Traveling Merchant moves to battlefield, triggering its on-move ability

Opponent responds with Flash, removing their unit

Combat stages then unstages because the battlefield is no longer contested

Non-combat showdown begins instead

Nuances:

This situation may not be precisely covered by the current rules as written due to an issue with unstaging certain combats

In tournament play, players should ask the Head Judge about this interaction before matches if it might come up

question: Can a player use resource cards from another game as runes in Riftbound?
answer:
Ruling: No, using resource cards from another game as runes is not legal.

Nuances:

The thread does not specify where in the rules this is stated, as the original question about rule citation was not answered.

question: What happens if TF (Twisted Fate) with Red Rune attacks a defender at Reaver Row?
answer:
Ruling: When TF with Red Rune attacks a defender at Reaver Row, both the "When I Attack" trigger and the "When I Defend" trigger go on the Initial Chain, with the defend trigger resolving first, then the attack trigger.

Sequence:

TF moves into enemy occupied Reaver Row

Both "When I Attack" and "When I Defend" triggers go on the Initial Chain

The opponent targets a unit of theirs when Reaver Row's trigger goes on the chain

The opponent decides whether to resolve Reaver Row's trigger before TF's trigger resolves (before TF flips up a Rune)

Defend trigger resolves first

Attack trigger resolves second

question: In FFA modes (1v1v1, etc) during a showdown, how is priority/focus passed?
answer:
Ruling: Priority and focus are passed in turn order, starting with the player who has priority, regardless of which players are currently controlling units at the battlefield.

Sequence:

Priority passes in turn order (regardless of game mode)

Focus passes to the "next player" when a chain resolves (next in turn order)

When players pass rather than start a new chain during a showdown open state, focus continues to pass in turn order

Nuances:

The initial chain order for triggered effects at the start of a showdown may differ from turn order, but priority/focus passing during the showdown follows turn order

Going later in turn order can be advantageous for reactions since reactions played later resolve earlier on the chain

question: Can you activate Hidden Within in response to Deathknell triggering during cleanup, before losing control of the battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can activate Hidden Within in response to Deathknell before losing control of the battlefield. When cleanup finishes, Deathknell is placed on the chain as a pending trigger, and you must resolve the chain before proceeding to the step where control is lost.

Sequence:

During cleanup, triggered abilities like Deathknell become pending but cannot be added to the chain yet

Once cleanup finishes, pending triggers are finalized onto the chain

The chain must be fully resolved before moving to the control-loss step

During chain resolution, you still control the battlefield and can activate abilities like Hidden Within

Only after the chain resolves does the game proceed to losing control of the battlefield

Nuances:

While cleanup is ongoing, no spells or abilities can be activated - triggers only wait as pending

Deathknell effectively stops the loss of control until it resolves because the chain must be resolved first

question: Can you recycle runes at reaction speed to float power in response to an opponent's action?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can recycle runes at reaction speed to float power because the rune itself has the ability to be recycled, which creates the limited action.

Sequence:

Opponent plays an action (e.g., Divine Judgement)

In response, you can recycle runes to float power

You retain both the floated energy and power in your rune pool

Nuances:

A card must specifically instruct you to recycle it; you cannot recycle cards at will without an ability that allows it

The rune's own ability is what makes recycling it a limited action that can be performed at reaction speed

This interaction can be used to trigger abilities that care about recycling runes (like Sivir's legend ability), though such abilities may have their own restrictions like requiring exhaust

question: If you use Aurora's end of turn effect to play Deadbloom, win the showdown, and conquer Targon's Peak, do you ready 2 runes from Targon's Peak since you're already in end of turn?
answer:
Ruling: No, you do not ready 2 runes from Targon's Peak. Once the Ending Step begins, all "at end of turn" triggers that are currently active go on the chain at that moment. After this point, no more "at end of turn" triggers can trigger for the rest of that turn.

Sequence:

At the Ending Step (317.1.a), all current "at end of turn" triggers go on the chain (Aurora's delayed ability in this case)

Aurora resolves, playing Deadbloom and staging combat

If you win the showdown and conquer Targon's Peak, its "at end of turn" trigger becomes active

However, the window for "at end of turn" triggers has already passed for this turn

Targon's Peak never "saw" the start of the Ending Step, only became active after that moment

Nuances:

This is consistent with how phase-based triggers work in all other phases

Phase-based triggers occur precisely when you hit the step specified in the rules, not a moment after

The Ending Step happens once per turn, and all relevant triggers must be present at that exact moment to trigger

question: Can a unit have multiple instances of Assault 1?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, a unit can have multiple instances of Assault 1.

Nuances:

The early understanding that multiple Assault 1s couldn't stack on a unit was incorrect.

question: When an opponent contests a battlefield with Stalwart Poro and you Rush to War into that battlefield, who is the attacker and defender? Does Stalwart Poro get its +1 bonus?
answer:
Ruling: When your opponent contests a battlefield and you Rush to War into it, your opponent becomes the attacker and you become the defender. Stalwart Poro does not get the +1 bonus because it is the attacker, not the defender.

Sequence:

Opponent moves unit to contest the battlefield (non-combat showdown)

You Rush to War, moving a unit in and staging a combat showdown

After the first showdown ends, the second (combat) showdown starts

The player contesting is designated as the attacker

You are designated as the defender

question: Can I respond after an enemy vanilla is played, like with Rebuke?
answer:
Ruling: No, when a vanilla is played, it goes onto the chain and immediately resolves and leaves the chain as a permanent, with neither side having priority for reactions.

Nuances:

Rebuke is action speed, so you cannot react with it anyway

question: If Karma (7 might, hit by Smokescreen) is targeted twice by Falling Star and saved by Sett's ability after the first resolution, does she die when the second Falling Star resolves?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Karma dies when the second Falling Star resolves. After being saved by Sett's ability (which recalls and debuffs her), she returns at 2 might with 3 damage marked, causing her to die.

Sequence:

First Falling Star resolves: Karma has 3 might and 3 damage marked

If Sett's ability is used: Karma is recalled and debuffed (doesn't die, buff removed)

Second Falling Star resolves: Karma has 2 might with 3 damage marked and dies

If Sett's ability is NOT used: Karma dies to the first Falling Star and the second one has no valid target

Nuances:

Technically Karma only dies once total, not "again" - either Sett replaces the first death or she dies the first time without Sett's intervention

question: When playing equipment cards, do they go to the board first before being equipped, or are they immediately equipped when played?
answer:
Ruling: Equipment cards go to your base first when played, then you must pay the Equip cost separately to attach them to a unit. The initial play cost does not include equipping.

Nuances:

Quick-Draw is an exception that allows equipment to bypass this normal process

The Equip cost shown on equipment is used both for the initial equip and for re-equipping after a unit dies

question: If I activate 2 Orb of Regrets against Stalwart Poro and then challenge the battlefield it's on, will the second Orb cancel out the shield effect?
answer:
Ruling: No, the second Orb of Regret will not cancel out the shield effect. The second Orb trigger will not reduce the Poro's might again since it's already at 1 might from the first Orb.

Sequence:

Both Orb of Regret triggers resolve, reducing the Poro to 1 might (the second trigger has no additional effect)

When you attack the 1 might Poro, the shield activates and increases it to 2 might

question: When do you tap Kaisa to add a Power when playing Hextech Ray in response to an opponent moving a unit to a battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: You tap Kaisa at the point when you play Hextech Ray, paying 1 energy and declaring the target. Kaisa's "add" ability can be activated during the process of paying costs for cards.

Sequence:

Opponent moves into a battlefield and passes priority

You gain priority and focus during the showdown

You tap Kaisa while playing Hextech Ray at action speed, paying 1 energy and declaring the target

Pass priority to opponent who can respond with a reaction or pass

If opponent passes, Hextech Ray resolves

Nuances:

"Add" abilities can be activated during paying costs for cards

question: If a unit is removed from a battlefield during a showdown, does priority continue and can players still cast actions even though no units are present?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the showdown proceeds as normal until both players pass, even if no units are left at the battlefield. Players can still cast action cards during the showdown.

Sequence:

Priority passes to the attacker to react to the removal effect

Once both players pass priority, the chain resolves

Focus shifts to the attacker (where they can play action cards)

If both players pass focus, the showdown ends

question: If a unit moves to an unoccupied battlefield and casts Cleave, does it get +3 attack since there are no defenders?
answer:
Ruling: No, the unit does not get +3 attack when casting Cleave on an unoccupied battlefield because without defenders present, it does not count as attacking.

Nuances:

The Assault 3 keyword lasts until the end of the turn

If an opposing unit is moved in during the showdown, a combat is staged and the unit retains its attacker status from the first showdown, gaining the +3 bonus during that combat

Multiple instances of Assault stack (e.g., two Cleaves would grant Assault 6)

question: When Player A controls a battlefield, Player B moves Traveling Merchant to that battlefield (triggering contested status), and Player A plays Flash in response to remove their own unit, what type of showdown occurs?
answer:
Ruling: This is a known rules gap that the current rules do not properly handle. The two reasonable interpretations are either a combat showdown occurs (skipping damage assignment since no opposing units are present) or the defender loses control and a non-combat showdown begins.

Nuances:

The contested status locks control of the battlefield, preventing the normal loss of control when a player has no units present

The rules don't clearly specify what happens when all defending units are removed in response to a move trigger before the move resolves

Kelly (a Riot representative) indicated the rules would likely be tweaked so the answer is "combat showdown," though they personally find "lose control + noncombat showdown" more intuitive

A potential fix being considered is moving the control lock to occur during a showdown/combat rather than when contested status is applied

question: If Phoenix is discarded with Get Excited, can Phoenix's ability trigger from the discard of that same action, or do the discard and damage happen simultaneously?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Phoenix's ability can trigger. The unit targeted by Get Excited dies during cleanup after Get Excited resolves, at which point Phoenix is already in the trash and can trigger.

Sequence:

Get Excited resolves, discarding Phoenix

Phoenix goes to the trash

The targeted unit dies during cleanup

Phoenix's ability can trigger from the trash

question: Does Heimerdinger's ability copy Renata's legend ability, which has an Exhaust cost but no Exhaust symbol?
answer:
Ruling: No, Heimerdinger does not copy Renata's legend ability. An Exhaust ability must be an activated ability that has the Exhaust symbol as its cost.

Nuances:

Having an Exhaust cost in text is not sufficient; the ability must have the actual Exhaust symbol to qualify as an Exhaust ability that Heimerdinger would copy.

question: When an opponent uses an effect to move one of my units to a battlefield they occupy (starting a showdown), who gains focus and priority?
answer:
Ruling: The player who owns the unit that was moved gains focus. The moved unit applies contested status and becomes the attacker, giving its owner focus (assuming the unit has no "when I attack" abilities).

Sequence:

Opponent moves your unit to their occupied battlefield

Your unit applies contested status to the battlefield

You gain focus as the attacker

Showdown proceeds with you having focus

Nuances:

This works the same whether you move your own unit or your opponent moves it - what matters is who owns the unit applying contested

If the unit has "when I attack" abilities, those would trigger and affect focus

If moved to an open (unoccupied) battlefield, focus and priority work the same way, but the unit is not considered an attacker unless there is actual combat

question: Does Zenith Blade heal between combat showdowns?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Zenith Blade heals between combat showdowns.

Sequence:

First combat showdown must end completely

Then the new combat showdown starts

Healing occurs in between these events

question: If you use Ride the Wind to move to an unoccupied battlefield during your opponent's turn (while they attack a different battlefield), do you score a conquer point?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can score on the opponent's turn if you successfully gain control of a battlefield.

Sequence:

Opponent attacks battlefield 2 where you are standing

You use Ride the Wind to move to battlefield 1 (which opponent previously controlled but is now empty)

After the showdown at battlefield 2 ends (both players had a chance to use abilities), you gain control of battlefield 1 since you are the only one there

You score the conquer point

question: When Watcher gives -3 Might (to a minimum of 1) to a 2 Might Poro, and then the Poro receives +3 Might from other effects later in the turn, what is the Poro's final Might?
answer:
Ruling: The Poro ends at 4 Might. Watcher's effect applies once when it resolves, calculating the actual reduction based on each unit's current Might at that moment (respecting the minimum of 1), and that specific reduction value is what persists for the turn, not the full -3.

Sequence:

Watcher resolves: 2 Might Poro receives -1 Might (not -3, because it can only go down to 1 Might minimum)

Later, when combat occurs, Poro receives +1 from Shield and +2 from Yi

Final calculation: 2 (base) - 1 (from Watcher) + 1 (Shield) + 2 (Yi) = 4 Might

Nuances:

Watcher's effect is a one-time triggered effect that snapshots the actual reduction applied to each unit

A unit already at 1 Might would receive 0 reduction from Watcher and be unaffected

The "-3 to a minimum of 1" restriction only applies at the moment Watcher resolves, determining what reduction value gets snapshotted

question: When casting a spell like Dragon's Rage or Charm, do you need to declare targets and destinations before opponents can counter it?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you must declare the target and destination when you cast the spell, before opponents can counter it with cards like Defy or other counter spells.

Sequence:

Declare target and destination when casting the spell

Opponent has opportunity to counter the spell

If spell resolves, Dragon's Rage creates a reflexive trigger (the "do this:" part) that targets a unit to fight

The reflexive trigger cannot be countered (only the original spell can be countered)

Nuances:

Dragon's Rage is unique because it uses a reflexive trigger - you only declare the initial target and destination when casting, not the unit it will fight

The fight target is chosen when the reflexive trigger is created upon resolution

Charm works the same way as Dragon's Rage's first part (declare target and destination, can be countered)

question: Can you win the game by moving a champion from one battlefield to another (using Ganking and Mistfall) to conquer both battlefields in one turn when at 7 points?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can win by scoring on both battlefields in one turn. When you move a champion from one battlefield to another and conquer the second battlefield, both scores count toward the "all battlefields" win condition even though the first battlefield is no longer occupied.

Sequence:

First, score the champion onto the first battlefield (Ganking/Windswept) via conquer or hold

Second, move that champion to the second battlefield and win the showdown

Score from conquering the second battlefield for the winning point

Nuances:

If you were at 7 points, you would draw 1 card from scoring on the first battlefield, then win from scoring on the second battlefield

This works the same way on both your turn and your opponent's turn

To win on an opponent's turn via conquer, you need to score on all battlefields during that turn (hold points from your previous turn don't count)

question: Does Flurry of Blades require paying the recycle cost for Deflect when there are multiple units with Deflect at battlefields?
answer:
Ruling: Flurry of Blades does not require paying recycle costs for Deflect because it does not target units.

Nuances:

Flurry of Blades programmatically selects units rather than having the controller choose targets

The phrase "deal 1 to" does not mean targeting - the spell blankets all units at battlefields without the controller making choices

Unlike targeted spells which cannot be played without valid targets, Flurry of Blades can be played even with no units at battlefields

question: Unable to determine - the original question was deleted or not included in the visible thread
answer: Unable to determine - the thread shows a user (Fernando) realizing they misread something and deciding to delete their post, but the actual question and answer are not present in the thread.

question: Does playing Sneaky Deckhand to an open battlefield earn you a point?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, if you play Sneaky Deckhand to an open battlefield and conquer it (opponent doesn't respond with removal like Gust), you score a point.

Nuances:

Playing a unit to a battlefield is not the same as moving, but the unit still contests the battlefield for scoring purposes

question: If opponent plays Icathian Rain and I respond with Hidden Blade using Sett's ability to save my unit and bring it back to base, does Icathian Rain fizzle or still persist?
answer:
Ruling: Icathian Rain persists and does not fizzle. The IR triggers don't require the unit to be at a battlefield, and Sett's replacement effect keeps the unit on the board (just at base), so the triggers will still have a valid target and continue to resolve.

Sequence:

Icathian Rain resolves and creates six reflexive triggers targeting units

If you play Hidden Blade after IR triggers target, you can kill your buffed unit at various points in the sequence

When the unit would die, Sett's replacement effect can prevent it from leaving the board by recalling it to base

The remaining IR triggers still see the unit as a legal target at base and continue dealing damage to it

If the unit was saved by Sett from the first death, the remaining triggers will kill it again

Nuances:

If the buffed unit is exactly 7 Might with the buff, you must choose between drawing 2 from Hidden Blade or saving the unit - you cannot do both (the unit will be recalled at 6 Might after the buff is spent and then take 6 more damage from remaining triggers)

If the unit is 7 Might or higher without the buff, you can both draw 2 and save it with Sett

If the unit is 6 Might or less, Icathian Rain can kill it regardless of timing

You can kill your buffed unit before IR resolves and decline Sett replacement to redirect all IR triggers to opponent's units (if you only control the buffed unit)

question: When Yasuo moves to a battlefield using Ride the Wind during a showdown, does he trigger his 'when I attack' ability, or is he classified as a defending unit?
answer:
Ruling: Yasuo will not trigger his "when I attack" ability because he gains the defender designation, not the attacker designation, when moved to a battlefield that is already being contested.

Nuances:

Units gain attacker or defender designation based on when they arrive at the battlefield, not based on which player is the turn player

The unit that moves to the battlefield last gets the defender designation in a showdown

question: How does Trifarian's passive +1 might interact with might reduction effects like Stupefy?
answer:
Ruling: Additions are applied before subtractions in the arithmetic layer, and snapshots occur. A unit with +1 from Trifarian and -1 from Stupefy would have 1+1-1=1 might.

Sequence:

Apply all additions first (e.g., +1 from Trifarian)

Apply all subtractions second (e.g., -1 from Stupefy)

Calculate final might using arithmetic

Nuances:

If a unit leaves the source of the addition (like leaving the war camp), the subtraction persists as a snapshot, so a recruit token that was 1+1-1=1 would become 1-1=0 after leaving

question: What does Annie specifically do? Does she get 2 extra runes at the end of her turn?
answer:
Ruling: Annie does not give you 2 extra runes. At the end of your turn, she creates a trigger where you choose 2 runes, and when that trigger resolves, those 2 runes will become ready if they are exhausted.

Sequence:

At end of turn, Annie creates a trigger

You choose 2 runes

When the trigger resolves, those 2 runes become ready if they are exhausted

Nuances:

This happens even if you only have 1 rune on the board

The specific word used to gain additional runes is "channel" (which is different from what Annie does)

question: If I activate Baited Hook targeting a unit, then respond by playing Hidden Blade to kill that unit, does Baited Hook still resolve and do I get its effect?
answer:
Ruling: Baited Hook will still resolve, but since the targeted unit is now dead, its Might Value is null. You will reveal 5 cards but be unable to play any of them, and all 5 will be recycled.

Sequence:

Activate Baited Hook targeting a unit

Respond with Hidden Blade, killing the unit

Unit dies, draw 2 cards from Hidden Blade

Baited Hook resolves with null Might Value

Reveal 5 cards but cannot play any

Recycle all 5 revealed cards

question: Does Volibear Imposing have to tank ability damage first, or just combat damage? Can Yasuo Remorseful target other units with his ability when Volibear Imposing is defending?
answer:
Ruling: Tank only applies to combat damage. Yasuo can target any unit at the battlefield with his ability, even when Volibear Imposing is defending.

Sequence:

Yasuo can use his ability to target any unit (including Snapvine Predator)

Combat damage occurs at the end of combat when both players sum their might and allocate lethal damage

Tank only applies during this combat damage step

Nuances:

Combat damage specifically refers to might calculations at the end of combat, not ability damage

question: When playing Promising Future with Lux as your Legend and revealing Final Spark while opponent reveals Mindsplitter, what is the correct order of resolution?
answer:
Ruling: When Promising Future resolves with Lux, both revealed cards are placed on the chain as pending during resolution, then Lux's legend trigger is added as pending. During cleanup, all pending items finalize in order (Mindsplitter, Final Spark with target declared, Lux trigger), then Mindsplitter skips reactions and instantly resolves adding its trigger to the chain.

Sequence:

Play Promising Future (costs 5+ energy)

Reactions can be made

Promising Future begins resolving, each player looks at their cards

Opponent places Mindsplitter on chain as pending, then you place Final Spark as pending

Promising Future finishes resolving, Lux legend trigger added to chain as pending

Cleanup happens: chain items finalize in order (Mindsplitter, Final Spark, Lux trigger). Final Spark target must be declared here

Mindsplitter skips reaction stage and instantly resolves, adding its trigger to the chain

Chain is now: Final Spark (already targeted), Lux trigger, Mindsplitter trigger

Reactions may happen

Mindsplitter trigger resolves

Lux trigger resolves (draw from Promising Future)

Final Spark resolves

Lux trigger from Final Spark resolves (draw from Final Spark costing 5+)

Nuances:

Final Spark also costs 5 or more, so it triggers an additional Lux draw when it resolves

You do not draw from Promising Future before Mindsplitter resolves

question: Can Miss Fortune - Captain use her Move trigger to ready another unit that attacked with her (Traveling Merchant), since both units are exhausted after declaring the attack?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Miss Fortune - Captain can target and ready another unit that attacked with her, such as Traveling Merchant, because triggers resolve after the triggering event completes.

Sequence:

Both Miss Fortune and Traveling Merchant exhaust and move to the battlefield when declaring the attack

After the attack is declared, Miss Fortune's Move trigger resolves

At this point, both units are exhausted and at the battlefield

Miss Fortune can target the exhausted Traveling Merchant to ready it

question: Can Defy counter spells like Cleave when they are played outside of showdowns (e.g., at a player's base)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Defy can be used to counter spells like Cleave even when they are played outside of showdowns, such as at a player's base.

Nuances:

Playing spells before entering showdown can help avoid other counter-effects like Gust, which can only be played at battlegrounds

Playing spells pre-combat allows you to know if they will be countered by Defy before committing to combat, helping you decide whether the combat is still viable

Units that gain bonuses from Assault will have those bonuses already applied if the spell is played before the showdown, making them immune to certain counters that check current Might values

question: Can the attacking player choose the order of their 'When I attack' triggers, and when are units considered 'in combat' for the purposes of playing Cannon Barrage as a reaction?
answer:
Ruling: When multiple triggers happen simultaneously, the controller decides the stack order, so the attacking player can sequence their attack triggers (like Anivia before Warwick). Units are considered in combat immediately when showdown starts at a contested battlefield, which occurs when moving units to an occupied battlefield resolves.

Sequence:

Move units to contested battlefield; showdown and combat start immediately

Attacker declares order of their attack triggers (e.g., Anivia first, Warwick last)

Defender triggers are added to the stack

Attacker gets priority and can play reaction-speed cards like Cannon Barrage

Stack resolves in reverse order (Cannon Barrage, then Anivia, then Warwick)

After all triggers resolve, attacker gets focus and priority for action-speed spells

Nuances:

Cannon Barrage can be played as a reaction on the stack after attack triggers are declared but before they resolve, allowing it to damage enemy units before other effects like Warwick's kill trigger

question: Can you play Reactions (like Shen or flip Hidden Units) after your units die to a spell during combat, and maintain control of the battlefield before losing it?
answer:
Ruling: During combat (when a battlefield is Contested), you maintain control of the battlefield even after all your units die to a spell, until both players pass focus without taking actions. This allows you to play Reactions like Shen or flip Hidden Units after your units die but before losing control. Outside of combat, you cannot do this - any Reaction would go on the chain before the killing spell resolves, causing the Reaction unit to also die.

Sequence:

Opponent attacks your battlefield (making it Contested)

Opponent plays a spell to kill your units

Spell resolves and kills your units

Cleanup happens but battlefield remains Contested, so you maintain control

Focus passes back to you

You can now play Reactions (Shen, Hidden Units) at the battlefield you still control

Combat continues until both players pass

Nuances:

This only works during combat when the battlefield is Contested

Outside combat, Reactions go on the chain before the killing spell resolves, so they would also be killed

You can play new Reactions onto the chain after some abilities resolve - there's a priority window after each chain link resolves

If a Deathknell ability triggers during combat, it creates a priority window where you could React and maintain control

question: In a 3+ player game, if Player A moves a unit to start a showdown but after the showdown only Players B and C have units remaining at the battlefield, who is the attacker in the resulting combat?
answer:
Ruling: This is an edge case not fully covered by the current rules. The attacker should be the player who applied the Contested status (Player A), but since they have no units present, combat cannot resolve properly.

Sequence:
To avoid this situation:

Player B moves their unit to the battlefield

Someone kills Player A's unit (removing Staged Combat)

Player C can then move their unit

Nuances:

CR 422.2.a prevents third players from moving units to battlefields with Staged Combat

The rules need clarification to handle cases where the player who applied Contested status no longer has units present

Suggested rule changes would tie Staged Combat status to the presence of units from the player who applied Contested, not just their identity as attacker

question: When a 1 Might unit is buffed to 2 Might by Trifarian War Camp and attacks Ahri (who applies -1 Might), does it stay at 2 Might because War Camp's buff is static, or does it become 1 Might?
answer:
Ruling: The unit becomes 1 Might. Ahri snapshots the unit's Might when her ability sees it (at 2 Might), then applies -1 Might continuously for the rest of the turn.

Sequence:

Unit starts at 1 Might base

War Camp buffs it to 2 Might while at the battlefield

Unit attacks Ahri

Ahri's ability sees the unit at 2 Might and snapshots -1 Might

Unit is now 1 Might for the rest of the turn while at the battlefield

Nuances:

If the unit leaves the battlefield, it loses War Camp's +1 Might buff and would go to 0 Might (due to still having Ahri's -1 Might applied)

A unit at 0 Might doesn't die unless it has non-zero damage marked on it greater than or equal to its Might

question: When a defender plays an action in combat, does focus pass back to the attacker after it resolves, or does the defender get to play a second action first?
answer:
Ruling: Focus bounces back and forth between attacker and defender after each action resolves.

Sequence:

Defender plays an action

Action and any reactions resolve

Focus passes back to attacker

Nuances:

When a player plays an action, they can choose to hold priority and play a reaction immediately, but this is uncommon and must be explicitly stated

A player who plays an action or reaction can continue to hold priority and play additional reactions if they wish

question: If Thousand Tailed Watcher is played and later in the turn the opponent plays a reaction speed unit (like Shen or Teemo) from hidden, will those units have the -3 applied to them?
answer:
Ruling: No, units played after Thousand Tailed Watcher resolves will not have the -3 applied to them. Thousand Tail and other spells and abilities that change stats do so when they resolve, and the amount added/removed and the number of units affected aren't updated until the effect wears off.

Nuances:

The exception is for passive abilities (like a battlefield that constantly gives everything +1), which continuously update. Thousand Tail is a triggered ability (indicated by 'When' in 'When you play me'), not a passive ability.

question: Does Unyielding Spirit prevent kill effects?
answer:
Ruling: Unyielding Spirit does not prevent kill effects because "kill" is not damage.

Nuances:

Replacement effects like Zhonyas can prevent kill spells, but those are not in red/orange colors

Reaction speed movement is an option to avoid kill effects like Hidden Blade

Unlicensed Armory exists as a counter option in red/orange

question: If a unit is moved to a battlefield on an opponent's turn (via Charm or Ride the Wind) and defeats the units there, does the unit's controller gain a Conquer point immediately, and then a Holding point at the start of their next turn?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you gain a Conquer point immediately when your unit defeats opponents and takes control of a battlefield on your opponent's turn, and then you gain a Holding point at the start of your next turn.

Nuances:

For Ride the Wind specifically, a showdown must be happening for the card to be played, so you must wait for your opponent to start one before you can use it to move your unit.

question: In a best of 3 tournament, if you have 2 different champion units that can qualify as chosen champion (like Ahri - Inquisitive and Ahri - Alluring) in your deck, can you choose which one is your chosen champion in game one after seeing the opposing Legend, or does the chosen champion have to stay the same for each game 1?
answer:
Ruling: The chosen champion must stay the same for game 1 of each match in a best of 3. You must register your chosen champion as part of your deck registration, and you cannot change it during game one. You can only swap your chosen champion during sideboarding between games.

Sequence:

Register your chosen champion as part of your deck list before the tournament

Play game 1 with the registered chosen champion

During sideboarding (between games), you may switch your chosen champion

Present your deck for subsequent games with either the original or new chosen champion

Nuances:

When registering your deck, you must specifically list your chosen champion separately (not just as part of the 40-card main deck)

Presenting a deck that doesn't match your registered deck is a rules violation

Sideboard cards cannot be used during game one

question: How does Targon's Peak work, specifically regarding when it triggers and when runes are chosen and readied?
answer:
Ruling: Targon's Peak triggers when conquering and creates a delayed trigger that resolves at end of turn, at which point runes are chosen as targets and then readied.

Sequence:

Targon's Peak triggers when conquering

It enters the chain with no targets

When it resolves, it creates a Delayed Trigger that will occur at the end of the turn

At the end of the turn, the delayed trigger occurs and 0-2 runes are chosen as targets

The trigger enters the chain

Runes are readied on resolution

question: When Smokescreen is played on a unit that later gains might from another effect (like Cleaver), does Smokescreen's might reduction snapshot at resolution or apply based on the unit's current might?
answer:
Ruling: Smokescreen's effect is "snapshotted" when it resolves, meaning the might reduction is determined by the unit's might at the time Smokescreen resolves and that reduction amount applies for the rest of the turn.

Sequence:

If Smokescreen is played before Cleaver resolves, it checks the unit's might at that moment and applies the corresponding reduction for the rest of the turn

If Smokescreen is played after Cleaver has completely resolved, it checks the unit's might (including the Cleaver bonus) and applies the corresponding reduction for the rest of the turn

Nuances:

In the example given, if the Noxus Hopeful has 4 might when Smokescreen resolves, Smokescreen only applies -3 might for the rest of the turn (not -4)

Waiting for Cleaver to fully resolve before playing Smokescreen allows the full -4 might reduction to apply, since the unit would be at 7 might when Smokescreen resolves

question: Can you use Teemo's leader ability to hide a Teemo Strategist directly from the champion zone onto the board, or do you have to pay 1 resource to put it in your hand first?
answer:
Ruling: You can hide Teemo Strategist straight from the champion zone onto the board without paying to put it in your hand first.

Nuances:

The original asker noted this is not intuitive based on the card language

question: Can a player play a reaction at the end of their opponent's turn when the opponent passes priority without starting a chain?
answer:
Ruling: You do not get priority by default on your opponent's turn unless they start a chain (via starting a showdown, finalizing a spell, activating or triggering an ability, etc).

Nuances:

Simply playing a unit does not give the opponent an opportunity to play a reaction unless something is triggered

You cannot play a reaction like Consult the Past in response to an opponent passing their turn if no chain was started

question: Can I cast a spell without legal targets (like Stupefy) just to draw a card?
answer:
Ruling: No, if a spell needs a target, you can't cast it without a valid target.

Nuances:

If there is a valid target when you cast the spell, but the target becomes invalid before resolution, you'll still draw the card

You cannot cast a spell with mandatory Deflect cost and decline to pay it (you can only decline Deflect for triggered abilities)

question: How does priority work during a Showdown in Riftbound, specifically regarding when Reaction cards can be played, when Action cards can be played after chains resolve, and how passing priority works?
answer:
Ruling: Reaction cards can be played anytime Action cards can be played, not just in response to Action cards. When a chain resolves fully, focus passes to the player who didn't start the chain, who now has priority to play actions.

Sequence:

When a chain is created, the player who controls the topmost item gets first priority to react

Only when that player passes priority can the opponent react

If both players pass priority on a card, that card resolves

When things resolve off the chain, both players get priority again (starting with the player who owns the next link on the chain)

After a chain resolves fully or a player passes without playing anything, the other player gets a window to play actions

To play multiple cards during your priority window, you must hold priority and play them consecutively; passing priority to your opponent counts as passing

Nuances:

For the Initial Chain (created by "When I attack/defend" abilities), the attacker retains focus after it resolves

For each chain afterwards, focus shifts to the next player

question: If my opponent moves a 1/1 unit to a battlefield and passes priority, then I play Hextech Ray to deal 3 damage to it, is there any window where they could play Primal Strength to save the unit?
answer:
Ruling: No, there is no window to play Primal Strength to save the unit in this scenario. Once the opponent passed focus to you without playing an action, they cannot respond to your Hextech Ray with an action. The unit will die when Hextech Ray resolves.

Sequence:

Opponent moves unit and passes focus without playing actions

You play Hextech Ray (starting a chain)

Opponent cannot play Primal Strength (actions cannot be used as reactions)

Chain resolves and unit dies from Hextech Ray damage

After the chain resolves, focus automatically passes back to opponent

Opponent could now play Primal Strength, but it's too late to save the unit

Nuances:

You can never react with an action - only reactions can be played in response to a chain

Focus automatically passes after each chain resolves, but this automatic passing does not count toward "both players passing"

Units die as soon as lethal damage resolves, not after all chains resolve

The opponent's only chance to save the unit was to play Primal Strength before passing focus initially

question: When an opponent plays Falling Star and you respond with Retreat to return your unit, does the opponent have to target their own unit twice (potentially killing it with Deflect)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, if Retreat removes your unit before Falling Star's reflexive triggers resolve, the opponent must still choose two targets. If only their Deflect unit remains, they must target it twice but do not pay additional power (Deflect only makes opponents pay extra, not the controller).

Sequence:

Falling Star is played (no targets declared yet)

Reaction window opens

Retreat is played, returning your unit to hand

Falling Star resolves, creating 2 reflexive trigger abilities on the chain

Opponent declares targets for each trigger (must target remaining units)

Reaction window opens again

Each trigger resolves individually

Nuances:

Spells with "do this:" wording create reflexive triggers that go on the chain after the spell resolves, so targets are chosen after opponents can react to the initial spell

Deflect only makes opponents pay extra power to target that unit, not the controller themselves

You get multiple reaction windows: one when Falling Star is initially played, and another after the reflexive triggers are created with targets declared

question: If a battlefield has one unit and one hidden unit, and the opponent plays Unchecked Power, can the hidden unit be flipped after the damage to prevent losing control of the battlefield, or must it be flipped before taking damage?
answer:
Ruling: The hidden unit must be flipped before taking the damage. You cannot flip it after damage to save it from being trashed when you lose control of the battlefield.

Sequence:

Unchecked Power deals damage to the unit

If the unit dies and you have no other units at the battlefield, you immediately lose control

When you lose control, any hidden card at that battlefield is immediately placed into the trash

Nuances:

There is no window to flip the hidden unit in reaction to losing control of the battlefield

The hidden unit will either die from Unchecked Power (if flipped before damage) or be sent from the hidden zone to trash during cleanup (if not flipped)

question: If Tasty Faefolk dies at a battlefield with Zhonya's hidden, can you flip Zhonya's in reaction to the Deathknell trigger to save the Zhonya's proc?
answer:
Ruling: You can flip Zhonya's in response to Deathknell, but this only saves the Zhonya's proc (prevents it from being trashed) - it does not save the Faefolk itself, which is already dead. Whether this works depends on if the battlefield is contested.

Sequence:

If Faefolk dies during combat (contested battlefield): Deathknell triggers, you still have control of the battlefield during the chain, you can flip Zhonya's in response to save the proc

If Faefolk dies outside combat (not contested): You immediately lose control of the battlefield when Faefolk dies, Zhonya's is trashed before you can react to Deathknell

Nuances:

The key factor is whether the battlefield is contested, not whether death was caused by combat damage vs ability

If Faefolk dies by ability mid-showdown (while contested), you can still save Zhonya's because control is locked until contested is removed

Control is locked during combat until the contested state is cleared, even if you have no units remaining

Flipping Zhonya's before Faefolk dies would save the unit but prevent the Deathknell trigger entirely

question: How does focus work in Riftbound combat, particularly regarding who gets priority to act and when combat/showdowns end?
answer:
Ruling: Focus is not retained by a player. Whenever a chain closes in combat or a showdown, focus passes to the next player in turn order. A showdown only ends when all players pass without starting a chain in succession.

Sequence:

Player plays an action (e.g., Hex Ray)

Players pass priority in succession

Action resolves

Focus immediately passes to the next player in turn order

If all players pass without starting a chain in succession, the showdown ends

Nuances:

Even if player A plays an action and all other players pass, player A will still have a chance to start a chain again when focus returns to them

The attacking player does not automatically get "final say" - focus continues to rotate until all players pass in succession

question: Are deck list submissions mandatory for Summoner Skirmish events?
answer:
Ruling: Deck list submission is mandatory for Summoner Skirmish at high OPL events according to the tournament rules.

Nuances:

The system does not currently allow submission via Carde

Common methods include email submission using Piltover Archive export registration sheets or paper lists

Digital decklists should be submitted as PDFs or typed in email, not as links to pages that could be updated during the tournament

Piltover Archive supports generating filled out PDFs for submission

Judges should perform deck checks randomly at Skirmishes

question: Do replacement effects like Sett and Zhonya use the stack/chain, and how do they work when multiple units are dying simultaneously?
answer:
Ruling: Replacement effects like Sett and Zhonya do not use the chain. They replace the core game mechanic of an object dying with what their card says to do instead.

Sequence: (when multiple units are dying simultaneously)

Active player chooses first whether to use their replacement effect

Non-active player then makes their choice

Nuances:

When something would die, the player confirms if they want to use the replacement effect (Zhonya is automatic, Sett involves a choice)

question: When you already have 7 points and conquer Zaun Warrens, what is the order of card draw effects?
answer:
Ruling: When you conquer Zaun Warrens at 7 points, you first attempt to score but draw a card instead (since you're at the 8-point limit), then Zaun Warrens' battlefield trigger goes on the chain since a conquest happened.

Sequence:

Conquer Zaun Warrens

Attempt to score the 8th point but draw a card instead (due to point limit)

Zaun Warrens' battlefield trigger goes on the chain

Nuances:

This assumes you didn't hold to get point 7, meaning you controlled zero battlefields going into the turn

question: If a unit with 2 Guardian Angels equipped dies, do both Guardian Angels get destroyed or just 1?
answer:
Ruling: Only one Guardian Angel will be destroyed when the unit dies, because only one can replace the dying event.

Nuances:

This interaction is similar to how Zhonya works with replacement effects

question: If an opponent plays Piercing Light targeting my unit, can I respond with Wages of Pain to kill that targeted unit before Piercing Light resolves, and if so, does Piercing Light still deal its second 2 damage to another unit?
answer:
Ruling: You can react with Wages of Pain after Piercing Light is played and targets are chosen. Piercing Light will still deal 2 damage to the other unit even if the first target is killed by Wages of Pain before Piercing Light resolves.

Sequence:

Opponent plays Piercing Light and declares both targets

You can respond by playing Wages of Pain to kill the first targeted unit

Wages of Pain resolves first, killing the targeted unit

Piercing Light resolves, dealing 2 damage to the second unit (the first damage instance has no valid target)

Nuances:

Once Piercing Light is on the chain and choices are made, those choices are locked in

All damage from Piercing Light is dealt while the spell is resolving; there is no moment between damage instances to respond

Wages of Pain can only target a unit at the battlefield where it was hidden

question: Is there an overtime procedure for best of 3 matches when both players have won 1 game each?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, there is an overtime procedure for best of 3 matches when the series is tied 1-1. The player with the most points at the end of 5 turns wins the overtime game.

Sequence:

When the overtime round is called, whoever's turn it is becomes turn 0

Play continues for 5 turns total

At the end of 5 turns, the player with the most points wins

question: Can Deflect stack, specifically with multiple Spirit's Refuge or with units like Fiora that gain Deflect conditionally?
answer:
Ruling: Deflect can stack as a keyword, but Spirit's Refuge specifically prevents stacking because it only grants Deflect "if they didn't already" have it. Multiple Spirit's Refuge in play will only grant Deflect once to buffed units.

Sequence:

When multiple Spirit's Refuge are in play, layers require choosing an order for abilities to apply

The first Spirit's Refuge grants Deflect to buffed units

The second Spirit's Refuge sees units already have Deflect, so its condition is not met

Result: buffed units only have Deflect x1

Nuances:

The keyword Deflect itself can stack in general

Spirit's Refuge's specific wording "if they didn't already" prevents it from stacking with itself

Units with "While I'm Mighty I have Deflect" type effects use "have" wording for passive abilities, which may interact differently with stacking

question: Does Heart of Dark Ice count as 'choosing' a unit when activated, triggering Irelia's ability to gain +1/+1 and potentially become active?
answer: Ruling: Yes, Heart of Dark Ice counts as choosing a unit when activated, which triggers Irelia's ability to gain +1/+1 and potentially become active through her legend effect.

question: If both players pass their actions sequentially in combat, can either player then play a reaction before combat damage?
answer:
Ruling: No. If both players pass sequentially on an empty chain, combat immediately progresses to combat damage with no opportunity to play additional cards.

Sequence:

Player 1 passes their action

Player 2 passes their action

Combat immediately progresses to combat damage

No opportunity to play reactions or other cards

question: Does Immortal Phoenix's effect work in the graveyard to revive when you play Cull the Weak and kill your own unit?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, if you play Cull the Weak and kill one of your own units, Immortal Phoenix can return from the graveyard.

Nuances:

Phoenix's effect does not require an enemy unit to be killed, so killing your own unit with Cull the Weak triggers the revival effect.

question: If a unit targeted by Void Seeker is moved off the battlefield by a chained Fight or Flight before Void Seeker resolves, does the unit still take damage?
answer:
Ruling: The unit will not take damage. The game checks legality again on resolution, and if the unit is no longer at a battlefield, it is no longer a legal target. You resolve as much as possible, which means you draw 1 card but deal no damage.

Sequence:

Void Seeker targets a unit on a battlefield

Fight or Flight is chained to move the targeted unit off the battlefield

On resolution, the game checks target legality again

The unit is no longer a legal target

Resolve as much as possible: draw 1 card, but deal no damage

question: If Vi is played and moved to an open battlefield with Ride the Wind (scoring a point and readying her), can she then use her Gank ability to move to another battlefield and score again, potentially scoring the 8th point if the first was the 7th?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Vi can use her Gank ability after being moved to a battlefield with Ride the Wind and scoring. If the first battlefield scored your 7th point, conquering the second battlefield with Gank would score your 8th point.

Sequence:

Play Vi and use Ride the Wind to move her to an open battlefield

Score a point (Vi is readied)

Use Vi's Gank ability to move to another battlefield

If that battlefield is open or conquered, score another point

question: Can you play reaction cards in response to spells/abilities resolving in the middle of a chain (after the chain is closed and resolution has begun)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, every time an item resolves from the chain, all players get a chance to add more reactions.

Sequence:

The chain closes and begins resolving backwards

After each item resolves, players can add reaction cards

This continues until the chain is fully resolved

question: If you control Zaun Warrens on your turn, then move all units back to base (e.g., with Flash), can you send another unit back to Zaun Warrens and get the conquer effect even though you already scored the hold point that turn?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot get the conquer effect again. You can only score each battlefield once per turn, and to conquer you must be able to score.

Nuances:

Even if you leave and return to a battlefield in the same turn, you cannot trigger conquer effects again if you already scored that battlefield

question: When a showdown starts and multiple attacker and defender abilities trigger, in what order do they go on the chain and who decides the order? When can players add reactions?
answer:
Ruling: When a showdown starts, all "when attacking" triggers are placed on the chain in an order chosen by the controller of those units, then all "when defending" triggers are placed on the chain in an order chosen by the defender. After triggers are arranged, the defender has priority to add reactions first (as the player who owns the top item on the chain), then the attacker can add reactions. Once both players pass without playing reactions, the chain resolves from the most recent (last) item.

Sequence:

All "when attacking" triggers go on the chain, order chosen by attacker

All "when defending" triggers go on the chain, order chosen by defender

Defender has opportunity to add reactions (as owner of top chain item)

Attacker can add reactions

Once both players pass, chain resolves from last to first

Nuances:

The first player able to react to items in the chain is the player that owns the top item in the chain

question: What is the correct sequence for setting up and starting a 1v1 game in Riftbound?
answer:
Ruling: Players reveal legends and champions first, then select battlefields (simultaneously in best of 3, randomly in best of 1), determine turn order, draw 4 cards, mulligan up to 2 cards in turn order, then the first player begins their turn.

Sequence:

Each player reveals legend and chosen champion

Each player selects a battlefield (in best of 3: set aside chosen battlefield and reveal simultaneously once both decided; in best of 1: select randomly)

Determine turn order (typically roll dice, winner chooses to go first or second)

Draw 4 cards

In turn order, mulligan up to 2 cards (recycle them and draw as many as recycled)

First player takes their first turn

Nuances:

In best of 3 matches, after the first game you cannot choose a battlefield used in a previous game of that match

Each subsequent game in a best of 3 requires selecting one of your remaining unused battlefields

question: Can a player play an action after an opponent's action or ability resolves outside of combat/showdown?
answer:
Ruling: Outside of a showdown, there is no window for a player to play actions after an opponent's spells or abilities resolve.

Nuances:

Actions cannot be played when there is a chain by definition

This restriction applies specifically to playing actions outside of showdowns

question: Can Daughter of the Void's legend ability be used on an opponent's turn, or does the reaction speed only allow it to be used at particular points during your own turn?
answer:
Ruling: Reactions that add energy/power can be tapped any time when you need to pay a cost for a spell/unit you are casting, including on your own turn.

Nuances:

Reactions that have "add" resolve immediately and do not start or interfere with a chain

question: Are digital devices (mobiles/electronics) allowed at high OPL Riftbound events to track life totals if in airplane mode?
answer:
Ruling: Digital devices are not allowed at high OPL events. Players are supposed to use pen and paper to keep track of history and changes. Dice are also not allowed to track points.

Nuances:

Some stores are allowing mobiles in airplane mode, but this violates the Tournament Rules

There is currently no formal mechanism to report stores not enforcing the Tournament Rules

Stores doing their own thing represents inconsistent enforcement across venues

question: If I Hextech Ray my own Immortal Phoenix, can I bring that same Phoenix back from the trash using its ability?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can use Immortal Phoenix's ability to bring itself back from the trash after using Hextech Ray on it.

Nuances:

This interaction is specifically cited as an example in the official rules

question: In a showdown, if both players pass on playing action cards during the action phase, can they still play reactions before the showdown ends?
answer:
Ruling: If both players pass during the action phase of a showdown, the showdown ends. However, you can play a reaction to start a chain anytime you could normally play a reaction.

Nuances:

Both the attacker's and defender's action plays can be reacted to during the action phase

Reactions can be played at any valid reaction timing to start a chain

question: Does the new Disintegrate errata 'Deal 3 to a unit at a battlefield. If this kills it, do this: draw 1' work within the rules, specifically regarding when the conditional reflexive trigger checks if the unit was killed?
answer:
Ruling: Disintegrate works as intended. The conditional reflexive trigger should be treated as a delayed triggered ability that checks whether the unit died from the spell damage during the cleanup step immediately following the spell's resolution.

Sequence:

Play Disintegrate

It deals 3 damage and creates a conditional reflexive trigger

Cleanup occurs

During cleanup, the unit dies from lethal damage

The delayed trigger condition is met and goes on the chain

The draw effect resolves and you draw 1

Nuances:

The ability doesn't use typical delayed trigger templating (like "when" or referencing a specific time), but should still be treated as a delayed trigger whose timeframe is implicitly "the cleanup following this spell"

The templating is considered suboptimal - it would work better as an explicit delayed trigger or as an unconditional reflexive ("Then do this: If it killed it, draw 1")

If the unit is removed by other means (like Hidden Blade) before cleanup, you do not draw because Disintegrate didn't kill it

question: Does Not So Fast counter Falling Star?
answer:
Ruling: Not So Fast cannot counter the Falling Star spell itself, but it can counter one of the two reflexive triggers that deal 3 damage, since those triggers target.

Nuances:

The Falling Star spell itself does not target, so it cannot be countered by Not So Fast

Falling Star creates two reflexive triggers that each deal 3 damage and do target

Not So Fast can counter one of these two reflexive triggers, but not both

question: Can a player react to a unit moving onto a battlefield before a showdown starts?
answer:
Ruling: A standard move without abilities triggering does not allow players to react before the showdown starts. The move triggers a cleanup, stages the showdown, and proceeds directly to the showdown without priority unless something triggers to open a chain.

Sequence:

Move occurs

Cleanup is triggered

Showdown is staged

Move triggers happen before showdown starts

If there are attack or defend triggers, players get priority to respond to the initial chain

If no triggers create an initial chain, no priority is given before showdown begins

Focus doesn't pass until the showdown is in progress

Nuances:

Players can only react to a move if something triggers to open a chain (like certain card abilities)

Move triggers happen before the showdown starts with it being staged

Players do get priority to respond to the initial chain if one exists, but focus doesn't pass until the showdown is in progress

question: Can the deal 6 damage triggered ability from Riptide Rex be reacted to?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the deal 6 damage can be reacted to. While permanents (units and gear) themselves cannot be reacted to because they don't linger on the chain, play effects are triggered abilities that enter the chain separately and can be reacted to.

Sequence:

You play Riptide Rex by paying its cost

It enters the chain but resolves immediately (no reaction window)

Its play effect (deal 6) triggers and enters the chain

Here each player can react with reactions

Nuances:

Permanents themselves don't linger on the chain and cannot be reacted to

Play effects are triggered abilities that are put on the chain as pending items after the permanent enters the board

The distinction is between the permanent itself (can't be reacted to) and its triggered ability (can be reacted to)

question: If a unit gains Deflect after it has already been targeted by a spell or ability, does the Deflect trigger and force the opponent to pay memory or recycle?
answer:
Ruling: Deflect only matters when targets are selected. If a unit gains Deflect after it has already been targeted, the Deflect does not trigger because targeting costs (including Deflect) are paid only once when players finalize the spell or ability.

Sequence:

Opponent selects targets for their spell/ability

Opponent pays all costs including any Deflect costs at that time

If the unit gains Deflect after this point, it has no effect on the already-targeted spell/ability

Nuances:

Deflect is an additional cost effect that must be paid during finalization

There is no window to make a spell fizzle via Deflect after targets have been chosen and costs paid

question: Can you play an action spell (like Primal Strength or Cleave) in response to an opponent's reaction spell (like En Garde) during a showdown?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot play action speed spells in direct response to a reaction spell like En Garde because there is already a chain active. You can only react (not act) when a chain exists.

Sequence:

You initiate showdown and gain Focus

You can use Focus to play action spells at this point, or pass Focus

If you pass Focus, opponent can use their Focus to start a chain (e.g., En Garde)

You may react to the chain, but cannot play action speed spells since a chain is active

After En Garde resolves, you get Focus back

You can now start a new chain with action spells like Primal Strength or Cleave

The showdown doesn't end until both players pass Focus in sequence

Nuances:

When initiating a showdown, you gain Focus first and have a window to play actions before your opponent can respond

Saying something like "move X to battlefield, any response?" is a shortcut for initiating the showdown and passing Focus

You have multiple opportunities to use action spells: when you first gain Focus at showdown start, or after opponent's chain resolves and you regain Focus

question: When using Charm to move an enemy to my backfield, who is considered the attacker?
answer: Ruling: When you use Charm to move an enemy to your backfield, that enemy is considered the attacker.

question: Can a player reveal a hidden Tideturner from one battlefield and use its swap ability to swap with a unit at a different battlefield where a showdown is occurring?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, this is legal. You can play reactions from any battlefield when there is an item on the chain, regardless of where the showdown is occurring. Hidden restrictions only apply to targeting, and Tideturner has errata that allows its ability to bypass that restriction.

Nuances:

You need something on the chain to react to, or a priority window to play Tideturner from hidden

If the attacking unit has an attack trigger, you can respond to that

Otherwise, you must wait until the opponent plays an action speed effect or passes focus and priority to you before you can play Tideturner

question: When I charm an opponent's unit to a battlefield I control, does that unit become the attacker, or is there no attacker since it's not the opponent's turn?
answer:
Ruling: When you charm an opponent's unit to a battlefield you already control, that unit becomes the attacker because it is the one contesting the battlefield.

Nuances:

The key factor is who controls the battlefield, not whose turn it is

The unit contesting the battlefield is designated as the attacker

question: If you score a point from a battlefield at the start of your turn, then move your unit out and move another unit into that same battlefield during the same turn, does this create a new showdown?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, this creates a new showdown because the control of a battlefield is being contested.

Nuances:

You cannot score another point from the same battlefield in the same turn, even though a new showdown is created

question: When Player A plays Stand United from hidden at battlefield A targeting their unit, and Player B plays Mystic Reversal to gain control of it: (1) Does Stand United retain the targeting restriction to the battlefield it was hidden from? (2) If Player B controls no units at battlefield A, how does resolution proceed?
answer:
Ruling: When a spell played from hidden is controlled by another player via Mystic Reversal, it retains the targeting restriction to the battlefield it was played from. The new controller cannot make new choices for targets, and if the original target is no longer friendly to them, the buff portion fails but other effects (like "buffs grant +1 Might this turn") still apply.

Sequence:

Stand United is played from hidden at battlefield A with targeting restriction "here"

Player B gains control via Mystic Reversal

The spell keeps its original target (cannot be changed)

On resolution, the buff fails because the target is not friendly to Player B

Player B still gets the "buffs grant +1 Might this turn" effect

Nuances:

Gaining control of a spell does not allow replaying it or changing its state - it was already finalized to the chain

The original target becomes illegal for the new controller because it's not a friendly unit to them

Secondary effects of the spell that don't depend on the illegal target still resolve for the new controller

question: Is it angle shooting or punishable for a player to announce 'I have Time Warp' (without playing it) to fish for a reaction from their opponent?
answer:
Ruling: Simply announcing you have a card or revealing private information is not angle shooting or punishable under current tournament rules, as players are allowed to reveal private information. However, if a player reveals a card in an ambiguous way that makes it seem like they are playing the card when they are not, judges should hold them to having played it.

Sequence:

Player may reveal private information (including cards in hand) without playing them

Opponent is not required to respond or reveal any information

If the reveal is ambiguous about whether the card is being played, judges should rule the card was played

If the reveal is unambiguous (e.g., holding card up without placing on table), opponent revealing information in response is their own mistake

Nuances:

Bluffing (positioning as if you have something without lying about game state) is allowed and distinct from angle shooting

Lying about private information appears to be allowed under current rules (though this varies by region - China explicitly prohibits lying)

Revealing cards to save time when showing deterministic/overwhelming game states is common and acceptable practice

If a player explicitly asks for information or a concession while revealing (e.g., 'I have Time Warp, wanna move to game 2?'), that would be angle shooting

The key distinction is whether the player misrepresents what game action is occurring

question: Can Temporal Portal be used with Defy?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Temporal Portal can be used with Defy.

Nuances:

Temporal Portal must be tapped ahead of time since it is not reaction speed

This makes the combination unlikely to occur in practice

question: Can you tap mana runes in the middle of resolving Stacked Deck (e.g., to float mana before recycling when you see cards you want to play)?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot tap mana runes in the middle of resolving Stacked Deck. You pay for cards (like Nocturne) while finalizing after Stacked Deck is fully resolved.

Sequence:

Stacked Deck resolves completely

You finalize and pay for any cards you want to play (like Nocturne)

During finalization, you can tap mana runes, float mana, and recycle

Nuances:

You technically need to tap mana in reaction to something, not in the middle of an ability resolving

When paying for a card like Nocturne after Stacked Deck, you can tap runes, float mana, then recycle before playing the card

question: Can Monastery of Hirana spend an enemy buff?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot spend enemy buffs. Players may only spend buffs on units they control.

Nuances:

The buff must be one you control

You can only control something in play, but it does not have to be a buff at a battlefield

question: Does a unit heal after taking damage from spells during a showdown on an uncontested battlefield (no combat)?
answer:
Ruling: Units do not heal after this showdown because no combat occurred. Units only heal during special cleanup after combat and at end of turn, and combat only starts if attacking and defending units are at the same battlefield.

Sequence:

Player 1 moves a unit to an uncontested battlefield

Player 2 casts Hextech Ray to damage/kill it during their focus

Player 1 casts Discipline in response to save the unit

No combat occurs (no opposing units present)

Unit does not heal after the showdown

Nuances:

Healing only occurs during special cleanup after combat and at end of turn

Combat requires both attacking and defending units to be at the same battlefield

question: Where do you play Zhonya's Hourglass - battlefield or base, and how does its activation work?
answer:
Ruling: You can choose to play Zhonya's Hourglass either to your base (open and ready) or hide it at a battlefield. When played to your base, it functions as a passive replacement effect that automatically triggers when the next friendly unit dies, regardless of whose turn it is.

Sequence:

If played to base: Goes down ready, opponent cannot react to it being played, remains in base looking for the next friendly unit death

If played hidden to battlefield as a reaction: Goes to the battlefield when activated, then returns to base during cleanup

Nuances:

Zhonya's uses a replacement effect, not an activated ability - it automatically saves the next unit it sees die

Playing it hidden to battlefield offers a cheaper payment method and surprise factor

When Zhonya's is visible in base, opponents can strategically kill a small unit first to waste its effect

question: When is first player decided in 1v1 - before or after battlefields are revealed?
answer:
Ruling: First player is determined after battlefields are placed. Battlefields are placed face-up in the battlefield zone (a public information zone) before turn order is chosen.

Sequence:

Legend revealed

Chosen Champion revealed (already set during deck registration, modified during sideboarding)

Battlefields chosen and placed face-up

Decks shuffled and presented

Turn order determined (first player chosen)

Opening hands drawn

Mulligans

Nuances:

Many players incorrectly hide battlefields and reveal them after choosing turn order, but this is not supported by the rules

Battlefields are public information once placed in the battlefield zone, so there is no rule requiring them to be "revealed" - they are simply placed face-up

During sideboarding (between matches), you do not know your opponent's battlefield before making sideboard decisions

question: Do conditional passive abilities apply mid-resolution of a spell/ability, or only during the next cleanup?
answer:
Ruling: Passive abilities check constantly, including during the resolution of spells and abilities.

Sequence:

When a spell begins resolving that changes game state (like drawing cards)

Passive abilities immediately recognize those state changes

The passive ability applies before the spell finishes resolving

Nuances:

In the first example (Draw 2, Deal 1 damage to all units), the unit gains +1 Might from drawing cards before damage is dealt, so it survives with 2 Might

In the second example (Draw 2, Kill all units with 1 or less Might), the unit gains +1 Might from drawing cards before the kill effect checks, so it survives with 2 Might
