Showdown begins at the battlefield Teemo Strategist controls

Teemo's defend trigger goes on the chain

When Teemo's ability reveals Nocturne from the deck, Nocturne's triggered ability allows him to be played

Nocturne can be played into any battlefield his controller controls, including the battlefield being defended

Nuances:

Normal units cannot be played during showdowns because the game state is "showdown closed" (not neutral open)

Units with "action" or "reaction" tags have different timing exceptions than Nocturne's specific triggered ability

The restriction isn't specifically about playing units into battlefields you're defending - it's about the game state during showdowns

Card text supersedes normal rules when there's a contradiction

question: Does Ember Monk get +2 might when a card from hidden is played at a different battlefield than where Ember Monk is located?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Ember Monk gets +2 might when any card from hidden is played, regardless of which battlefield either card is at.

Nuances:

Ember Monk tracks all hidden cards regardless of zone as long as you control the hidden card

question: In a surprise defense scenario (when a player moves a unit to an unoccupied battlefield and the opponent responds by moving a unit there with Ride the Wind), does the initial open showdown end immediately and combat start, or do players continue passing priority in the open showdown before combat begins?
answer:
Ruling: Players continue passing priority in the initial open showdown until both pass without starting a chain. Only after the open showdown ends naturally does combat begin.

Sequence:

Player moves a unit to an unoccupied battlefield, starting an open showdown

Opponent plays Ride the Wind, moving their unit to the battlefield (this stages a combat)

Players can continue playing actions and passing priority during the open showdown

Units do not gain attacker/defender designations yet during this open showdown

Once both players pass without starting a chain, the open showdown closes

During cleanup, the staged combat begins and units gain attacker/defender designations

Combat proceeds normally

Nuances:

Combat cannot start during a showdown - it requires a neutral open state (no items on chain and no showdown in progress)

The patch notes clarification that "the current showdown will end and a second showdown will begin" is misleading - the showdown ends naturally through normal priority passing, not immediately

The player who first applied contested status to the battlefield is the attacker; any units moved there afterward are defenders

Abilities that trigger "when I attack" or "when I defend" trigger when combat begins and units gain those designations, not during the open showdown

question: When a unit with an attack trigger (like Yasuo Remorseful) is moved or killed during a showdown after the trigger has been added to the chain, does the triggered ability still resolve and deal damage?
answer:
Ruling: Once a triggered ability is added to the chain, it always resolves regardless of whether the unit is killed or moved. However, if the ability references the unit's location (like "here") or stats (like "my might"), it may resolve to do nothing if the unit is no longer in the referenced location or no longer exists.

Sequence:

Targets for the ability must be chosen when the ability is added to the chain

If the unit is moved or killed after targets are chosen, the ability still resolves

The ability checks its conditions upon resolution

Nuances:

For Yasuo's ability specifically: if he is moved to a different battlefield or base, the chosen target is no longer valid for "here" so no damage is dealt

If Yasuo is killed, he has no might to deal damage with, so the ability does nothing

If an ability doesn't reference the unit's location or stats (e.g. "deal 5 damage to a unit"), it would still work even if the unit is moved or killed

There is no "fizzling" like in Magic - abilities always resolve, they just potentially do nothing

Any other effects on the ability would still resolve as much as possible

Spells still count as played for effects like Ravenbloom Student even if they do nothing

question: Can Stand United be legally activated if the only unit at the battlefield is already buffed, and can it target a unit on the bench for the buff?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot buff a unit at a different location when playing Stand United from hidden. However, buffed units are legal targets for buff effects, so you can legally activate Stand United targeting your already-buffed unit (though the buff itself will have no effect). The secondary effect that gives +1 to all your units with buffs will still apply.

Sequence:

Play Stand United from hidden on the battlefield

Target your already-buffed unit at that battlefield (legal target)

The buff effect resolves with no change to that unit

The secondary effect gives +1 to all your units with buffs

Nuances:

You cannot target a unit on your bench when playing from hidden

Buffed units are legal targets for additional buff effects even though nothing happens from the buff itself

question: In the top 8 of a tournament, does the higher seed decide if they want to go first or do players randomly determine it?
answer:
Ruling: For January summoner skirmishes, the top seed gets to choose first turn in top cut matches. This is a recent change while tournament rules are being updated.

Nuances:

The official rules documents say to do it randomly

Top cut is now optional for January summoner skirmishes

Tournament rules are currently being updated to reflect this change

question: When playing Fight or Flight in showdown, if the opponent plays Retreat in response, must you now target your own unit? When do you choose the target?
answer:
Ruling: You choose the target upon playing Fight or Flight, not upon resolving. If the opponent plays Retreat after you've chosen an enemy target, you do not need to retarget your own unit.

Sequence:

Choose target when playing Fight or Flight

If opponent plays Retreat in response, the card is still considered played but does nothing

Nuances:

Fight or Flight is still considered played even if it does nothing due to the target being removed

question: Can hidden cards be played directly to battlefields, and where can hidden cards be played from?
answer:
Ruling: Hidden cards can only be played at Battlefields you control, not at your own base. If you play a hidden card at a Battlefield you control, you have to wait until your opponent's turn to be able to play them.

Nuances:

Hidden cards must be placed facedown at a Battlefield you control

You cannot play hidden cards to your own base

Playing hidden cards at Battlefields you control allows you to avoid paying their normal energy/power cost

question: If you scored a hold point on a battlefield, can Kai'sa still draw a card when you move her to that battlefield after moving your unit off?
answer:
Ruling: No, Kai'sa cannot draw a card because you cannot conquer a battlefield you have already scored this turn.

Nuances:

You could move Kai'sa to base/bounce her and replay her with accelerate to try to conquer a different battlefield you haven't scored yet this turn

question: Does winning combat happen before Candlelit Sanctum triggers?
answer:
Ruling: The timing of when "win a combat" happens relative to Candlelit Sanctum triggers is not definitively answered in the thread.

Nuances:

The timing was expected to be covered in V1.2 of the rules but may not have been included

As of the thread discussion, the timing was unclear

question: Can you have a different Legend in your sideboard than in your main deck?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot have a different Legend in your sideboard. You must use the same Legend throughout the tournament.

Nuances:

You can change your Chosen Champion to one from your sideboard or main deck that matches your Legend

A player may not change their Legend or Battlefields at any point after deck registration

Sideboard limits on copies of named cards apply to the combination of Main Deck and sideboard

question: Can Defy or Windwall counter play abilities like Shieldbearer's stun or Harnessed Dragon's kill effect?
answer:
Ruling: No, Defy and Windwall cannot counter play abilities because they specifically counter spells, and play abilities are not spells.

Nuances:

To prevent kill effects from play abilities, you can use replacement effects like The Boss or Zhonya's, or move the unit to a different zone with effects like Retreat

If a play ability has a target restriction (e.g. "a unit at a battlefield"), you can cause it to whiff by making the unit no longer a legal target

Harnessed Dragon's kill ability does not have the "at a battlefield" restriction, so moving the unit out of the battlefield won't help

question: Does Zhonya's prevent Phoenix from triggering when a unit would die?
answer:
Ruling: Zhonya's prevents Phoenix from triggering because Zhonya's replaces death, so the unit never actually died.

Nuances:

This applies regardless of whether the kill effect is direct removal (like Blade) or damage-based (like Hextech Ray)

Phoenix requires the unit to actually die to trigger

This works similarly to how Hook interacts with death prevention effects

question: When Fallen Star would kill two units simultaneously, can the caster choose the order to kill them (to play around Zonya's Hourglass), or does the opponent choose which unit to save since they die at the same time?
answer:
Ruling: The units die at the same time, so the opponent chooses which unit to save with Zonya's Hourglass.

Nuances:

Fallen Star can target separate units

question: If a spell kills the only unit at a location you control, do you immediately lose control of the location and cause Hidden cards there to expire?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, if a spell kills your only unit at a location, you immediately lose control of that location and Hidden expires.

Sequence:

Spell kills the only unit at the location

Control of the location is immediately lost

Hidden cards at that location expire

question: When a gear card adds power to a unit, does the power only last for the turn or is it taken from the rune deck?
answer:
Ruling: Gear cards (Seals) are exhausted to generate Power, which is done by recycling a rune (not taking from the rune deck). If a card were to add a new rune from your rune deck, it would say "Channel a rune".

Nuances:

Gear goes to the base, not on units

Any unused generated resource lasts until either the next draw step or end of turn

question: If Mundo's might is decreased to 1 by 2 copies of Smokescreen (while a card is in trash triggering his ability), then that card leaves trash, what does his might become? And what happens if a third Smokescreen is played after that?
answer:
Ruling: When the card leaves trash, Mundo's might becomes 0. If a third Smokescreen is played while Mundo is at 0 might, he remains at 0.

Sequence:

Mundo starts at 6 might base

His ability increases him to 7 might (while card is in trash)

Two Smokescreens resolve, each "snapshotting" their decreases, reducing him to 1 with a total snapshotted decrease of -6

When the card leaves trash, the -6 decrease no longer has the "minimum of 1" limitation, so Mundo goes to 0 might

A third Smokescreen played at this point would snapshot as -0, leaving Mundo at 0

Nuances:

Units can have 0 or less might without dying

Units only die from non-zero damage, not from having 0 might

The "minimum of 1" limitation on Smokescreen only applies when the effect resolves and snapshots; once snapshotted, the decrease persists without that limitation

question: If a Hidden Blade is reacted to with another Hidden Blade targeting the same unit, how many cards should you draw: 2 or 4?
answer:
Ruling: You draw 2 cards total. The first Hidden Blade resolves, killing the unit and drawing a card. The second Hidden Blade cannot establish "its controller" because the unit is now out of play, so it does not draw a card.

Sequence:

First Hidden Blade resolves, killing the unit and drawing 1 card

Second Hidden Blade cannot establish its controller since the unit is out of play

Total cards drawn: 2 (1 from the first Hidden Blade resolving, 1 from the second Hidden Blade being played but not resolving fully)

question: Does the chain start when playing a spell with no keyword on your turn outside of a showdown, and can opponents react to it with cards like Defy?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the chain starts when you play a spell with no keyword on your turn, even outside of a showdown.

Nuances:

Opponents can use cards like Defy to cancel the spell even if played before entering a showdown

The statement that players can only react during showdown is incorrect

question: In Summoner Skirmish top cut, does the highest seed get to decide who goes first in game 1, or is it determined randomly?
answer:
Ruling: In top cut of Summoner Skirmish, the highest seed gets to decide who goes first in game 1. This was communicated directly to stores via email.

Nuances:

This information was sent directly to stores rather than being publicly posted, which caused confusion among players

This ruling represents a change from the previous practice where first player was always determined randomly

question: When a Sett Brawler that has buffed itself to 8 might is saved from death by The Boss's replacement effect, does it retain its 8 might or reset to 4?
answer:
Ruling: The Sett Brawler retains its 8 might when saved by The Boss's effect because the unit never leaves the board zone and remains the same game object.

Nuances:

The Boss uses a replacement effect, not banish, so the unit never actually leaves the board

Since the game object stays the same and never changes zones, all effects and buffs remain active

This ruling holds true even after the errata to The Boss (which changed "when" to "if" to make it not a trigger)

question: Can a unit lose the +1 Might buff from War Camp without leaving the War Camp?
answer:
Ruling: A unit can only lose the +1 Might buff from War Camp by leaving the War Camp.

Nuances:

The buff persists as long as the unit remains in the War Camp

question: If I control battlefield A with one unit during opponent's turn, opponent moves my creature to battlefield B with Charm, and in the same showdown I use Ride the Wind to move my unit back to battlefield A, do I score a conquer?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you score a conquer at battlefield A.

Sequence:

During the cleanup after the Charm (where the combat/showdown are staged at B), control of battlefield A is cleared

When you move back to battlefield A with Ride the Wind, you contest it again because you no longer control it

After the showdown/combat at B is resolved, a showdown will start at A

If your unit isn't removed from battlefield A during that second showdown, you will conquer it

question: Can you play multiple reaction cards after each other (e.g., retreat after a retreat), and do you need focus to do so?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can play multiple reaction cards after each other. You only need priority to play the first reaction, not focus.

Sequence:

Play the first reaction card (requires priority)

When you add an item to the chain, you receive priority first

You can then play another reaction card with that priority

Nuances:

Focus is required for Actions and cannot chain like priority

Priority works differently than focus when chaining reactions

question: Does Rune Prison last for the whole turn or only until the end of the showdown?
answer: Ruling: Rune Prison lasts until the end of the turn.

question: Can you tap Kaisa's legend ability to pay for Deflect's increased spell cost?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can tap Kaisa's legend ability to pay for Deflect's increased spell cost for regular spells. However, you cannot use it to pay Deflect for reflexive triggers (like Fallen Star's damage triggers) because reflexive triggers are abilities, not spells.

Nuances:

Deflect increases the cost of spells, so Kaisa's legend ability can be used to pay that increased cost

Reflexive triggers (such as Fallen Star's damage triggers after resolution) are abilities, not spells, so Deflect cannot be paid for them

You can still use Kaisa's ability to react to reflexive triggers and play a different spell, but not to pay Deflect on the reflexive trigger itself

question: If I hold a battlefield at the start of my turn, move all units out of it, then move a unit back in later that same turn, does it count as a conquer and trigger conquer effects?
answer:
Ruling: No. If you score a battlefield through any means, you cannot score it again that same turn. Since conquer effects are part of the scoring process, they will not trigger.

Nuances:

This restriction applies regardless of how the battlefield was initially scored

Moving units out and back in during the same turn does not reset the battlefield's scored status

question: When does a player lose control of a battlefield with a hidden card after their defending unit dies, and can they still use the hidden card as a reaction?
answer:
Ruling: If a unit dies to combat damage during a showdown, control is lost immediately when the showdown ends, and no reactions are allowed from the hidden card. If a unit dies outside of combat (such as from a damage spell), control is lost immediately when no units are present, and the hidden card cannot be used.

Sequence:

During combat: Lethal damage is assigned, the showdown ends, control is gained/lost, points are gained, then the hidden card is trashed with no reaction window

Outside combat: When an effect kills the last unit, control is lost immediately and both the unit death and hidden card trashing happen in the same cleanup with no window for reactions

Nuances:

If a unit dies during the showdown to an effect (not combat damage), control stays until the combat resolves when damage would be dealt

Deathknell triggers create a special case where chain items can intercede after combat damage but before contested/control is cleared, allowing reactions in that specific window

Effects like Unchecked Power that kill units outside combat are "checkmate" for hidden cards with no opportunity to use them

question: When an opponent plays Hidden Blade targeting a unit with Deflect, and you want to Defy the Hidden Blade, does the opponent still have to pay the Deflect cost?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the opponent must pay the Deflect cost even if you Defy the Hidden Blade. Deflect costs are paid during finalization, which happens before the opponent passes priority and before you can respond with Defy.

Sequence:

The spell is cast and goes onto the chain as pending

The spell finalizes (targets are chosen and Deflect costs are paid during this step)

The caster passes priority

The opponent can now respond with cards like Defy

Nuances:

Defy only looks at the printed base cost of a card, not additional costs like Deflect

A card like Sky Splitter cannot be Defied even if played for reduced energy cost, because Defy checks the base printed cost

Multi-target reflexive spells like Icatian Rain work differently: the spell itself finalizes with no targets, then when it resolves it creates reflexive triggers that each finalize separately with their own targets and Deflect costs

question: When Yasuo attacks and triggers abilities from both Ahri Legend and Ahri Inquisitive defending, what is the order of resolution and when can players play reactions?
answer:
Ruling: All attack and defend triggers go on the chain first (attacker's triggers, then defender's triggers in defender's chosen order), but nothing resolves until players pass priority. The attacker gets priority first and can play reactions before any triggers resolve, and players get additional priority windows as each ability resolves from the chain.

Sequence:

Yasuo attacks (ability on stack)

Defender orders their triggers: Ahri Legend and Ahri Inquisitive abilities go on stack in defender's chosen order

Attacker gets priority and can play reactions to the chain

Players continue adding to the chain until both pass priority

Chain resolves last-in-first-out, with priority windows after each resolution

Nuances:

There is only ever one chain at a time in Riftbound

The chain can be added to before things resolve

In this scenario, the Ahri player can play reactions like Smokescreen to reduce Yasuo's ability damage before it resolves

question: If a unit at base with an active Zhonya's is targeted by Falling Star, can the second damage trigger kill it after Zhonya's activates?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Falling Star can kill a unit with Zhonya's. The first reflexive trigger deals damage, Zhonya's heals and recalls the unit, then the second reflexive trigger can kill it again if it deals enough damage.

Sequence:

First reflexive trigger deals damage to the unit

Zhonya's activates, heals the unit, and recalls it

Second reflexive trigger deals damage and can kill the unit

Nuances:

Zhonya's does not clear negative modifiers (like stat reductions from Smoke Screen) because the unit is only healed and recalled, not banished and replayed as a new object

The unit would need to be banished or replayed (like with Portal Rescue) to become a new object and clear modifiers

question: Are the new/clarified missed trigger rules applicable only to Houston until the TRM is updated in January, or will they apply to Summoner Skirmishes before January as well?
answer:
Ruling: The new trigger rules are officially for Houston, with tournament rules being updated in January. However, it is up to Head Judges of individual events to decide whether to use the Houston rules or standard tournament rules before the January update.

Nuances:

The rules were described as "hot fixed into the TR as an addendum" by one contributor, though the official article states they are for Houston with TRM updates coming in January

Different events may have different rulings depending on Head Judge discretion until the January update

question: If I see 3 Nocturnes from Stacked Deck, can I pay for all 3 even though I will be drawing one off Stacked Deck before the trigger resolves?
answer:
Ruling: You can banish all three Nocturnes when revealed by Stacked Deck. Stacked Deck won't do anything since the banished Nocturnes are no longer valid cards to add to your hand or recycle.

Sequence:

When you reveal 3 Nocturnes from Stacked Deck, you can choose to banish all three

A new chain starts with all 3 Nocturnes (which can't be reacted to because units can't be reacted to)

Before each Nocturne goes on the chain, you choose between finalizing the unit (by paying its cost) or leaving it in banish

If you choose not to finalize, the Nocturne stays in banish and the unit is not finalized on the chain

Nuances:

Nocturne's trigger works with any effect that instructs you to publicly reveal cards from the top of the deck or allows you to secretly see them (like Stacked Deck, Candlelight Sanctum, or the purple Poro with Vision)

The "and don't draw them" text prevents you from drawing regularly and cheating Nocturne into play that way

You are not required to play Nocturne if you banish it; the wording is "you may banish, then play"

question: In what order are cards revealed and chosen at the start of the game?
answer:
Ruling: At the start of the game, the order is: legend, CC (Command Center), BF (Battlefront), turn order, then mulligans.

Sequence:

Legend

CC (Command Center)

BF (Battlefront)

Turn order

Mulligans

question: Does Reckoner's Arena trigger Yone, Blademaster's conquer ability even though the battlefield is not open because Yone is already there?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Reckoner's Arena triggers Yone's conquer ability even when the battlefield is not open. The card activates conquer effects by skipping their trigger conditions entirely.

Sequence:

Reckoner's Arena causes you to hold a battlefield (not conquer it)

The card activates all conquer effects, bypassing their normal trigger conditions

Yone's ability is placed on the chain and resolves normally

Nuances:

Conquer abilities have two parts: the trigger condition ("When I conquer an open battlefield") and the effect ("deal damage...")

Reckoner's Arena skips the entire trigger condition, including any additional requirements like "open battlefield"

If Yone's ability were phrased differently with the open battlefield requirement as part of the effect (e.g., "When I conquer, if I conquered an open battlefield..."), then it would not work with Reckoner's Arena

Once a triggered ability is activated and on the chain, nothing in its original trigger condition prevents it from resolving

question: Can you play Chinese legend cards and runes in an otherwise English deck?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can play Chinese legend cards and Chinese runes in an otherwise English deck.

Nuances:

You must use all runes in the same language - you cannot mix Chinese and English runes together

The champion must remain in English per the rules

It is recommended to have a proxy of the legend available for opponents unfamiliar with the card

question: In a 4-player game, if Player A moves to an empty battlefield starting a showdown, Player B uses Ride the Wind to join, then Player B uses Fight or Flight to remove Player A's unit, can Player A use Ride the Wind to move back to that battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: No, Player A cannot move back to the battlefield. Once combat is staged between two players, CR 437.1 prevents units controlled by players who don't already have permanents at that battlefield from moving there, even if one of the original combatants has no units remaining.

Sequence:

Player A moves to empty battlefield, starting a showdown

Player B uses Ride the Wind to move a unit there (becomes defender)

Combat is now staged between Player A (attacker) and Player B (defender)

Player B uses Fight or Flight to remove Player A's unit

Player A cannot Ride the Wind back because they no longer have permanents at the battlefield and combat is still in progress

Nuances:

Rule 423.2 prevents units from moving to a battlefield that already has units from 2 other players present

Rule 421.2.b causes units to recall if they try to move to a battlefield where a combat is happening between two other players

CR 437.1 prevents moves to battlefields with staged combats or combats in progress by players who don't already have permanents there

There appears to be a rules gap if the original attacker's unit is removed before combat resolves, as the attacker designation remains but they have no units present

question: Does Petricite Monument's effect that gives units Deflect persist after the gear leaves play?
answer:
Ruling: Petricite Monument's effect is only active while the gear is on the board. When the gear goes to the trash, units lose the Deflect keyword.

Nuances:

The effect does not persist for the rest of the game

The effect does not apply only to units that were on the field when it was played

The effect is an ongoing aura that applies to units while the gear remains in play

question: Can Overzealous Fan be played with Ride the Wind during the focus step of defending, and then trigger its ability when it becomes a defender?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can play Overzealous Fan with Ride the Wind during your focus step while defending, and when Overzealous Fan becomes a defender, it can trigger its ability.

Sequence:

Declare your unit as a defender

During the focus step, use Ride the Wind to play Overzealous Fan

Overzealous Fan becomes a defender

Overzealous Fan's ability triggers

question: Can a reaction ability be played without either player playing an action ability first?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, if you have priority, you can play a reaction ability without either player playing an action ability first.

Nuances:

Actions cannot be played onto an existing chain

Everything adding to an existing chain must be a Reaction

question: Does Volibear Legend's ability trigger when Sett enters play and gains Might from his own effect?
answer:
Ruling: No, Volibear Legend will not trigger from Sett's self-buff. Volibear Legend checks Sett's Might value at the moment Sett enters play, before Sett's triggered ability goes on the chain, so Sett will still only have 4 Might at that time.

Sequence:

Sett enters play

Volibear Legend checks if any unit has 5+ Might (Sett has 4 at this point)

Volibear Legend does not trigger

Sett's triggered ability goes on the chain

Sett's ability resolves and grants him +1 Might (now at 5)

The trigger window for Volibear Legend has already passed

Nuances:

Draven Showboat will trigger Volibear Legend because his effect doesn't use the chain and applies immediately, so the Might increase happens before the trigger check

question: If something is targeted and then dies on the chain, can you target something new?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot target something new. Targets are chosen when you play the card. If the original target is not there at resolution, that part of the spell won't have an effect.

Sequence:

Targets are chosen when you play the card

Validity of targets is checked again at resolution

If target is invalid at resolution, that part of the spell has no effect

Nuances:

Some rare cards make you choose things at resolution, but those are not targets

For cards that split damage among multiple targets, you choose the targets when played but decide how to split the damage among those targets at resolution

question: Can Teemo Swift Scout's ability put a Teemo champion unit from your trash into your hand?
answer:
Ruling: No. Swift Scout specifies it can place a Teemo unit into your hand from your champion zone of the board. Your trash is neither of those places.

Nuances:

The trash is specifically a non-board zone, so it cannot be targeted by abilities that reference "the board" or specific board zones.

question: If Carnivorous Snapvine targets a Travelling Merchant on the battlefield, but the Merchant gets Flashed back to base before Snapvine resolves, does Snapvine still kill it?
answer:
Ruling: No, Snapvine does not kill the Merchant. Since Snapvine specifies "battlefield" and the Merchant is no longer on the battlefield when the spell resolves, it is not a valid target and the spell does nothing.

Sequence:

Carnivorous Snapvine is cast and targets Travelling Merchant on the battlefield

Merchant is Flashed back to base in response

Snapvine resolves, but Merchant is no longer on the battlefield

Snapvine does nothing because the target is not in the valid zone

Nuances:

Spells that can target units anywhere (like Challenge, which can target units at bases) would still resolve even if the unit moves zones

If a unit gains Deflect after costs are paid but before resolution, the caster does not need to pay additional costs because costs have already been calculated and paid

question: Can Blind Fury be played during a showdown as a defender, and does it allow you to take your opponent's revealed card and play it on your side of the battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Blind Fury can be played during a showdown if you have focus, but it reveals and plays a card from the top of the main deck, not from hidden cards at the showdown battlefield. In a 1v1 game, your opponent reveals the top card of their deck and you play it to your side of the battlefield.

Sequence:

Play Blind Fury (requires focus)

Opponent reveals the top card of their deck

You play that revealed card to your side of the battlefield

Nuances:

In multiplayer games, you choose which opponent's deck to reveal from and play the card

The card comes from the main deck, not from hidden showdown cards

You play the opponent's card to your own board, not force them to play it on theirs

question: If I use Possession on a creature, do I get any equipment the creature has as well?
answer:
Ruling: When you use Possession on a creature, the equipment stays attached to the creature and your unit gets all the effects of the equipment, but the equipment still belongs to the original controller.

Sequence:

You take control of the creature with Possession

Equipment remains attached to the creature

Your unit benefits from all equipment effects

If the unit dies or equipment is unattached, it returns to the opponent

Nuances:

The opponent can still use effects like Weaponmaster to attach that equipment from your unit to theirs since they still control the equipment

Equipment cannot be unattached without a separate effect doing so (like Weaponmaster or the unit being killed)

Attached cards may have different controllers from their top-most card

question: Does Yasuo Remorseful deal damage twice - once from his attacker trigger and once from regular combat damage?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Yasuo Remorseful deals damage twice - first from his attacker trigger effect, then from regular combat damage.

Sequence:

You attack into battlefield

Yasuo's attacker trigger goes on the chain and you declare a target unit at the battlefield

Both players pass priority

Yasuo deals his might to that target unit

Both players pass priority

Cleanup occurs and Yasuo deals might and takes damage in the combat damage step

Nuances:

The damage from Yasuo's attacker trigger lingers (it is not healed immediately)

Damage is only healed at end of turn or at end of combat

This means you can deal damage with the attacker trigger to a unit and then hit it again during the combat damage step

question: When a 6 Might unit attacks a 5 Might unit, the defender gives -2 Might to the attacker (reducing it to 4 Might). Does the attacking unit die or does it survive and return to base?
answer:
Ruling: The attacking unit dies. The attacker assigns damage first, but since it only has 4 Might after the -2 Might modifier, it cannot deal lethal damage (6) to the defender. The attacker then fails to conquer and dies.

Sequence:

Defender gives -2 Might to the attacker (reducing it from 6 to 4)

Attacker assigns its damage first (4 damage)

Defender assigns its damage (5 damage)

Attacker fails to deal lethal damage and dies

Nuances:

Might is not the same as life/HP; Might determines both damage dealt and damage that can be received

Reducing Might reduces both offensive and defensive capability

Damage persists outside of combat and is only cleared at end of combat and end of turn

Damage does not reduce Might, so a damaged unit still deals full Might as damage

question: Does Sivir, Battle Mistress trigger when Twisted Fate, Gambler's attack trigger recycles a rune from the top of the rune deck?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Sivir triggers when Twisted Fate recycles a rune from the rune deck. Recycling a rune counts regardless of where it's recycled from.

Nuances:

The game recognizes cards in the rune deck as runes even when they are hidden information, as evidenced by Twisted Fate's wording "reveal the top rune of your rune deck, then recycle it"

This differs from "unit" which specifically refers to unit cards on the board as permanents, not unit cards in other zones

There is no equivalent rule for runes that differentiates them when on the board vs in the rune deck (unlike units and gear)

The ability looks for the game action (recycling) and card type (rune), not the zone the rune is recycled from

question: Can you use Not So Fast to counter an opponent's Not So Fast that is targeting your unit's play effect?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot use Not So Fast to counter another Not So Fast. Not So Fast targets spells and abilities, not units or gear, so it cannot be a legal target for another Not So Fast.

Sequence:

Attacker attacks

Defender plays Janna (unit enters battlefield)

Janna's play effect triggers and targets attacker's unit

Attacker plays Not So Fast targeting Janna's play effect

Defender cannot play Not So Fast to counter the attacker's Not So Fast

Nuances:

When Not So Fast counters a unit's play effect, the unit still enters the battlefield; only the ability is countered

When countering an ability with multiple effects (like Janna's heal and target), the entire ability is countered, not just one part

question: Does Thousand Tail Watcher's effect work as a continuous aura, and specifically would Wielder of Water become 3 defense when blocking Thousand Tail Watcher or stay at 1?
answer:
Ruling: Thousand Tail Watcher's effect is not a continuous aura. When Wielder of Water blocks Thousand Tail Watcher, it will become a 3 defense.

Nuances:

Even though Wielder of Water enters combat with 1 defense (copying the attacker), it then gets the +2 defense bonus from Thousand Tail Watcher's effect, resulting in 3 total defense.

question: Can you play reaction cards during phase changes, and do you need a chain to exist to play reactions during opponent's turns?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot react to phase changes or end of turn itself. During your opponent's turn, you can only play reactions when there's a chain or when there's a showdown and you have focus.

Nuances:

While you cannot react to phase changes/end of turn directly, you can react to abilities that trigger due to a phase change or end of turn (such as end of turn triggered abilities or start of phase triggered abilities)

question: If I play Get Excited and discard Sky Splitter while Kadregrin is on base, does Get Excited deal 0 damage (due to Kadregrin's cost reduction) or 8 damage (Sky Splitter's printed cost)?
answer:
Ruling: Get Excited deals 8 damage. When effects reference a card's cost, they always reference the printed value on the card, not any modified cost from other effects.

Nuances:

Kadregrin's cost reduction only applies when casting the card into play, not when the card's cost is referenced by other effects

The card is discarded before it would actually be cast, so the cost reduction never applies

question: If lethal damage is dealt to a unit controlled by Sett, The Boss with a spell, and Sett's Legend ability is used to recall the targeted unit, does the unit still die from the temporary damage marked on it?
answer:
Ruling: No, the unit does not die. Sett, The Boss's text has been errata'd to include healing.

Nuances:

Despite the general rule that recalling does not affect the state of the object, Sett's specific ability has been updated to heal the recalled unit

question: Are the origin promo cards tournament legal?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, origin promo cards are tournament legal. The cards are printed with the OGN set code (visible on the card itself), which is part of the current Standard format.

Nuances:

The promo cards may be registered online as OGNX, but the physical card shows OGN, which is what matters for legality

You cannot shuffle cards of different languages together, so if your promo is in a different language than the rest of your deck, it cannot be used

question: If you play Gust on your own Ravenbloom Student at 3 might, does it get sent to your hand, or does it become 4 might first (from its trigger) and become an invalid target?
answer:
Ruling: The Ravenbloom Student will be sent to hand before its trigger can resolve. The student's trigger responds to the resolution of the spell, not to the spell being put on the chain.

Sequence:

Gust resolves and sends the 3 might student to hand

The student's trigger (which would give +1 might) does not resolve because the spell must finish its entire process before triggers respond

A spell is only considered "played" when it has finished resolving in its entirety

Nuances:

"Play" in this game means resolve, except when used in contexts like "you may play a unit"

question: Can Zero Drive play opponent's units that were banished by its Deathknell effect?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Zero Drive can play opponent's units that were banished by its Deathknell effect, even though those units go to their owner's banished zone.

Sequence:

Gain control of opponent's unit (e.g., via Hostile Takeover)

Equip Zero Drive to that unit

The unit dies and is banished by Zero Drive's Deathknell

The unit goes to opponent's banished zone but is tracked as banished by Zero Drive

Zero Drive's ability can play that unit from opponent's banished zone

Nuances:

Units are always banished to their owner's banished zone, not the controller's

Players typically place cards banished by Zero Drive physically under it for tracking purposes

This interaction works similarly to comparable effects in Magic: The Gathering

question: Does Anivia Primal's "deal 3 to ALL enemy units here" deal 3 damage to each enemy unit individually, or 3 damage total that can be allocated across enemy units?
answer:
Ruling: Anivia Primal deals 3 damage to each enemy unit individually.

Nuances:

This can be compared to Volibear, Furious for similar templating

question: Can you play Meditate and exhaust Lee Sin Ascetic to both draw an extra card from Meditate and trigger Lee Sin's "Exhaust me: buff me" ability?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot use the same exhaust to pay for both Meditate's card draw and Lee Sin Ascetic's self-buff ability.

Nuances:

Both effects require exhausting as a cost

You cannot use the same resource (exhausting the unit) to pay two different costs simultaneously

question: What are the deck legality rules regarding card language/printing for Legend, Rune deck, and Main deck in Riftbound?
answer:
Ruling: The Legend may be any language, the Rune deck can be any language as long as all cards in it are the same language, and the Main deck can be any language as long as all cards in it are the same language. The languages do not have to match between the three decks (e.g., Chinese Legend, Chinese Runes, English Main deck is legal).

Nuances:

This rule is found in the Tournament Rules section

question: If holding a battlefield at the start of your turn gives you your 7th point, can you then capture another battlefield that same turn to score your 8th point and win?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can. You need to score all battlefields on the same turn only if you want your final point to come from a conquer. Holding counts as scoring on your turn.

Sequence:

Hold a battlefield at the start of your turn (scores 7th point)

Capture another battlefield during that same turn (scores 8th point for the win)

Nuances:

The restriction about scoring all battlefields in one turn only applies when your final winning point comes from a conquer action

Holding is considered a score that happens on your turn, so it satisfies the requirement for winning

question: Can you conquer a battlefield without scoring points (to trigger its ability) if you've already scored that battlefield previously?
answer: Ruling: No, you cannot conquer a battlefield without scoring points. Conquering is a subsection of scoring, so if you can't score, you can't conquer.

question: Can you play Gust on your turn or does your opponent have to do something for you to use it as a reaction?
answer:
Ruling: You can use Gust on your turn. Reactions with "Play at any time" can be used on your turn whenever you please.

Nuances:

The "Play at any time" text on a reaction card allows it to be played during your own turn, not just in response to opponent actions

question: When Player 1 moves a unit to Reaver's Row, then Player 2 plays Ride the Wind to contest it, can Player 1 use Reaver's Row's ability to retreat?
answer:
Ruling: No, Player 1 cannot use Reaver's Row's ability to retreat. Player 2 is the defender in this combat because Player 1 was the one who applied contested to the battlefield first, so Player 2 gets to use Reaver's Row's ability.

Sequence:

Player 1 moves a unit to Reaver's Row (applies contested)

Player 2 plays Ride the Wind to contest (stages a combat but doesn't immediately start it)

Both players must pass focus in succession without starting a chain to end the showdown

When the showdown ends, combat begins

Combat opens with an initial chain including Reaver's Row's trigger

Player 2, as the defender, has the choice to move a unit to base when Reaver's Row resolves

Nuances:

The player who applied contested to the battlefield is NOT the defender; the other player is

Moving a unit to contest does not immediately end the showdown and start combat

question: Is there a functional difference between "When you play me" and "When I'm played" trigger wordings?
answer:
Ruling: There is no functional difference between "When you play me" and "When I'm played" trigger wordings.

Nuances:

The different wording may be used for smoother readability depending on the card's other trigger conditions

question: When moving a unit with Showstopper (or Leona's spell), can other units from the base join the same attack, or must the moved unit attack alone?
answer:
Ruling: When you move a unit with a spell like Showstopper or Leona's spell, you cannot move other units alongside it - the unit must attack alone.

Nuances:

You can only move multiple units together using the standard move option, not when moving via spells

question: Does '8+ runes' include exactly 8 runes, or do you need at least 9?
answer: Ruling: 8+ includes exactly 8. If you needed 9 or more, the card would say "9+" or "more than 8 runes".

question: Does an initial chain get created if no units have 'When I attack' or 'When I defend' abilities?
answer:
Ruling: If there are no "When I attack" or "When I defend" abilities, there is no initial chain and combat goes straight into a showdown, giving the attacker focus to start a chain.

Sequence:

Check for "When I attack" or "When I defend" abilities

If none exist, skip initial chain

Proceed directly to showdown

Attacker receives focus to start a chain

question: Can Dragon's Rage target a unit that is already at the destination location (e.g., targeting Lee Sin when Wizened Elder is already where Lee Sin would be moved to)?
answer:
Ruling: No, Dragon's Rage cannot target a unit if there is no actual movement because you cannot move to where you already are.

Sequence:

Dragon's Rage requires the target to move to a destination

If there is no move/destination, the reflexive trigger does not activate

You cannot move a unit to its current location

Nuances:

While nothing explicitly forbids targeting the same location, the lack of a "destination" means the card's reflexive trigger will not work

question: Does Ka'sai's ability pay for a card's power cost, and if so, does it reduce the number of runes that need to be recycled?
answer:
Ruling: Ka'sai's ability provides 1 power of any color that can only be used to pay for Spell cards. This power can substitute for recycling one rune, but does not pay for energy costs.

Sequence:

To play a spell card, you must pay both its energy cost and its power cost separately

Ka'sai's ability provides 1 power (of any color) that counts toward the power cost

You still need to pay the full energy cost through other means

If a spell needs 2 power, you can use Ka'sai's 1 power plus recycle 1 rune (instead of recycling 2 runes)

Nuances:

Ka'sai's power can ONLY be used for spell cards, not other card types

The power must match the color requirement of the spell (Ka'sai can provide any color)

Power and energy are separate costs - Ka'sai only helps with power, not energy

question: Does Glasc Deathknell's ability work with Drag Under (i.e., can you play Drag Under on Deathknell)?
answer:
Ruling: No, Glasc Deathknell's ability does not work with Drag Under because Drag Under is not a unit and costs more than 3 energy.

Nuances:

When determining if a card meets cost requirements for abilities, always use the printed cost on the card, not any reduced or altered cost

This means even if you play a card with a cost reduction, effects that check cost thresholds use the original printed cost

question: Can you play Gust targeting a 4 Might unit and then react to it with Stupefy to reduce the unit's Might to 3 or less before Gust resolves?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot target a 4 Might unit with Gust. The targeting requirement "a unit at a battlefield with 3 might or less" must be met when the card is played, before any reactions can be added to the chain.

Sequence:

Stupefy must be played first to reduce the unit's Might to 3 or less

Then Gust can be played targeting the now-valid unit

Nuances:

If Gust were worded "return a unit at a battlefield to its owner's hand if its Might is 3 or less," then you could target any unit and the Might would be checked on resolution

The "3 might or less" restriction in Gust is part of the targeting requirement, not just an instruction that resolves later

question: Can Ride the Wind move a unit from one battlefield to another battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Ride the Wind can move a unit from one battlefield to another battlefield.

Nuances:

Units' standard move cannot move from one battlefield to another without ganking

Spells and abilities that cause units to move are not restricted in the same way as standard moves

Movement spells and abilities describe their own limitations, if any

question: For Baited Hook, when do you pick the target, and what happens if the target is missing when the ability resolves?
answer:
Ruling: You pick the target when activating the ability. If the target is missing at resolution, the "kill a friendly unit" part fizzles, but you still look at the top 5 cards of your main deck and recycle them.

Sequence:

Kill a friendly unit: fizzles if the target is not present anymore

Look at the top 5 cards of your main deck: do as much as you can, so you do it even if target is missing

Banish a unit with might up to 1 more: can't find any because there is no might to compare

Recycle the rest: do as much as you can, recycle the 5 cards

Nuances:

The game does not use last known information for checking unit stats like Might

If the unit is not killed or is missing, you cannot check the unit might and won't resolve the "search a unit" part, but other parts of the ability resolve as much as possible

question: Does Divine Judgement target units, runes, and gears when activated, and can it be played if there are 0 or 1 gears on the board?
answer:
Ruling: Divine Judgement does not target anything upon entering the chain. The resolution instructs players to choose, but this is not targeting because both players are choosing together, not you alone.

Sequence:

Divine Judgement enters the chain without targeting

Upon resolution, players make choices according to the card text

Turn player chooses first

You resolve as much as you can with available options

Nuances:

For an effect to be targeting, you must meet three criteria: (1) You and you alone pick, (2) In a public space, (3) Not from the list of exceptions (must, modifiers, part of costs or targeting restrictions, etc.)

If there is only 1 gear on the entire board, you can still play Divine Judgement and keep that one gear (resolve as much as you can)

If your opponent has 3 gears and you have 1, you will choose your gear first (as turn player), then be forced to choose their gear, meaning they get to save all their gears

question: Are there any currently released cards that actually apply the golden rule (where card text overrides game rules)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, several cards apply the golden rule where card text overrides game rules. Examples include Brynhir (prevents opponents from playing cards despite normal timing rules allowing it), Mageseeker Warden (similar restriction), Magma Wurm (changes how units enter), and Zhonyas (overrides game rules).

Nuances:

Tideturner is debatable as an example because its interaction with hidden card targeting restrictions is explicitly covered in the rulebook with the clause "unless the ability explicitly restricts targeting in a way that makes this impossible"

The hidden card targeting rule states targets must be chosen from the same battlefield unless the ability explicitly restricts targeting in a way that makes this impossible, which covers Tideturner without needing the golden rule

question: Can an opponent buff their units in response to Teemo Strategist's ability before the damage is dealt?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the opponent can use reactions to buff their units after Teemo's ability goes on the chain but before the damage is dealt.

Sequence:

Teemo's ability goes onto the chain

Opponent has a chance to use reactions

Cards are revealed and damage is dealt

Nuances:

The opponent must react before knowing how much damage Teemo will do (before cards are revealed)

question: When playing a spell in a multiplayer game, at what point must you designate the target, and does it need to be announced before opponents can react?
answer:
Ruling: You must choose the target when the spell goes on the chain, before giving other players the opportunity to react.

Nuances:

Any time you (and only you) have to choose an object on the board, it targets

Effects that automatically select objects are not targeting (example given: Ahri Legend)

Effects like 'stun a unit' are targeting because you choose the unit

question: Can you react with Shakedown before Sett Brawler gets buffed by Sett Legend's power, preventing him from being saved?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can react with Shakedown before Sett Brawler gets buffed. Sett's ability is a WYPM (When You Play Me) trigger that goes on the chain, and Shakedown is at reaction speed, so you can respond to it before it resolves.

Sequence:

Sett Brawler is played, triggering the WYPM ability

The buff ability goes on the chain

Before it resolves, you can react with Shakedown at reaction speed

Shakedown resolves first, removing Sett before the buff can save him

Nuances:

When Sett's Legend power spends the buff to give +4, the buff falls off as a cost. While the +4 ability is on the chain, Sett would be 4M (not 5M anymore), making him vulnerable to effects like Stupefy or Gust during that window.

question: Can Yasuo's leader skill move a unit from base to battlefield, from battlefield to base, or both?
answer:
Ruling: Yasuo's leader skill allows you to move a unit either from base to battlefield OR from battlefield to base. You choose one of these two options.

Nuances:

This ability is activated during your turn and cannot be used as a reaction to spells or abilities

If a unit is moved to base or hand by some other effect, targeted spells like Rebuke that affect units on the battlefield would resolve to no effect (though they don't "fizzle" - they still resolve for purposes of abilities that care about resolution)

question: Do hidden cards need to target at the battlefield they are hidden at, and does targeting text change when a card is hidden?
answer:
Ruling: All hidden cards receive the additional targeting restriction of "Here" (meaning they must target at their own battlefield), except for Tideturner which cannot target at its own location due to errata.

Nuances:

The targeting restriction is not printed on the cards themselves but is added by the rules when cards become hidden

Tideturner is the sole exception to this rule

question: In 2v2, can I play cards that say 'your base' to my friend's base?
answer:
Ruling: No, your friend's base is not your base. You cannot play cards that reference "your base" to your teammate's base.

Nuances:

If you attempt to move a unit controlled by another player into your base, it just doesn't move (though this may be changed in the future so it goes to their base instead)

Yasuo will receive errata to clarify that he moves friendly units to their controller's base

question: When an attacker stuns and kills a defender but another defender survives, do the attackers remain on the battlefield or return to base, and who scores the conquest point?
answer:
Ruling: When combat ends, if there are still defenders present on the battlefield, all attacking units are recalled to base. No one scores a conquest point immediately - the defender retains control of the battlefield and will score a point for holding it at the beginning of their next turn.

Sequence:

Combat damage is dealt and units heal

If defenders still remain, all attackers are recalled to base

The defender retains control of the battlefield

At the beginning of the defender's next turn (during their beginning step), they score one point for holding the battlefield

Nuances:

Units cannot coexist with opposing units on a battlefield outside of combat

Conquering (and scoring immediately) only happens if all defenders are eliminated

Defending successfully does not score a point by itself - the point is scored during the beginning step of the controlling player's turn

"Hold" abilities and scoring both trigger during the turn player's beginning step, not on the opponent's turn

Units with "when I hold" abilities must be actively holding battlefields (not at base) to trigger

question: In a 1v1 Riftbound best-of-3, after game one, does the losing player see battlefields before choosing who goes first or second?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, in a best-of-3, the loser of the previous match picks turn order after battlefields are revealed.

Sequence:

Battlefields are revealed

The loser of the previous game chooses turn order

Nuances:

The setup order is always the same, but turn order is only random in game 1

After game 1, the loser always picks turn order

question: Can you use Ride the Wind to target a unit and move it to its current location?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot use Ride the Wind to move a unit to where it already is. A move requires both an origin and a destination that are different locations.

Nuances:

You can move the unit anywhere else (battlefield to battlefield, base to battlefield, battlefield to base)

question: Can Imperial Decree allow you to split damage between a Tank and another unit (Ahri) when attacking with multiple 1M recruits?
answer:
Ruling: No, Imperial Decree does not change how you assign damage to units. When a Tank is present, you must assign all damage to it first before dealing lethal damage, and you cannot reassign damage before doing lethal to a unit.

Sequence:

Send recruits one at a time to work around the Tank

Kill the Tank with one 1M recruit (due to Imperial Decree)

Kill Ahri with another 1M recruit

Conquer with the third 1M recruit

Nuances:

If you send all recruits at once, all damage must be assigned to the Tank first

Imperial Decree increases damage but doesn't bypass Tank's damage assignment rules

question: What is the proper order of operations between games in a match?
answer:
Ruling: The order between games in a match is: Sideboard, Legend, Chosen Champion, Battlefield, Turn Order, Draw/Mulligan.

Sequence:

Sideboard

Legend

Chosen Champion

Battlefield

Turn Order

Draw/Mulligan

question: If a unit with an attack/defend trigger is removed from the battlefield in response to the trigger, does the trigger still take effect?
answer:
Ruling: The trigger will always still resolve, but it rechecks legality. If the unit has "here" in its text (like Yasuo), the effect won't work if the unit is no longer on the battlefield when the trigger resolves.

Sequence:

The attack/defend trigger goes on the stack

If the unit is removed (e.g., by Fight or Flight) in response

The trigger still resolves

The game rechecks legality based on the trigger's text

If the trigger requires the unit to be "here" and it's not, the effect whiffs

Nuances:

Most attack/defend triggers have "here" in their text, which means they require the unit to still be on the battlefield

Yasuo specifically has "here" on his text, so if he's moved to base/trash, his damage effect won't inflict any damage

question: If my opponent plays Bullet Time when I have Embermonk and a hidden Teemo on my battlefield (outside of combat), does it kill the monk and then allow me to play Teemo, or does it kill the monk and prevent me from playing Teemo?
answer:
Ruling: Outside of combat, if Bullet Time kills your only unit at a battlefield, the hidden card goes to trash during spell cleanup and you cannot play Teemo. You lose control of the battlefield when your last unit dies.

Sequence:

Bullet Time resolves and deals damage

Embermonk dies if enough damage is dealt

Hidden Teemo is put in trash during cleanup of the spell

You lose control of the battlefield

Nuances:

During combat, you could pass priority and reveal Teemo before Bullet Time resolves to keep the battlefield

You do not know how much damage Bullet Time will deal until it resolves (value is decided during resolution)

Just because your only unit at a battlefield dies does not mean combat ends or you lose control during a showdown

question: Does a unit with 0 might die if it has taken no damage?
answer:
Ruling: No, units at 0 might do not die if they have no damage. Units need at least 1 damage in order to die.

Nuances:

A unit that loses might due to losing a keyword (like shield) during cleanup will not die if it has taken no damage

If such a unit were saved by Zhonya's Hourglass, it would not immediately die again since it still has no damage

question: If a unit gains an Attack trigger ability (like from Recurve Bow via Angle Shot) after already being designated as an attacker, does that Attack trigger get processed?
answer:
Ruling: No, Attack triggers added after a unit has already gained the attacker designation do not trigger. The trigger condition requires the unit to gain the attacker designation while having the ability, not to gain the ability while having the designation.

Sequence:

Unit is designated as an attacker

Attack triggers on that unit process at that moment

If the unit later gains new Attack trigger abilities during the same combat, those new triggers do not process

If the unit leaves and returns to the battlefield during the same combat, Attack triggers still do not process again (they only trigger the first time a unit gains attacker designation per combat)

Nuances:

This ruling applies specifically to triggered abilities (like Attack triggers), not passive abilities

Passive abilities like Assault work differently - they only care whether the unit currently has the attacker designation, not the timing of when it was gained

A unit can only trigger Attack abilities the first time it gains the attacker designation in a given combat

question: If I Flash a unit from battlefield B back to base during my opponent's turn (when they start a showdown at battlefield A), then use Ride the Wind to return it to battlefield B, do I score a point for conquering battlefield B?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you score a point. You can score on your opponent's turn, and this sequence results in conquering battlefield B.

Sequence:

Opponent starts showdown at battlefield A

You Flash your unit from battlefield B back to base (losing control of battlefield B)

You use Ride the Wind to return the unit to battlefield B (gaining control)

You score for conquering battlefield B

Nuances:

You lose control of a battlefield the moment you don't have units on an uncontested battlefield

Conquering is defined as gaining control over a battlefield that you did not score this turn

You can only score 1 point per battlefield, per turn

question: Does moving a unit to an empty battlefield cause a showdown?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, moving a unit to an empty battlefield causes a showdown if you don't control that battlefield.

Sequence:

When you move a unit to a battlefield you don't control, that battlefield becomes contested

A showdown will be opened

Nuances:

Control becomes contested when a unit is moved to a battlefield whose controller doesn't control the battlefield

question: What exactly does the Hidden keyword do?
answer:
Ruling: You pay one power to set a unit hidden to a battlefield you control. Starting next turn, you can play the card for free as a reaction, with the restriction that it only affects the battlefield it's been placed on.

Sequence:

Step 1: Pay one power to set the unit hidden to a battlefield you control

Step 2: Starting next turn, you can play the card for free as a reaction

Nuances:

The card can only affect the battlefield it's been placed on

You ignore the casting cost when playing it from hidden

question: If Lee Sin (Ascetic) has multiple buffs and I play Wallop to spend one buff to ready him, does he keep his remaining buffs or do all buffs go away?
answer:
Ruling: Only one buff is spent by Wallop. Lee Sin retains any remaining buffs after spending one to pay for Wallop's effect.

Nuances:

Each buff on Lee Sin is a separate entity, not a stacking counter

You can play multiple different copies of Wallop by spending multiple buffs from Lee Sin

You cannot play the same copy of Wallop multiple times

question: Why does Zenith Blade allow a yellow Leona to trigger her 'When I attack' ability when played during the Focus window after attackers are already declared?
answer:
Ruling: When I attack/defend triggers now happen whenever a unit becomes an attacker or defender, not just during the initial declaration phase. When Zenith Blade moves yellow Leona to the battlefield during the Focus window, she becomes an attacker and her 'When I attack' ability triggers.

Nuances:

Enemy units that were already declared as defenders earlier do not trigger their 'When I defend' abilities again when a new attacker joins

The Teemo section in the FAQ provides additional clarification on this timing rule

question: When summoning Riptide (with a When You Play Me effect that targets), can an opponent respond with Gust to bounce the targeted unit, and does this save the unit from Riptide's damage?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the opponent can respond to Riptide's When You Play Me ability with Gust. If Gust resolves first and bounces the targeted unit to hand, Riptide's ability will resolve but cannot find the target anymore, so no damage is inflicted.

Sequence:

Riptide is summoned and its WYPM effect is added to the chain with target declared

Opponent gets priority and can respond with Gust targeting the unit

If both players pass, Gust resolves and moves the unit to hand

Players get priority again and pass

Riptide's ability resolves but cannot find the target, so no damage is dealt

Nuances:

You cannot play a reaction card in response to a unit being played itself (just the permanent entering play)

You can react to abilities of the unit, including When You Play Me effects

question: If I play Brynhir Thundersong, can the opponent still reveal hidden cards this turn?
answer:
Ruling: No, the opponent cannot reveal hidden cards this turn after you play Brynhir Thundersong. Cards from hidden are also played, so Brynhir's effect prevents revealing them.

Nuances:

If it was somehow the opponent's turn when you played Brynhir, they can still hide cards (the restriction only applies to playing/revealing cards)

question: Can a unit without Ganking in Vilemaw's Lair be charmed to another battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, a unit without Ganking in Vilemaw's Lair can be charmed to another battlefield. Ganking only affects standard moves between battlefields, not other types of movement like Charm.

Nuances:

Vilemaw's Lair only prohibits moving to base, not to other battlefields

You can target a unit in Vilemaw's Lair to move it to base (though the spell will resolve with no effect since the movement is prohibited)

question: When a unit with a triggered 'when you play' ability is played during chain resolution, does it go on the chain immediately after that chain link resolves? And when does a deathknell trigger resolve during combat?
answer:
Ruling: When you play a unit with a triggered ability during chain resolution, after that chain link completely resolves, the triggered ability goes on the chain as a new link. Deathknell triggers do not wait for combat to fully end - they are finalized onto the chain during the special cleanup that happens within combat cleanup.

Sequence:

Combat damage is dealt

Special cleanup occurs (deathknell unit dies from damage and adds trigger as pending, then trigger is finalized onto the chain)

Chain created by special cleanup resolves

Contested is cleared from battlefield (this happens after the special cleanup)

Combat officially ends

Nuances:

Chains can intercede game steps

Reactions to deathknell can still happen before contested is cleared and control is established (but after combat damage)

Combat cleanup is not itself a cleanup - it's the steps of ending combat, which includes a special cleanup

Clearing contested from the battlefield is a step of combat cleanup that occurs after the special cleanup, not part of the special cleanup itself

question: If Falling Star targets a unit at a battlefield, and the unit is then moved to base with Flash before damage is dealt, does the damage still apply?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Falling Star's damage will still apply to the unit even after it moves to base with Flash, because Falling Star does not specify a location requirement for its damage.

Sequence:

Player B plays Falling Star, which resolves

Player B announces targets (6 damage on Player A's unit at battlefield)

Player A casts Flash on their unit, moving it to base

Falling Star's damage still applies to the unit

question: Does Viktor, Leader's effect activate while he is in the Champion slot?
answer: Ruling: No, Viktor's effect does not activate while in the Champion slot. A card in the Champion slot is not considered in play, so you must play the card for its effect to be active.

question: Can both players reveal the same battlefield during the blind flip?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, it is fine for both players to reveal the same battlefield. The game proceeds to first turn determination.

Sequence:

Both players blind flip and reveal battlefields

If battlefields are the same, continue with the game

Proceed to first turn determination

Nuances:

No re-selection is required when battlefields match

question: When a card reduces Might (like Smokescreen or Stupefy), does it reduce both the damage dealt and the health, or only the damage?
answer:
Ruling: Might is a single stat that represents both combat damage dealt and durability. Reducing Might affects both how much damage the unit deals and how much damage it can take before dying.

Nuances:

There is no separate "health" stat in Riftbound

A unit dies when damage on it is at least equal to its Might

question: Is Rengar considered Mighty when played into a battlefield that you are attacking, for effects like Volibear that trigger when you play a Mighty unit?
answer:
Ruling: No, Rengar is not considered Mighty when played. He enters play at 3 power without the attacker designation, and only gains the attacker designation (and becomes 5 power) during the cleanup triggered by his entering the board.

Sequence:

Rengar enters play at 3 power without attacker designation

His play effect triggers (relevant for effects like Volibear)

Cleanup is triggered by his entering the board

During cleanup, he gains the attacker designation and becomes 5 power

Nuances:

Because he enters at 3 power, he would trigger effects that care about non-Mighty units entering play (like Fiora in sealed)

This differs from a unit with a passive ability like base 4:Might - such a unit would have the passive take effect as soon as it enters (when it's resolving) and would be Mighty for effects like Volibear

question: When a reaction is played during showdown and the opponent responds with another card, which resolves first?
answer:
Ruling: The chain resolves from last to first, meaning the last effect added to the chain resolves first.

Sequence:

Player A plays reaction "Gust" (bounce a 3 might unit)

Player B responds with "Discipline" (give a unit +1)

"Discipline" resolves first (last in, first out)

"Gust" resolves second

Nuances:

In this specific case, Discipline could increase a unit's might above 3 to prevent it from being bounced by Gust

question: When do you have to activate Zhonya's Hourglass to save a unit from dying in combat or from Icathian Rain damage?
answer:
Ruling: Zhonya's has a replacement effect, so you only need to make sure it's face up on the board before the unit actually dies. You can play it in response to whatever spell, ability, or trigger will kill the unit you want to save.

Sequence:

In combat: Reveal Zhonya's with Focus before passing priority, because if both players pass focus you go directly into combat damage and lose the chance to play it

With Icathian Rain: Wait until the reflexive triggers are finalized to the chain, then play Zhonya's in reaction to whichever specific trigger would kill the unit you want to save (you can wait through multiple triggers resolving)

Nuances:

If you only control units at the battlefield where Zhonya's is hidden, and one of those units dies, you lose control of the battlefield and Zhonya's goes to trash

The latest you can play Zhonya's is in reaction to whichever trigger would kill the unit at the battlefield with the Zhonya's (if that's the unit you want to save)

Against Icathian Rain, the opponent should try to kill the unit at the battlefield with Zhonya's first, forcing you to save that one instead of units in base

question: Can you win the game by holding for your 7th point and then conquering for your 8th point in the same turn?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can win by holding for your 7th point and then conquering another battlefield for your 8th point in the same turn. You can score the last point through holding, card effects, or by scoring/conquering a battlefield, as long as you scored at least one battlefield through any method that turn when conquering.

Sequence:

Start your turn at 6 points while holding a battlefield

Gain 1 point from holding (now at 7 points)

Conquer the other battlefield to reach 8 points

Win the game

Nuances:

The winning point can be obtained through holding, card effects (like Ahri or Tryndamere), or conquering/scoring a battlefield

For multiplayer: if conquering is your winning point, you must have scored a point at each battlefield that turn

You cannot "hold at 8 points" because once you reach 8 points, you have already won

question: If Yellow Darius (6 Might) and a 1 Might unit battle a 7 Might unit, can you conquer the battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can conquer the battlefield. Darius (6 Might) boosts the 1 Might unit to 2 Might for a total of 8 Might vs 7 Might, winning the battle. The 1 Might unit survives because its damage heals immediately after combat, before it checks for lethal damage again, leaving it at 1 Might with 0 damage after Darius dies.

Sequence:

Darius (6 Might) and boosted unit (2 Might) battle the 7 Might unit

You win with 8 total Might vs 7 Might

The 1 Might unit takes 1 damage (now 2 Might with 1 damage)

Damage heals immediately after combat

Unit becomes 1 Might with 0 damage after Darius leaves

Unit survives and conquers the battlefield

Nuances:

This ruling was clarified in the FAQ after initial confusion about timing

The key is that damage heals before checking for lethal damage again, even when Darius dies

question: Can Defy be played without a spell on the chain to counter?
answer:
Ruling: No, Defy cannot be played without a spell on the chain because it requires a target.

Nuances:

Defy cannot target itself

question: Does a Chosen Champion need to be designated when registering a decklist, or can you choose between multiple legal Chosen Champions in your deck for game one?
answer:
Ruling: The Chosen Champion must be designated as part of deck registration and cannot be changed for game one. You cannot register multiple legal Chosen Champions and choose between them after revealing Legends.

Sequence:

Chosen Champion is specified during deck registration as part of your main deck

Game one must use the registered Chosen Champion

Between games 2 and 3, you may change your Chosen Champion as part of sideboarding to a different champion from your deck or sideboard

Nuances:

Deck registration requires "main deck including chosen champion", meaning the CC is a fixed part of the registered decklist, not just any legal champion present in the deck

question: Why does Red Darius enter untapped when played as the second card?
answer:
Ruling: Red Darius enters untapped when played as the second card because triggered abilities (indicated by "when" or "at") trigger after the event they're looking for has fully resolved. When you play Darius as your second card, he fully resolves and enters the board first, then his ability checks if he was the second card played this turn and triggers.

Sequence:

Play Darius as your second card

Darius fully resolves and enters the board

Check for triggered abilities that care about what just happened

Darius' ability sees that a second card was just played (himself) and triggers

Darius enters untapped

Nuances:

All triggered abilities with "when" or "at" timing work this way - they check after the event occurs, not during

"Play" abilities trigger after a card has been fully resolved and is on the board

question: Can Player 2 play Stupefy in response to Arena Bar, let it resolve, and then play Gust on the now-reduced might unit before Player 1 can act?
answer:
Ruling: No. Once Player 1 passes priority after Stupefy is played, the chain resolves completely. Player 2 cannot play Gust targeting the reduced-might unit before the chain finishes resolving and the unit moves to the battlefield.

Sequence:

Player 1 plays Arena Bar to buff a unit

Player 2 responds with Stupefy

Player 1 passes

Stupefy resolves, reducing the unit's might

The chain completes resolution

Only after the chain fully resolves can new spells be played

Nuances:

You cannot cast Gust targeting a unit with more than 3 might and then hold priority to cast Stupefy, because Gust requires a legal target (3 might or less) at the time of casting

Legend abilities without Action or Reaction keywords cannot be used to respond to Action/Reaction speed spells

question: In a best of one (duel), do you sideboard after revealing legends?
answer:
Ruling: In official best of one games, you do not sideboard. You play with your game 1 main deck only.

Nuances:

Some Chinese tournaments have used sideboarding in Bo1 as a house rule, but this is not part of the official rules

question: Can Mask of Foresight trigger multiple times in a battle, such as when a unit is moved out and back in with Ride the Wind?
answer:
Ruling: Mask of Foresight can trigger multiple times per battle, but only once per unit per combat. Attack and Defend triggers only apply the first time a specific unit gains the attacker/defender designation during a combat.

Sequence:

When a unit first gains defender designation in a combat, Mask triggers

If that same unit leaves and re-enters the battlefield during the same combat, Mask will not trigger again for that unit

If attacking a second battlefield in a different combat (e.g., using Ride the Wind to start a new combat), Mask can trigger again

Nuances:

The restriction is per unit per combat, not per turn

Different units gaining defender status in the same combat will each trigger Mask once

A new combat (even in the same turn) resets the trigger eligibility

question: When a chain resolves during a showdown, does the showdown end immediately, or do players get another opportunity to play actions?
answer:
Ruling: After a chain resolves during a showdown, players get another opportunity to play actions. The showdown only ends when both players consecutively choose not to start a new chain.

Sequence:

Showdown begins

When I attack/defend triggers are added to the chain (if any) and resolve

Attacker gets focus and can start a chain (play actions)

Chain resolves completely

Focus passes to defender, who can start a new chain
