question: If all units at a battlefield die in combat and there is still a hidden unit on that battlefield, can the hidden unit be activated after showdown resolution, or does it trash?
answer:
Ruling: If combat has fully resolved with no deathknell or other triggers/abilities remaining, you cannot activate the hidden unit. The hidden unit will trash.

Nuances:

If there is a deathknell trigger from a unit that died, you can activate the hidden unit during the cleanup step (specifically between the special cleanup and remove control steps) before the cleanup step ends.

question: Can Ride the Wind move a unit from one Battle Field to another Battle Field without a ganking unit present?
answer: Ruling: Yes, you can move a unit with Ride the Wind from one Battle Field to another Battle Field without a ganking unit. When a spell or ability tells you to move, you just do what the spell says - only the standard move has restrictions about ganking units.

question: If a unit gains deflect after a spell targeting it is already on the chain, does the caster have to pay the deflect cost?
answer:
Ruling: No, the caster does not have to pay for deflect retroactively. Deflect is an additional cost that must be paid when declaring targets; if a spell is already on the chain, adding deflect to the targeted unit does not affect that spell.

Sequence:

Player A casts a spell targeting unit B (spell goes on chain)

Player B gives unit B deflect

Player A's spell resolves without needing to pay deflect cost

Nuances:

Deflect only applies at the moment targets are declared, not after a spell/ability is already on the chain

question: Can actions and reactions be played before or after "when attack" and "when defend" effects resolve?
answer:
Ruling: Only reactions can be played in response to "when I attack/defend" triggers. After those effects resolve, both actions and reactions can be played (when no chain is present).

Sequence:

"When I attack/defend" effects trigger

Only reactions can be played in response to these triggers

After the "when I attack/defend" effects resolve, actions and reactions can be played (if no chain is present)

question: Does Divine Judgment force you to choose your opponent's units/gear if you don't have enough of your own to fulfill the requirement of choosing 2 of each type?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Divine Judgment forces you to choose from any units/gear in play, including your opponent's, if you don't have enough of your own. Since the card does not say "up to" and does not restrict choices to things you control, you must choose 2 of each type from all available options.

Sequence:

Turn player makes their choices first

Then each other player makes choices in turn order

Each player chooses 2 units, 2 gear, 2 spells from among all permanents in play

Each player chooses 2 cards in their own hand (this is the only category restricted to your own)

Everything not chosen is recycled

Nuances:

The card does not target, so it can be played even if there aren't enough permanents to fulfill all choices

If you only control 1 unit and your opponent controls 3, you must choose your 1 unit and 1 of theirs, then your opponent can choose the 2 you didn't pick

This means playing Divine Judgment when behind (with fewer permanents) can actually help your opponent keep more than 2 of each type

The card is most effective when you have 3+ of each type and your opponent has fewer

question: Are there end of round rulings for determining winners when time runs out in Riftbound?
answer: Ruling: There are currently no tournament rules for Riftbound, including no end of round rulings for determining winners when time runs out.

question: Can Riposte be played in response to Cleave during a showdown after Cleave has already resolved?
answer:
Ruling: Riposte cannot be played after Cleave has resolved. Riposte requires both a friendly unit and a spell on the chain as targets to be played legally. Once Cleave resolves, there is no spell on the chain anymore, making it too late to play Riposte.

Sequence:

Cleave is played and opens a Chain

Both players have the opportunity to play Reactions while Cleave is on the chain

Once Cleave resolves, Riposte can no longer be played because there is no spell on the chain to target

Nuances:

Units and Gears don't provide Reaction windows as they fall right off the chain

Riposte specifically requires both a friendly unit AND a spell on the chain to be played legally

question: Does a showdown start if I move a unit to a battlefield I've already scored at?
answer:
Ruling: A showdown does not start if you move units to a battlefield you control, even if you've already scored at it. However, if you move all units out and lose control, then move back in later, a showdown will start (though you won't score another point or get conquering procs).

Sequence:

If you maintain control of a battlefield, moving units in or out does not trigger a showdown

If you move all units out, you lose control of the battlefield

When you move units back in after losing control, a showdown begins

Control is contested and a showdown starts, but you don't score again or trigger conquering effects

Nuances:

A showdown only begins when control of a battlefield is contested and the turn is in a neutral open state

Moving back to a previously scored battlefield after losing control gives the enemy a chance to play an action/reaction

You can regain control of a battlefield you already scored at in the same turn (units are not recalled)

question: When Kai'Sa Survivor conquers at Zaun Warrens, can I choose the order of the triggers to draw from Kai'Sa before discarding and drawing from Zaun Warrens?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, both "when you conquer" triggers are simultaneous, so you can order them however you like.

Sequence:

Both triggers go on the chain simultaneously

You choose the order (CL1 and CL2)

You can put Kai'Sa at CL2 to draw before Zaun Warrens resolves at CL1

question: If you defend with Teemo, Strategist while having Rabadon's Deathcrown equipped and reveal 0 cards with Hidden, will Teemo create a 'Deal 0' damage trigger that can be impacted by Rabadon's Bonus Damage?
answer:
Ruling: No. Teemo does not create a damage event if 0 cards with Hidden are revealed. You cannot deal 0 damage - 0 damage is not a valid damage event.

Nuances:

"Deal 1 for each card revealed this way" is a single deal action, not multiple separate damage instances

The effect counts cards with Hidden and deals that much damage; if there are no Hidden cards revealed, no deal action is performed

The rules specify that only non-zero damage is valid damage (found in the splitting rules section)

With Rabadon's Deathcrown, Teemo's possible damage range is 0, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 (where 0 means no damage event occurs)

question: If you kill your own unit in a battlefield after scoring a hold point, can you conquer that same battlefield in the same turn?
answer:
Ruling: You can move to and conquer the battlefield in the same turn after scoring a hold point there, but you will not score an additional point or trigger any conquer abilities.

Nuances:

You can score each battlefield only once per turn

If you've already scored a battlefield on any turn (yours or opponent's), conquering it again that turn triggers no conquer effects and awards no points

You can always move to a battlefield regardless of whether you've scored there

This applies whether the battlefield becomes uncontested due to killing your own unit or your opponent killing your unit

question: If a unit targeted by Void Seeker leaves the battlefield before Void Seeker resolves (e.g., returns to base), does it still take damage?
answer:
Ruling: The unit does not take damage. When Void Seeker resolves, target legality is checked again, and if the unit is not at a battlefield, the damage part won't resolve. You still draw 1 card due to the "do as much as you can" rule.

Sequence:

Void Seeker targets a unit at a battlefield

Before resolution, the unit leaves the battlefield (returns to base)

On resolution, target legality is checked again

The unit is no longer at a battlefield, so damage does not apply

You still draw 1 card

Nuances:

The "do as much as you can" rule allows partial resolution of the spell effect

question: Does Last Breath count as choosing with a spell for Deflect?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Last Breath counts as choosing with a spell for Deflect purposes.

Nuances:

The determination is based on whether you clearly choose an enemy, even if the card text doesn't explicitly use formal targeting language like "Choose an enemy unit"

The informal wording on cards is an intentional design choice, with pros and cons compared to more formal templating

question: Does casting Primal Strength on Bilgewater Bully trigger its Ganking ability?
answer:
Ruling: No, Primal Strength does not trigger Ganking on Bilgewater Bully because Primal Strength does not use the "buff" mechanic.

Nuances:

Buff is a specific game mechanic with its own keyword

Only effects that explicitly state they "buff" count as buffs for triggering abilities like Ganking

question: If Fiora gains Mighty (and thus Deflect) after I've already paid for and finalized a spell targeting her, do I have to pay for Deflect? What about with Falling Star's reflexive triggers if the opponent reacts with Call to Glory?
answer:
Ruling: Once a spell or ability has chosen a unit as its target and been finalized to the chain, you do not have to pay for Deflect if the unit gains the keyword afterward.

Sequence:

If Falling Star resolves first, then its reflexive triggers pick targets and finalize afterward - if Fiora gains Deflect before those triggers finalize, you must pay for Deflect

If the opponent reacts to Falling Star (before it resolves) to give Fiora Deflect, then when Falling Star's reflexive triggers are created and pick targets, you will have to pay for Deflect

If the opponent waits until after Falling Star resolves to give Fiora Deflect, the reflexive triggers have already finalized their targets, so you don't have to pay

Nuances:

You can decline to pay costs incurred by triggered abilities when finalizing them, causing the trigger to be retracted and never go on the chain

This means you cannot be forced to recycle runes to pay for Deflect on triggered abilities

You can choose to decline Falling Star triggers if Fiora with Deflect is the only legal target, or if you don't want to kill other units for any reason

question: If you use Baited Hook to play Cruel Patron, do you still have to kill a friendly unit? What happens if Cruel Patron is the only unit you control?
answer:
Ruling: When Baited Hook plays Cruel Patron, you must still pay the additional cost of killing a friendly unit because Baited Hook only ignores printed costs, not additional costs. If you cannot pay the additional cost (e.g., Cruel Patron is your only unit), the card is placed on the chain but then returned to banishment since the cost cannot be paid.

Sequence:

Baited Hook allows you to play the card ignoring its printed cost

Additional costs (like Cruel Patron's kill effect) must still be paid

If the additional cost cannot be paid, the card goes onto the chain but returns to its original zone (banishment)

Nuances:

You are not required to banish a card with Baited Hook if you know you won't be able to pay its additional cost - you can choose nothing instead

Effects that check or ignore "cost" only refer to printed cost, not additional costs

Printed cost includes both energy and power costs if both are printed on the card

question: Does Sett trigger Volibear's ability when played, since Sett gains +1/+1 on play and could become Mighty?
answer:
Ruling: Sett does not trigger Volibear's ability when played. Volibear's trigger condition requires the unit to be Mighty at the time it is played, and Sett only becomes Mighty after his on-play effect resolves.

Sequence:

When Sett is played, triggers are checked

At this moment, Sett is not yet Mighty (still 4/4)

Volibear's condition "When you play a Mighty unit" is not met, so it does not trigger

Sett's on-play buff then resolves, making him Mighty

This is too late for Volibear to trigger

Nuances:

If an effect applied instantly (like Trifarian War Camp), Volibear would see the increased might and trigger

If Volibear's text read "When you play a Unit, channel a Rune if it is Mighty" instead, then it would work with Sett

The key difference is whether "Mighty" is part of the trigger condition or part of the effect resolution

question: If both players are at 7 points during turn 5 of overtime and you control a battlefield and cast Time Warp, do you win or does the extra turn not work?
answer:
Ruling: You do not get a 6th turn in overtime. The game ends in a tie.

Sequence:

If Time Warp is cast on turn 4 of overtime, you would get the extra turn 5

If Time Warp is cast on turn 5 of overtime (the final turn), you do not get a 6th turn

The game ends in a tie when overtime turn 5 concludes

question: How does damage work during showdown?
answer:
Ruling: You add up all the might of living units you control to determine total damage available, then assign lethal damage to opponent units one at a time.

Sequence:

Add up all the might of your living units you control

Assign lethal damage to opponent units one at a time

question: If a unit uses Ride the Wind to join a combat showdown after Ahri's debuff has already been applied and multiple cards have been played, does the new unit still get -1?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Ahri will trigger and apply her debuff to the new unit.

Nuances:

Ahri triggers the first time a unit gains the attacker designation at a battlefield her player controls, regardless of when during combat they gain that designation

The timing of when the unit joins combat (even mid-showdown after other cards have been played) does not prevent Ahri's trigger

question: Does Bullet Time only damage at a single battlefield or any battlefield that opponent has a unit at?
answer:
Ruling: Bullet Time only damages at a single battlefield.

Nuances:

If the card affected multiple battlefields, it would use plural wording ('at battlefields' instead of 'at a battlefield')

question: How to install Riftbound modules on Tabletop Simulator?
answer:
Ruling: Find the Riftbound workshop on the TTS community page, search for it, and subscribe to it to install everything needed.

Nuances:

This is not a rules question but a technical setup question

question: What type of ability is the standard move?
answer:
Ruling: The Standard Move is a Discretionary Action, not one of the four main ability types (activated, triggered, passive, or replacement). The term "Inherent Ability" in the rules is using "ability" in the general sense to indicate all units can perform this action, not as a keyword or ability type.

Nuances:

You cannot respond to a move and it does not start a chain

The capitalization of "Inherent Ability" in the rules is not indicating a keyword despite appearing bolded

question: If the attacking player's only unit dies during a showdown (killed by Hextech Ray with no reaction), does the showdown end immediately or can the attacking player still play action cards like Hidden Blade?
answer:
Ruling: Killing the attacking unit does not automatically end the showdown. The attacking player can still play action spells like Hidden Blade.

Sequence:

Unit is killed during showdown

Showdown continues

Players can still play action cards

Showdown ends only when both players pass Focus in a row

Nuances:

A showdown does not end simply because one side has no units remaining

The showdown only ends through the normal passing mechanism

question: Does Zenith Blade target a friendly unit?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Zenith Blade targets a friendly unit. Even though the card uses "you may" language, it still targets a friendly unit according to the targeting rules, meaning you cannot play Zenith Blade without a friendly unit on the board.

Nuances:

The "may" wording does not change the targeting requirement - you still need a valid friendly unit target to play the card, even if you choose not to move it

This is similar to how Salvage worked before it received errata

The card targets both an enemy unit and a friendly unit

question: Does Master Yi with Svellsongur get +8 Might when you have 8+ runes?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Master Yi gets +8 Might total when you have 8+ runes with Svellsongur.

Sequence:

Svellsongur causes Master Yi's textbox to repeat

The textbox becomes: "while you have 8+ runes, I have +4:Might:. while you have 8+ runes, I have +4:Might:"

Both instances of the ability trigger when you have 8+ runes

This results in +4 Might + +4 Might = +8 Might total

question: Does gusting a victor token count as killing the unit for the purpose of revival effects like Phoenix?
answer:
Ruling: No, gusting a token does not count as killing the unit.

Sequence:

The unit returns to hand

The token ceases to exist

This happens off the board, so it is not counted as a kill

question: When using Falling Star on a unit with Deflect, do you have to recycle 2 runes (one for each instance of 3 damage) or only 1 rune?
answer:
Ruling: You must recycle 2 runes when targeting a Deflect unit with Falling Star because it creates 2 separate reflexive triggers, and you pay the additional cost for each trigger that targets a unit with Deflect.

Sequence:

Play Falling Star

Players can react

Falling Star resolves, putting 2 reflexive triggers on the chain

Pick targets for the 2 reflexive triggers

Pay additional cost for each trigger that targets a unit with Deflect

Players can react

First trigger resolves dealing 3 damage

Players can react

Second trigger resolves dealing 3 damage

Nuances:

The "do this ... :" wording on Falling Star indicates it creates reflexive triggers

Players can react between each trigger resolution

question: If I have 2 Hourglass cards, do I lose just one or both when I would take lethal damage?
answer:
Ruling: You lose only one Hourglass. When you would die, both Hourglass replacement effects trigger and you order them. The first one replaces your death, and the second one has nothing to replace since death was already replaced.

Sequence:

Both Hourglass replacement effects trigger when you would die

You choose the order of the replacement effects

The first Hourglass replacement effect resolves, replacing your death

The second Hourglass replacement effect cannot replace anything (since death was already replaced by the first effect)

Only one Hourglass is lost

Nuances:

Replacement effects don't use the chain

A replacement effect cannot replace another replacement effect

The order you choose will matter for future cards like Guardian Angle

question: Does Sett's healing effect restore Might that was reduced by Thousand-Tailed Watcher?
answer:
Ruling: No, healing effects like The Boss only heal damage. Might gain and loss are retained and not restored by healing effects.

Nuances:

This applies to other similar healing effects like Zhonya's as well

question: Can hidden units be played at Rockfall Path, and how do they interact with it?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot play hidden units at Rockfall Path. While you can hide a unit card there, you cannot reveal and play it because you need a valid location to play a unit and cannot make illegal choices.

Sequence:

You can hide a unit card at Rockfall Path

When attempting to reveal it, you would need to choose a valid location to play the unit

Since no valid location exists at Rockfall Path, you cannot reveal and play the card

The card remains in hidden state

Nuances:

Hiding a unit at Rockfall Path can be used as a bluff to make opponents think you have a spell

This is a tempo loss but provides a strategic deception option

Choosing a location to play a unit is not targeting, but you still need a valid location

question: Does Jinx Legend's ability trigger and open a chain at the start of the Beginning Phase even when the player has more than 1 card in hand, allowing them to play cards and potentially draw if they meet the condition after resolving those cards?
answer:
Ruling: Jinx Legend's ability triggers at the start of your Beginning Phase regardless of how many cards are in your hand, opening a chain. The condition of having 1 or fewer cards is checked on resolution, not when triggering. This allows players to play reactions during the chain and potentially meet the draw condition before the ability resolves.

Sequence:

At start of Beginning Phase, Jinx Legend's ability triggers and opens a chain

Players can respond with reactions/cards

On resolution, check if you have 1 or fewer cards in hand

If condition is met, draw 1 card

This all happens before channeling a rune or drawing normally

Nuances:

The wording "At start of your Beginning Phase, draw 1 if you have 1 or fewer cards" causes the ability to trigger based on timing, with the card count condition checked on resolution

If it were worded "At the start of your beginning phase while you have 1 or fewer cards in your hand, draw 1" it would only trigger when the condition is already met

A player with 6 cards could theoretically play reactions down to 1 card and still get the draw, all before the normal draw step

question: When an effect like Baited Hook kills a Deathknell unit and hits a unit with WYPM in the same effect, do the pending items get added in the order the instructions happened, or are they considered simultaneous?
answer:
Ruling: Different instructions inside the same effect happen sequentially for the purpose of adding pending items to the chain. The Deathknell trigger becomes pending before the WYPM unit becomes pending, even though they're part of the same effect.

Sequence:

Baited Hook resolves, killing the Deathknell unit first, then revealing the WYPM unit

The Deathknell trigger becomes pending first, then the unit becomes pending

During cleanup, they finalize in that order: Deathknell becomes chain item 1, unit becomes chain item 2

The unit auto-resolves, triggering WYPM which becomes chain item 3

Final chain order is: Deathknell > WYPM

These resolve in reverse order (WYPM first, then Deathknell)

question: When Adaptatron attacks and conquers a field where the defending player has Zhonyas in base and a 2m defender on battlefield, does Zhonyas or Adaptatron trigger first?
answer:
Ruling: Zhonyas applies before Adaptatron triggers because scoring happens after combat cleanup.

Sequence:

Combat cleanup occurs

Zhonyas applies (as a replacement effect, not a triggered ability)

Scoring happens

Adaptatron triggers

Nuances:

Zhonyas is a replacement effect, not a triggered ability, so it doesn't use the chain and can apply in between resolutions or cleanups

question: Can a Hidden Zhonya's be used as a reaction when an opponent Charms your unit to their battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can react with Hidden Zhonya's to the Charm effect. Hidden cards gain the 'reaction' tag, and since Zhonya's doesn't target, its effect isn't restricted to the battlefield where it was hidden.

Sequence:

React to the Charm before your unit moves

Use the Hidden Zhonya's during this reaction window

Nuances:

Zhonya's doesn't target, so it can affect units on any battlefield

You must react to the Charm trigger before the unit actually moves to the other battlefield

question: Can you conquer the same battlefield twice in one turn by moving a unit away and then moving another unit back to it?
answer:
Ruling: You can only score one point per battlefield per turn. If a battlefield is conquered or held, it cannot be re-conquered or re-held on the same turn.

Nuances:

You can move units back and forth to/from a battlefield you hold, but it will not result in additional points or trigger conquering effects again

question: Does Assault trigger when moving to an empty battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Assault does not activate when moving to an empty battlefield.

Nuances:

Assault is a passive ability (on or off), not a trigger

question: Do triggers on the chain still resolve if the permanent that put the trigger on the chain is removed from the board in response? Specifically, if Volibear attacks (placing a 5 damage trigger on the chain) and is then removed by Hidden Blade, does the 5 damage trigger still resolve?
answer:
Ruling: No, the 5 damage trigger does not resolve if Volibear is removed from the battlefield. Because Volibear's ability references "here" (the battlefield), when Volibear dies the targets become invalid since he is no longer at the battlefield the original targets were at.

Sequence:

Volibear attacks, placing the "deal 5 damage" trigger on the chain

Hidden Blade is played in response, removing Volibear

Hidden Blade resolves, killing Volibear

When the 5 damage trigger attempts to resolve, the targets are now invalid because Volibear is no longer "here" (at the battlefield)

The trigger fails to resolve

Nuances:

This ruling depends on the ability referencing "here" or the stats of the permanent itself - such effects won't resolve properly if the permanent is removed

Effects that target a battlefield or a different unit (without referencing "here") would still resolve fully even if the source permanent is removed

Targets and split amounts are declared when the trigger is added to the chain, but validity is checked again at resolution

question: Can you mix languages between your main deck, legend, runes, and battlefields in tournament play?
answer:
Ruling: Each of the four deck categories (main deck, legend, rune deck, and battlefields) must be in the same language within itself, but each category can be in a different language from the others.

Sequence:

Main deck: all cards must be same language

Legend: must be one language

Rune deck: all runes must be same language

Battlefields (3 cards): all must be same language

These four categories can each be different languages from each other

Nuances:

You can have English main deck with all Chinese runes

You can have Chinese battlefields and legend with English runes

question: In a showdown, if the opponent's unit leaves the battlefield after I pass priority, can the opponent still play actions before the showdown ends?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the opponent can still play actions. A showdown ends the same way combat always would: once both players pass focus in sequence. Even if the opponent's unit is moved off the battlefield, if you pass again, the opponent can still play their action before the showdown resolves.

Sequence:

Player initiates showdown and passes priority

Opponent can play actions (even if their unit leaves the battlefield)

Showdown only ends when both players pass focus in sequence

After both pass, instead of going to combat damage, the game goes right to the resolution step

Nuances:

You can play as many actions as you want during a showdown until everyone passes while the chain is empty

Each action needs to be the first link on the chain (cannot use them as reactions)

question: Can both players play the same battlefield while setting up the game?
answer: Ruling: Yes, both players can play the same battlefield during game setup.

question: Does Ahri's legend ability trigger the enemy unit's Deflect?
answer:
Ruling: No, Ahri's legend ability does not trigger Deflect because it does not target.

Nuances:

Ahri's ability does not require choosing a target, which is why Deflect is not triggered

question: If Voli is my legend and I play a unit with Weaponmaster that takes a weapon causing it to become mighty, does it trigger Voli's legend ability?
answer:
Ruling: No, it does not trigger Voli. Weaponmaster makes a unit mighty after it is played, so the unit is not mighty when played.

Sequence:

Passive abilities become active just before a unit is considered "Played"

The unit is considered played (this is when Voli would check if it's mighty)

Weaponmaster triggers after the unit is played, making it mighty too late for Voli

Nuances:

Units that become mighty through Passive Abilities (like Origins Draven at 2 points, or a 4:Might: unit played to Trifarian Warcamp) would trigger Voli because passives activate before the unit is considered played

This interaction would trigger Fiora instead (Voli and Fiora are mutually exclusive)

question: Does Yasuo deal 6 or 5 damage when attacking if Stupefy is used on him?
answer:
Ruling: Yasuo deals damage equal to his current might, whatever that might may be at the time his ability resolves.

Nuances:

Stupefy must be used before Yasuo's ability resolves to affect the damage dealt

The timing of when Stupefy is used determines Yasuo's might value when his ability calculates damage

question: When Zhonya's Hourglass is played from hidden, does it only save units at the battlefield where it was hidden, or can it save units anywhere (including base or other battlefields)?
answer:
Ruling: When Zhonya's Hourglass is played from hidden at a battlefield, the design intention is that it should only save units at that specific battlefield. However, the current rules do not support this intention, and updated rules are expected to clarify this interaction.

Nuances:

Rules as written (RAW) would allow Zhonya's to bounce to base immediately and save any friendly unit anywhere, which is not the intended behavior

The general rule for hidden cards adds implicit "here" targeting to limit effects to the battlefield where they're hidden

Tournament organizers currently use their own specific interpretations until official clarification

If played normally as a gear in base (not from hidden), it would save the next friendly unit that would die anywhere, though opponents could force it to trigger on a token

question: Does Dragon's Rage deal damage when the moved unit is prevented from moving by Vilemaw's Lair, since the card text references 'its destination' rather than 'its location'?
answer:
Ruling: If the unit fails to move due to Vilemaw's Lair, it fails to enter "its destination" so the reflexive trigger fails to finalize and no damage is dealt.

Nuances:

"Destination" refers to where the unit is going to be moved to, not where it currently is

The unit must successfully move and enter its destination for the reflexive trigger to resolve

question: What is the structure and timing information for Summoner Skirmish events in Riftbound?
answer:
Ruling: Summoner Skirmishes are held twice per set (sets release every 3 months). The first should be held between Nov 24th and Dec 28th, and the second between Dec 29th-Feb 1st. Matches are Best of 3. The format appears to be Swiss into a top cut.

Nuances:

The judge program starts November 11th with more details to come at that time

Specific time limits per match round were not answered in the thread

Player to swiss round breakdown was not answered in the thread

Top cut/playoff time limits were not answered in the thread

Whether stores are required to run monthly events was not answered in the thread

Whether one person can act as both Judge and TO was not answered in the thread

Most structural details beyond the date ranges and basic format are not yet available

question: What are commonly asked rules questions or confusing concepts that new Riftbound players frequently encounter?
answer:
Ruling: This thread is a brainstorming discussion for creating a community FAQ, not a single rules question with a definitive answer. Multiple commonly confused topics were identified by contributors.

Topics Identified:

Cost vs what is paid (e.g., Defy)

No-speed vs Action vs Reaction

Focus & Priority

Different Languages

8th point misconceptions

Move vs Standard move

Damage does not reduce might

There is no such thing as HP

Legend > CC > Battlefield (including reveal) > Turn Order > Draw Mulligan

Condensing the targeting FAQ

Salvage

Hidden (can't play turn you hide, target restrictions from hidden)

Nuances:

This is a collaborative list-building exercise rather than a resolved rules question

question: Does a Showdown still occur at a scored battlefield when a player moves a unit there after moving all their units out?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, a Showdown always happens if a unit applies contested to a battlefield.

Sequence:

Player holds battlefield and scores a point

Player moves all units out (no one controls it)

Player moves another unit in

Showdown occurs (though no point is scored again)

Nuances:

A Showdown is triggered whenever a unit moves to a battlefield they don't currently control, regardless of whether the battlefield has already been scored

question: How does target selection work for spells with 'Do this' (like Falling Star) versus spells without it (like Void Seeker), and when can players react?
answer:
Ruling: Spells with 'Do this' are played with no target choices initially. When they resolve, they create reflexive triggers that go on the chain separately, and targets are chosen at that time. Spells without 'Do this' require target declaration when the spell is played.

Sequence:

For 'Do this' spells: Play the spell → Opponent can react → Spell resolves and creates reflexive triggers → Choose targets for each trigger → Opponent can react to each trigger → Each trigger resolves

For non-'Do this' spells: Declare targets when playing the spell → Opponent can react → Spell resolves

Nuances:

Counter spells like Wind Wall must be used before a 'Do this' spell resolves (before targets are chosen), as the reflexive triggers are triggered abilities, not spells

Buff spells like Discipline are usually better played after targets are confirmed

Players can react after each individual damage trigger resolves

question: Can you use Retreat on a recruit token and channel 1 rune from it?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can use Retreat on a recruit token and channel 1 rune from it. The token does go to your hand but ceases to exist immediately after moving there.

Sequence:

The recruit token moves to your hand

The token ceases to exist immediately after entering the hand zone

You channel 1 rune as normal from the Retreat effect

Nuances:

The token going to hand (before ceasing to exist) matters for effects that trigger when permanents move to specific zones

The token is not banished; it simply ceases to exist

This distinction is relevant for potential future "when you banish" effects

question: If a 7 might unit at a battlefront is hit first with Comet and then Stupefy, does it die?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the unit will die. It will have 6 damage and be at 6 might, causing it to die.

Nuances:

Stupefy doesn't get kill credit for effects that care about what killed a unit (such as Immortal Phoenix)

question: If Hidden Blade targets a unit that is then Retreated (returned to hand) before Hidden Blade resolves, does Hidden Blade retarget another unit or draw cards?
answer:
Ruling: Hidden Blade does not retarget another unit, nor does it cause the player to draw cards. Once targets have been chosen, they cannot be changed, and if the target is no longer visible when Hidden Blade resolves, it whiffs completely.

Sequence:

Player attacks with 1M unit and 2M unit

Opponent plays Hidden Blade targeting the 1M unit

Player Retreats the 1M unit (returns it to hand)

Hidden Blade cannot retarget the 2M unit

Hidden Blade whiffs completely (no card draw occurs)

question: If a unit is killed in response to its ability triggering, does the ability still resolve?
answer:
Ruling: All triggered abilities still resolve as much as they can, even if the unit dies. However, if the ability requires valid targets or references the unit's location, those parts will fail if the target is no longer valid or the unit is no longer at the specified location.

Sequence:

The ability triggers and goes on the stack

If the unit is killed before resolution, the ability still resolves

The game checks if targets are still valid and if location references can be satisfied

Effects that don't depend on invalid targets or locations still apply

Nuances:

Abilities that reference "here" or a specific battlefield location (like "a unit at my battlefield") will fail if the unit is no longer at that location

Abilities with simple effects like "draw 1" that don't reference location or require targets will fully resolve

Targeting must still be valid at resolution for that part of the ability to do anything

question: Can gold/universal power tokens be used to pay for specific recycle costs that require a particular domain (like blue or red)?
answer:
Ruling: Universal power (gold tokens) can be used to pay any power cost of any domain, including specific recycle costs that require blue, red, or any other specific domain.

Nuances:

When required as a cost, universal power can be paid by power of any domain

When added to a player's Rune Pool, universal power can be spent to pay a power cost of any domain

Universal power is equivalent to any single domain power (fury, calm, mind, body, chaos, or order)

question: Does Irelia get +1/+1 when she readies at the beginning of turn?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Irelia gets +1/+1 when she readies at the beginning of turn.

Nuances:

She must have been exhausted for this to trigger

question: Does the losing player of a game in a match choose their turn order in game 2/3, or is it randomly chosen again?
answer: Ruling: The losing player of a game chooses turn order in the next game of the match.

question: If Brynhir is played and resolves first, does it prevent opponents from playing their cards when Promising Future is played afterward?
answer:
Ruling: No, Brynhir does not prevent opponents from playing cards from Promising Future when played in this order. When Brynhir resolves before Promising Future is played, her ability is active and prevents opponents from playing cards.

Sequence:

Play Brynhir and let it resolve

Play Promising Future

Opponents look at the top 5 cards and banish one

The banished card stays banished because they cannot play it due to Brynhir's effect

Nuances:

If Brynhir were played after Promising Future, it would not work because all cards from Promising Future would already be pending on the chain before Brynhir's trigger could register

Opponents still get to look at and banish a card, but cannot play the banished card

question: If Aurora is readied by Ride of Wind after Deadbloom starts a showdown, will Aurora's ability trigger again at end of turn?
answer:
Ruling: No, Aurora will not trigger again. Aurora is not an exhaust ability, it is an end of turn trigger that only triggers once at the end of your turn.

Nuances:

Some players physically exhaust Aurora cards to track that they've been used (especially when multiple Auroras are in play), but this is just a tracking method - Aurora does not actually have an exhaust ability.

question: Is the battlefield considered empty for Yone's ability if Stormbringer is used to move Yone in and there are units on the battlefield that get cleared by Stormbringer?
answer:
Ruling: The answer is currently unknown and under discussion.

Nuances:

This question relates to timing of when the battlefield is checked for being "empty" relative to Stormbringer's clearing effect

There is a relevant thread discussing this interaction but no definitive ruling has been established

question: What counts as 'playing a card' in Riftbound?
answer:
Ruling: A card counts as "played" regardless of whether it's played from hand or cheated out through other means. Tokens are not cards and therefore spawning a token does not count as playing a card.

Nuances:

Spells specifically are only considered played if they resolve. If a spell is countered, it is not "played".

When a spell is countered (e.g., by Windwall or Defy), you still pay the cost of the spell before the opponent gets an opportunity to counter it.

question: When a unit equipped with Zero Drive dies, does the order of tap3/recycle then banish matter, and how does the banish cost work?
answer:
Ruling: When a unit equipped with Zero Drive dies, only the unit gets banished (not the equipment). Later, when Zero Drive is unattached, you can pay the cost and banish Zero Drive itself to play all units that died while wearing it this game for free.

Sequence:

Unit equipped with Zero Drive dies

Only the unit gets banished (Zero Drive becomes unattached)

Later, when Zero Drive is unattached, you can announce you are playing its ability

Pay the power, energy, and banish Zero Drive itself as costs (all at the same time)

You can use add/reaction abilities (like exhausting for energy or recycling for power) to help pay these costs

Play all units that died while wearing Zero Drive this game for free

Nuances:

You cannot use Zero Drive's ability while it is attached to a unit

This applies to all equipment - their additional abilities cannot be used while attached to a unit

question: Can Immortal Phoenix be played from the crypt if it is killed by your own Cull the Weak?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can play Immortal Phoenix from the crypt if you kill it with your own Cull the Weak.

Nuances:

This works similarly to other effects like Hidden Blade that can trigger Phoenix's ability to be played from the crypt.

question: Does Darius's ability trigger based on when a card is played (resolves) rather than when it leaves your hand, meaning the order is determined by stack resolution?
answer:
Ruling: A card is played when it resolves, not when it leaves your hand. Darius's ability triggers based on resolution order on the stack, so the second card to resolve (even if third from hand) triggers his ability.

Sequence:

Darius is played first

You play a spell (goes on stack)

Enemy plays a reaction (goes on stack)

You play a reaction to their reaction (goes on stack, resolves first)

Your reaction resolves as the second card played, triggering Darius

Darius readies and gets +2M before the opponent's spell resolves

Nuances:

Your opponent could theoretically react to the trigger of Darius's ability

question: Does Yasuo's Unforgiven ability (which moves him) cause attack triggers?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, if you use the ability to move Yasuo into a battlefield occupied by your opponent, it causes attack triggers.

Nuances:

Any time a unit moves to a battlefield occupied by the opponent, regardless of how the move is made, they are contesting the battlefield and therefore are the attacker.

question: Can Seal of Focus be played from hand and used to add a resource on the same turn it enters play?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Seal of Focus can be used to add a resource on the same turn it is played because gear comes into play ready.

Nuances:

Seals can be tapped at reaction speed but cannot be played from hand at reaction speed (only on your own turn at normal speed)

question: Can I use different colored sleeves for my Legend, main deck, Runes, and Tokens?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can use different colored sleeves for different deck types (Legend, main deck, Runes, Tokens), since these cards have different colored backings anyway.

Nuances:

All sleeves within each individual deck type must be identical to each other

All cards within a deck must be placed in sleeves in the same manner

Cards in decks must have the same number of layers and be the same orientation at all times

question: If you play 2 Cleaves on 1 unit, does it get Assault 6?
answer: Ruling: Yes, playing 2 Cleaves on 1 unit gives it Assault 6. The Assault keyword stacks when multiple instances are applied to the same unit.

question: In modified champion deck format, can you add a third color from cards opened in packs, and do you need to run the champion+legend from the champion deck or can they be replaced/removed?
answer:
Ruling: You must keep the champion the same and stay within the original colors of the champion deck.

Nuances:

You cannot add a third color from cards opened in packs

The champion cannot be replaced or removed

Full official rules were not yet available at the time of this discussion

question: In a Summoner Skirmish event, if only one person shows up, do they win the top prize?
answer:
Ruling: There is no definitive answer provided in this thread. One participant suggests yes based on other tournament precedents, while another doubts it's in the spirit of the event and notes that in other games these events cannot fire without 8 players, and Carde.io may not allow it.

Nuances:

In other games, similar events require a minimum of 8 players to fire

Carde.io (the tournament platform) may have restrictions preventing single-player events

No official messaging or rules clarification was available at the time of discussion

question: Can you play a hidden Zhonya's at one battlefield in response to someone killing your unit at another battlefield, forcing it to be recalled to base where it will see the unit die?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can play Zhonya's from hidden at one battlefield and it will affect units dying at other battlefields. However, you cannot play it "in response" to something being killed during damage assignment - you must play it from hidden before the showdown enters damage assignment (e.g., in response to a Falling Star or similar effect).

Sequence:

Play Zhonya's from hidden before damage assignment (e.g., in response to another effect like Falling Star)

Zhonya's either gets recalled immediately to base or is played directly to base

Zhonya's at base can see and affect units dying at any battlefield

Nuances:

Zhonya's is not limited to its battlefield since it does not target anything

Hidden cards have reaction:0, so they can only be played in response to other effects, not during damage assignment

There is ambiguity in the rules about whether Zhonya's goes to the battlefield and is immediately recalled, or is played directly to base when played from hidden, but either way it ends up at base

Effects that don't target still affect everything at all locations

question: Are battlefields chosen simultaneously during setup, and are the set aside battlefields public information?
answer: Ruling: Battlefields are chosen simultaneously during setup. The set aside battlefields are not public information.

question: Does Repeat need to be called out immediately when playing the card, and does Ezreal Prodigy reduce the cost of Repeat?
answer: Ruling: Yes, you must call out Repeat as soon as you play the card. Yes, Ezreal Prodigy makes Repeat cost less.

question: Can Teemo hide cards on your teammate's battlefield in 2v2?
answer:
Ruling: No, you can only hide cards at a battlefield you control, not your teammate's battlefield.

Nuances:

This restriction applies to Teemo and any other hide effects

question: When Baited Hook kills a unit with buffs that increase its might, does it check the buffed might or the printed might to determine what unit you can play?
answer:
Ruling: Baited Hook checks the current might of the unit at the time of death, including all modifications from buffs or other effects.

Sequence:

When Baited Hook kills a unit, it locks in the might value at the moment of death

All modifications (buffs, debuffs, etc.) are included in this value

You can then play a unit with might equal to one more than that modified value

The opponent can respond with reactions to shrink the might before the ability resolves

Nuances:

If Sett's leader ability replaces the death, there is no "killed unit" and you cannot play any unit (the reference becomes NULL)

You cannot choose between printed might and current might - it always uses current might at time of death

Accelerate costs must still be paid when playing a unit with Baited Hook, as "ignoring its cost" only refers to the printed base cost

question: If a unit with 2 Zhonyas attached dies, do both Zhonyas get destroyed?
answer:
Ruling: No, you choose one of the Zhonyas to trigger. When 2 replacement effects happen on the same unit from the same source, you choose which one triggers.

Nuances:

Guardian Angel has similar mechanics but its wording ("kill GA" rather than "kill a GA") creates ambiguity about whether you could kill a different GA on the board, though this interpretation is disputed and may not be intended.

question: Does Strike Down remove Guardian Angel before the damage can kill the unit, or does Guardian Angel prevent the death?
answer:
Ruling: Strike Down will kill the unit. The Guardian Angel is removed before the damage can kill during cleanup.

Sequence:

Strike Down deals damage and removes Guardian Angel

Damage doesn't kill until the following cleanup phase

Guardian Angel is removed before that cleanup occurs

Unit dies in cleanup without Guardian Angel protection

question: How to set up a 2v2 tournament in Carde.io?
answer:
Ruling: Carde.io does not have native 2v2 support. Use the multiplayer unpaired option with external pairing via swisssystem.org, or set up a swiss tournament with only one person from each team signing up.

Sequence:

Set up multiplayer unpaired in Carde.io OR set up a swiss tournament

If using multiplayer unpaired: use swisssystem.org for team pairing

If using swiss: have only one person from each team sign up

Nuances:

The original asker chose the swiss tournament method with one person per team signing up

question: Can you spend multiple buffs on Monastery of Hirana when you conquer to draw multiple cards?
answer:
Ruling: No, you can only spend one buff to draw one card when you conquer with Monastery of Hirana.

Sequence:

The triggered ability triggers once when you conquer

You may spend a single buff as part of that one trigger

You draw one card

Nuances:

Even if you have multiple units with buffs, the ability only triggers once per conquer and allows spending only one buff ("a buff", not "buffs")

question: When Hidden Blade is played from Hidden targeting Qiyana with Deflect, does the player have to pay a rune for Deflect even though they already paid to play Hidden Blade Hidden?
answer:
Ruling: You must pay the rune for Deflect when you finalize the Hidden Blade to the chain targeting Qiyana, even though you already paid to play it Hidden.

Sequence:

Pay to play Hidden Blade Hidden earlier

When finalizing Hidden Blade to the chain targeting Qiyana, pay the rune for Deflect

Nuances:

You can target your own unit with Hidden Blade, and if you kill your own unit you will draw 2

You must pay Deflect for each spell or ability that targets a unit with Deflect

question: Can Nocturne be played directly to a battlefield during a showdown when revealed by an effect like Teemo's ability?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Nocturne can be played immediately to a battlefield you control during a showdown when his triggered ability activates from being revealed/looked at, even though he doesn't have the Action or Reaction keyword.

Nuances:

The interaction specifically with Teemo might change pending future clarification (there's discussion about whether "look" counts as "reveal" for Nocturne's trigger)

The general rule is you can only play units to battlefields during showdown if they have Action/Reaction keywords OR if an effect allows you to play them

Nocturne falls into the second category - his triggered ability allows immediate play

You must control the battlefield to play a unit there during showdown

question: In a 3-player Skirmish, do you need to control all 3 battlefields to win on your last point?
answer:
Ruling: You can win off of holding a single battlefield for your last point. The last point rule only affects conquering when you haven't scored every other location that turn.

Nuances:

You don't need to still be in control of the other battlefields, you just have to have scored them previously

Any point can be your last point except if you conquer and haven't scored every other battlefield that turn

question: When a unit or spell has an additional cost of killing a friendly unit, when does Deathknell (or any 'Dies' trigger) go on the chain?
answer:
Ruling: For permanents (units), the permanent fully resolves off the chain before Deathknell is put on the chain. For spells, the Deathknell trigger is put on the chain on top of the spell.

Sequence:

For units: Unit enters play and resolves completely, then Deathknell and "when you play a unit" triggers go on the chain simultaneously (controller chooses order)

For spells: Spell goes on the chain, then Deathknell trigger goes on the chain on top of it

Nuances:

Even though the unit dying (from the additional cost) technically happened before the card being played, Deathknell and "when you play a unit" triggers are considered simultaneous for units and the controller chooses the order

question: Are players required to deck check their opponent's list before playing the first round, and how can they detect violations like pre-siding?
answer:
Ruling: Players are not required to deck check the opponent's list as it is private knowledge. However, players are required to verify the overall construction is correct (1 Legend, 1 CC, 39 Main, 12 Runes, 3 BF) and legal.

Sequence:

Players may request a judge to do a deck check on their opponent at an appropriate time

This should only be used if there are reasons to suspect the opponent might have altered their deck

Players must inform judges of any problems as soon as they occur or are noticed

Nuances:

If a judge determines you purposefully avoided informing them of a deck list error to gain an advantage, you can be penalized

Examples of suspicious situations include: opponent starting with a non-standard chosen champion that has a good matchup, or playing cards game 1 that should only be sideboard options

For big tournaments, deck lists become practically open for top cut as they're shown before matches start

Event organizers are required to deck check 10% randomly per round

question: When Anivia moves to an occupied battlefield and her attack trigger kills the defending unit during the initial chain, do players get action windows during the showdown steps?
answer:
Ruling: The showdown still proceeds through all its normal steps with focus windows for both players, even though the defender was killed during the initial chain. Players cannot play action cards in response to Anivia's When I Attack trigger because it's on a chain (closed state).

Sequence:

Anivia moves to occupied battlefield, starting a showdown

Initial chain: Anivia's attack trigger activates and resolves, killing the defending unit

Showdown proceeds through all normal steps with attacker/defender focus windows

Players gain focus and opportunities to play cards during these windows

After all showdown steps complete, a point is scored

Nuances:

No action cards can be played during the initial chain while Anivia's trigger is resolving (closed state)

The attacker/defender focus pattern continues even though the defender is dead

Points are only scored after all showdown steps unless a card specifically states otherwise (like Yasuo's 3rd move)

question: For Blazing Scorcher, can you pay the 1 energy and 1 Fury cost by exhausting 1 rune and recycling 1 red (which can be exhausted)?
answer:
Ruling: The 1 energy and 1 Fury power is an additional cost you may choose to spend while casting Blazing Scorcher, not a cost reduction. You determine the base cost of 5 energy first, then optionally pay the additional cost of 1 energy and 1 Fury power to have the unit enter ready instead of exhausted.

Sequence:

Determine the base cost of the card (5 energy)

Optionally pay the additional cost of 1 energy and 1 Fury power

If additional cost is paid, unit enters ready; if not paid, unit enters exhausted

Nuances:

When paying for the Fury power, you are able to recycle an exhausted rune to pay its cost

question: Can Chemtech Enforcer be played if you have no cards in hand?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can play Chemtech Enforcer with no cards in hand.

Sequence:

Chemtech Enforcer enters the board first

The "When You Play Me" (WYPM) trigger occurs after the unit is already on the board

Since the trigger happens after the unit is in play, having no cards in hand does not prevent playing the unit

question: Does Yasuo Remorseful's attack trigger occur before or after Master Yi's defense bonus applies?
answer:
Ruling: Master Yi's defense bonus applies before Yasuo's attack trigger resolves. Yi's effect is a passive that activates instantly when defender status is assigned, while Yasuo's trigger must go on the chain and resolve.

Sequence:

Units receive attacker/defender status

Yi's passive defense bonus applies immediately (not a trigger)

Yasuo's attack trigger goes on the chain

Yasuo's trigger resolves

Nuances:

Yi's defense bonus is not a trigger but a passive effect, similar to Assault/Shield

Yi's bonus only applies when you have exactly one defending unit

In general, attacker triggers go on the chain first, then defender triggers, resolving in reverse order (but Yi's effect bypasses this as it's not a trigger)

question: Can Seal of Unity pay for itself (can you activate its ability to generate power while finalizing it to pay for its own cost)?
answer:
Ruling: No, Seal of Unity cannot pay for itself. Abilities can only be activated when the game object is in the appropriate zone, and permanents like seals need to be on the board to activate their abilities. You have to pay their costs as you finalize them, which is before they are on the board and can be activated.

Sequence:

You must pay the seal's costs during finalization

The seal is not yet on the board during finalization

Only after finalization is complete does the seal enter the board

Only once on the board can the seal's ability be activated to add power

question: Can an exhausted unit with ganking move from one battlefield to another?
answer:
Ruling: No, a unit must be ready to move from battlefield to battlefield using ganking.

Nuances:

Ganking removes the restrictions of the Standard Move Action, but does not allow exhausted units to move between battlefields

question: When Rell's attack trigger and Reaver's Row both go on the chain, do you have to reveal which gear you're attaching to Rell when placing the trigger on the chain, or can you wait until resolution?
answer:
Ruling: You do not have to reveal which gear you're attaching to Rell when placing the trigger on the chain. The gear is selected at resolution.

Sequence:

Rell's attack trigger goes on the chain

Reaver's Row trigger goes on the chain

You do not declare which gear at this point

On resolution of Rell's trigger, you select and play the gear

Nuances:

Because Rell chooses a card in a private zone (your hand), it's not a target and doesn't need to be declared when added to the chain

You don't even have to tell your opponent what you're going to do until resolution

question: If a unit dies during a showdown on the opponent's turn, causing temporary loss of control, and another unit is moved into that battlefield during the same showdown to win it, does the player score a point?
answer:
Ruling: No, you do not score a point if you move a unit back into the battlefield during the same showdown. Control is not checked during active showdowns, so you never lost and regained control - you maintained control throughout the showdown.

Sequence:

Opponent attacks battlefield with Yasuo, killing your unit A

Control is not lost because the battlefield is contested (showdown is active)

If you move unit B into the battlefield during that same showdown and win, you don't score (no conquest occurred)

If the showdown ends first, then you move a unit back in to beat Yasuo, you would conquer and score

Nuances:

Control is only checked continuously outside of showdowns or when battlefields are not being contested

During an active showdown, control status is frozen regardless of might changes

question: Can you score on an opponent's turn, and does scoring on your turn prevent scoring the same battlefield again on the opponent's turn?
answer:
Ruling: You can score on an opponent's turn. The only restriction is you cannot score the same battlefield twice in one turn (your turn or opponent's turn are separate turns).

Sequence:

If you scored Battlefield A on your turn, then move to base, then Ride the Wind to Battlefield B on opponent's turn, you score at Battlefield B

If you scored Battlefield A on your turn, then Ride the Wind back to Battlefield A on opponent's turn, you score there again because it's a different turn

Nuances:

The restriction only applies within a single turn - your turn and opponent's turn are counted as separate turns for scoring purposes

question: Do seals enter tapped or untapped?
answer:
Ruling: Gears always enter untapped.

Nuances:

This applies to all gears, including seals

question: If I start a combat with Yasuo Green, and later use Ride the Wind (RTW) during that combat, does Yasuo's 'when I attack' ability trigger?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Yasuo's "when I attack" ability triggers when you use Ride the Wind during combat.

Nuances:

The ability triggers even though the combat was already started before using Ride the Wind

question: When a hidden card is revealed or a unit is played, does it enter the battlefield ready or exhausted?
answer:
Ruling: Units inherently enter the battlefield exhausted when played or revealed from hidden. However, specific card text can override this default rule.

Nuances:

Sprite Call specifically states the token enters ready, so it comes in ready despite the general rule

Revealing a hidden card counts as playing it, so the exhausted rule applies unless the card text says otherwise

question: Can I respond to a leader ability activation with a reaction (e.g., playing Hidden Blade in response to Teemo bouncing a card)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can respond to a leader ability activation with a reaction, unless it is an ADD ability (like Kai'Sa or Darius).

Nuances:

ADD abilities (Kai'Sa, Darius) cannot be responded to

The response must be a reaction, not an action

question: Can you play Harnessed Dragon if the opponent doesn't have a unit out?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can play Harnessed Dragon even if the opponent has no units. The ability will fail to finalize (enter the chain) if there is no valid target.

Sequence:

Play Harnessed Dragon and it resolves fully

The "When you play me" trigger is evaluated

If no enemy unit exists, the ability fails to finalize and does not enter the chain

There will be no chain item to react to or resolve

Nuances:

This is not a Silver Rule situation about fulfilling as much as you can during resolution

"When you play me" triggers are evaluated after the unit fully resolves

If killing a unit were required to play Harnessed Dragon, it would need to state "as an additional cost"

question: Can you play your Legend Card in a toploader or graded case during tournaments?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you should be allowed to play your Legend Card in a toploader or graded case during tournaments.

Nuances:

The rules indicate that different sleeves for different decks are permitted, which would extend to allowing the Legend Card to be in a distinct sleeve or protective case

question: If there is a showdown at battlefield A and someone plays Ride the Wind to battlefield B, does the showdown at A conclude first before moving to B, or does B start first?
answer:
Ruling: You must complete the showdown at battlefield A before proceeding with the showdown at battlefield B.

Sequence:

Complete showdown at battlefield A

Then proceed to battlefield B

question: Can Vi's ability be used when defending in a showdown declared by the opponent?
answer:
Ruling: No, Vi's ability cannot be used during a showdown. Vi's ability does not have the "Action" or "Reaction" keywords, so it can only be used during your own turn, outside of a showdown, and only while no chain currently exists.

Nuances:

The ability must be used during your own turn

It cannot be used while any chain exists

It cannot be used during any showdown (whether attacking or defending)

question: If a unit with a 'when I attack/defend' effect enters the battlefield after the initial 'when I attack/defend' chain has already resolved during a showdown, does it still get that effect?
answer:
Ruling: Units that enter the battlefield during combat still get their 'when I attack/defend' effects as long as it is the first time they are gaining the attacker or defender designation during this combat.

Sequence: (for trigger ordering)

Attacker triggers are added to the chain first

Then other players in turn order if they have any

Then defender triggers

question: When Malzahar's ability is activated during a Showdown to kill a unit with Deathknell, does the Deathknell trigger cause focus to pass before the player can take further actions?
answer:
Ruling: Malzahar's Add ability generates resources without using the chain (can only be activated during an open state). When it kills a Deathknell unit, both the intended action being paid for and the Deathknell trigger go pending together, then both finalize. Focus passes to the opponent only after the entire chain resolves.

Sequence:

Player activates Malzahar's ability during an open state (typically when paying for an action)

Malzahar's ability generates power immediately without using the chain

If a Deathknell unit dies, the trigger goes pending along with the action being paid for

Both items finalize on the chain

The chain resolves

Focus passes to opponent

Nuances:

The Add ability can only be activated during an open state, preventing use at reaction speed

This prevents the Deathknell trigger from causing premature focus passing

The exact mechanics await CRD revision for full technical support

question: Does Cithria of Cloudfield's ability trigger if she already has a buff?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Cithria of Cloudfield's ability triggers even if she already has a buff, but she will not gain an additional buff (the trigger effectively does nothing).

Nuances:

You can respond to the trigger with effects like Call to Glory even though she won't gain a buff

question: Can I play a reaction spell in response to my opponent playing a unit?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot react to a unit being played. Permanents resolve immediately without priority passing upon being finalized on the chain.

Nuances:

If a unit has a "When I'm played" trigger, you can react to that trigger, but you are not reacting to the unit itself

Additional costs (like effects that must be paid to play the unit) must be paid before the unit can finalize from the chain

"When I'm played" triggers happen after a unit resolves and always look back at the immediately resolving action

question: What happens when Dazzling Aurora reveals a unit (like Perched Grimwyrm) that can't be played due to unmet conditions?
answer:
Ruling: The revealed unit remains banished.

Nuances:

This applies to Dazzling Aurora after it received errata

Most Origins cards that play from deck received similar errata

question: Can a game result be changed after the game has finished when an illegal play (using Hextech Ray in response to Time Warp) was made that neither player noticed during the game?
answer:
Ruling: The game cannot be rewound after it has already finished, even if an illegal play occurred that neither player noticed at the time.

Nuances:

Hextech Ray is not reaction speed, so it cannot be played in response to Time Warp

In low OPL (Organized Play Level), rewinding is allowed during a game, but this does not apply once the game has concluded

Players should know the rules better for next time

question: If my opponent uses Falling Star on my only unit while they also have a unit on their field and I use Retreat at reaction speed to save my unit, are they required to damage their own unit or does the spell miss?
answer:
Ruling: If you use Retreat in response to Falling Star before targets are chosen, your opponent must choose their own unit as the only valid target. Falling Star does not target on activation.

Sequence:

Falling Star is played and goes on the chain

There is a reaction window before targets are chosen

If you use Retreat during this window, your unit is removed from play

When Falling Star resolves, the opponent must choose targets (this is when deflect is checked)

Since your unit is gone, their unit becomes the only valid target

Two instances of 3 damage are put on the chain targeting their unit

Each instance of damage creates its own reaction window before resolving

Nuances:

You have two timings to react: before opponent chooses targets and after

To force damage to the opponent's unit, you must react before they choose targets, not after

The two instances of damage are separate items on the chain, each with their own reaction window

question: If Void Seeker targets a unit that becomes illegal (e.g., removed by Retreat as a reaction), can you still draw a card?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can still draw a card. The spell must have a legal target to finalize, but once finalized, "do as much as you can" applies—you skip game actions involving illegal targets but perform all other game actions.

Sequence:

The spell must have a legal target when it finalizes

Once finalized, resolve the spell using "do as much as you can"

Skip any game actions that involve the now-illegal target

Perform all other game actions (like drawing a card)

question: When you move a unit with Charme to your battlefield, who is the defender?
answer: Ruling: You are the defender when you move a unit with Charme to your battlefield.

question: When a stunned unit is recalled to base, does it return in its current state (ready/exhausted)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, a unit returns to base in whatever state it was in on the field unless the recall effect specifically states it changes state.

Nuances:

Some recall effects explicitly change the unit's state (e.g., recalling a unit exhausted)

question: If Yone moves to a battlefield where Ezreal is defending, and in response to Ezreal's defend ability, Arcane Shift moves Ezreal home, does Yone's battlefield count as an open battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: No, it does not count as an open battlefield because the combat showdown had already started when Ezreal used his defender ability, so at the time combat started it was not an open battlefield.

Sequence:

Yone moves to battlefield where Ezreal is defending

Ezreal uses defender ability (combat showdown starts)

Arcane Shift moves Ezreal home in response

Combat cleanup occurs, but this is not conquering an open battlefield

question: Can you spend the buff from Showstopper on Sett Brawler before moving him into a battlefield?
answer: Ruling: No, you cannot spend the buff from Showstopper on Sett Brawler before moving him into a battlefield because you would be trying to do that during Showstopper's effects.

question: Can you react to 'when I attack' abilities, and what is the timing/sequence for when I attack and when I defend triggers?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can react to 'when I attack' abilities using reactions. These abilities create a chain.

Sequence:

When I attack triggers are declared first (so they resolve last in the chain)

When I defend triggers are declared last (so they resolve first in the chain)

Then players can add reactions to the chain

Nuances:

Only effects that use "when" or "at" are triggers that can be reacted to

Passive effects that use "while" (like Assault) are not triggers and cannot be reacted to

question: Can you react to Anivia entering a battlefield to increase your creatures' might before they get killed?
answer:
Ruling: Anivia does not trigger when she moves into a battlefield. She triggers once the combat showdown starts and she is attacking, with her effect going on the initial chain of a showdown.

Sequence:

Combat showdown starts with Anivia attacking

Anivia's effect goes on the initial chain

You can react on that chain with reactions

Nuances:

The trigger timing is at showdown start, not when Anivia moves to the battlefield

question: Does the new Teemo errata mean he triggers twice - once from Hidden and once from defending?
answer:
Ruling: Teemo does not trigger twice. The errata was only to clarify the existing text, specifically that Teemo needs an enemy unit to target for his trigger. The functionality remains the same.

Nuances:

The image shown was the old text, not the new errata

Teemo can only deal damage to one unit total, even if multiple Hidden cards are revealed

question: For Baited Hook, if you sacrifice a 4 might unit, can you grab any unit with 5 might or less, or only units with exactly 4 or 5 might?
answer:
Ruling: You can play a unit with might anywhere from 0 to 5 (0 to X+1, where X is the killed unit's might).

Nuances:

The card text "up to 1 more than the killed unit" means the entire phrase "1 more than the killed unit" is the ceiling, not that "up to 1" creates a range from X to X+1

If you substitute the actual number (e.g., killed unit has 3 might), it reads "has Might up to 4" which includes 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4

The alternative interpretation (only X or X+1) would require different wording like "exactly the same might or one more might than the killed unit"

question: Do units heal damage after a showdown ends, including units that weren't in the showdown (at base or other battlefields)?
answer:
Ruling: At the end of combat and at the end of turn, all units everywhere in play heal all damage on them at the same time, regardless of how that damage was assigned or where the units are located.

Nuances:

Damage does not reduce a unit's might value; damage is tracked separately and a unit is destroyed when damage marked on it equals or exceeds its might

The healing applies to all units across all battlefields and bases simultaneously, not just units that participated in the showdown

question: Can you respond to Reckoner's Arena trigger by killing a unit (like Qiyana) to prevent its conquer effect?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can respond to the Arena trigger by killing a unit to prevent its conquer effect from being added to the chain.

Sequence:

Arena's trigger goes on the chain

You can respond by killing the unit before the trigger resolves

When Arena's trigger resolves, it checks which units are present at the battlefield with conquer abilities

Only units present when the trigger resolves are added to the chain

If a unit was killed in response, it will not be included

question: Can a player play a reaction when the opponent proceeds to the end step (i.e., when changing phases)?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot play a reaction when changing phases. You can only play a reaction during an opponent's turn if the chain is not empty and you get priority, or if there is a showdown and you get focus.

Nuances:

This differs from Magic: The Gathering, where players commonly perform actions during the opponent's end step.

question: Can Charm move an enemy unit directly from one battlefield to another (without the Ganking keyword)?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Charm can move an enemy unit directly from one battlefield to another, even if that unit doesn't have the Ganking keyword.

Nuances:

When you use Charm to move an enemy unit to your battlefield, that enemy unit is considered attacking for assault purposes.

question: If I see two Nocturnes with Called Shot, can I play both of them before drawing a card, or do I have to draw 2 cards since Nocturne says 'if you look but don't draw'?
answer:
Ruling: You can play both Nocturnes before drawing any cards. Since you now have no relevant cards to look at, you damage cycle which does nothing.

Sequence:

Look at top card and see first Nocturne

Play first Nocturne without drawing

Look at top card and see second Nocturne

Play second Nocturne without drawing

No cards remain to look at, so damage cycle does nothing

question: Can Petal rescue bring back a unit from trash?
answer:
Ruling: No, Petal rescue cannot bring back a unit from trash. "Unit" refers to objects on the board unless specified otherwise, and the card does not specify a zone like "from your trash."

Sequence:

When a card says "friendly unit" without specifying a zone, it refers only to units on the board

Units in trash are treated as cards and cannot be affected by spells or abilities that target units on the board

To target units in trash, the card text must explicitly specify the zone (e.g., "from your trash")

Nuances:

Units retain the properties of being a unit while in trash, but are treated as cards similar to when in hand

The term "unit" in card text defaults to units on the board per the targeting rules

Actions like "Banish" can take cards from any zone, but the object being chosen ("a friendly unit") still must meet targeting requirements

question: Do move triggers get resolved before attack/defend triggers get put on the chain?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, move triggers resolve on a chain outside the showdown before it starts. You cannot start a showdown while there is a chain, so once the move trigger chain fully resolves, the showdown can begin with its initial chain containing attack/defend triggers.

Sequence:

Move trigger is added to the chain as pending

Cleanup finalizes the trigger onto the chain (step 8)

The chain resolves completely

Showdown begins (step 9 of cleanup, only if there is no chain)

Attack/defend triggers go onto the initial chain of the showdown in order: attacker triggers first, then defender triggers

Initial chain resolves (LIFO - last in, first out)

Nuances:

Move triggers happen before showdown begins, so the rules about combat and showdowns don't apply to move triggers

You cannot react in response to a move itself

A showdown only begins during cleanup if there is no existing chain

question: What is the function/playstyle of each color in Riftbound?
answer: This question was not answered in the thread. The only response was a link to another Discord message, with no explanation of color identities or playstyles provided in this thread.

question: Can Stealthy Pursuer move with a friendly unit if it is exhausted, and can it move with Ride the Wind on a friend?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Stealthy Pursuer can move with a friendly unit regardless of whether it is exhausted or not. There is no additional cost to its ability.

Nuances:

It can be used to add extra might to every move without limitation

It can move with Ride the Wind on a friendly unit

question: Can Super Mega Death Rocket's conquer trigger be added to the chain if it gets discarded to the trash by another conquer trigger during the same conquer event?
answer:
Ruling: Super Mega Death Rocket's trigger cannot be retroactively added if it moves to the trash while other conquer triggers are resolving. All conquer triggers are evaluated at the same moment when the conquer occurs.

Sequence:

When a conquer occurs, all conquer triggers are evaluated at that moment

For SMDR's trigger to be added to the chain, it must already be in the trash when the conquer happens

If SMDR is discarded by another conquer trigger during resolution, its trigger won't be retroactively added

Nuances:

This differs from Immortal Phoenix, which checks its condition ("when a spell kills") after the spell fully resolves, at which point Phoenix is already in the trash

The key distinction is "when the condition is met" - SMDR's condition must be met at the moment of conquer, not during the resolution of other conquer triggers

question: If an opponent reacts to Shen being played onto Trifarian War Camp with Gust (which targets units with 3 or less Might), can Gust target Shen, or does Trifarian War Camp's +1 Might apply instantly?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot react to a permanent (unit/gear/add ability) being played.
