The Legend version of Ahri works differently because it doesn't target

question: Can Draven Vanquisher's defend trigger activate multiple times in a single combat if the attacking unit is removed and then returns?
answer:
Ruling: Draven's defend trigger can only be fulfilled once per combat. It will trigger the first time he gains the defender designation in a given combat, even if the attacking unit is removed and returns during the same showdown.

Nuances:

Removing the attacking unit (e.g., with Force of Fire) and having it return (e.g., with Ride the Wind) during the same combat does not allow Draven's trigger to activate again

question: Does Viktor's ability trigger if he and another non-Recruit unit die simultaneously from the same spell?
answer:
Ruling: Viktor's ability does not trigger if he and another non-Recruit unit die at the same time from the same spell or game action.

Sequence:

Viktor's ability only triggers when he is on the board immediately after another non-Recruit unit dies

If Viktor leaves the board at the same time as the other unit, he cannot evaluate his trigger condition

The ability is only active while Viktor is on the Board zone, not in Trash

Nuances:

This applies to any simultaneous death effect, such as both units being killed in the same Cleanup due to damage from a card like Unchecked Power

question: Can you hold priority and cast multiple spells in a row during a showdown before passing priority?
answer:
Ruling: You can hold priority and play multiple cards in a row, but only Reactions. If you want to play multiple Actions, each must resolve and your opponent will get Focus in between.

Sequence:

When you have priority, you can cast a Reaction

Hold priority to respond to your own spell on the chain (it hasn't resolved yet)

Cast another Reaction

Repeat as desired before passing priority

Note: You can opt to play Reactions as Actions if you want

Nuances:

Focus is the permission to play Actions in a showdown and to start a chain

Priority is the permission to play Reactions onto an existing chain

Focus passes when a chain fully resolves or a player with focus passes on an empty chain

Exception: In combat, after the initial chain (where "When I attack/defend" triggers are handled) resolves, the attacker retains focus rather than it passing

question: Can Salvage be played when there is no gear in the game, given the new errata changing it to "You may kill up to one gear. Draw 1." and the rule allowing "up to" effects to choose zero targets?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Salvage can now be played even when there is no gear in the game. The "up to one" wording allows you to choose zero gear as targets, play the card, and still draw a card.

Sequence:

Play Salvage

Choose zero gear as targets

Draw 1 card

Nuances:

This only applies to cards with "up to" wording; cards without "up to" wording still require valid targets to be played

The errata was specifically designed to prevent Salvage from being a dead card when no gear is in play

question: When you conquer a battlefield, can you immediately deploy units to it on the same turn?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can play units to a battlefield immediately after conquering it on the same turn. Units come in exhausted like any other unit would.

Sequence:

Conquer the battlefield

You gain control of it after conquering

You can then play units to it (they enter exhausted)

Nuances:

You keep control of a battlefield until you have no units present there

You cannot lose or gain control of a battlefield during a showdown

During a showdown, you cannot play units normally - you are limited to legally timed cards

Units played as a result of actions or reactions (like Shen) can be played to a battlefield you are defending during a showdown

question: If Darius is played and then Kai'Sa, does Darius count himself toward his play requirement?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Darius counts himself when checking if cards have been played. When Kai'Sa is played after Darius, she becomes the second card played, triggering Darius's effect.

Nuances:

The order doesn't matter - even if played in reverse order (Kai'Sa then Darius), Darius would still trigger because he sees himself as the second card played

question: Can you cast Stupefy on a 1 Might unit to draw a card even though it won't reduce the unit's Might?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, 1 Might units are valid targets for Stupefy. You can cast it on a 1 Might unit to draw a card even though the Might reduction has no effect due to the "minimum of 1" clause.

Nuances:

The unit's Might stays at 1 because Stupefy specifies "to a minimum of 1"

You still get to draw a card from Stupefy's second effect even when the Might reduction doesn't change the game state

question: If a unit is moved back to base (e.g., with Flash) in response to a targeted action spell like Hextech Ray, does the spell fizzle, or can the caster choose a new target?
answer:
Ruling: When a targeted action spell like Hextech Ray resolves, if its target is no longer at a battlefield, it won't deal damage to its target. You cannot choose a different target at any point.

Sequence:

When you play the spell, you choose its target

If the target is moved before the spell resolves, the spell still resolves but does not deal damage

The spell does as much as it can (e.g., Void Seeker would still draw a card even if the target is gone)

Nuances:

This is different from spells with "do this:" wording, which create triggers that choose targets upon resolution (like Falling Star)

Moving a unit with Flash before a spell resolves does not allow retargeting for normal targeted spells

Dragon's Rage has been errata'd to function as a "do this:" spell even though it doesn't say so on the card

question: In Riftbound, can you change the targets of Falling Star after the first 3 damage is dealt (e.g., after opponent plays Discipline)?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot change targets after they are chosen. Both targets must be chosen at effectively the same time when Falling Star resolves, and cannot be changed later even though there are windows to react between damage instances.

Sequence:

Falling Star is played (opponents can react here before targets are chosen)

Falling Star resolves and both targets are chosen simultaneously

Two damage effects are created and go on the chain (opponents can react here before any damage)

First 3 damage resolves (opponents can react here)

Second 3 damage resolves

Nuances:

There is a window to play Discipline (or other reactions) after Falling Star is played but before targets are chosen, allowing you to avoid targeting that unit - but this would be a bad play since the opponent can just wait until after targeting

Reactions can occur at three different points, but targets are locked in at step 2

If units are removed before targets are chosen (e.g., via Retreat), the caster must target remaining legal units, including their own if necessary

question: Can Death Rocket create an infinite loop if you have one rocket in hand and one in discard, by discarding the rocket in hand to retrieve the one in discard, which then triggers again?
answer:
Ruling: No, this does not create a loop. When you conquer, all "when I conquer" triggers from cards currently in trash are declared and put on the chain at that moment. A rocket discarded during the resolution of another rocket's trigger was not in trash when you conquered, so it does not trigger.

Sequence:

You conquer with one rocket in hand and one in trash

All triggers from the conquer event (including the rocket in trash) are declared and put on the chain at once

You choose the order your triggers resolve

When resolving the rocket trigger, you may discard a card (the rocket in hand) to get the rocket back from trash

The newly discarded rocket does not trigger because it was not in trash when the conquer event occurred

Nuances:

"When I conquer" is a one-time event, not a lasting state

All triggers happen at the moment of conquering, not continuously throughout resolution

If Death Rocket said "while you have a battlefield in control" instead, it would be loopable since that refers to a game state rather than an event

question: If a 2 might unit is targeted by En Garde (+1 might, chain 1), then targeted by a 2 damage spell (chain 2), does the unit survive with 3 might and 1 health, or does it die?
answer:
Ruling: The unit dies. The chain resolves in reverse order, so the 2 damage spell resolves first, killing the 2 might unit before En Garde can resolve.

Sequence:

En Garde is played targeting the 2 might unit (goes on chain as link 1)

Opponent responds with a 2 damage spell (goes on chain as link 2)

Chain resolves starting with most recent: the damage spell resolves first

The spell deals 2 damage to the 2 might unit

Cleanup occurs after the spell resolves, and the unit dies

En Garde attempts to resolve but its target is no longer in play, so it does nothing

Nuances:

Cleanup happens after each spell resolves, not after the entire chain resolves

When a card's target is no longer in play when it resolves, it does nothing

question: If a spell's target is removed before the spell resolves (e.g., via Retreat), does the spell fizzle or must it retarget to another valid target?
answer:
Ruling: Spells do not fizzle in Riftbound. Targets are chosen when an effect is finalized on the chain and cannot be changed. When the spell resolves, if the target is no longer legal, that part of the spell does nothing (do as much as you can), but the spell still resolves and any other effects still happen.

Sequence:

Targets are declared when an effect is finalized on the chain

If a target becomes illegal before resolution, that part does nothing

The spell still resolves and performs any other effects that don't require the illegal target

The spell cannot retarget to a different unit

Nuances:

Cards with reflexive triggers (like Falling Star) are more complex - targets for the reflexive triggers are chosen when the triggers are added to the chain, not when the original spell is played

If you respond to Falling Star before it resolves (before triggers go on chain), the triggers must still choose valid targets when added, which could include your own units

If you respond after the triggers are on the chain with targets already chosen, those targets cannot change

question: Does Imperial Decree affect units that enter the battlefield after it has been played?
answer:
Ruling: Imperial Decree affects all units, even if they entered after it was played. The trigger goes on the chain during the combat damage step and players can react to it.

Sequence:

Imperial Decree creates a lingering effect that triggers when a unit takes damage

During the Combat Damage Step, when units take damage, Imperial Decree's trigger goes on the chain

Players can respond to the trigger while it's on the chain

However, you cannot save a unit that already took damage in combat, because the trigger to kill it is already on the chain

Nuances:

Imperial Decree does not modify units themselves; it creates a lingering effect that applies to any unit that takes damage after it resolves

This is different from effects like Grand Strategem which only affect units present when it resolves

There is no official rule text clarifying which effects create lingering effects versus one-time modifications

question: Can you respond to spells on the chain after other spells/abilities have been added on top of them, and does the chain resolve one by one with opportunities to react between resolutions?
answer:
Ruling: You can target any spell on the chain at any point, even when other spells/abilities are on top of it. The chain resolves one by one, and between each resolution you have the ability to react again.

Sequence:

Spells/abilities are added to the chain

The chain resolves one item at a time (top to bottom)

Between each resolution, players can react and add new spells/abilities to the chain

This continues until the chain is empty

Nuances:

While you can respond to any spell on the chain at any time, it's strategically better to wait as long as possible to avoid giving your opponent unnecessary information

You can let one spell resolve, then respond to remaining spells on the chain before they resolve

question: Can you use Gust (or any 'react' response) immediately after a unit is played, or in response to unit movement?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot react directly to a unit being played or to movement itself. You can only react if the unit or movement triggers an ability.

Sequence:

When a unit is played or moves, check if it has a triggered ability (e.g., "When you play me..." or "When I move...")

If there is a triggered ability, you can react to that ability

If you react to kill the unit (like Harnessed Dragon), the triggered ability still resolves

Nuances:

You are reacting to the triggered ability, not to the unit or movement action itself

Even if you kill a unit in response to its triggered ability, that ability still resolves (example: Harnessed Dragon's ability to kill your unit will still happen)

question: If a 3 might unit is reduced to 1 might by Thousand Tail (Watcher), and then receives a buff, does it go to 2 might or remain at 1?
answer:
Ruling: The unit goes to 2 might. Debuffs like Thousand Tail check on resolution how much they will reduce a unit's might, then apply that fixed amount. The buff is applied after the debuff resolves, so it increases the might from 1 to 2.

Sequence:

3 might unit gets debuffed by Thousand Tail/Watcher (reduces to minimum 1 might)

Unit is now at 1 might

Buff is applied after the debuff resolves

Unit goes to 2 might

Nuances:

The debuff amount is set when it resolves and doesn't continuously recalculate

Units can exist at 0 might and won't die unless they have at least 1 damage marked on them

If a buffed unit at 2 might (originally 1 might + buff) takes 1 damage and then loses the buff, it becomes a 1 might unit with 1 damage and dies

Might does not equal HP; damage doesn't lower might, only marks damage on the unit

question: If Dragon's Rage targets a unit at a Battlefield and the opponent reacts with Fight or Flight to move that unit to their base, how does Dragon's Rage resolve?
answer:
Ruling: Dragon's Rage does not fizzle. The unit will move according to the declared destination, and a trigger is created targeting a different enemy unit at the unit's new location. When that trigger resolves, the units deal damage to each other.

Sequence:

If the destination was declared as base, there will be no movement

If the destination was a different battlefield, the unit moves from base to that battlefield

In both cases, a trigger is created targeting a different enemy unit at the unit's current location

When that trigger resolves, the units deal damage to each other

Nuances:

Riftbound does not have fizzling; effects resolve with 0 effect instead

question: Can points granted by card abilities instantly win you the game when you're at 7 points, or do you draw a card instead because of Final Point restrictions?
answer:
Ruling: Points earned from card abilities (sources other than Conquer or Hold) can instantly win you the game even when you're one point away from victory. The Final Point restrictions do not apply to points granted by card abilities.

Nuances:

The Final Point restrictions only apply to points earned from Conquer or Hold

Examples include points from moving Yasuo Windrider or killing opponent's Draven Audacious

question: Do units played from hand during showdown gain assault/shield bonuses, and does playing Rengar (3 might, assault 2) trigger Volibear's legend ability?
answer:
Ruling: Units played from hand during showdown will gain assault/shield bonuses because a cleanup occurs when the permanent is played, assigning attacker/defender status and applying the bonuses at that time.

Sequence:

When a permanent is played during showdown, a cleanup occurs

During cleanup, units at the battlefield without attacker/defender designation gain the same designation as their controller

Assault/shield bonuses are then applied based on that designation

Nuances:

Playing Rengar (3 might, assault 2) as an attacker does NOT trigger Volibear's legend ability because Rengar enters as 3 might and only becomes 5 might after cleanup

In contrast, playing a 4 might unit at Trifarian Warcamp DOES trigger Volibear because Trifarian Warcamp applies instantly as the unit enters, not requiring cleanup

question: When playing a unit with Portal Rescue (which lets you play without paying its cost), do you still need to pay the additional cost to Accelerate it?
answer:
Ruling: When a card effect references "Cost", it only refers to the printed energy and power cost. You still must pay all additional costs and may pay optional additional costs like Accelerate if you want to use them.

Sequence:

Portal Rescue allows you to play the unit without paying its printed cost

If you want to Accelerate the unit, you must still pay the Accelerate cost (1 energy and 1 power)

Nuances:

This principle applies to all additional costs (mandatory ones like Cruel Patron, and optional ones like Accelerate)

question: If I have a Jinx Rebel on board, 3 cards in hand and 3 Super Mega Death Rockets in my trash, then conquer a battlefield, can I discard all 3 cards in hand to get back all 3 death rockets and increase Jinx's might by 3 off a single conquer trigger? Can I instead discard 1 card to get the first death rocket back, then discard it for the second and discard that for the 3rd?
answer:
Ruling: Yes to both scenarios. When you conquer, all three Super Mega Death Rocket abilities trigger and go onto the chain simultaneously, then each resolves separately one after the other.

Sequence:

All three SMDR abilities are put on the chain when you conquer

Each ability resolves individually in the order you choose

When each resolves, you may discard a card to return that SMDR to hand

Jinx's might increases by 1 for each card discarded this way

Nuances:

You can discard a newly reacquired SMDR to get back a different one

This allows you to resolve all three triggers without losing net cards in hand

The "you may" choice happens when each ability resolves, not when they're put on the chain

question: When attacking a battlefield and choosing not to play an action card, does the opponent gain priority only, or both priority and focus?
answer:
Ruling: When you attack a battlefield you control focus and priority, but if you choose not to play an action card, your opponent gains both priority and focus.

Nuances:

The attacker initially has both focus and priority

Passing without playing an action transfers both elements to the opponent

question: What are the appropriate penalties for various deck presentation errors in Summoner Skirmish, including: having extra sleeved cards in deck box, having 16 sideboard cards instead of 8, submitting wrong number of battlefields, having incorrect rune distribution, and having 8 incorrect main deck cards?
answer:
Ruling: Most of the judge's calls were appropriate, though scenario 5 (8 incorrect main deck cards) should have been a Game Loss rather than Match Loss according to the rules. Scenario 2 (16 sideboard cards) was handled appropriately with a Match Loss due to the high potential for abuse, even though it's not explicitly covered by rules.

Sequence:

Scenario 1 (4th extra Watcher): Deck presentation error warning (appropriate)

Scenario 2 (16 sideboard cards): Match Loss and fix for later rounds (appropriate due to abuse potential)

Scenario 3 (only 2 battlefields submitted): Deck presentation error warning (appropriate)

Scenario 4 (7/5 runes vs 6/6): Deck presentation error warning, forced to 6/6 with proxy (appropriate)

Scenario 5 (8 incorrect main deck cards): Should be Game Loss, not Match Loss, per rule about when restoring deck is not easily possible

Nuances:

For scenario 1, if there were only 48 cards instead of 49, DQ would have been appropriate

For scenario 2, the judge initially considered it harsh but the community agreed the Match Loss was justified because all 16 cards were fully sleeved in matching colors, creating too much flexibility to counter different decks

Scenario 2 represents a gray area not explicitly covered by rules, but the potential for malicious conduct at High OPL justified the harsher penalty

Players at High OPL are expected to know tournament rules

question: In a showdown, does the attacker or defender get focus first, and how does the action/reaction card speed system work when passing focus?
answer:
Ruling: The attacker always gains focus first in a showdown. When a player passes focus without playing a card, the opponent can then start a chain with either action or reaction cards, but the passing player can only respond with reaction cards.

Sequence:

Attacker declares showdown and gains focus first

Attacker can play action or reaction speed cards

If attacker plays a card, defender can only respond with reaction cards

If attacker passes focus, defender can then play action or reaction cards

When defender starts a chain after attacker passes, attacker can only respond with reaction cards

Nuances:

The ability to play action speed cards is only available to the player who currently has focus and hasn't passed it yet

Once you pass focus, you can only respond with reaction speed cards to any chains your opponent starts

question: When attempting to retreat but getting gusted instead, does the retreating player still channel a rune?
answer:
Ruling: No, you do not channel a rune when gusted during a retreat attempt.

Sequence:

Gust resolves first

When retreat resolves, it cannot determine an owner to channel a rune

Nuances:

The retreat effect still resolves, but without a valid owner present, the rune channeling portion cannot occur

question: With the errata changing Salvage from 'You may kill a gear' to 'You may kill up to one gear', can you play Salvage when there are no gears on the board to get the Draw 1 effect?
answer: Ruling: Yes, with the new errata text 'up to one gear', you can play Salvage when there are no gears on the board and still draw 1 card.

question: If green Leona is on a battlefield with 2 enemy units (Sprite Mother and its token), and Sprite Mother is stunned (reducing it to 1 power), does Convergent Mutation set Sprite Mother to 3 power or does it stay at 1 power due to Leona's -8 aura?
answer:
Ruling: Sprite Mother would be set to 3 power. The game applies positive modifiers before negative modifiers, and since Leona's ability is an aura effect (not a snapshot effect), it applies last after Convergent Mutation's set effect.

Sequence:

Convergent Mutation sets Sprite Mother's power to 3

Leona's -8 aura applies after as a negative modifier

Final result: Sprite Mother has 3 power

Nuances:

Leona (Zealot) always applies last

Aura effects like Leona's don't snapshot, unlike triggered abilities such as Ahri's

This interaction is expected to be clarified in an updated Comprehensive Rules

question: When Dragon's Rage (or similar card) instructs you to move a unit, what are the legal destinations and does it trigger combat/defender bonuses?
answer:
Ruling: When a card instructs you to move a unit, you can move it from wherever it is to any legal location of your choice (including between battlefields or to/from base), other than its current location. The move does not exhaust the unit and does not trigger combat or any attacker/defender bonuses.

Sequence:

Move the unit to any legal location (except its current location)

No exhaustion occurs from the move

No showdown/combat is triggered by the move itself

Nuances:

This differs from the standard move action which has costs and restrictions (like not being able to move between battlefields without ganking)

Card-instructed moves have no cost and no restrictions

Attacker/defender buffs do not apply because showdown/combat cannot start until the chain is empty

question: When tokens are killed (recruits, sprites, etc), are they sent to trash pile?
answer:
Ruling: Tokens do go to the trash pile when killed, but then they immediately cease to exist.

Nuances:

This matters for cards like Wraith of Echoes and Viktor, Leader, which will trigger when unit tokens hit the trash

Viktor, Leader triggers for unit tokens as long as they aren't recruits

Tokens aren't cards, which is relevant for some game effects

question: Does Mask of Foresight retroactively stop applying if the attacking/defending unit is no longer alone during the reaction window in a showdown?
answer:
Ruling: No, Mask of Foresight does not retroactively stop applying. Once the "when I attack or defend alone" condition triggers and the triggered effect is applied, it is no longer affected by whether the unit remains alone.

Nuances:

"When" creates a trigger that goes on the stack, so the condition only needs to be true at the moment of triggering

This differs from passive abilities that evaluate their conditions almost constantly

question: If a player has an invalid decklist (missing runes) that is discovered during a deck check after the match has already finished, should they receive a game loss for that completed match?
answer:
Ruling: An illegal decklist is a game loss. If it's discovered between rounds (after a match has finished), the game loss is applied to the next round, not to the already-completed match.

Nuances:

Once a match has finished, it's unlikely for a game loss to be applied to that match

If someone other than the player notices the illegal decklist after the game starts, it's a game loss

The specific penalty may be at the head judge's discretion

question: Can a player use cards entirely in a foreign language (e.g., Chinese cards in Europe) at Riftbound tournaments, and can tournament organizers prevent certain languages from being played?
answer:
Ruling: Official printed cards from any language are legal for Riftbound organized play, but all cards in your deck must be of the same language to prevent identifying specific cards by feel. Based on this rule, a European player can play a deck entirely in Chinese in Europe.

Nuances:

Players are advised to have an easy way ready to provide card translations to opponents

The quoted language rule appears in official game communication but is not yet included in the Tournament Rules document itself

Whether tournament organizers can prevent specific languages from being played remains unanswered in this thread

question: If Fiora gains Deflect after an opponent has already targeted her with a spell (by increasing her might in reaction), does the opponent need to recycle a card for Deflect?
answer:
Ruling: No, the opponent does not need to recycle a card. Once a spell is finalized (costs paid and targets chosen), gaining Deflect afterward does not trigger the Deflect cost requirement.

Sequence:

Opponent plays spell targeting Fiora (who does not have Deflect yet)

Opponent pays costs and chooses targets (spell is finalized)

Player reacts by increasing Fiora's might, giving her Deflect

Spell resolves without requiring the Deflect cost

Nuances:

It doesn't matter if Fiora gains Deflect before the spell resolves; what matters is whether she had Deflect when the spell was finalized (when costs were paid and targets were chosen)

question: Can you change your chosen champion after legends are revealed during setup, and do both players mulligan at the same time or in turn order?
answer:
Ruling: You reveal legend and chosen champion at the same time, so you cannot change your chosen champion after legends are revealed. Mulligan is done in turn order, not simultaneously.

Sequence:

Reveal legend and chosen champion simultaneously

Players mulligan in turn order (one after another)

Nuances:

In tournament play, every game 1 of a match must use the same chosen champion

question: How do chains resolve in Riftbound?
answer:
Ruling: Chains resolve last-in, first-out (LIFO), meaning the most recently added effect resolves first.

Sequence:

Player plays an ability or effect

Opponent responds with their own ability or effect (added to the chain)

The most recent effect (opponent's response) resolves first

Then the original effect resolves

Nuances:

This is similar to a "stack" system in other card games

Players can continue adding to the chain before anything resolves

Once both players pass priority, the chain begins resolving from top to bottom

question: Can you play a unit directly to a battlefield you don't control, or does it need to go to base first?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot play units directly to a battlefield unless you already have control of it. Units must be played to your base first if you don't control the target battlefield.

Sequence:

To play a unit directly to a battlefield, you must already have control of that battlefield

Control requires having units present at that battlefield

If you don't control a battlefield, units must go to base first

Nuances:

If you gank away from a battlefield you previously controlled, you lose control and cannot play units there anymore

Some units may have text that allows them to be played to battlefields you don't control

question: When Icathian Rain creates 6 reflexive triggers against two units (3 might and 4 might) and the opponent has Zhonya's Hourglass hidden, can the remaining triggers still kill a unit that was moved to base by Zhonya's, and when should Zhonya's be activated?
answer:
Ruling: All targets for Icathian Rain's 6 reflexive triggers must be chosen when the triggers are added to the chain, before any resolve. Zhonya's Hourglass should be activated right before the trigger that would deal lethal damage to the unit you want to save. In the scenario with a 3 might and 4 might unit, the defender can always save one unit but not both - if the attacker targets the 4 might unit with 4 triggers, that leaves only 2 triggers for the 3 might unit (which the defender can save), and vice versa.

Sequence:

Icathian Rain is played (reaction window)

Icathian Rain resolves, creating 6 reflexive triggers

Attacker chooses targets for all 6 triggers

Reaction window occurs after all targets are chosen but before any triggers resolve

Each trigger resolves one at a time with a reaction window after each

Zhonya's Hourglass should optimally be revealed right before the trigger that would kill the targeted unit

Nuances:

Once targets are chosen, the defender knows which unit can be saved and which cannot based on how many triggers targeted each unit

Zhonya's must be activated before lethal damage is dealt (as a replacement effect)

After a unit is moved to base by Zhonya's, remaining triggers targeting it still resolve and can kill it again in the base

There is a reaction window after all 6 targets are selected but before any damage is dealt, in addition to windows after each individual trigger

question: When using Ride the Wind to move a unit with Assault into a showdown, does that unit count as an attacker or defender?
answer:
Ruling: The unit moved into combat via Ride the Wind takes the same attacker/defender status as the player who controls it. If you are the defender in the showdown, any unit you bring into combat (including via Ride the Wind) will be a defender, not an attacker, and will not trigger Assault.

Sequence:

Determine who initiated the showdown by moving to the opponent's battlefield

The initiating player is the attacker; the other player is the defender

Any units brought into the combat by either player inherit their controller's attacker/defender status

Nuances:

If your opponent uses Charm to move your unit to a battlefield they control, you become the attacker in that showdown

The attacker/defender status is determined by who controls the battlefield being contested and who initiated the showdown, not by which units move where

question: When a unit with a 'When you play me' effect dies in response to its triggered ability, does the effect still resolve?
answer:
Ruling: When you play a unit, it enters immediately and its triggered ability goes on the chain. If the unit dies in response, the triggered ability still resolves, but effects that reference the unit's location (like 'here') will fail to do anything because the unit is no longer present.

Sequence:

Play the unit (it finalizes immediately and enters)

The 'When you play me' triggered ability goes on the chain

Opponent can respond (e.g., by killing the unit)

Response resolves first

Original triggered ability resolves (but may whiff if it references the unit's location)

Nuances:

Effects like 'draw 1' will still resolve even if the unit dies

Effects that reference 'here' (the unit's location) will fail to do anything if the unit has died

Units and gear finalize immediately and do not cause a priority pass

Triggered abilities are identified by 'when' followed by a condition, 'at' followed by a time, or 'the [n]'th time you...'

question: If you play Retreat after an opponent targets your unit with Hidden Blade, does the Hidden Blade controller still draw 2 cards?
answer:
Ruling: No, the Hidden Blade controller does not draw 2 cards. When Hidden Blade resolves without a valid target, it cannot determine "its controller" to give them the draw.

Sequence:

Hidden Blade is played targeting a unit

Retreat is played in response, returning the unit to hand

Retreat resolves first, removing the unit from the battlefield

Hidden Blade attempts to resolve but has no valid target

Since there is no valid target, "its controller" cannot be determined

No cards are drawn

Nuances:

If the unit is moved to base (instead of hand) before Hidden Blade resolves, it also becomes an invalid target and no draw occurs

If the unit's death is replaced (like with Zhonya's) but it stays at the battlefield, it remains a valid target and the controller still draws 2

The key distinction is whether Hidden Blade has a valid target at resolution - it needs to be able to reference "its controller" which requires a valid target

Moving a unit with Flash has the same effect as Retreat - no valid target means no draw

Targeting in Riftbound is implicit and doesn't require the word "target" to appear on the card

question: Do cards that move units without specifically saying 'move' count as movement for effects that trigger on movement?
answer:
Ruling: Cards must explicitly say "move" to count as movement. Effects that use different wording like "recall" do not count as moves.

Nuances:

Tideturner does say "move" so it counts as movement

Zhonya's says "recall" and its reminder text explicitly states "This isn't a move"

question: Can multiple showdowns happen simultaneously when Ride the Wind causes a unit to move to another occupied battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: No, multiple showdowns cannot happen at once. They stage and resolve one at a time sequentially.

Sequence:

First showdown stages and resolves

Then the next showdown begins

Nuances:

The person who applies contested (moves to the battlefield first) gets focus first

If there is a defender present, the person applying contested is the attacker

If there is no defender, you are not an attacker but still get focus first as the person applying contested

question: Can you Gust a unit at a Battlefield that is being killed by Baited Hook to prevent the opponent from getting a new unit?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, if the unit is a valid Gust target, you can Gust it in response to the Hook trigger on the chain. The Hook will still resolve, but since the target left the field, it will not successfully kill anything and the opponent will not be able to play a new unit.

Sequence:

Baited Hook's trigger is placed on the chain (after paying costs including exhaust, 1 energy, 1 order power)

The target unit is chosen as the ability is placed on the chain

You can React with Gust on that chain

If Gust removes the target, Hook still resolves but fails to kill the target

No new unit can be played from the revealed cards

Nuances:

Under current rules, Hook resolving with no valid target would produce a might value of 0, allowing a unit with 1 or less might to be played (though this is rare)

After an upcoming Comprehensive Rules update, failing to resolve a target will produce "null" (no valid value), meaning no unit could be played at all

You cannot choose a new target if the original target is removed, as targeting happens when placing the ability on the chain, not upon resolution

The costs of Baited Hook must still be paid when activated, regardless of whether the target is later removed

question: If a unit has Deflect, do cards like Falling Star (which deal multiple instances of damage) need to return multiple runes, or just one?
answer:
Ruling: Cards like Falling Star target for each instance of damage. If a unit has Deflect 1 and gets targeted twice, you would have to pay 2 power (one for each instance).

Sequence:

Each instance of damage from the spell counts as a separate target

Deflect triggers for each time the unit is targeted

The caster must pay the Deflect cost for each instance

question: Can you react to Traveling Merchant's move trigger with Hidden Blade at reaction speed and kill him? Does he count as being at a battlefield when his move trigger goes on the stack?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can use Hidden Blade at reaction speed to kill Traveling Merchant when his move trigger goes on the stack, but only if the Hidden Blade was already hidden at that battlefield. However, killing him will not deny his discard/draw triggered ability.

Sequence:

Traveling Merchant's triggered ability is added onto the chain

You can then react to it with Hidden Blade (if it was hidden at that battlefield)

Even if you kill Traveling Merchant, his triggered ability still resolves

Nuances:

The showdown has not begun yet when the trigger happens, but Traveling Merchant is considered to be at the battlefield for targeting purposes

The triggered ability on the chain is not contingent on Traveling Merchant being alive, so it resolves even if he is killed or bounced

question: Can you use the Equip ability on an Equipment that is already attached?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot use the Equip ability on an Equipment that is already attached.

Nuances:

Effects that allow you to attach already attached gear will specify that explicitly, like Jax Legend or Weaponmaster

question: When Garen Commander (who gives other units +1 might at his location) moves to a battlefield, and the defender plays a reaction spell that does 1 damage to a unit with 1 might, does that unit die or survive with 1 HP?
answer:
Ruling: The unit survives with 1 HP. Garen's passive ability is always on and applies immediately when he arrives at the new location, giving the +1 might bonus before any reactions resolve.

Sequence:

Garen moves to the battlefield (movement doesn't go on the chain)

Garen's passive ability immediately applies at the new location, giving friendly units +1 might

Attacking player passes on reactions

Defending player plays reaction spell dealing 1 damage

The unit has 2 might total (1 base + 1 from Garen), takes 1 damage, survives at 1 HP

Nuances:

Passive abilities (worded as statements of fact) are always on and don't go on the chain, so they can't be reacted to

Triggered abilities (worded "When X, do Y") and activated abilities (worded "Cost: Effect") do go on the chain and can be reacted to

Movement itself doesn't go on the chain, so you can't react to the movement before passive abilities apply

If the ability were worded "When I move here, other units have +1 might" (triggered ability), it would go on the chain and could be reacted to, resolving differently

question: When conquering The Candlelit Sanctum with Kai'Sa Survivor, which effect resolves first?
answer:
Ruling: When both effects trigger on conquer at the same time and both belong to you, you can choose the order in which they resolve.

Sequence:

Both effects trigger simultaneously on conquer

Since you control both triggers, you choose which resolves first

Resolve the second trigger

question: If Ravenbloom Student is at 3 might and an opponent targets it with Hextech Ray (dealing 3 damage), can the controller activate a spell in response to trigger Ravenbloom Student's ability and gain +1 might before Hextech Ray resolves and kills it?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Ravenbloom Student triggers and gains +1 might before Hextech Ray resolves, allowing it to survive at 4 might when the 3 damage is dealt.

Sequence:

Hextech Ray is activated targeting Ravenbloom Student

Player A activates a spell in response (e.g., Consult the Past)

The spell resolves

Ravenbloom Student's "play a spell" trigger goes on the chain

Ravenbloom trigger resolves, granting +1 might

Hextech Ray resolves, dealing 3 damage to the now 4-might Student

question: Can you react to a Deathknell trigger with a hidden Zhonya's Hourglass to prevent losing control of it when the unit dies?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can react to a Deathknell trigger with a hidden Zhonya's Hourglass. Because control does not change until after combat cleanup and all subsequent cleanups, you can resolve a chain from that Deathknell before you lose control of the battlefield.

Sequence:

Unit dies and Deathknell triggers

Priority passes to you while Deathknell is in the chain

You can play the hidden Zhonya's (which has Reaction when hidden) before control changes

Control change only happens after all cleanup resolves

Nuances:

This only works if something triggers to start a chain (like Deathknell). Without a trigger, no priority passes between combat damage and control change.

Hidden cards are not units until played - they're like cards in your hand

During a showdown, control cannot change until the showdown is over, so you maintain access to hidden cards

This ruling was under debate and expected to be clarified in version 1.2

question: Can Tryndamere's ability get you the 8th point to win the game?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Tryndamere's ability can get you the 8th point. Only conquering has the restriction that you need to have scored from all other battlefields that turn for it to give you the final point.

Nuances:

You can hold one battlefield and conquer the other to win

You cannot conquer a battlefield you held that same turn

You don't need to control the first battlefield anymore at the time you conquer the second

You just need to have scored from the other battlefield that turn, either from holding or conquering

The final point can be gained by holding a single battlefield; you do not need to hold both

question: Are players required to verbally declare when they score points, and should a player be allowed to take back a pass action if they were mistaken about the opponent's point total?
answer:
Ruling: Players must verbally announce when they score points as it is a change to public information. A player cannot take back a pass action once made, even if they were mistaken about the game state. However, obfuscating public information (like hiding a point tracker behind a deck box and not announcing point changes) is a violation of tournament rules.

Sequence:

Players must announce point changes whenever they hold/conquer a battlefield

Players must answer truthfully when asked how many points they have

Players should track points with pen and paper for accuracy

Once a player passes, they cannot take back that decision

Nuances:

Writing down points without verbally declaring them when scoring is not sufficient

Hiding point trackers behind deck boxes while not announcing changes is unsportsmanlike and violates tournament rules about obfuscating public information

If a player lies about or conceals point totals, they are presenting a dishonest board state

question: Does a unit heal after using Challenge, or does it remain damaged if sent into a battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Units do not heal after using Challenge. They remain damaged until they heal after combat or at the end of turn.

Nuances:

Challenge is not combat, so it does not trigger healing that occurs after combat

Units heal only after combat and at the end of turn

question: When Stacked Deck reveals Nocturne, does triggering Nocturne's automatic play count as the card you take from Stacked Deck, or do you get to take another card?
answer:
Ruling: Nocturne cannot be both the card you choose from Stacked Deck and the card that is banished for his automatic play effect. You must choose one of the other two cards revealed by Stacked Deck, then banish and play Nocturne separately.

Sequence:

Stacked Deck reveals three cards including Nocturne

Choose one of the other two cards (not Nocturne) to take

Banish and play Nocturne due to his automatic play effect

The remaining card goes to the bottom of the deck

question: What defines whether or not an ability is optional or mandatory?
answer:
Ruling: Triggered abilities always go on the chain when their trigger condition is met. Whether the effect itself is optional or mandatory is determined by the word "may" - if "may" is present, the effect is optional; otherwise it is mandatory by default.

Sequence:

When a trigger condition is met (often starts with "When" or "At"), the triggered ability must be put on the chain

The controller of the last item in the chain gets priority first

Upon resolution, if the effect contains "may", you can choose whether to perform the action; if not, the effect is mandatory

Nuances:

You don't "activate" triggered abilities - triggered abilities are triggered, while activate abilities are activated

The distinction between putting an ability on the chain (mandatory for triggered abilities) and resolving its effect (which may be optional with "may") is important

question: When is the last moment to exhaust Ekko's runes before his Deathknell refreshes them?
answer:
Ruling: You can exhaust runes as a Reaction to Ekko's Deathknell trigger on the chain.

Sequence:

Ekko dies

Ekko's Deathknell trigger goes on the chain

Before the Deathknell resolves, you can exhaust runes as a Reaction

Deathknell resolves and refreshes the runes

question: What happens when Hidden Blade is chained with Gust or Flash in different orders?
answer:
Ruling: When Hidden Blade's target becomes illegal before it resolves (due to being returned to hand by Gust or moved to base by Flash), Hidden Blade resolves with no effect and no one draws cards. When Hidden Blade resolves first (Chain 2), it kills the unit and the controller draws 2 cards, then the Chain 1 spell (Gust or Flash) resolves with no effect since its target is gone.

Sequence:

Hidden Blade Chain 1, Gust Chain 2: Gust resolves first returning unit to hand, then Hidden Blade resolves with no effect (no draw)

Hidden Blade Chain 1, Flash Chain 2: Flash resolves first moving unit to base, then Hidden Blade resolves with no effect (no draw)

Gust Chain 1, Hidden Blade Chain 2: Hidden Blade resolves first killing unit and controller draws 2, then Gust resolves with no effect

Flash Chain 1, Hidden Blade Chain 2: Hidden Blade resolves first killing unit and controller draws 2, then Flash resolves with no effect

Nuances:

When a spell resolves without a legal target, resources are still spent and the spell is discarded

A unit must be a legal target when the spell is cast, but may become illegal before resolution

Cards do as much as they can even if some parts aren't possible (e.g., Flash targeting two units would still move the other unit)

question: Can a hidden Zhonya's Hourglass be played from one battlefield to affect a unit at a different battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Zhonya's Hourglass can be played while hidden at one battlefield and affect units at another battlefield. When a gear is played hidden at a battlefield, it is placed in your base instead, and Zhonya's effect is global.

Sequence:

When you play a gear that is hidden at a battlefield, it is placed in your base

Gears cannot stay at a battlefield on their own

The gear's effect then applies according to its normal rules

Nuances:

Hidden cards that make choices must select/choose from the battlefield they're hidden at (like Foxfire)

Zhonya's Hourglass doesn't require choosing, so it works globally regardless of where it's played from

This follows the same logic as playing it as a normal gear - you wouldn't get a choice of battlefield in either case

question: Can you decline to pay Deflect costs for reflexive triggered abilities like Icathian Rain, and how does this work with targeting multiple units?
answer:
Ruling: You can decline to pay Deflect costs for triggered abilities (including reflexive ones like Icathian Rain), which causes those specific triggers to fail to finalize and be removed from the chain. You choose targets for each trigger individually and can decline payment for any that target enemy units with Deflect.

Sequence:

Cast the spell (e.g., Icathian Rain)

Players can react

Spell resolves, creating reflexive triggers

Pick target for each trigger individually

For each trigger targeting an enemy unit with Deflect, you may decline to pay the cost (trigger fails to finalize)

Players can react after all triggers are placed

Triggers resolve in reverse order

Nuances:

Deflect costs only apply to spells/abilities controlled by opponents, so friendly units with Deflect don't increase costs

For reflexive triggers (like Icathian Rain), units can gain Deflect after the spell is cast but before triggers target, and Deflect will apply

For non-reflexive spells that target (like Singularity), targets are locked in when the spell finalizes to the chain; if a unit gains Deflect afterward, it's too late to apply

You can target a unit with Deflect even if other non-Deflect targets are available, and still decline to pay the cost

If a trigger's target becomes illegal (e.g., through Retreat), you don't get to reassign it; the trigger does nothing and you lose that trigger

question: If Stand United is hidden on battlefield A, can I react to an attack on battlefield B by playing it to buff a unit on A, and will the +1 to all buffs effect also apply to units on battlefield B?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can react with Stand United from battlefield A when battlefield B is attacked. The direct buff targets a unit on battlefield A (where it was played from), but the +1 to all buffs effect applies board-wide to all battlefields.

Sequence:

Stand United is played from the facedown zone at battlefield A

The "buff a friendly unit" effect becomes "buff a friendly unit here" (at battlefield A only)

The "+1 to all buffs to friendly units this turn" effect applies globally across all battlefields

Nuances:

When played from the facedown zone, the direct buff is restricted to the battlefield where Stand United was hidden

The secondary effect that increases all buffs is not restricted by location and affects all friendly units regardless of which battlefield they're on

question: Does a unit played with Gentleman's Duel get healed after the card resolves?
answer:
Ruling: No, units are not healed after Gentleman's Duel resolves. Units are only healed after combat finishes and at the end of turn.

Nuances:

Combat specifically refers to when two players are at the same battlefield and do a showdown, not just units damaging each other

question: If the only enemy unit has deflect, must I choose it as a target when I play Blitzcrank at a battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you must target the enemy unit with deflect when playing Blitzcrank, even if it's the only enemy unit. However, you can decline to actually move the unit when the effect resolves.

Sequence:

When playing Blitzcrank, you must select a valid target (the enemy unit with deflect)

This triggers deflect's power cost requirement

On resolution, you may choose not to move the unit (declining the "may" effect)

You will not get back the resources spent on deflect's cost

Nuances:

The "may" in the effect text refers to the optional nature of the move on resolution, not the targeting requirement

You must have valid targets to play the card, but can decline the optional effect when it resolves

question: If I hold a battlefield at the start of turn and score the holding point, then move my units off and back onto it, does it trigger an Open showdown?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, moving units back onto a battlefield you previously held triggers an Open showdown, but you will not score another holding point.

Nuances:

You only score the holding point once (at the start of turn when you initially held it)

The showdown still occurs when you move units back onto the battlefield

question: Can you conquer a battlefield multiple times per turn to trigger 'on conquer' effects multiple times?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot conquer the same battlefield multiple times per turn. You can only conquer a battlefield that you have not yet scored this turn.

Nuances:

Conquering is defined as gaining control of a battlefield you did not yet score this turn

You can only score once per turn, which limits conquering to once per battlefield per turn

Even if you return your unit to base and move another ready unit to the same battlefield, it does not count as conquering again

question: If my unit is killed during a showdown after I pass focus, can I still play actions since focus returns to me, or does the showdown end immediately?
answer:
Ruling: Both players must pass focus consecutively without playing anything for combat to resolve and end. After a chain resolves, focus automatically passes back to you, allowing you to play actions even if your unit was killed.

Sequence:

Player passes focus

Opponent plays a reaction (like Void Seeker) instead of passing

The chain resolves

Focus automatically returns to the player who passed first

That player can now play actions again

Combat only ends when both players pass focus consecutively

Nuances:

This works the same whether you are attacking or defending

Even if your unit is killed and you are no longer contesting the battlefield, combat does not end until both players pass focus

question: Can I cast Gust on an opponent's Sneaky Deckhand as it enters a battlefield I control on their turn?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can cast Gust on the Sneaky Deckhand. When a unit exists at a battlefield its player doesn't control, it will always initiate a Showdown, which gives you an opportunity to cast Gust after any Actions your opponent may make before giving Focus to you.

Sequence:

Opponent's unit enters the battlefield you control

A Showdown is initiated

Opponent may take Actions

Focus passes to you

You can cast Gust on the unit

question: Does a unit get exhausted when it swaps places with another unit via Tideturner's ability?
answer:
Ruling: No, the unit does not get exhausted when swapping places via Tideturner's ability.

Nuances:

Only the standard move action exhausts units as a cost

Other move effects must explicitly state they exhaust a unit in order to do so

question: Can a hidden unit be played/flipped if its ability has no valid target, or does it become unplayable?
answer:
Ruling: Hidden units can still be flipped and played even if their abilities have no valid target. The unit enters play, but the ability simply does not resolve.

Nuances:

If a unit's ability requires targeting and no valid target exists, the ability does not happen but the unit still enters play

Units with abilities that can target themselves (like Blastcone Fae) must do so if they are the only valid target

Blue Teemo has a special case under review: it's unclear whether you can reveal the top 5 cards without having a target for the damage portion of the ability

question: Can you tap all or more runes than needed at the start of your turn to make it harder for your opponent to track your energy?
answer:
Ruling: No, this is not allowed. Rune Pools and resources in them are public information that must be tracked clearly and stated truthfully when asked.

Nuances:

Players don't have to track rune pool information visually, but if they track it non-visually (like on a note sheet) to deceive another player or avoid clear tracking, they will receive significant judge scrutiny

This behavior could result in an angle shooting error or be found as cheating

If an opponent asks about rune pool state, you must state the public information truthfully

If a player believes their opponent is not being accurate, they can call a judge

question: Can a judge (officially assigned as one) for a Summoner Skirmish also play in the event?
answer:
Ruling: No, a judge cannot play in a Summoner Skirmish. Judges can only play in Nexus Nights and Prereleases, which are Casual OPL events.

Nuances:

TR 303 states that if a competition official participates in an event, it must be run at Casual OPL, which is a prerequisite condition, not permission to downgrade an event

Summoner Skirmish is set at Competitive OPL and cannot be downgraded to Casual OPL

If a Summoner Skirmish were downgraded to Casual OPL, it would no longer qualify as a Summoner Skirmish and would lose its associated prizing (like the round one bye at regionals)

Competitive OPL requires deck checks and decklists, which a playing judge would not have time to properly administer

question: If my legend is Viktor, can I use cards of colors other than blue and yellow (e.g., a purple spell without a recycle cost)?
answer:
Ruling: When Viktor is your legend, you are restricted to only blue and yellow cards. You cannot use cards of other colors, even if they don't have a recycle cost.

Nuances:

You can build a deck using only blue cards with no power costs and run 12 yellow runes as a valid deck construction strategy.

question: If Riptide Rex's target moves to base, dies, or returns to hand during reaction, does it still deal 6 damage or can you choose a new target?
answer:
Ruling: Riptide Rex will deal 0 damage if the target is no longer at a battlefield when the effect resolves. You cannot choose a new target.

Sequence:

Targets are declared when the effect is added to the chain

Target legality is checked again when the effect resolves

If the target is not at a battlefield upon resolution, the effect deals 0 damage

Nuances:

Targets cannot change once declared

This applies whether the unit moved to base, died, or returned to hand during reaction

question: If you target Pouty Poro with Icathian Rain 6 times, can you recycle 1 and have Deflect negate the other ones?
answer:
Ruling: You pick targets for all 6 triggers simultaneously and decide which Deflect costs to pay before they go on the stack. You can choose to pay for only 1 Deflect and decline to pay for the other 5.

Sequence:

All 6 Icathian Rain triggers target at the same time

You decide which Deflect costs to pay (can choose to pay for 1 and not the others)

Only the ones you pay for go on the stack

The ones you don't pay for never go on the stack

This decision is made before your opponent can react

Nuances:

You must make all payment decisions before seeing what your opponent will do in response

question: How does equipment work in terms of timing and readiness - when can you equip it after playing it, does it enter exhausted, and what happens when the equipped unit dies?
answer:
Ruling: Equipment always enters the base ready, allowing you to immediately pay the equip cost to attach it to a unit. When the equipped unit dies, the equipment returns to your base ready, so you can pay the equip cost again to re-equip it.

Sequence:

Play the equipment card by paying its play cost

Equipment enters your base ready

Pay the equip cost to attach it to a unit (can be done immediately)

If the unit dies, equipment returns to base ready

Pay the equip cost again to re-equip to another unit

Nuances:

Currently, no gear has an exhaust symbol as part of its equip cost

question: Does Leona Determined's ability to stun an enemy unit count as choosing/targeting for the purpose of triggering Deflect?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Leona Determined's ability to stun an enemy unit does choose/target for the purpose of Deflect. Charm also triggers Deflect.

Nuances:

The rule that uses 'Kill a unit' as an example for targeting applies to similar effects like 'stun an enemy unit'

question: If you score a battlefield by conquering with a champion unit (Kaisa/Qiyana), then move that unit out and back to the same battlefield in the same turn, can you re-trigger the conquer abilities?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot score a battlefield more than once per turn. Since conquering is a form of scoring, you cannot conquer the same battlefield again in the same turn even if you move the unit out and back.

Nuances:

If your score has its point replaced (e.g., drawing 1 if you can't win the final point), any conquer effects will still trigger in those replacement cases.

question: For Candle Lit Sanctum, do you have to scry (vision) one card to the bottom or can both cards be put on top?
answer:
Ruling: Candle Lit Sanctum functions as scry 2, allowing you to leave both cards on top if desired.

Nuances:

You are not required to put any cards to the bottom

question: Can you use Salvage to kill a Hidden Zhonya after it's revealed but before it can trigger to save a unit in battle?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can start a chain with Salvage to kill the Zhonya after it is revealed but before it can trigger to save the unit.

Sequence:

Opponent reveals Hidden Zhonya, which goes to their base

You can now start a chain with Salvage

Salvage kills the Zhonya before it can trigger to save the unit

question: Can you equip equipment to another unit on the same turn that the previously equipped unit dies?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can equip equipment to another unit on the same turn that the previously equipped unit dies, following Base Speed timing.

Sequence:

Wait until it is your turn

Ensure the Chain is empty

Ensure there is no Showdown

Then equip the equipment to another unit

Nuances:

Base Speed timing means you can only use it when it is your turn, the Chain is empty, and there is no Showdown

question: If Soraka dies at a battlefield with other units, does she save the other units since she is a replacement effect and not a trigger?
answer:
Ruling: No, if Soraka and a friendly unit die simultaneously at a battlefield, you cannot save the friendly unit with Soraka's ability. Additionally, even if you save Soraka with a Zhonya's Hourglass (preventing her death), you still cannot save the other unit with Soraka's ability.

Nuances:

The ruling applies specifically when units die at a battlefield

Using Zhonya's Hourglass to save Soraka does not change the outcome - she still cannot save other units dying simultaneously

The comprehensive rules were not clear in either direction on this interaction at the time of discussion

There is debate about whether Soraka could save units if both Soraka and the other units were in base (rather than at a battlefield) when dying simultaneously, but this scenario is not definitively answered

This ruling comes from a Chinese FAQ document and may receive an English equivalent

question: If you deal damage to a unit with Voidseeker, then play Thousand Tail Watcher to reduce its Might, does the unit die if the damage now equals or exceeds its reduced Might?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, the unit dies. Damage does not reduce Might, so when Thousand Tail Watcher is played, the unit still has its original Might before being reduced. After the Might reduction, a cleanup is performed which checks if damage is greater than or equal to current Might, causing the unit to die.

Sequence:

Deal 4 damage to a 5 Might unit with Voidseeker (unit has 5 Might, 4 damage)

Play Thousand Tail Watcher to reduce Might by 3 (unit now has 2 Might, 4 damage)

Cleanup is performed after the status change

Damage (4) >= current Might (2), so the unit dies

Nuances:

Damage does not reduce Might; they are tracked separately

Cleanup checks occur after status changes

question: When Promising Future banishes units with 'when you play me' triggers, at what point do those triggers enter the chain and in what order do they resolve relative to other cards banished by Promising Future?
answer:
Ruling: When units with 'when you play me' triggers are played via Promising Future, their triggers enter the chain as pending items immediately after each unit resolves. These triggers are then finalized after all other Promising Future cards are finalized, and they resolve before the other Promising Future cards.

Sequence:

Promising Future fully resolves

Players finalize their banished cards in order (A, B, C, D)

When a unit with a trigger is finalized, it resolves immediately and its trigger enters the chain as pending

After all Promising Future cards are finalized, the unit triggers are finalized

The unit triggers resolve first (in reverse order of when they were added), then the remaining Promising Future cards resolve

Nuances:

The player who played Promising Future finalizes their card last, not first

Unit triggers enter the chain pending when the unit resolves, not when it's finalized

In the example, final chain order from top to bottom is: Pit Rookie trigger (full), Riptide Rex trigger (full), Meditation (full), Charm (full)

question: Can Volibear's legend ability trigger multiple times per turn to generate multiple runes when playing multiple Mighty units?
answer:
Ruling: Volibear's legend ability triggers and creates a chain each time you play a Mighty unit, but you can only generate one rune per turn because the ability requires you to exhaust Volibear to channel and get the rune. Once exhausted, you cannot use the ability again that turn unless you untap Volibear through another method.

Sequence:

Play a Mighty unit

Volibear's legend ability triggers and creates a chain

You may exhaust Volibear to channel and gain a rune

If you play another Mighty unit that turn, the ability triggers again and creates another chain, but you cannot exhaust Volibear again to gain another rune (he's already exhausted)

Nuances:

The ability still creates multiple chains when multiple Mighty units are played, even though you can only get one rune

Even effects that play multiple units do so sequentially, not simultaneously

You could potentially get multiple runes in one turn if you have a way to untap Volibear between playing Mighty units

question: Does a reflexive trigger count as a spell or ability for Deflect?
answer:
Ruling: Reflexive triggers are a type of triggered ability, so they count as abilities for Deflect and you will have to pay.

Nuances:

Reflexive triggers are not spells, so they would not count toward spell-counting effects like Ravenbloom

question: If you play Death Rocket and are at 7 points, can you still get the rocket back when you conquer a battlefield without winning, and does the draw from conquering happen before discarding for the rocket?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you still get the rocket back because you conquered even though you didn't gain a point. When at 7 points with no cards in hand, you can conquer, draw a card from the conquer effect, then discard that card to return Death Rocket to hand.

Sequence:

Conquer the battlefield

Draw a card (replacement for gaining the point)

Discard a card to return Death Rocket to hand

Nuances:

The draw effect is a replacement for gaining the point, not a replacement for conquering itself

Conquering still occurs even when at 7 points; you just don't gain the point

question: Does a Skirmish tournament require a top 8 cut?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Skirmish tournaments require a top placement cut after Swiss rounds.

Nuances:

The tournament system (Carde.io) enforces this requirement and will not allow a Summoner Skirmish to be created without a top 8 cut

There are no specific rules dictating when exactly to cut, but a top placement cut must occur after Swiss rounds

question: When does floating energy empty from a player's pool?
answer:
Ruling: Each player's pool empties at the end of each turn and after the draw phase.

Nuances:

Energy can be floated throughout a turn, allowing players to recycle runes and hold up resources until they decide to play something

The draw phase emptying prevents certain shenanigans

question: Does Cull the Weak work even when you don't have a unit to kill?
answer: Ruling: Yes, Cull the Weak works even when you don't have a unit to sacrifice. If a player has no units, they simply ignore the instruction to sacrifice a unit.

question: Do you have to play Deflect when using Unchecked Power?
answer: Ruling: No, you do not have to play Deflect when using Unchecked Power because Unchecked Power does not target any of their units.

question: When a unit moves to a battlefield during an ongoing showdown (after the initial unit that started the showdown moved there), who is the attacker and who is the defender?
answer:
Ruling: When a unit moves to a battlefield where a showdown is already in progress (the battlefield is already contested), the newly arriving unit becomes the defender, not the attacker. The unit that originally moved to the occupied battlefield and applied the "contested" status is the attacker.

Nuances:

This is different from moving to a battlefield after a showdown has already ended and the battlefield is conquered - in that case, the newly arriving unit would be the attacker

This interaction is important for units with "when I attack" effects like Leona, as those effects would not trigger if the unit is moved in as a defender during an ongoing showdown

question: If an opponent targets my 4 might Fiora with Foxfire, and I respond by playing Discipline to increase her might to 6 (giving her Deflect), does Foxfire have to recycle when it resolves due to the new Deflect?
answer:
Ruling: No, Foxfire does not have to recycle. Paying costs and choosing a target happens when the card is played, so Deflect gained after targeting is irrelevant.

Sequence:

Opponent plays Foxfire and targets Fiora (4 might, no Deflect)

You respond with Discipline, increasing Fiora to 6 might (gaining Deflect)

Foxfire resolves and affects Fiora normally because the target was already chosen

question: When Baited Hook says 'ignore costs', does that include the power cost in the top left corner? If hooking into Watcher, do you still have to pay the 1 energy and power, plus the optional accelerate cost?
answer:
Ruling: When Baited Hook says "ignore costs", it refers only to the Energy and Power costs printed in the top left corner of the card - those costs are ignored. Additional costs like Accelerate (optional) or Cruel Patron's sacrifice requirement (mandatory) must still be paid if you choose to pay them or are required to pay them.

Sequence:

Baited Hook allows you to play the card ignoring its top-left Energy and Power costs

Optional additional costs (like Accelerate) can be chosen to be paid or not

Required additional costs (like Cruel Patron's sacrifice) must be paid if you play the card

Baited Hook is a "may" ability, so you can choose not to play the card at all

Nuances:

You are never forced to play anything off Baited Hook since it says "you may" - you can fail to find

The distinction between optional and required additional costs matters for what you must pay

question: If a spell targets a creature and that creature is killed in response before the spell resolves, does the spell still resolve and produce its other effects?
answer:
Ruling: The spell will resolve and do as much as it can. If the target becomes illegal while the spell is on the chain, effects that don't depend on the target still happen.

Sequence:

Player A plays Discipline targeting a creature

Player B kills the creature in response

Discipline resolves, cannot give +2 to the now-illegal target, but Player A still draws a card

Nuances:

Spells cannot be played if their targets cannot be selected when casting

Targets can become illegal while the spell is waiting to resolve on the chain

The spell never goes on the chain if it can't choose its targets initially

question: When multiple units die simultaneously in combat, which unit does Zhonya's Hourglass save, and what happens if you have multiple Zhonya's?
answer:
Ruling: When multiple units die simultaneously, the Zhonya's Hourglass controller chooses which unit to save. Zhonya's must already be face-up at that moment. If you have multiple Zhonya's, you still lose one Zhonya per death prevented.

Nuances:

All units marked with lethal damage die simultaneously during the resolution step after damage is assigned

Zhonya's is a mandatory effect that applies immediately without using the chain

You cannot choose not to activate Zhonya's if a unit would die

question: Can Guerilla Warfare be used in a showdown as a reaction if it doesn't specify action or reaction?
answer:
Ruling: If a spell or ability does not have the keyword "action" or "reaction," it can only be played/used during your turn. It cannot be used in showdowns or to react to other spells/abilities/units unless it has the keyword reaction.

Nuances:

The absence of action/reaction keywords means the card defaults to only being playable on your turn

Reaction keyword is specifically required to use cards in showdowns or in response to opponent actions

question: When Dazzling Aurora reveals Nocturne as the first unit, does Nocturne's alternative cost effect trigger immediately and allow Aurora to continue searching, or does Aurora's effect end after revealing Nocturne?
answer:
Ruling: Dazzling Aurora stops when it first reveals a unit. If Nocturne is the first unit revealed, Aurora's effect ends there and plays Nocturne normally. Nocturne's alternative cost effect does not trigger from being revealed.

Sequence:

Dazzling Aurora begins revealing cards from deck

When Nocturne (a unit) is revealed, Aurora's effect stops

Aurora plays the revealed Nocturne

Aurora's effect is complete

Nuances:

You are allowed to pay Nocturne's alternative cost instead of having Aurora play it for free, but Aurora's effect still ends after revealing the first unit regardless

If you pay the alternative cost, Aurora does not continue searching for another unit

question: When a unit is recalled after being stunned on a different battlefield, does it return to its original battlefield or to the base?
answer:
Ruling: Recall always sends units to the base, not to their previous battlefield location.

Nuances:

This clarification is present in the updated 1.1 version of the core rules, but was unclear in earlier versions

question: Does Cleave (Assault 3) stack when playing 2 copies, resulting in Assault 6?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Cleave (Assault 3) stacks when playing 2 copies, resulting in Assault 6. Assault is a stacking keyword where each new occurrence adds to previous ones.

Nuances:

Shield and Deflect also stack in the same way

Spirit's Refuge is an exception that doesn't stack Deflect

question: Can you swap your Chosen Champion between games in a match, as long as it matches your Champion Legend's tags?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot swap your Chosen Champion between games in a match. The Chosen Champion is part of the deck building process, similar to your Legend, and must remain the same throughout the match.

Nuances:

While the rules don't explicitly forbid swapping between games, developer guidance indicates the Chosen Champion is locked in during deck construction

The Chosen Champion must match your Champion Legend's tags during setup, but this doesn't allow for swapping between games

question: If Gemcraft Seer is in play, does a recruit token played via Viktor, Herald of Arcane's ability have Vision and trigger the scry effect?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, recruit tokens played while Gemcraft Seer is in play have Vision and cause you to scry the top card of your deck.

Nuances:

Tokens are not cards, but they are units

Tokens can have and trigger keywords like Vision when played

question: If I play Gust targeting my own Ravenbloom Student with 3 current Might, does Ravenbloom's ability trigger to increase its Might before Gust resolves?
answer:
Ruling: Gust resolves first and returns Ravenbloom to hand. Since Ravenbloom is no longer on the field, its effect does not activate.

Sequence:

Gust resolves

Ravenbloom returns to hand

Ravenbloom's effect does not trigger because it is no longer on the field

Nuances:

A card isn't considered played until it resolves

question: When casting Icathian Rain and choosing the same Deflect unit multiple times, can you decline to pay some of the Deflect costs, and when can opponents react?
answer:
Ruling: When Icathian Rain resolves, you choose all 6 targets and decide which Deflect costs to pay simultaneously. You can decline to pay Deflect for any triggered abilities, and only the triggers you paid for enter the chain. Opponents can then react to those triggers before they resolve.

Sequence:

Cast Icathian Rain

Window for reactions (if none, it resolves)

When it resolves, choose all 6 targets at once

Decide which Deflect costs to pay (you may decline any)

Only the triggers you paid for enter the chain

Players gain priority to react to those triggers

Each trigger resolves individually with reaction windows between them

Nuances:

This ability to decline Deflect costs only applies to triggered abilities (like Icathian Rain's reflexive triggers), not to casting spells directly

If there are other legal targets available, you cannot choose to hit nothing - you must select legal targets

No one can react in the middle of the targeting and paying costs process

This rule changed in a recent rules update; it did not work this way previously

question: When Fox-Fire is played from hidden, can it only target the battlefield it is on because it 'chooses'?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, when Fox-Fire is played from hidden, it can only target the battlefield it is on because it chooses a target.

Nuances:

The limitation applies to effects that choose, based on the FAQ

You don't need to see the word "choose" explicitly written on the card for it to be considered a choice

Choosing a game object is targeting rulewise, though some cards may say "choose" without issuing targeting

The FAQ is the most up-to-date source for this ruling

question: Does Hostile Takeover create a trigger at the end of turn when you lose control of the unit and recall it?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, it is a trigger that you can react to.

Nuances:

The wording may not follow standard delayed trigger formatting due to the card being designed early in development

question: When does Viktor - Innovator's ability trigger and resolve when casting a spell during an opponent's turn?
answer:
Ruling: "When you play" triggers occur after the spell resolves, and the trigger goes onto the chain as a triggered ability that allows responses before it resolves.

Sequence:

Cast the spell (e.g., Stupefy)

The spell resolves

Viktor's "when you play" trigger goes onto the chain

Players can respond to the trigger

When the trigger resolves, play the 1-might recruit token to your base

Nuances:

The trigger can occur mid-chain if the spell that triggered it resolves while other items are still on the chain

If the spell is countered, the "when you play" trigger never occurs because countered spells are not played

question: Can Janna be played to base at reaction speed, and will her ability work there?
answer:
Janna can be played to base at reaction speed (anywhere you could play a unit whenever you can play reactions), and her ability will trigger because of an errata.
