Partial Resolution: Under Rule 356.3.e.11, instructions that can be partially followed are followed as much as possible. Since you have no units, you simply ignore the instruction to kill one of your own units.

Opponent's Requirement: Your inability to kill a unit does not prevent the rest of the spell from resolving. Your opponent must still kill one of their units if they have any.

Sequence:

You play Cull the Weak (it does not require you to have a unit to be legally played).

The spell resolves.

You have no units to kill, so you do nothing for your part of the effect.

Your opponent must choose and kill one of their units.

question: Does First Mate's "When you play me, ready another unit" open up a chain to be reacted to?
answer:
Yes, First Mate's "When you play me" ability creates a chain that can be reacted to.

According to the rules and FAQs regarding "When you play me" triggered abilities:

Playing the Unit: When you play First Mate, the unit itself enters the battlefield immediately and does not use the chain (it cannot be reacted to).

Triggered Ability: The "When you play me" ability triggers immediately upon the unit entering play. This ability is added to the chain as a pending item.

Reaction Window: Because the ability is now on the chain, the game state becomes "Closed." This creates a window where players can play Reaction cards in response to the ability before it resolves.

Sequence:

You play First Mate.

First Mate enters the battlefield.

The "When you play me" ability is added to the chain.

Players receive priority to play Reaction cards.

Once all players pass, the ability resolves, and you must ready another unit (if a valid target exists, it must be chosen, even if it is an enemy unit).

question: If my opponent has Vex at a battlefield and I have a hidden card there, do I have to pay the additional cost to cast that spell?
answer:
Yes, you must pay the additional cost.

According to the official ruling for this interaction:

Hidden sets the base cost of the spell to 0.

Vex's ability acts as a cost increase, which is applied after the base cost is set to 0.

Therefore, you must pay the additional cost imposed by Vex to activate the spell from Hidden.

Sequence:

Hidden removes the base cost of the spell.

Additional costs (such as the cost increase from Vex) are added after.

You must pay these additional costs to activate the spell.

question: Does "not so fast" counter "Cull the Weak"?
answer:
No, Not So Fast cannot counter Cull the Weak.

According to the card text and official rulings, Cull the Weak does not "choose" or "target" a unit. The instruction to kill a unit is performed by each player during the resolution of the spell, rather than being a targeted choice made when the spell is played.

Because Not So Fast specifically requires the spell or ability to "choose a friendly unit or gear" in order to be played, it cannot be used against Cull the Weak.

question: What happens if I cast Invert Timelines while my opponent has 4 cards in hand and 0 cards in deck?
answer:
Ruling: Your opponent will Burn Out when attempting to draw 4 cards from an empty deck. They will recycle their Trash into their Main Deck, grant you 1 point, then complete drawing the required cards.

Sequence:

Both players discard their hands simultaneously

The active player (caster) draws first due to turn order

The non-active player then attempts to draw 4 cards

If the opponent's deck has fewer than 4 cards, they Burn Out: draw what they can, recycle Trash into Main Deck, grant the caster 1 point, then complete the draw

Nuances:

Running out of cards does not cause you to lose the game in Riftbound

If the opponent's Trash is also empty when recycling, their deck remains empty and they may Burn Out again on subsequent draws

The active player always resolves simultaneous effects first due to turn order

question: Can 'Not So Fast' counter the ability of 'Zaun Punk'?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can use 'Not So Fast' to counter the triggered ability of 'Zaun Punk' if your opponent chooses your gear as the target.

Nuances:

'Not So Fast' checks what target is actually chosen, not whether the card text explicitly says 'friendly'

If the opponent chooses your gear, it becomes an enemy ability choosing a friendly gear, which meets the criteria for 'Not So Fast'

The additional cost paid to trigger the ability (killing a friendly gear) cannot be countered and remains paid

If the opponent chooses their own gear, 'Not So Fast' cannot counter it since it would not be targeting a friendly gear

question: Does Kadregrin draw for itself?
answer:
Yes, Kadregrin can count itself.

According to the official FAQ:
Q: Can Kadregrin count itself?
A: Ruling: Yes, Kadregrin can count itself.

question: Is Renata legend ability active at 5 or 6 points?
answer:
In a standard game of Riftbound (which is played to 8 points), Chem-Baroness Renata's second ability becomes active when you have 5 points.

The ability states: "While your score is within 3 points of the Victory Score, your Gold [ADD] an additional [1]."

According to the official ruling for this interaction:

The threshold is calculated as: (Points needed to win) - 3.

In an 8-point game: $8 - 3 = 5$.

When counting "within 3 points," you do not count the starting number itself. From 5 points, you need 3 more points (6, 7, and 8) to reach the Victory Score.

Important Note: If a card like Aspirant's Climb is in play (which increases the Victory Score to 9), the threshold shifts to 6 points.

question: If you summon Akshan, Mischievous with Baited Hook, can you still pay his additional summon condition cost to activate his ability?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can still choose to pay Akshan, Mischievous's additional cost of [C][C] when playing him with Baited Hook, which will activate his ability to move an enemy gear to your base.

Sequence:

Activate Baited Hook and choose Akshan, Mischievous to play

Akshan's base Energy and Power costs are ignored

You have the option to pay Akshan's additional cost of [C][C]

If you pay the [C][C], Akshan's "When you play me, if you paid the additional cost" ability triggers and resolves

Nuances:

"Ignoring cost" effects only apply to base Energy and Power costs (printed in the top-left corner)

Additional costs (like Akshan's [C][C] or Accelerate costs) are separate from base costs and can still be paid even when base costs are ignored

The additional cost is optional - you can choose whether or not to pay it

question: Does Charme cast repeated with temporal Portal Start 2 Showdown 1 by 1 or in Showdown with both charmed units? What if I charm to two different battlefields I control?
answer:
When you use Temporal Portal to give Charm the Repeat keyword and move two units, the timing of the resulting Showdowns depends on where the units are moved.

1. Moving both units to the same Battlefield you control

If you move both units to the same Battlefield, they will participate in one single Showdown.

Reasoning: According to CR 443.1, a Showdown opens when a Battlefield becomes Contested. When the first Charm effect resolves, the Battlefield becomes Contested and a Showdown is "pending." However, the Chain containing the Repeated Charm must finish resolving all its effects before the game checks for state-based triggers like opening the Showdown.

Result: Both units arrive at the Battlefield. Once the spell finishes, the game sees multiple enemy units at your Battlefield and opens one Showdown. Both moved units will gain the Attacker designation (CR 443.1.a.3).

2. Moving units to two different Battlefields you control

If you move the units to two different Battlefields (e.g., one to Battlefield A and one to Battlefield B), you will have two separate Showdowns.

Reasoning: Each Battlefield is a distinct zone. Since both Battlefields now contain both your units and an opponent's unit, both meet the criteria for being Contested.

Sequence: Because these are two separate locations, the game will open one Showdown first (usually in the order the active player chooses or by battlefield position), resolve it completely, and then open the second Showdown.

Key Nuances

Attacker Status: In both scenarios, the opponent whose units were moved becomes the Attacker, and you are the Defender (CR 443.1.a.1).

Timing: Charm does not have the Action or Reaction keyword. Therefore, you must play this combo during your Main Phase. You cannot play Charm during an existing Showdown to bring more units in (as confirmed by official FAQ).

State: The moved units retain their current state. If they were exhausted before being Charmed, they remain exhausted during the Showdown.

question: If I play Counter Strike in a combat versus multiple units, does it block the damage from all units or just one, does the opponent choose what unit does the damage that gets blocked?
answer:
When you play Counter Strike, it prevents all damage that would be dealt to the chosen unit in that specific instance.

Because combat damage is dealt simultaneously (CR 444.1.d.1.a), all damage being dealt to your unit at that moment is considered a single event. Therefore, Counter Strike will prevent all of that damage, regardless of how many units are attacking it.

To answer your specific questions:

Does it block damage from all units or just one? It blocks all damage dealt to the chosen unit during that combat step, as all combat damage is dealt simultaneously.

Does the opponent choose what unit does the damage that gets blocked? No. The effect is not tied to a specific attacking unit; it is tied to the unit you chose to protect. It prevents the damage that unit would take from any source during that next damage event.

Summary: When you play Counter Strike, you choose one of your units. The next time that unit would take damage (which, in combat, is the simultaneous damage step), all of that damage is prevented.

question: When equipment has quick draw because of Jax Unmatched, do I still need to recycle the energy to equip?
answer:
When your Equipment gains Quick-Draw from Jax, Unmatched, you do not pay the Equip cost to attach it when you play it from your hand.

Here is the breakdown of how this works:

Play Cost: You must still pay the Energy and Power costs printed in the top-left corner of the Equipment card to play it.

No Equip Cost: Because the Equipment now has Quick-Draw, it gains the triggered ability: "When you play it, attach it to a unit you control." This triggered ability attaches the Equipment for free. You do not pay the Equip cost (the cost listed in the card's text box) for this initial attachment.

Regarding "Recycle": You only need to "recycle" cards if the specific Equipment card you are playing has a cost that explicitly requires recycling (like Last Rites). If the Equipment's Equip cost does not involve recycling, you do not need to recycle anything.

Summary: You pay the card's play cost (Energy/Power), but you bypass the Equip cost entirely thanks to the Quick-Draw ability granted by Jax.

question: Can Draven Audacious get you to 8 points?
answer:
Yes, Draven, Audacious can get you to 8 points to win the game.

According to CR 450.1.a.1, points earned from sources that are not "Conquer" or "Hold" actions are not subject to the final point restrictions (which require you to have scored on all battlefields that turn). Because Draven's ability is a triggered ability that grants a point upon winning a combat, it is not beholden to those restrictions and can be used to reach your 8th point.

question: Does Switcheroo keep the might of the card switched for the turn?
answer:
No, Switcheroo does not "keep" the might value in the sense of locking it to a specific number regardless of future changes. Instead, it applies a persistent modifier (an increase to one unit and a decrease to the other) that lasts until the end of the turn.

According to Rule 420.1 and the associated FAQs, "Swapping" is the act of increasing one numeric value and decreasing another so that their values are reversed.

Here is how it works:

It is a modifier, not a snapshot: When Switcheroo resolves, it calculates the difference between the two units' current Might and applies a +X or -X modifier to them. This modifier persists for the rest of the turn.

Future changes still apply: Because these are modifiers (increases and decreases), if a unit's Might changes after the swap (e.g., from a new buff, a trigger, or a passive ability), that new change is calculated on top of the modifier applied by Switcheroo.

Buffs stay put: Physical buffs (like equipment or attached cards) remain on their original units. They are not moved or swapped; only the final Might value is adjusted.

Example:
If Unit A has 5 Might and Unit B has 2 Might, Switcheroo applies a -3 modifier to Unit A and a +3 modifier to Unit B. If Unit A later gains +1 Might from another source, its final Might will be 3 (5 - 3 + 1).

question: Does Switcheroo count Shield?
answer:
Yes, Switcheroo counts Shield when it resolves.

According to the game's mechanics, Shield is a passive effect that continuously adds to a unit's Might while they are a defender. When you cast Switcheroo, it snapshots the current Might values of the two units—which includes any active Shield bonuses—and swaps them.

Here is how the interaction works:

Snapshotting: Switcheroo calculates the current Might of both units (including any active Shield or Assault bonuses) and swaps those values.

Passive Effects Remain: The Shield bonus itself is a passive effect and does not transfer to the other unit. It remains on the original unit.

Result: After the swap, the units will have the new Might values, and their original Shield bonuses will continue to apply to their new Might totals for the remainder of the combat.

Example:
If you have a unit with 2 base Might and Shield 1 (Total 3 Might) and another unit with 5 Might:

Switcheroo sees the current Might values as 3 and 5.

It swaps them by applying a +2 modifier to the first unit and a -2 modifier to the second.

The first unit now has 5 Might (4 base + 1 Shield), and the second unit has 3 Might.

question: Can you play Tideturner hidden in base?
answer:
No, you cannot play Tideturner hidden in the base.

According to Rule 737.1.b, the Hidden keyword allows you to hide a card facedown specifically at a battlefield you control. It does not allow you to hide cards in the base.

Furthermore, as clarified in the official FAQ:

Ruling: Tideturner can only be played at the battlefield where it was hidden, not into the base to switch with units on other battlefields.

question: Do I need to pay deflect costs when playing Switcheroo?
answer:
Yes, you must pay the Deflect cost when casting Switcheroo on a unit with Deflect.

According to the official ruling:

Yes, you must pay for Deflect when casting Switcheroo on a unit with Deflect, because Switcheroo is a spell and you are choosing (targeting) the unit with Deflect.

Nuance: This only applies if the unit with Deflect is controlled by an opponent.

Because Deflect is a mandatory additional cost (Rule 735.1.d), it must be paid when the spell is placed on the chain, before the spell resolves.

question: I have a First Mate with Warmog's Armor, so he is at 4 Might. I conquer Sunken Temple. Then I get a buff. But can I use the effect of Sunken Temple to draw a card? Because I buffed my First Mate with its conquer effect?
answer:
No, you cannot use the effect of Sunken Temple in this scenario.

Here is the breakdown of why:

Might Calculation: Your First Mate has a base Might of 3. With Warmog's Armor attached, it gains +1 Might, bringing its total to 4 Might.

Mighty Definition: According to the rules (and the text on Sunken Temple), a unit is only considered "Mighty" if it has 5 or more Might. Since your unit has 4 Might, it is not Mighty.

Trigger Timing: Sunken Temple's ability is a triggered ability that checks for a Mighty unit at the moment you conquer. Because your unit is not Mighty at the time the conquer occurs, the trigger condition is not met.

Even if you receive a buff after the conquer (from another card's effect), it is too late to satisfy the condition for Sunken Temple. The unit must be Mighty at the exact moment the conquer happens for the ability to trigger.

question: If I save a unit with the boss from hidden blade, do I still draw 2?
answer:
Yes, you still draw 2 cards.

According to the official rulings for this interaction:

When Hidden Blade resolves, its "kill" instruction executes. The Boss's ability acts as a replacement effect that intercedes during this execution, changing the outcome for the unit (recalling it instead of killing it). Because the Hidden Blade instruction still executed and the unit remains a valid referent for its controller, the draw effect still applies.

The key is that the replacement effect changes what happens to the unit, but it does not prevent the Hidden Blade spell from resolving or identifying the unit's controller.

question: On high OPL, what is the order of operations for deciding battlefields, revealing battlefields, and choosing who goes first, etc.?
answer:
In Riftbound (including High OPL/Competitive play), the setup sequence is strictly defined to ensure players have full information about the Battlefields before deciding who goes first.

The correct order of operations is:

Sideboarding: Players swap cards from their sideboards (if applicable). This is done before any information is revealed.

Reveal Legends: Both players reveal their Legend cards simultaneously.

Choose and Reveal Champions: Both players select their Chosen Champions and reveal them.

Select and Reveal Battlefields: Both players select their Battlefields. These are revealed simultaneously and placed in the Battlefield Zone. They are public knowledge before the next step.

Determine Turn Order:

In Game 1, turn order is determined by a fair random method (e.g., a die roll or coin flip).

In Games 2 and 3, the player who lost the previous game chooses whether to go first (Play) or second (Channel). This choice is made after seeing the revealed Battlefields.

Draw and Mulligan: Players draw their starting hand of 4 cards. The player going first performs their mulligan first, followed by the second player.

Key Nuances

Battlefields Before Turn Order: You must know which Battlefields are in play before deciding to go first or second. According to official rulings, "Battlefields are revealed before determining turn order."

Simultaneous Revelation: While players often place Battlefields face-down temporarily to prevent "counter-picking" during the selection process, they must be revealed at the same time before the turn order is decided.

BO3 Battlefield Rule: In a Best of 3 match, you cannot reuse a Battlefield you have already used in a previous game of that match.

Citations:

Rule 166.2.b: "Battlefields are established at the start of a game and remain in place for the duration of regular play."

Official FAQ: "The order is the same for every game: Legend > Chosen Champion > Battlefields chosen and revealed > Turn order > Draw & Mulligan."

question: Can you charm an enemy unit from one battlefield to the other if it doesn't have ganking?
answer:
Yes, you can use Charm to move an enemy unit from one battlefield to another, even if that unit does not have the Ganking keyword.

According to the official rulings for Charm:

Ganking restrictions (which limit how units perform a "Standard Move") do not apply to movement caused by spells or abilities.

Because Charm is a spell effect and not a "Standard Move," it is not restricted by the Ganking requirement.

When you use Charm to move an enemy unit to your battlefield, that unit is considered to be attacking for the purposes of combat.

question: Can I activate Sett Brawler on defense?
answer:
No, you cannot activate Sett, Brawler's ability while defending.

According to the established rulings for Sett, Brawler:

Timing Restriction: Sett, Brawler's ability does not have the ACTION or REACTION keywords. Therefore, it can only be activated during your turn and when there is no chain present and you are outside of a Showdown.

Defense: Because the ability is restricted to your turn and outside of Showdowns, it cannot be used while you are defending.

While Sett, Brawler does gain a buff when he conquers (which can happen when attacking or defending), you must wait until your own turn to spend that buff to grant him the +4 Might.

question: If I use Full the Weak and kill my own Immortal Phoenix, can I use the Immortal Phoenix that got killed to come back?
answer:
Yes, you can play that same Immortal Phoenix from your trash.

According to the official FAQ and Rule 376.2.c.1, this interaction works because the Phoenix is moved to the trash during the resolution of the spell, and its trigger condition is evaluated immediately after the unit is killed.

The Sequence:

You play Cull the Weak.

As the spell resolves, you choose to kill your Immortal Phoenix.

The Phoenix is moved from the board to the trash (Rule 415.1).

The spell finishes resolving. At this point, the game checks for triggers. Since a unit was killed by a spell and the Phoenix is now in the trash, its ability triggers.

You may then pay {1} Energy and {1} Fury Power to play it from the trash.

Relevant Rule:

Rule 376.2.c.1: "If a Game Object with a Triggered Ability that is active in a specific zone, it is evaluated and subsequently triggered if it enters that zone at the same time that its Trigger’s condition is met. Example: Immortal Phoenix... This ability triggers if Immortal Phoenix is in your trash immediately after you kill a unit with a spell, even if the unit you killed with a spell was that Immortal Phoenix."

question: In game three, we went to time, we played three turns and player one ended on 6 points and I ended on 4. Does player one win due to being 2 points ahead?
answer:
Yes, Player 1 is declared the winner of that game, and consequently the winner of the match.

According to Tournament Rule 408.2.b:

"If the game is incomplete at the end of the additional turns, a player is declared the winner of the game if they have a point lead of two or more. If no player has a point lead of two or more, the game is a draw."

Since Player 1 has 6 points and you have 4 points, they have exactly a two-point lead, which satisfies the requirement to be declared the winner of Game 3.

Because this was Game 3 of a Best-of-3 match:

Game 3 Result: Player 1 wins.

Match Score: Player 1 now has 2 game wins to your 1 game win.

Match Result: Player 1 wins the match (per Rule 408.3.a, which states the player with more game wins wins the match if the end of match procedure is completed).

question: Can my opponent use Overzealous ability if I move up with Ezreal dashing?
answer:
Yes, your opponent can use Overzealous Fan's ability when Ezreal, Dashing moves into the battlefield to attack, but the timing of the triggers is critical.

The Ruling

Both Ezreal, Dashing and Overzealous Fan have triggered abilities that occur when they gain their combat designations (Attacker and Defender). Because it is your turn (you are the one moving Ezreal to attack), your "When I attack" trigger goes on the chain first, followed by your opponent's "When I defend" trigger.

Because the chain resolves in LIFO (Last-In, First-Out) order, the Overzealous Fan's ability will resolve before Ezreal deals his ability damage.

The Sequence

Ezreal moves to the battlefield: He becomes the Attacker. Overzealous Fan becomes the Defender.

Triggers go on the Chain:

Ezreal's "When I attack" trigger is placed on the chain first (Active Player).

Overzealous Fan's "When I defend" trigger is placed on the chain second (Non-Active Player).

Resolution (LIFO):

Overzealous Fan's ability resolves first: The opponent chooses whether to kill the Fan. If they do, Ezreal is moved back to your base immediately.

Ezreal's ability attempts to resolve: Because Ezreal is no longer "here" (he is now at the base), his ability will "whiff" (fail to resolve) because he has lost his location and cannot find a target "here" (See Rule 356.3.e.12).

Summary

If your opponent chooses to sacrifice the Fan, Ezreal will be sent back to your base and will deal no damage.

Note: According to the official FAQ, the opponent must choose Ezreal as the target when the ability is put on the chain, but they don't make the final decision to "kill" the Fan until the moment the ability actually resolves.

question: Does equipment like Doran's Ring attached to a unit also trigger at Reckoners Arena?
answer:
Yes, equipment like Doran's Ring attached to a unit will trigger at Reckoner's Arena.

Here's how it works:

The Mechanism:

Doran's Ring has the effect: "When I conquer, discard 1, then draw 1."

Reckoner's Arena has the ability: "When you hold here, activate the conquer effects of units here."

The Interaction:
When you hold at Reckoner's Arena, the battlefield's ability activates the conquer effects of all units present at that battlefield. Equipment effects, such as Doran's Ring's, are considered part of the unit's effects while attached. Therefore, Doran's Ring's conquer effect becomes part of the unit's conquer effects and will be activated by Reckoner's Arena.

Result:
When you hold at Reckoner's Arena with a unit equipped with Doran's Ring, you will discard 1 card and draw 1 card as part of the triggered chain.

This follows the same principle as the Trinity Force + Skyfall of Areion interaction documented in the FAQs: equipment effects attached to units are activated when Reckoner's Arena triggers its "activate conquer effects" ability.

question: If I use Baited Hook on Honest Broker and I play Karthus off of the trigger, how many times does Honest Broker's Deathknell trigger?
answer:
Honest Broker’s Deathknell will trigger one time.

According to the official FAQ regarding the interaction between Baited Hook and Karthus, Karthus must be on the board at the moment the Deathknell trigger is created for his doubling effect to apply.

Sequence of Resolution:

Baited Hook resolves: You kill Honest Broker.

The Deathknell trigger for Honest Broker becomes pending. It cannot enter the chain yet because Baited Hook is still resolving (Rule 734.1.d.2).

Baited Hook continues: You look at the top 5 cards and find Karthus, Eternal. Karthus is played and becomes a pending item on the chain.

Baited Hook finishes resolving. Now, all pending items finalize in the order they were created:

First, the Deathknell trigger finalizes and enters the chain.

Second, Karthus finalizes and resolves immediately (as a unit permanent), entering the board.

Because the Deathknell trigger was already created and put on the chain before Karthus was on the board, Karthus's passive ability ("Your Deathknell effects trigger an additional time") does not see the event to double it.

Summary: Karthus needs to be on the board when the trigger happens, not just when it resolves. Since Honest Broker died while Karthus was still in your deck/pending, you only get the single trigger.

question: How do you play Poro Snax and why would you play it if it has no Might value?
answer:
Ruling: Poro Snax is a Gear card (not Equipment) that is played directly to your Base, not attached to a unit. When you play it, you immediately draw 1 card, and you can later use its activated ability to pay 1 Energy, 1 Calm, and Tap and Kill it to draw another card.

Sequence:

Play Poro Snax from hand to your Base

Its triggered ability activates: draw 1 card immediately

Later, you may activate its ability by paying 1 Energy and 1 Calm, Tapping it, and destroying it to draw 1 additional card

Nuances:

Poro Snax provides no Might and doesn't strengthen units in combat

It's played for card advantage: it replaces itself immediately when played, effectively thinning your deck

It can trigger "play a card" or "play a Gear" effects on other cards you control

Only Gear cards with the "Equipment" tag and "Equip" keyword attach to units; standard Gear cards like Poro Snax stay at your Base

question: Can I spend Udyr buff to stun a unit at another battlefield?
answer:
Yes, you can spend Udyr's buff to stun a unit at another battlefield.

Udyr's ability reads: "Spend my buff: Choose one you've not chosen this turn — ... * Stun a unit at a battlefield."

Because the ability specifies "a battlefield" rather than "this battlefield" or "the same battlefield," you are not restricted to targeting units at Udyr's current location. You may target any unit currently located at any battlefield, provided it is a valid target for a stun effect.

Important Reminders:

Base Speed: As an activated ability without the "Action" or "Reaction" keyword, you must activate this during your turn while there is no chain or showdown (CR 701/FAQ).

Targeting: You cannot target units in a base; the target must be at a battlefield.

Already Stunned: Per CR 411.1.a.1, you cannot stun a unit that is already stunned. While you can target an already-stunned unit with the effect, the stun will not apply.

question: If a 4 Might unit moves from base to Trifarian Warcamp, do they become Mighty and trigger Fiora's Legend ability?
answer:
Yes, moving a 4 Might unit from your base to Trifarian War Camp will cause it to "become Mighty" and trigger Fiora's Legend ability.

This is distinct from playing a unit directly onto the battlefield. When you move a unit that is already on the battlefield (your base) to Trifarian War Camp, it is already a game object in play. As it enters the War Camp, it gains the +1 Might bonus, causing its Might to increase from 4 to 5. Because the unit was already on the battlefield when this increase occurred, it satisfies the condition of "becoming Mighty," which triggers Fiora's Legend ability.

question: Do you still get gold when someone flashes your Blood Money or Wages of Pain target?
answer:
Ruling: Blood Money will NOT give gold if the target becomes illegal (leaves the battlefield). Wages of Pain WILL still give the gold token even if the target becomes illegal.

Sequence:

When a spell is played, its target is locked when placed on the chain

If the target leaves the battlefield before resolution, it becomes illegal

The spell still attempts to resolve (does not fizzle entirely)

Instructions that cannot be followed are ignored

Instructions that don't reference target information are still executed

Nuances:

Blood Money checks information about the target ("if it was an enemy unit" / "if it was a friendly unit"), which returns null when the target is illegal, causing those conditional instructions to be ignored

Wages of Pain's gold token generation is a separate instruction after a full stop that doesn't reference target information, so it executes even when the damage cannot be dealt

The presence of a full stop creates independent instructions, but only those that don't require checking information about illegal targets will execute

question: Can you not so fast Brynhildr trigger?
answer:
No, you cannot use Not So Fast to counter Brynhir Thundersong's ability.

According to the official ruling: Not So Fast can only counter spells or abilities that choose (target) a friendly unit or gear. Brynhir Thundersong's "When you play me" ability is a global effect that does not target or choose a specific unit or gear, so it does not meet the requirements for Not So Fast to be played.

question: Can I use Not So Fast to counter Riposte?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot use Not So Fast to counter Riposte. Not So Fast can only counter spells or abilities that target units or gear friendly to you (the player of Not So Fast). Riposte targets a unit friendly to its own controller, not your units, so it does not meet the targeting requirement for Not So Fast.

Nuances:

The term "friendly" is always relative to the controller of the spell or ability

Not So Fast is designed to protect your own board state from opponent targeting

Riposte does not interact with your board, so it cannot be countered by Not So Fast

question: If your opponent targets your unattached Hexdrinker, do they need to pay the Deflect cost?
answer:
Ruling: No, Hexdrinker does not have Deflect while it is unattached. Your opponent does not need to pay the Deflect cost to target it.

Sequence:

Hexdrinker's Deflect keyword is located in the Effect box, not the Rules Text box

Effect Text is Inactive unless the card is attached to a unit

When unattached and sitting on the board as a Gear, Hexdrinker's Deflect ability is Inactive

Once attached to a unit, the Effect Text (including Deflect) becomes active

Nuances:

Effect Text and Rules Text are distinct categories on equipment cards with different activation conditions

When equipment detaches, its Effect Text becomes Inactive and its Rules Text ceases being Inactive

question: If I have a sprite at a battlefield with a hidden Consult the Past. When it becomes my turn, am I able to react and resolve Consult the Past or would it be discarded?
answer:
Yes, you can absolutely react to the Sprite token's temporary trigger by flipping your hidden Consult the Past before the token is removed.

According to the rules and established FAQs for Riftbound:

Temporary Trigger: At the beginning of your turn, the Sprite token's temporary trigger goes on the chain.

Reaction Window: Because this trigger is on the chain, you have a window to play reactions.

Resolution: You can flip your hidden Consult the Past in response to this trigger. Because the chain resolves in Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) order, your Consult the Past will resolve first, allowing you to draw your cards before the Sprite token is removed from the battlefield.

The token is not removed automatically in a way that discards your hidden card; you have the priority to act before that happens.

question: Can I weaponmaster a piece of gear back to my unit if the enemy Akshan has stolen it and equipped it to a different unit?
answer:
No, you cannot use Weaponmaster to take back a piece of gear that an enemy Akshan has stolen.

According to Rule 747.1.b, the Weaponmaster keyword allows you to choose an Equipment you control. When an enemy Akshan steals your gear, they gain control of that equipment for as long as their Akshan remains on the board. Because you no longer control the equipment, you cannot target it with your own Weaponmaster ability.

question: Do I have to pay Deflect costs for a targeted ability and not a spell?
answer:
Yes, you must pay the Deflect cost for targeted abilities just as you would for a spell.

According to Rule 735.1.c, the Deflect keyword applies to both spells and abilities:

"It is functionally short for 'Spells and abilities an opponent controls that choose me cost an amount of Power equal to [Deflect Value] more to play as an additional cost for each time they choose me.'"

This means that any time an opponent's ability (activated or triggered) targets a unit with Deflect, the Deflect cost is a mandatory additional cost that must be paid to place that ability on the chain.

question: Can you target Ruin Runner with Falling Star?
answer:
No, you cannot target Ruin Runner with Falling Star.

Ruin Runner has the ability: "I can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities."

Because Falling Star is a spell that requires you to choose targets (as confirmed by Rule 352.14.a: "If a card specifies that an amount of damage may be split among some number of Units, then each Unit chosen is Targeted"), it is blocked by Ruin Runner's protection ability.

question: If I equip Brutalizer to a 2 might unit by recycling a rune and then activate Jax legend ability to re-equip it, what might is my unit?
answer:
Ruling: Your unit will have 5 Might total. When Brutalizer detaches during the re-equip, the unit loses all bonuses from it and returns to base Might, then gains the bonuses again when it re-attaches.

Sequence:

Initial state: Unit has 2 Might (base)

Equip Brutalizer: Unit gains +1 Might (base bonus) and +2 Might (conditional effect), totaling 5 Might

Activate Jax to re-equip: Brutalizer detaches, unit immediately loses all bonuses and returns to 2 Might (base)

Brutalizer re-attaches: Unit gains +1 Might and +2 Might again, totaling 5 Might

Nuances:

When a card detaches, its Effect Text becomes inactive and the top-most card ceases to have that Effect Text appended to its Rules Text

Brutalizer's "this turn" bonus does not persist when it detaches; all bonuses are removed immediately upon detachment

Brutalizer only ever provides either +1 Might or +3 Might to the unit it is attached to, never stacking effects

question: When killing a Deathknell unit with Baited Hook, what is the resolution order?
answer:
Ruling: When Baited Hook kills a unit with Deathknell and plays a new unit from your deck, the Deathknell trigger becomes pending first, then the new unit is played. The chain resolves in LIFO (Last In, First Out) order, so any "When You Play Me" ability on the new unit resolves before the Deathknell trigger.

Sequence:

Baited Hook kills the targeted unit (Deathknell trigger becomes pending)

Baited Hook continues resolving and plays a unit from your deck

The played unit enters play and finalizes immediately

If the played unit has a "When You Play Me" ability, it becomes pending on the chain

The chain resolves in reverse order: WYPM ability first (if any), then Deathknell trigger

Nuances:

The Deathknell trigger is created first but resolves last due to LIFO ordering

The unit played from Baited Hook finalizes immediately upon entering play, before any abilities resolve

question: Do I have to recycle Rune for the Quick Draw equip effect?
answer:
No, you do not need to recycle a rune to pay the Equip cost when using Quick-Draw.

When you play an Equipment card with Quick-Draw, you bypass the Equip cost entirely. Here is the breakdown of how this works:

Play Cost: You must still pay the Energy and Power costs printed in the top-left corner of the Equipment card to play it from your hand.

No Equip Cost: Because the Equipment has Quick-Draw, it gains the triggered ability: "When you play it, attach it to a unit you control." This ability attaches the Equipment for free, meaning you do not pay the Equip cost listed in the card's text box.

Regarding "Recycle": You only need to recycle a rune if the specific Equipment card you are playing has a cost that explicitly requires recycling (such as Last Rites). If the Equipment's Equip cost does not involve recycling, you do not need to recycle anything.

In summary, Quick-Draw allows you to attach the gear for free as part of playing it, bypassing the standard Equip cost.

question: If a unit is on a battlefield, can you equip an equipment to it?
answer:
Yes, you can equip an equipment to a unit that is on a battlefield.

According to Rule 744.1.b, the Equip ability allows you to attach the equipment to a chosen unit you control. There is no restriction in the rules stating that the unit must be at your base; as long as the unit is under your control, it is a valid target for the Equip ability.

Important Timing Restrictions:
While you can target a unit on a battlefield, remember that the Equip ability itself has specific timing restrictions:

You must be in your turn.

The Chain must be empty.

There must be no Showdown occurring.

As long as you meet these timing requirements, you can equip a unit regardless of whether it is at your base or on a battlefield.

question: Does Thousand Tailed Watcher give Ruin Runner -3 when played?
answer:
Yes, Ruin Runner will receive the -3 might reduction from Thousand-Tailed Watcher.

The reason for this interaction is that Thousand-Tailed Watcher's ability does not choose (target) specific units; it applies a global effect to all enemy units. Ruin Runner's ability states, "I can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities," which only protects it from effects that require a player to specifically target it. Because the Watcher's ability affects the entire board without targeting, Ruin Runner is affected normally.

Key Details:

Targeting: Because the Watcher's ability doesn't use the word "choose" or "target" for the units it affects, it bypasses Ruin Runner's protection.

Minimum Might: Per the text of Thousand-Tailed Watcher, Ruin Runner's might will be reduced from 5 to 2 (it cannot be reduced below 1).

Timing: This reduction only applies to units already on the board when Thousand-Tailed Watcher's "When you play me" ability resolves.

question: Can Teemo Strategist ability be used from hand if there are no units on the battlefield? If you want to find Nocturne...
answer:
No, you cannot activate the ability of Teemo, Strategist from Hidden if there are no valid enemy units at the battlefield.

According to the official ruling on this interaction:

Ability Activation: When activating any ability in Riftbound, all targets must be declared as the ability is placed on the chain. If there are no valid enemy units to target at the battlefield, the ability cannot enter the chain at all. Consequently, the reveal and recycle effects do not occur.

Regarding Nocturne:

Finding Nocturne: Yes, you can play Nocturne off Teemo, Strategist's effect, but only if the ability successfully enters the chain (i.e., there is at least one valid enemy unit to target). If the ability is successfully placed on the chain, you can reveal your cards and, if Nocturne is among them, use his ability to play him.

question: Does Assault affect the amount of damage I can take before dying, and what happens if I'm moved from battlefield to base while having marked damage that exceeds my base Might?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Assault increases your total Might while you are an attacker, which affects how much damage you can survive. Your Might determines the lethal damage threshold - you die if marked damage equals or exceeds your current Might.

Sequence:

Calculate total Might while attacking (base Might + innate Assault + equipment Assault + any bonuses)

During combat, you can survive damage up to one less than your total Might because healing occurs before Assault is removed

If moved from battlefield to base, you immediately lose your Attacker designation

A Cleanup occurs when the move action completes

During Cleanup, you lose the Assault bonus and your Might drops to base value

If marked damage now equals or exceeds your base Might, you are killed and placed in trash

Nuances:

Combat healing happens during Combat Special Cleanup before Attacker/Defender designations are removed, allowing you to survive damage that would be lethal at base Might

Moving a unit with Assault and marked damage to another location causes it to lose Assault immediately, potentially making previously survivable damage lethal

Any effect that removes Attacker designation will cause loss of Assault bonus before the next Cleanup check

question: If two Draven, Audacious units (one allied, one enemy) die simultaneously in combat, who scores the point? What happens if both players are at 7 points?
answer:
Ruling: When both Draven units die simultaneously in combat, both death triggers go on the chain. The turn player places their trigger first, then the non-turn player places theirs second. The chain resolves last-in-first-out, so the non-turn player's trigger resolves first, giving the turn player 1 point. If the turn player reaches 8 points from this, they win immediately before their own Draven trigger resolves.

Sequence:

Both Draven units die simultaneously, creating pending triggers

Turn player places their Draven death trigger on the chain first

Non-turn player places their Draven death trigger on the chain second (on top)

Chain resolves last-in-first-out: non-turn player's trigger resolves first

Non-turn player chooses turn player as opponent; turn player scores 1 point

If turn player reaches 8 points, they win immediately

Turn player's own Draven trigger does not resolve if the game has ended

Nuances:

Neither player scores from Draven's "win combat" ability because when both units die with no others remaining, the combat is a tie

Draven's death trigger is not restricted by the "Final Point" rules that apply to Conquer/Hold actions, so it can score the 8th point

At 7-7, the turn player wins because their opponent's trigger resolves first and brings them to 8

question: If my opponent initiates a showdown on an empty battlefield, can I use Ride the Wind on Overzealous Fan and use his ability to push the attacking unit back?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you can use Ride the Wind to move Overzealous Fan to the battlefield during the showdown, and his "When I defend" ability will trigger and allow you to push the attacking unit back.

Sequence:

Opponent moves a unit to an empty battlefield, beginning a showdown

During an Open state, you play Ride the Wind as an action

Ride the Wind resolves, moving Overzealous Fan to the battlefield

During the cleanup phase following Ride the Wind's resolution, Overzealous Fan gains the Defender designation

Overzealous Fan's "When I defend" ability triggers and is placed on the chain as a pending item

Players may respond to the trigger before it resolves

Nuances:

Units that enter the battlefield after a showdown has begun gain the Defender designation during the cleanup phase following the action that caused them to become present, not immediately

Defend triggers activate when a unit gains the Defender designation for the first time during combat, even if that designation is gained mid-showdown

question: Can I play the Recruit tokens from Vanguard Armory to an open battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot play the Recruit tokens from Vanguard Armory directly to an open battlefield. The tokens must be played to valid locations, which are your Base or a Battlefield you already control.

Nuances:

Vanguard Armory's text "You may play them to different locations" allows you to distribute the three tokens across multiple valid locations (e.g., one to your Base and two to a controlled Battlefield), but does not bypass the standard rules for where units can be played

An open battlefield is not a valid location because you do not control it yet

Playing a unit to an open battlefield would require specific permission that Vanguard Armory does not grant

question: What happens first, Draven's Legend ability (winning combat) or Conquering effect?
answer:
Draven's Legend ability triggers and resolves BEFORE conquer effects.

According to the FAQ 'If I win on the attack and conquer, does this happen before or after I score? Before or after conquer effects?':

Draven's ability will trigger and resolve before you gain your regular point for scoring the battlefield and before any conquer effects are triggered.

The sequence is:

Combat concludes and you win (only your units remain)

Draven's "When you win a combat, draw 1" ability triggers and resolves immediately

You gain control of the battlefield (Conquer)

Conquer effects trigger and resolve

Important note: This timing matters for the Final Point rule. If you're at 6 points and conquer a battlefield with Draven, you'll draw a card instead of scoring the Final Point—because Draven's draw resolves first, bringing you to 7 points before the conquer effect would trigger.

question: Can I use Orb of Regret on my opponent's turn?
answer:
No, you cannot use the activated ability of Orb of Regret on your opponent's turn.

In Riftbound, activated abilities (like the one on Orb of Regret) can generally only be used on your own turn when you have priority. Because the ability on Orb of Regret does not have the Reaction keyword, it cannot be activated in response to your opponent's actions or during their turn.

question: Can Cull of the Weak work if you have no units?
answer:
Yes, you can play Cull the Weak even if you have no units in play.

According to the official rulings for this card:

No Units Required: Cull the Weak does not target specific units when it is played. Instead, the choice of which unit to kill happens during the resolution of the spell. Because it doesn't require a target to be finalized on the chain, you can play it regardless of your board state.

"Do As Much As You Can": In Riftbound, if an instruction cannot be fully followed, you perform as much of the effect as possible (Rule 356.3.e.11). If you have no units, you simply do not kill one, but your opponent must still kill one of theirs if they have any.

Not a Cost: Killing a unit is part of the spell's effect, not an additional cost to play the card. If it were a cost, you would be required to have a unit to sacrifice in order to play it.

question: Can Bellows Breathe target Ruin Runner in base?
answer:
No, you cannot target Ruin Runner with Bellows Breath, regardless of whether it is in the base or on a battlefield.

Ruin Runner has the ability: "I can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities."

Because Bellows Breath is a spell that requires you to choose targets (as confirmed by Rule 352.14.a: "If a card specifies that an amount of damage may be split among some number of Units, then each Unit chosen is Targeted"), it is blocked by Ruin Runner's protection ability.

question: I attach Brutalizer to a unit, it gets +1 from Brutalizer and +2 because of Brutalizer effect. If I detach Brutalizer from the unit, does the unit keep the +2? If I reattach the equipment to the unit, does it get +2 again and push the equipment to 5 might?
answer:
No, the unit does not keep the +2 bonus when Brutalizer is detached.

According to the rules and the specific interaction for Brutalizer:

Detachment: When Brutalizer detaches from a unit, the unit immediately loses all bonuses provided by that equipment (both the base +1 Might and the conditional +2 Might). The unit returns to its base Might.

Re-attachment: If you re-attach Brutalizer to the unit, it will gain the bonuses again. If the unit had 2 base Might, it would gain the +1 (base bonus) and the +2 (conditional effect), totaling 5 Might.

As noted in the rules for attachments (Rule 136.3.a), the Might bonus is applied only while the card is attached and stops applying as soon as the card is no longer attached.

question: Can I use Jax legend ability when defending a battlefield and a showdown starts?
answer:
No, you cannot use the legend ability of Grandmaster at Arms (Jax) during a showdown.

Ruling:
Activated abilities that do not have the Action or Reaction keyword can only be activated during your turn when the game state is Open (the chain is empty). Because the legend ability of Grandmaster at Arms lacks these keywords, it cannot be used during a showdown, regardless of whether you are attacking or defending.

Reasoning:

Ability Timing: According to the rules for activated abilities, they must have a speed keyword (Action or Reaction) to be used during a showdown.

Showdown State: During a showdown, you are restricted to playing spells or activating abilities that are "legally timed" for that state (Rule 344). Since this ability does not have a speed keyword, it is not legally timed for use during a showdown.

This is my interpretation based on the standard rules for activated abilities and showdown timing. No official FAQ exists for this specific interaction.

question: Can Teemo Strategist target multiple units with his effect?
answer:
No, Teemo, Strategist cannot target multiple units.

According to the official ruling for Teemo, Strategist: You choose only one enemy unit with his ability, regardless of how many cards with [Hidden] are revealed.

question: Can Weaponmaster take an already equipped equipment from another unit and equip it on its own?
answer:
Yes, a unit with the Weaponmaster keyword can take an equipment that is already attached to another unit and equip it to itself.

According to the FAQ and Rule 747.1.b, Weaponmaster allows you to choose an equipment you control and attach it to the unit with the Weaponmaster ability, even if that equipment is already attached to a different unit. This effect is voluntary.

question: When Teemo, Strategist's ability targets a unit with Deflect while showing 5 hidden cards, how many times must the Deflect cost be paid?
answer:
Ruling: You pay the Deflect cost only one time, regardless of how many Hidden cards are revealed or how much total damage is dealt. Teemo's ability creates a single instance of targeting and deals damage from a single source.

Sequence:

Declare you are using Teemo, Strategist's ability

Pay the Deflect cost as a mandatory additional cost (or choose not to pay it and the ability doesn't go on the chain)

If paid, the ability goes on the chain and you flip 5 cards

Deal all damage from the revealed Hidden cards

Nuances:

The Deflect cost must be paid before flipping any cards - you cannot see the results first and then decide whether to pay

If you choose not to pay the Deflect cost, you don't get to flip the 5 cards at all

question: If I choose my Irelia fervent starting with 4 might with a spell and then use Irelia's legend ability to ready her, does she get +1 from Irelia's legend choosing her?
answer:
No, she does not get the +1 Might bonus for being "chosen" by the Legend ability, but she does get the +1 Might bonus for being "readied."

According to the rules and FAQs for these cards:

The Legend ability does not "choose" the unit: The Legend ability (Blade Dancer) readies a unit, but it does not count as "choosing" or "targeting" that unit. Therefore, it does not trigger the +1 Might bonus from Irelia, Fervent's ability that triggers when she is chosen.

She still gets the bonus for being "readied": Irelia, Fervent's ability states: "When you choose or ready me, give me +1 Might this turn." Because the Legend ability successfully readies her, she triggers the "ready" portion of her ability and gains +1 Might.

In summary: You do not get the bonus for "choosing," but you do get the bonus for "readying," resulting in a total of +1 Might from the Legend ability's effect.

question: On the board there are only 2 units: my Irelia Fervent, and my opponent's Irelia Fervent. Can I play Defiant Dance giving +2 to my Irelia, then refusing to pay the Deflect cost on the opponent's one so no one gets the -2?
answer:
No, you cannot do that.

According to Rule 353.2.a.2, the cost imposed by the Deflect keyword is a Mandatory Additional Cost. You must pay this cost in full to successfully play the spell.

If you choose to target an opponent's unit that has Deflect, you are required to pay the additional cost to play the spell. You cannot "refuse" to pay a mandatory cost while still playing the spell; if you do not pay the cost, the spell cannot be played at all. Furthermore, you cannot choose to play a spell and then opt out of one of its effects (like the -2 [M] reduction) while keeping the others. The spell resolves as written, applying both effects to the chosen targets.

question: Does Downwell return hidden cards to hand?
answer:
No, Downwell does not return hidden cards to your hand.

According to the official ruling:

Hidden cards are not affected: Hidden cards are facedown cards at a battlefield and are not considered "units" or "gear" while facedown. Therefore, Downwell's effect does not target or return them.

Cleanup process: When Downwell resolves and returns all units and gear to their owners' hands, the battlefield may become "Uncontrolled" (if no units or gear remain). During the subsequent Cleanup step, any hidden cards at an Uncontrolled battlefield are removed and placed in their owner's Trash.

Because this removal happens during the Cleanup step immediately after Downwell resolves, you do not have an opportunity to play or reveal the hidden cards before they are sent to the Trash.

question: If I attack an open battlefield, do I get an Assault 2 trigger?
answer:
No, you do not receive the Assault bonus when attacking an open (unoccupied) battlefield.

According to the rules and FAQs regarding Assault:

Assault is not a trigger: Assault is a passive ability, not a triggered ability. It is either "on" or "off" based on the unit's status.

Requires Combat: Assault is functionally short for "While I am an attacker, I have +X [M]." A unit only gains the "Attacker" designation during Combat.

Open Battlefields are not Combat: Moving a unit to an open or unoccupied battlefield initiates a non-combat Showdown. Because there is no opposing unit to create a Combat, your unit does not gain the "Attacker" designation.

Since your unit is not designated as an Attacker in a non-combat Showdown, the Assault passive ability does not activate, and the might bonus is not applied.

question: Do I still draw for Hidden Blade if I retreat my unit?
answer:
No, you do not draw 2 cards.

According to the established rulings for this interaction:

Hidden Blade requires a legal target at a battlefield to resolve.

When you play Retreat in response, it returns your unit to your hand before Hidden Blade resolves.

Because the unit is no longer on the battlefield, Hidden Blade no longer has a legal target. Consequently, it cannot identify "its controller" to grant the draw effect, and the instruction to draw is ignored.

question: If I'm playing Vex in combat and use a 2-cost spell targeting a unit with Deflect, how much should I pay?
answer:
Ruling: You pay 1 Energy total. The spell's base cost is 2 Energy, Deflect adds 1 Power as an additional cost, then Vex's discount of 1 Energy and 1 Power reduces the total to 1 Energy.

Sequence:

Start with the base cost (2 Energy)

Apply additional costs like Deflect (adds 1 Power, making it 2 Energy + 1 Power)

Apply discounts like Vex's ability (reduces by 1 Energy and 1 Power)

Final cost: 1 Energy + 0 Power = 1 Energy

Nuances:

Vex's ability only applies to friendly spells, not units

Discounts can be applied to additional costs, not just base costs

Vex's minimum of 1 Energy applies only to the spell's base cost, not the total cost including additional costs

Deflect is a mandatory additional cost that must be included before applying discounts

question: Can I "not so fast" a "Cull the Weak"?
answer:
No, you cannot use Not So Fast to counter Cull the Weak.

According to the official rulings for these cards:

Not So Fast can only counter a spell or ability that "chooses a friendly unit or gear."

Cull the Weak does not target or choose any units when it is played. The instruction to kill a unit is performed by each player during the resolution of the spell, rather than being a targeted choice made when the spell is played.

Because Cull the Weak does not meet the requirement of choosing a friendly unit or gear, it is not a valid target for Not So Fast.

question: If I have a Stellacorn Herder in base, and play a Tideturner in base, can I choose Stellacorn as a target for Tideturner's effect? What happens?
answer:
Now I understand the situation. Let me address this:

No, you cannot choose Stellacorn Herder as a target for Tideturner's effect, and you cannot play Tideturner in base in the first place.

Here's why:

Tideturner cannot be played in base: According to Rule 737.1.b and the official FAQ, the Hidden keyword allows you to hide a card facedown specifically at a battlefield you control—not in the base. When you later play Tideturner from hidden, it must be played at the battlefield where it was hidden.

Even if you could play Tideturner in base: Tideturner's ability reads "choose a unit you control at another location." The base is not a location in the same sense as battlefields. The ability requires targeting a unit at a different location than where Tideturner is played. If Tideturner were in base, it could only target units at battlefields (and vice versa).

Stellacorn Herder is in base: Since Stellacorn Herder is also in base, it would be at the same location as Tideturner, making it an illegal target (Tideturner requires "another location").

Bottom line: You'd need to play Tideturner at a battlefield to use its effect, and then you could swap it with a friendly unit at a different location (either base or another battlefield).

question: If I play from hidden a Teemo Strategist during a Showdown and one of the cards that I look at is a Nocturne, can I play it directly at the battlefield in question?
answer:
Yes, you can play Nocturne directly to the battlefield in question, provided you control that battlefield.

According to the established rulings for these cards:

Playing Nocturne: Nocturne's ability allows you to play him when he is looked at or revealed from the top of your deck. Card text supersedes normal timing restrictions. While units normally cannot be played during a "showdown closed" state, Nocturne's specific triggered ability allows him to be played into any battlefield his controller controls.

Control Requirement: You can play Nocturne to the battlefield you are defending as long as you control it. In almost all cases where you are defending with Teemo, you retain control of that battlefield for the duration of the showdown.

Interaction: If you play Teemo, Strategist from Hidden during a showdown and his ability reveals Nocturne, you may choose to play Nocturne using his ability instead of recycling him.

Nuance: If you are in a rare situation where you are defending but do not control the battlefield (such as a "surprise defense" where you moved into an open showdown), you would not be able to play Nocturne to that battlefield.

question: Can I target the same unit with Singularity?
answer:
No, you cannot target the same unit twice with Singularity.

According to the official rulings for Singularity:

Singularity must target two different units if you choose to target two units. You cannot target the same unit twice to deal 12 damage.

"Up to two units" means you can choose to target 0, 1, or 2 units.

If you target only one unit, it takes 6 damage. If you target two units, each takes 6 damage.

This is a single trigger that requires choosing distinct units if you want to target two of them.

question: When an Gear gets removed after unit killed is it ready?
answer:
When a unit with attached gear is killed, the gear detaches and remains at the base. According to the established rulings, the gear returns to your base ready.

As stated in the FAQ:

"When the equipped unit dies, the equipment returns to your base ready, so you can pay the equip cost again to re-equip it."

This is consistent with the general rule that gear enters and exists at the base in a ready state unless otherwise specified (Rule 147.1).

question: If I have only Travelling Merchant in hand and play it, do I draw a card?
answer:
Ruling: No, you do not draw a card. Playing Travelling Merchant does not count as moving it, so its ability does not trigger.

Nuances:

The ability only triggers when Travelling Merchant moves, not when it is played

If you do move Travelling Merchant while having no cards in hand, you would skip the discard and draw 1 card

Effects worded as "discard, then draw" resolve each part independently, so failing to discard doesn't prevent the draw

question: If I'm in combat with Vex, and they try to use Rebuke on me, can I use defy against it?
answer:
Yes, you can use Defy to counter Rebuke.

Here is the breakdown of the interaction:

Reaction Timing: Rebuke is an Action spell. When your opponent plays it, it goes onto the chain. Because Defy is a Reaction, you are allowed to play it in response to the Rebuke on the chain.

Cost Check: Defy checks the printed cost of the spell in the upper left corner of the card, not the actual cost paid. Even if Vex, Cheerless is in combat and increases the cost of your opponent's spells, Defy ignores that increase and only looks at the base printed cost of Rebuke (2 Energy, 2 Power). Since this is within the range of what Defy can counter, it is a legal target.

According to the rules regarding Defy (as noted in the FAQ), it always evaluates the printed cost of the card, and it can be used to counter any spell that meets those cost requirements, regardless of additional costs or modifiers applied during the casting process.

question: If I target Ornn, Forge God equipped with Svellsongur, do I have to pay Deflect 2 or Deflect 4?
answer:
Ruling: You must pay Deflect 4. When Svellsongur is attached to Ornn, Forge God, it copies Ornn's text (including Deflect 2) into its own effect text. Since attached equipment's effect text is active and appended to the unit's rules text, Ornn has two instances of Deflect 2. Because Deflect is a stacking keyword, these sum together for a total of Deflect 4.

Sequence:

Ornn, Forge God has Deflect 2 as printed text on the unit

Svellsongur attaches to Ornn and copies all of Ornn's text into Svellsongur's effect text

Svellsongur's effect text (now containing Deflect 2) becomes active and is appended to Ornn's rules text

The two instances of Deflect 2 stack, resulting in Deflect 4 total

Any opponent's spell or ability targeting Ornn costs an additional 4 power to play

Nuances:

Deflect is explicitly a stacking keyword - multiple instances sum their values

Equipment effect text is active while attached and counts as part of the unit's text

The equipment itself doesn't have Deflect; rather, it grants a second instance of Deflect to the unit it's attached to

question: Can you use Arcane Shift to replay a banished friendly unit back to a contested battlefield you are attacking during combat?
answer:
Ruling: No, you cannot replay the unit to the contested battlefield you are attacking. As the attacker, you do not control that battlefield—the defender does, even while contested. You can only play the unit to your base or to a battlefield you control.

Sequence:

The unit is banished from the contested battlefield

You must play it to either your base or a different battlefield you control

If played to a battlefield during showdown, the unit enters exhausted and gains attacker/defender designation during the cleanup phase

Nuances:

Arcane Shift can be played during showdowns, but the replayed unit must go to a legal location

A player maintains control of their battlefield while it is being contested by an opponent

This is different from a Recall effect, which would specifically force the unit to return to your base

question: If I move a unit to a battlefield and the enemy plays Ride the Wind on an Irelia Fervent into that battlefield, can I then play Arcane Shift to damage Irelia for 3, banish a unit, and play Vex to the same battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot use Arcane Shift to banish one unit and play a different unit like Vex. Arcane Shift requires you to banish a friendly unit and then play that same unit back. Additionally, because Irelia has [Deflect], you must pay an additional [A] (any domain rune) to target her with Arcane Shift's damage.

Sequence:

Ride the Wind resolves (moving Irelia to your battlefield)

Chain resolves and state returns to OPEN

You regain Focus and Priority

You can now play Arcane Shift (starting a new chain), paying the additional [A] cost to target Irelia

Arcane Shift banishes your chosen friendly unit and plays that same unit back

The banished unit can be played back to the contested battlefield since you are now in combat there

Nuances:

Arcane Shift is [ACTION] speed, so it cannot be played in response to Ride the Wind (which is [REACTION] speed). It can only be played after Ride the Wind fully resolves when the state returns to OPEN.

You need both Focus and Priority to play Arcane Shift after Ride the Wind resolves.

If you want to play Vex, that would be a separate action entirely, subject to standard playing rules.

question: If you choose and ready Irelia Fervent with Ride The Wind would she get +1 or +2 Might?
answer:
If Irelia, Fervent is exhausted when you play Ride the Wind, she gains +2 Might total.

According to the official ruling for this interaction:

+1 Might is gained when she is chosen as the target for the spell.

+1 Might is gained when she is readied by the spell's effect.

The sequence of events is as follows:

Ride the Wind is played and becomes a pending chain item.

Irelia is chosen as the target, triggering her ability (+1 Might).

Irelia's ability enters the chain above Ride the Wind and resolves first.

Ride the Wind resolves, moving and readying Irelia.

Irelia's "ready" trigger adds to the chain as a pending item and resolves (+1 Might).

Nuance: Irelia must be exhausted beforehand to receive the full +2 bonus, as a unit that is already ready cannot be readied again.

question: Does Scrap Head draw a card when discarded from Sabotage?
answer:
No, Scrapheap does not draw a card when targeted by Sabotage.

Here is the breakdown:

Sabotage instructs you to recycle a card from your opponent's hand.

Scrapheap's ability triggers only when it is "played, discarded, or killed."

Because recycling is a distinct game action from discarding (as defined in CR 404.1 and Rule 409.1), Sabotage does not trigger Scrapheap's ability.

question: If you cast Cull the Weak does that trigger Deflect?
answer:
No, casting Cull the Weak does not trigger Deflect.

According to the official rulings for this interaction:

Deflect only activates when a spell or ability specifically targets (chooses) the permanent with Deflect (Rule 735.1.c).

Cull the Weak does not target. The choice of which unit to kill happens during the resolution of the spell, not when it is played. Because no targeting occurs, Deflect does not trigger.

question: If I play Card Sharp and my opponent chooses to play a token, do I get 2 tokens?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, in a 1v1 game you get 2 Gold gear tokens total if your opponent chooses to play one.

Sequence:

First, you and each opponent may play a Gold gear token exhausted (you get 1, opponent may play 1)

Then, for each opponent who did play a token, you play an additional Gold gear token exhausted (you get 1 more)

Nuances:

Card Sharp has two separate effects that resolve in order

If your opponent declines to play a token, you only get 1 token total (from the first effect only)

With multiple opponents, you could get even more tokens (1 from the first effect + 1 for each opponent who participates)

question: Can Rune Runner be chosen with King's Edict?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, Rune Runner can be chosen by King's Edict. The players make the choice during resolution, not the spell itself, so Rune Runner's protection from being chosen by enemy spells and abilities does not apply.

Nuances:

This follows the same logic as Cull the Weak, where player choices during resolution are distinct from the spell doing the choosing

Rune Runner's ability only protects it from being chosen directly by enemy spells and abilities, not from choices made by players as instructed by those spells

question: If I have a Lonely Poro at a Battlefield and another at Base with a Zhonya's Hourglass, and my opponent plays Falling Star targeting the Battlefield Poro first then the Base Poro, will I draw from the Base Poro's Deathknell when it dies?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you will draw a card from one of the Lonely Poros. Falling Star deals all its damage before checking for lethal, so both Poros are marked to die simultaneously. Zhonya's Hourglass can save one Poro (preventing its Deathknell), but the other Poro still dies and triggers its Deathknell to draw a card.

Sequence:

Falling Star resolves completely, dealing 3 damage to the Battlefield Poro and 3 damage to the Base Poro

The game checks for lethal damage on both Poros simultaneously

Both Poros have taken lethal damage and are marked to be killed at the same time

Zhonya's Hourglass can save ONE of the Poros as a replacement effect (it is healed, exhausted, recalled, and its Deathknell does not trigger)

The other Poro dies and its Deathknell triggers, drawing you 1 card (if it was "alone" at its location)

Nuances:

Falling Star received an errata so both damage instances resolve as part of a single spell resolution, not as separate triggers

The "alone" condition for Lonely Poro checks if there were other friendly units at its location when it died

Zhonya's Hourglass is a replacement effect that prevents the unit from dying, so a saved unit never triggers Deathknell

question: If my opponent uses Falling Star against 2 of my 3 Might units while there is a Zhonya's Hourglass at base, can I choose which unit to save?
answer:
Yes, you can choose which unit to save.

According to the rules regarding replacement effects and simultaneous events, when multiple units would die at the same time, the controller of Zhonya's Hourglass chooses which unit to save.

In your scenario, Falling Star deals 3 damage to two of your 3-Might units. Because damage from a single spell resolves simultaneously, both units would die at the same time. Since Zhonya's Hourglass is a replacement effect that triggers when a unit would die, you (as the controller of the gear) get to decide which of those two death events to replace.

Important Nuances:

Timing: Zhonya's Hourglass must be face-up on the board before the damage from Falling Star is dealt. You cannot wait to see the results of the damage and then decide to flip it; it must be active to replace the death event.

One Gear per Save: If you only have one Zhonya's Hourglass, it can only save one of the two units. The other unit will die as normal.

Not a Trigger: Zhonya's Hourglass is a replacement effect, not a triggered ability. It does not use the chain and applies automatically to the death event you choose.

This is my interpretation based on the mechanics of replacement effects and simultaneous death events as outlined in the game rules. No official FAQ exists for this specific interaction with Falling Star, but it follows the established ruling for simultaneous deaths.

question: If my opponent plays Cull the Weak and I choose to kill my Irelia, Fervent, does she get +1 Might from her ability?
answer:
Ruling: No, Irelia, Fervent does not get the +1 Might bonus when killed by Cull the Weak.

Nuances:

Cull the Weak uses the structure "Each player kills a unit they control" which does not count as "choosing" or "targeting" for the purpose of triggering abilities like Irelia's

The choice is made as part of the spell's resolution by multiple players, which is treated differently from a single player choosing or targeting a unit

Even though players make a choice about which unit to kill, this type of programmatic selection does not trigger "when you choose" abilities

question: Does Confront affect token units?
answer:
Yes, Confront affects token units.

According to Rule 179.1.d, token units are units and follow all rules for their type unless otherwise specified. Because they are units, they are subject to effects that target or modify units, such as the effect of Confront, which causes units you play this turn to enter ready.

Additionally, Rule 179.1.a states that tokens are played by their owner following all applicable steps for playing a card, including any modifications from effects that created the token or other active effects like Confront.

question: For Obelisk of Power Battlefield, can you get channel 1 rune every turn?
answer:
No, you cannot get a channel effect from the Obelisk of Power battlefield every turn.

According to the card text for Obelisk of Power, its ability states: "At the start of each player's first Beginning Phase, that player channels 1 rune."

Because the effect is restricted to the "first" Beginning Phase, it only triggers once per player during the game, rather than every turn.

question: When conquering with a unit equipped with both Skyfall of Areion and Trinity Force while at 6 points, do you win the game and what is the correct timing?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you win the game by reaching 8 points. You gain 1 point from the conquer action itself (reaching 7 points), then gain 1 additional point when the Trinity Force trigger resolves from the chain (reaching 8 points).

Sequence:

You successfully conquer the battlefield with the equipped unit

You immediately score 1 point from the conquer action (6 → 7 points)

The Trinity Force "When I hold" ability (which Skyfall makes also a "When I conquer" ability) triggers and is placed on the chain

The chain state becomes CLOSED; players may play reaction cards

Once all players pass priority, the Trinity Force trigger resolves

You gain 1 point from the trigger (7 → 8 points)

You win the game upon reaching 8 points

Nuances:

Skyfall of Areion's effect does not stack; equipping multiple copies only provides additional Might, not additional triggers

The point from conquering is gained as a game action before any triggers resolve

The point from Trinity Force is gained when its triggered ability resolves from the chain

To score more points in a single conquer, you would need to equip additional copies of Trinity Force, not additional Skyfall of Areion

question: When tap a unit and play Meditation with Temporal Portal, do I draw 4 or 3?
answer:
To determine how many cards you draw, we must look at how Meditation and Temporal Portal interact.

Ruling

You draw 3 cards total.

Reasoning

Temporal Portal's Effect: When you activate Temporal Portal, it gives the next spell you play this turn the [Repeat] keyword equal to its cost. Since Meditation costs 2 energy, you have the option to pay an additional 2 energy to repeat its effect.

Meditation's Effect: Meditation has two outcomes based on whether you pay the additional cost of exhausting a friendly unit:

If you exhaust a unit: Draw 2.

If you do not exhaust a unit: Draw 1.

The Sequence:

You activate Temporal Portal (exhausting it) to grant your next spell [Repeat] (cost 2).

You play Meditation. You choose to exhaust a friendly unit to pay its additional cost.

First Resolution: Meditation resolves. Because you exhausted a unit, you draw 2 cards.

Second Resolution (Repeat): You pay the 2 energy cost to trigger the [Repeat] effect granted by the Temporal Portal. You resolve the effect of Meditation again. Since you have already paid the cost of exhausting a unit (or if you choose not to exhaust another unit for the second resolution), you draw 1 card (or 2 if you exhaust a second unit).

Note on the "3 cards" total:
If you exhaust one unit for the initial cast of Meditation, you draw 2. When you trigger the [Repeat] effect, you are repeating the effect of the spell. Since the cost of exhausting a unit was an "additional cost to play" the spell, that cost is not repeated. Therefore, the repeated effect resolves as if you did not exhaust a unit, drawing you 1 additional card, for a total of 3.

This is my interpretation based on the mechanics of [Repeat] and additional costs. No official FAQ exists for this specific interaction.

question: Can I have multiple buffs on 1 card?
answer:
No, a unit cannot have multiple buffs on one card, unless a specific card effect states otherwise.

According to CR 702.3: "There can only be one Buff on a Unit at a time."

Additionally, CR 702.3.a clarifies that if a buff is added or instructed to be added to a unit that already has a buff, it is not placed. This is also supported by the FAQ in the game rules: "A unit can only have one buff at a time unless a card specifically states otherwise."

question: If I use another effect to spend the buff on Sett, Brawler, do I get to use his effect, "Spend my buff: Give me +4 Might this turn"?
answer:
No, you do not get to use his effect if another card spends the buff.

According to the official FAQ for Sett, Brawler:
"Ruling: No, Sett must spend his own buff to activate his ability. Another card spending a buff (like Call to Glory) will not trigger Sett's ability."
