If only your units remain (e.g., if the opponent's unit left), a Non-Combat Showdown occurs (Rule 344.2).

3. Combat or Resolution

If a Combat Showdown is staged, you proceed through the Steps of Combat (Combat Damage Step, then Combat Cleanup/Recall).

If a Non-Combat Showdown is staged, the turn player initiates the showdown, and you establish control of the battlefield if only your units remain (Rule 348.2.a).

Summary

You cannot trigger a Showdown while an ability is still resolving on the chain. You must wait for the chain to fully empty. Once it empties, if the battlefield is Contested, the game will automatically transition into a Showdown (either Combat or Non-Combat) during the next cleanup or state check.

Disclaimer: This is my interpretation based on the mechanics of the Chain (LIFO resolution) and the rules for Showdowns. No official FAQ exists for this specific timing interaction.

question: If my opponent has Carrion Dredger in his base and I play Repeated Bellows, can I kill the bird token after with the second trigger of Bellows?
answer:
No, you cannot kill the Bird token created by Carrion Dredger with the second execution of a repeated Bellows Breath in this scenario.

Reasoning

Timing of Choices: According to Rule 820.2, when you pay the Repeat cost for a spell, you must make all choices for both the initial execution and the repeated execution at the Make Relevant Choices step of playing the card. This step occurs when the spell is being played, before it is finalized on the chain.

Targets Must Exist: Because you must choose all targets for both instances of the effect at the time you play the spell, any unit you intend to target must already be on the board at that moment.

Interaction: When you play Bellows Breath with Repeat, you choose your targets for the first and second executions upfront. The Bird token created by Carrion Dredger does not exist when you are making your targeting choices; therefore, it cannot be selected as a target for the second execution.

Sequence

Play Phase: You announce Bellows Breath, choose to pay the Repeat cost, and declare your targets for both the first and second executions.

Finalization: The spell is placed on the chain.

Resolution: Bellows Breath resolves. It executes its first instance of damage, then its second.

Deathknell: Because your targets were locked in during the Make Relevant Choices step of playing the spell, you cannot retroactively choose a unit that enters play as a result of the spell's own resolution.

Note: I could not fully verify this ruling against the retrieved rules.

question: Can I use an action to an opponent reaction?
answer:
No, you cannot.

According to the Showdown timing flow and Riftbound FAQ #9306, an Action spell can only be played when the state is Open (the chain is empty).

When your opponent plays a Reaction, they are starting or adding to a Closed State (a chain). While that chain exists, you are restricted to only playing cards or abilities with the Reaction keyword. You must wait for the chain to fully resolve and the state to return to Open before you have the opportunity to play an Action spell.

Why this happens:

Action spells require an Open State: You cannot start a chain with an Action if one is already in progress.

Reaction spells create a Closed State: When a Reaction is added to the chain, it closes the state, meaning no Actions can be played until that chain is cleared.

LIFO Resolution: The chain will resolve in "Last-In, First-Out" order. Even if you have priority, you are restricted by the current "Closed" state until the chain is empty again.

Sequence:

A chain is currently open/active (e.g., your opponent played a Reaction). The state is Closed.

You cannot play an Action spell.

You may only play a Reaction card to respond to the existing chain.

Once the chain resolves completely and the state becomes Open again, the player with priority may then play an Action spell.

question: Creating a Sand Soldier with Emperor's Dais gives plus 1 to another unit using Rengar's Legend?
answer:
Yes, creating a Sand Soldier token with Emperor's Dais will trigger your Pridestalker (Rengar) legend ability, allowing you to give +1 Might to another unit.

Why this works:

Playing a Token: According to RiftJudge FAQ #10901, when Emperor's Dais instructs you to "play a 2 [S] Sand Soldier unit token," this action satisfies the condition for "When you play a unit" abilities. Even though tokens are not Main Deck cards, they are units that are played.

Trigger Condition: Your Pridestalker legend ability states: "When you play a unit, give a unit +1 [S] this turn." Since playing the Sand Soldier token qualifies as playing a unit, the legend ability triggers.

Targeting: As established in RiftJudge FAQ #9769, you can choose any unit on the board as the target for this +1 Might bonus. You are not required to give it to the Sand Soldier token itself; you may choose another friendly unit to receive the bonus.

Sequence:

Conquer/Dais Ability: You activate the Emperor's Dais ability on the chain. You pay the cost and return your unit to your hand.

Resolution: The Emperor's Dais ability resolves, and you play the Sand Soldier unit token to the battlefield.

Trigger: Because you just "played a unit," your Pridestalker legend ability triggers and is placed on the chain.

Resolve Legend Ability: When the Pridestalker trigger resolves, you target a unit (other than the Sand Soldier, if you wish) to grant it +1 Might this turn.

question: Can Thrill of the Hunt instantly activate a Darius unit ability?
answer:
Yes, using Thrill of the Hunt to play Darius, Trifarian can activate his ability, provided that his entry onto the battlefield coincides with him being the second card played in your turn.

According to RiftJudge FAQs #10800, #10910, and #9495, playing a unit via a game effect (like Thrill of the Hunt) counts as "playing a card," and a card is considered fully "played" once it has resolved and entered the board. Because Darius is already on the board when his triggered ability checks for the "second card" condition, he can "see" himself as that second card.

The Sequence

Play Thrill of the Hunt: This is your first card played this turn.

Resolution: You banish a unit (which detaches any gear, per FAQ #10792).

Darius Enters: As part of the resolution of Thrill of the Hunt, you play Darius to a battlefield. He enters exhausted by default (Rule 811.1.c.3).

Trigger Check: Because Thrill of the Hunt was your first card, Darius entering the board now makes him the second card played this turn.

Ability Resolution: Darius’s triggered ability sees that he is the second card played. The ability is placed on the chain, and upon resolution, he gains +2 Might and readies himself.

Important Constraints

The "Second Card" Rule: If you had already played another card (or cards) before casting Thrill of the Hunt, Darius would become the third (or later) card played, and his ability would not trigger.

Token Exception: Tokens do not count toward the "second card" condition (FAQ #8290).

Chain Timing: Remember that units played via Thrill of the Hunt enter the board before the "when you play" trigger check happens, which is why he is able to trigger his own arrival.

question: Can I defy a sacrifice?
answer:
Yes, you can Defy a Sacrifice once it is on the chain.

However, it is important to understand the timing of when this happens. According to Rule 357 and RiftJudge FAQ #10480, the additional cost of a spell (in this case, killing a friendly Mighty unit) is paid instantly when you play the spell, before the spell is finalized and added to the chain.

The Sequence:

Announcement: The player announces they are playing Sacrifice.

Payment of Costs: The player kills a friendly Mighty unit (5+ might) as the additional cost. This unit is sent to the trash immediately.

Finalization: With the cost paid, Sacrifice is finalized and placed on the chain.

Reaction: You (the opponent) receive priority and play Defy to counter Sacrifice.

The Result:

Because the unit was already killed as a cost to play the spell, it is already in the trash by the time Defy is even played. CR 426.1.c states that countering a card does not refund any costs paid to play it. Therefore, Sacrifice is countered and cleared from the chain, but the unit sacrificed to play it remains in the trash and does not return to play.

question: Does Garbage Grabber work if I can't recycle cards?
answer:
No. Garbage Grabber's "Recycle 3 from your trash" is a cost, not an effect. Costs must be paid in full to activate the ability, so if you have fewer than 3 cards in your trash, you can't activate it at all (CR 417.3).

This is different from recycling as an effect (like Dr. Mundo), where "do as much as you can" applies. But on Garbage Grabber everything before "Draw 1" is the cost — recycle 3, pay 1 energy, and exhaust — and all three must be possible to use it.

question: Does Teemo Strategist need to pay Deflect to do the effect? If so, can they choose not to pay Deflect, and what would happen if they don't?
answer:
Yes, if you target a unit with Deflect (e.g. Deadbloom Predator), the Deflect cost is incurred once — Deflect is paid per targeting instance, not per damage.

However, you may decline to pay that cost. Under Rule 404.2 and the updated trigger cost rules, players can refuse Deflect costs incurred by triggered abilities. If you decline, the ability ceases to be a Pending Item and is removed from the Chain — it never becomes a Chain Item. This means no cards are revealed and no damage is dealt; the ability fizzles entirely.

If you do pay the Deflect cost, the ability finalizes normally: you reveal 5 cards, deal 1 damage per Hidden card revealed, then recycle.

question: If someone counters your spell, does it not count as being played for Ravenbloom Student or Abandoned Hall?
answer:
No — if a spell is countered, it does not count as being played for either Ravenbloom Student or Abandoned Hall.

Per CR 426.1.b, a card that is countered is not considered to have been played. Both abilities trigger only when a spell successfully resolves — a countered spell never reaches that point, so neither trigger fires. Multiple FAQ rulings (#9548, #8945, #10782, etc.) consistently confirm this interaction.

question: If I hide a card like Smoke & Mirrors at Battlefield B with a Sprite token at that Battlefield, then move a Lillia to Battlefield A and start Showdown, am I allowed to react with Smoke & Mirrors to swap the Sprite at Battlefield B with my Lillia?
answer:
Yes, you can do this.

Here's why: FAQ #10085 directly confirms that Smoke and Mirrors played from hidden can target a unit at the hidden battlefield (B) and another unit at a different location (A), because the card's requirement of "another unit at a different location" makes it impossible to fulfill using only targets at the hidden battlefield — an exception to the normal hidden targeting restriction.

On timing: Hidden cards gain Reaction (Rule 811.6), and FAQ #7354 confirms you can play a hidden card from one battlefield during a Showdown at a different battlefield. Since the Showdown at A is in Open State (before any chain resolves), you have Focus as the Attacker (since Lillia applied Contested), and Smoke and Mirrors has Action — you can play it.

The Sprite has Temporary, so the swap condition is satisfied. Lillia moves to B, the Sprite moves to A, and the Showdown at A continues with the Sprite there instead. This is consistent with FAQ #10888 and #11212 which cover the same Lillia + Smoke and Mirrors swap pattern during a Showdown.

One note: You must choose one unit at B (where Smoke and Mirrors is hidden) and one at a different location (A) — you cannot swap two units at locations neither of which is the hidden battlefield.

question: When Lilia Fae Fawn is the only unit at a battlefield and moves from a battlefield to base, do I still have control of the battlefield from the sprite that gets created (so no hidden card gets removed)?
answer:
Yes. When Lillia, Fae Fawn moves from a battlefield where she's the only unit, you maintain control — the Sprite token she creates will be there to keep it, and any hidden card stays put.

Here's why: Lillia's triggered ability ("When I move from a location, play a 3 Sprite token there") goes on the chain as soon as she moves. Per Rule 187.4.c, control of a battlefield cannot be lost while the turn is in a Closed State (i.e., while there are items on the chain). So the moment she moves and her trigger becomes pending, you're protected — the Sprite token then resolves and is present at that battlefield to establish control once the chain empties and the state opens.

No hidden card is removed, because you never lost control at any point. (FAQ #11108, #10369)

question: If I flash my unit back to base from Abandoned Hall, can I use the Abandoned Hall trigger to buff the unit I flashed back?
answer:
No, you cannot. The unit left Abandoned Hall during Flash's resolution, so it is no longer "here" when the Abandoned Hall trigger resolves.

Here's the sequence:

Play Flash targeting your unit at Abandoned Hall.

Flash resolves — the unit moves from Abandoned Hall to base.

Abandoned Hall trigger condition met — because Flash resolved, the "when you play a spell" condition is fulfilled.

Trigger placed on the chain — "give a unit you control here +1 [S]."

Trigger resolves — you need to choose a unit at Abandoned Hall. Your unit is at base now.

Same principle as the Challenge + Abandoned Hall FAQ (#10497): if the unit leaves Abandoned Hall during the spell's resolution, it's not there to receive the buff when the trigger resolves. Contrast this with Ride the Wind, where the unit arrives at Abandoned Hall during the spell's resolution and is there for the trigger — direction matters here.

question: Can you Not So Fast a Defy?
answer:
No. You cannot use Not So Fast to counter Defy.

Not So Fast can only counter an enemy spell or ability that "chooses a friendly unit or gear." Defy does not choose a unit or gear — it targets a spell on the chain (one costing ≤4 energy and ≤1 power). Spells are not units or gear, so Defy doesn't meet Not So Fast's targeting requirement.

This is the same reason you can't Not So Fast another Not So Fast (RiftJudge FAQ #9272) — counter spells that target other chain items simply aren't valid targets for Not So Fast.

question: Can I attack with a unit, kill it with Headless Resurrection to play an ambush unit to the battlefield that unit was attacking?
answer:
No, you cannot — once you kill your attacking unit as the cost, you no longer control any units at that battlefield, so the Ambush condition fails.

Here's why. Ambush lets you play a unit to a battlefield where you control units (Rule 822.1.b). But the condition is checked before Finalization (Rule 822.3) — if by that point you have no units at that location, Ambush no longer grants permission to play there.

The sequence is:

You attack with a unit to an occupied enemy battlefield.

You play Heedless Resurrection as a [Reaction], paying the additional cost by killing that attacking unit.

When Heedless Resurrection resolves and instructs you to play a unit from trash, you choose your Ambush unit and a destination.

By this point, the attacking unit is already in the trash. If it was your only unit there, you control no units at that battlefield → Ambush's location condition is not met → that battlefield is not a valid destination.

The general ruling from FAQ #9753 and FAQ #10961 is consistent: the attacker cannot play a unit to the contested battlefield via Heedless Resurrection. While FAQ #8743 confirms you can Ambush into an ongoing attack, that's predicated on still having units there — which you don't after killing your only attacker.

If you had multiple units attacking that same battlefield, you'd still control units there after killing one, and Ambush would let you join the combat. But killing the one and only attacker? No.

question: If I hold a Battlefield with Allay Eager Admirer, and I have Ornn, does he have 3 Deflection instead of just 2?
answer:
Yes, Ornn would have Deflect 3 in that scenario.

Here's the breakdown:

Ornn, Forge God has printed Deflect 2.

Allay, Eager Admirer grants Deflect (value defaults to 1 per Rule 809.1.b.3) to your other units at its battlefield.

Per Rule 809.2, Deflect values from multiple sources sum together.

So Ornn gets his own Deflect 2 plus the Deflect 1 from Allay, for a total of Deflect 3 — opponents must pay 3 Power (any domain) to target him.

question: What happens when I react to a Deathknell trigger of one of my units in a combat with Janna? Will all units be healed?
answer:
No, playing Janna in reaction to a Deathknell trigger after combat will not result in your units being healed by her — they've already been healed by Combat Cleanup.

Here's the sequence per the FAQs (#9514, #10157):

Combat damage is dealt.

Units with lethal damage trigger Deathknell (added as pending items).

Those units are killed (moved to trash).

Combat Cleanup heals all units in play — every unit on the board, regardless of location.

Only after that does the game return to FEPR, where the pending Deathknell triggers are placed on the chain and players get priority to respond.

So by the time you have a window to play Janna as a Reaction to the Deathknell trigger, the Combat Cleanup healing has already happened. Janna would heal "your units here" at her location, but they're already at full health from step 4. The heal is redundant — not because Janna doesn't work, but because there's nothing left to heal.

One nuance: If the Deathknell trigger itself deals damage (some do), then you could use Janna after that damage resolves to heal your units at that location. But the initial Combat Cleanup healing happens before any Deathknell triggers resolve.

question: Can Heimerdinger use the tap ability of Renata to gain a point even when not on a battlefield?
answer:
Yes. Heimerdinger can use Renata's exhaust ability from base to gain a point.

Heimerdinger copies Renata's exhaust ability (pay 4 blue, tap 4, and tap himself → Score 1 point) but does not inherit her passive battlefield restriction. That restriction is a separate line of text, not part of the exhaust ability itself (Ref: FAQ 650).

One caveat: Heimerdinger still needs 4 blue runes, 4 channeled power, and the ability to exhaust himself. And since he can only exhaust once per turn, you can only fire this ability once unless you have a way to read

question: When you score your 8th point outside your turn, do you still need to control all the battlefields?
answer:
Yes, with a key clarification: the rule is about scoring (not just controlling) all battlefields that turn.

Ruling: To win by scoring the 8th point on an opponent's turn, you must conquer every battlefield that same turn. A single conquer on the opponent's turn will only draw you a card instead.

Here's why: The only way to score outside your turn is by conquering — Hold only happens during your Beginning Phase (CR 466.2). And CR 468.1.b.2 says that when you try to gain the winning point through a Conquer, you must have Scored every Battlefield through either method this turn — otherwise you draw a card instead of getting the point.

Since you haven't held anything this turn (it's not your turn), you'd need to conquer both battlefields on that same opponent's turn to win. Conquering just one puts you at 7 while drawing a card, no win.

question: Can I choose not to target a unit with the ability of Teemo, Strategist?
answer:
No. Teemo's ability says "choose an enemy unit here" — there's no "up to" or "any number" qualifier. You must target exactly one enemy unit at his battlefield if any exist (Rule 355.13).

If at least one valid enemy unit is present when the trigger goes on the Chain, you must choose one as the target. You cannot opt to deal zero damage by declining to target.

If no valid enemy units exist at the battlefield when the trigger would finalize, the ability can't enter the Chain at all (Rule 355.8; FAQ #8572) — but that's a different scenario from choosing to withhold targeting when a legal option is available.

question: Does Forbidding Waste and Master Yi cancel each other out when a unit is damaged?
answer:
Yes, they effectively cancel each other out — the unit ends up at its printed Might regardless of damage.

Master Yi (Wuju Bladesman, Starter) gives a defending-alone unit +2 Might, while Forbidding Waste gives a defending-alone unit -2 Might. Per the arithmetic layer system (CR 474.3.d), all increases are applied first, then all decreases — so the unit gets +2, then -2, netting to its base Might.

Damage does not interact with this calculation. Damage is tracked separately from Might (Rule 142) — it doesn't reduce the stat, it just marks how close the unit is to being killed. So whether the unit has 0 damage or 10 damage, the Might calculation stays the same: base Might + 2 (Yi) − 2 (Waste) = base Might.

question: If I Hidden Blade my Recruit then my opponent in reaction uses Wages of Pain, do I still draw 2?
answer:
No, you do not draw 2 cards.

Here's why: You play Hidden Blade targeting your Recruit (Chain). Your opponent responds with Wages of Pain targeting the same Recruit (added on top). Wages of Pain resolves first — it deals 3 damage and kills the Recruit, sending it to the trash. When Hidden Blade then tries to resolve, its target (the Recruit) is no longer at a battlefield. Because Hidden Blade cannot identify "its controller" from a unit that no longer exists, the draw instruction fails and no cards are drawn.

This is the same principle as FAQ #3700 / #3182: if the targeted unit leaves the battlefield before Hidden Blade resolves — whether by kill, retreat, or any other means — the draw does not happen.

question: If Vex is on a BF and a unit is played with Aurora at the end of turn, is it stunned the turn after?
answer:
Yes, the unit is stunned and will remain stunned into the next turn.

Here's the timing breakdown:

Ending Step (317.1) — Dazzling Aurora's end-of-turn trigger fires. The unit is played.

Vex, Apathetic triggers ("When an opponent plays a unit while I'm at a battlefield, [Stun] it") and resolves, stunning the unit.

Expiration Step (317.2) — All units heal, and "this turn" effects expire (Vex's "can't move it this turn" wears off).

Turn ends.

The key rule is 423.1.a.2: Stunned units lose the status "at the beginning of the next Ending Step." Since the stun was applied during this turn's Ending Step, the next Ending Step is the next turn's Ending Step. So the unit enters your opponent's turn still stunned, and can't contribute its Might to combat damage until the next turn's Ending Step begins.

Vex's "can't move it this turn" clause does expire during the Expiration Step, but the Stunned status itself persists — they are separate effects with different durations.

question: If I have Spirit Wheel and then play Cull the Weak and kill one of my units with it, have I chosen a unit and thus be able to draw a card with Spirit Wheel?
answer: No. Cull the Weak does not target or "choose" a unit in the game-mechanics sense — the choice happens during resolution, not when the spell is placed on the chain. Spirit Wheel triggers when you choose (i.e., target) a friendly unit, and Cull the Weak's instruction is a non-targeting resolution choice (Rule 355.10.e). So you don't get the draw off Spirit Wheel.

question: If you play Switcheroo from hand, do you get a draw with Yordle Explorer?
answer:
Yes, you draw a card — Yordle Explorer triggers when Switcheroo is played from Hidden.

Yordle Explorer checks the printed Power cost on the card, not what you actually paid. Switcheroo has a printed Power cost of 2 (A A), so it satisfies the "cost 2 or more" condition even though playing it from Hidden costs 0.

This is the same principle as Lux triggering on discounted spells or Yordle Explorer triggering on cards with Repeat — the printed value is what matters (FAQ #6912, confirmed by #8453 and #8807).

question: If I attack an occupied battlefield with both Lucian Gunslinger and Warwick Hunter, would the Lucian attack trigger enable Warwick's attack trigger?
answer:
Yes, you can. Both are "When I attack" triggers that fire simultaneously when both units gain the Attacker designation. Since you control both, you choose the order they go on the Chain (Rule 383.3.d). Put Lucian's trigger on top (resolves first) — he deals damage to an enemy unit at that battlefield — then Warwick's trigger resolves and kills all damaged enemy units there.

This is directly confirmed by FAQ #1361: the same sequencing works for Crackshot Corsair dealing 1 damage followed by Warwick's kill effect. Just note that Lucian's damage is equal to his Assault value — while he's an attacker, that's the stat bonus shown on his card.

question: If I repeat Bellows Breath, does it target twice so I can't activate Ezreal Prodigal Explorer?
answer:
No — Repeat helps you activate Ezreal, it doesn't block you.

When you pay the Repeat cost for Bellows Breath, you make choices for both instances during the Make Relevant Choices step of playing the spell (Rule 820.2). That means you choose enemy units for the first volley and enemy units for the second volley — both sets of choices happen before the spell even goes on the chain. Since you've now chosen enemy units twice with the same spell, you satisfy Ezreal, Prodigal Explorer's "chosen enemy units and/or gear twice this turn" condition.

This is consistent with FAQ #9742 on Frigid Touch + Repeat and Ezreal: targeting with the initial effect and again with the repeated effect counts as two instances of choosing.

So you can cast Bellows Breath with Repeat targeting enemy units, and once the spell is on the chain, you can exhaust Ezreal (if you have priority in an Open State or after the chain resolves) to draw 1 — condition met.

question: When I have Darius Trifarian and my opponent has a Vex on the battlefield, I played my Darius after killing the Vex, but I played the Darius Trifarian as the fifth card on my turn, so does my Darius enter ready, or does he need to be the second card or see the second card played in order to be ready?
answer:
No, Darius enters exhausted. His ability only triggers when he is exactly the second card played in your turn. Playing him as the fifth card means the condition ("second card") has already passed — he won't see it and won't ready himself.

This is consistent across multiple rulings (FAQ #3905, #7612, #9420). Darius can count himself as the second card if he is the second card, but as the fifth card he's past that window entirely. The fact that you killed Vex first is irrelevant to his trigger condition — only the card order matters.

question: If I am holding Grove of the Garden with Blue Sentinel, do I draw 2 cards extra?
answer:
Yes, you draw 2 cards total — that's 1 extra card beyond the normal 1.

When you hold the battlefield where Blue Sentinel is at Grove of the God-Willow, Blue Sentinel's passive causes all your hold effects at that battlefield to trigger an additional time. Grove's "When you hold here, draw 1" triggers normally once, then a second time, for a total of 2 draws. You do not draw 3 cards (the extra trigger gives +1 additional draw, not +2).

Blue Sentinel also makes its own "When I hold, Add [A]" trigger twice, giving you 2 Power at the start of your next Main Phase.

question: Baited Hook on Glasc Mixologist → finds Harnessed Dragon which occurs first, Harnessed Dragon entering the battlefield or Glasc Mixologist deathknell?
answer:
Harnessed Dragon's "When you play me" resolves first. Glasc Mixologist's Deathknell resolves after.

Here's the full sequence:

Baited Hook begins resolving — kills Glasc Mixologist.

Glasc Mixologist's Deathknell trigger is created as a pending item (before it moves to trash, per Rule 808.1.d.2).

Baited Hook continues — you look at top 5, find and play Harnessed Dragon.

Harnessed Dragon enters and its "When you play me" (WYPM) ability becomes a pending item on the chain.

During FEPR, both pending items finalize in the order they were created: Deathknell first, then WYPM. But the chain resolves LIFO — newest item first.

So the resolution order is:

1st to resolve: Harnessed Dragon's WYPM — kill an enemy unit.

2nd to resolve: Glasc Mixologist's Deathknell — play a unit (cost ≤ 3 and ≤ A) from your trash.

This means if you kill an enemy unit with Harnessed Dragon first, you can then use the Deathknell to revive something from your trash afterward — the board state may have changed in between.

question: Am I able to decline to pay the Deflect cost, fizzling the Deathknell ability of the Ruined Rex when it dies?
answer:
Yes, you can decline to pay the Deflect cost, and the Deathknell ability will be removed from the Chain without resolving.

Here's how it works step by step:

Ruined Rex dies → its Deathknell triggers automatically (you cannot opt out of the trigger — it's mandatory per Rule 808.1).

When the Deathknell trigger tries to finalize on the Chain, it must choose a target enemy unit. If that unit has Deflect, the ability incurs a mandatory additional cost of [A] (1 Power).

However, CR 405.2 gives a special exception for triggered abilities: "players may decline to pay for Triggered Abilities that have incurred a cost. If they do, the ability will cease being a Pending Item and be removed from the Chain."

If you decline, the Deathknell never becomes a Chain Item and does nothing. No damage is dealt.

This is confirmed by FAQ #5102 (Ahri Inquisitive's triggered ability + Deflect) — the same principle applies here. The Patch Notes from 2025-10-24 also note this is a specific design choice: "Players can now refuse Deflect costs incurred by triggered abilities."

One nuance: this is not "fizzling" — Riftbound doesn't use that term. The ability simply fails to finalize and is removed before it ever enters the Chain. Also, this only applies to triggered abilities (like Deathknell). For spells, Deflect remains a mandatory cost you cannot decline (FAQ #9431).

question: Can I play Rengar Trophy Hunter as a reaction to an open Battlefield?
answer:
No. Rengar, Trophy Hunter cannot be played to an open battlefield.

An open battlefield is unoccupied and uncontrolled — it has no enemy units (Rule 169.10.c). Rengar's card text lets him Ambush to "a battlefield where there are enemy units," and an open battlefield has none. The standard Ambush keyword also requires "a battlefield where you control Units" (Rule 822.1.b), which you don't at an open battlefield. Neither condition is met.

Even outside of Ambush, units can only be played to your Base or a Battlefield you Control (Rule 813.3.a). An open battlefield is uncontrolled, so standard play rules don't permit it either.

question: If Fiora Peerless is defending alone with Master Yi Legend, and my opponent attacks with 1 enemy, do I go to 10 might or 8 might?
answer:
You go to 10 Might.

Here's why:

Master Yi's bonus (+2) is a passive ability — it applies immediately in the Arithmetic layer the moment Fiora is designated as the lone defender. Her Might becomes 3 (base) + 2 = 5.

Fiora's "When I defend" is a triggered ability — it goes on the Initial Chain. When it resolves, it doubles her current Might (which is already 5 thanks to Yi), so 5 × 2 = 10.

This is confirmed by FAQs #10960 and #11088 — the passive applies first, then the trigger doubles the boosted value. You don't double the base 3 to 6 and then add Yi's +2 (which would give 8). The layering order and the fact that passives are applied before triggers resolve guarantees 10.

question: I play Heedless Resurrection and kill my Fizz as additional cost. Can I resurrect that Fizz for the Heedless?
answer:
No, you cannot resurrect the same Fizz you killed to pay the cost.

Why: When playing Heedless Resurrection, targets are chosen before costs are paid (step 2 of playing a card). Fizz is still on the board at that point — not in the trash — so he's not a legal target. By the time you kill him as the additional cost (step 4), the target choice is already locked in and cannot be changed (Rule 355.15). You'd need to pick a different unit already in your trash.

FAQ #9523 confirms this ruling directly.

question: If my unit is holding a gear, can I recycle a card to equip it to another unit even if they don't have weapon master?
answer:
No — not while it's already attached to another unit.

When a gear is attached, its printed Rules Text (including the Equip ability) becomes Inactive (Rules 135.4, 718.2). Inactive abilities "cannot be activated" (Rule 721.2). So the Equip cost that includes "Recycle 2 from your trash" is unavailable — you can't pay it to move the gear directly.

The only built-in exception is Weaponmaster, which is specifically allowed to reference an attached gear's Inactive Equip ability (Rule 725.3) and transfer it.

How you can do it without Weaponmaster:

Let the unit die — unattached gear at a battlefield gets Recalled to your Base during the next Cleanup (CR 454.1). Once it's back at your Base unattached, its Rules Text becomes Active again, and you can activate the Equip ability normally (paying the recycle + power cost) to attach it to a different unit.

Play it fresh — if the gear is in your hand or at your Base unattached, you can activate its Equip ability right away. For Last Rites, that means paying [C] and recycling 2 cards from your trash to attach it to the unit you want.

question: If my opponent attacks with yellow Vi and tries to stun my unit, I react with Janna to push it back to base. Does the Vi stun still apply?
answer:
No, the stun does not resolve.

Here's the sequence:

Vi attacks, and her "When I attack, [Stun] an enemy unit here" trigger goes on the chain.

You play Janna, Savior as a [Reaction]. Janna resolves first (LIFO) — she heals your units and moves Vi to its owner's base.

When Vi's trigger attempts to resolve, it needs to check "here" — Vi's current location — to define where the stun happens. Since Vi is now at base rather than the battlefield, the ability fails to find its source location and does nothing.

This is consistent with established rulings — the term "here" is referenced from the source of the ability, and that information is checked on execution (Rule 359.3.f.2). If Vi is no longer at the battlefield when her trigger tries to resolve, the instruction mistargets and the stun is not applied.

question: I move a unit to a battlefield. The opponent reacts with Rengar Trophy Hunter. I play Vi Peacekeeper. Does Vi stun?
answer:
Yes, Vi stuns.

You moved into an occupied battlefield, making you the Attacker. The opponent then plays Rengar via Ambush (as Defender). When you respond by playing Vi, Peacekeeper via Ambush, she enters the ongoing combat and is designated as an attacker — this triggers her "When I attack" ability, letting you stun an enemy unit at that battlefield.

This is directly supported by FAQ #10034 and FAQ #10437: units entering mid-combat gain the Attacker or Defender designation upon entry based on which side played them, and Vi's trigger fires exactly once when she first gains that designation. As long as she's still on the battlefield when her trigger resolves (not removed by a reaction), the stun goes through.

question: For Ivern Brush and Power Nexus, if I remove the Brush, can I still use the Power Nexus after?
answer:
It depends on the timing — specifically, which turn you swap back and try to use Power Nexus.

On the same turn you swap back: No. When you score at Brush (which allows the swap back), that's already a score at that battlefield location this turn. When Power Nexus returns via the swap back (CR 439.7.b), it inherits "all current effects and statuses" — including the fact that this battlefield has already been scored this turn. CR 467 says you can only score once per battlefield per turn. So you cannot use Power Nexus's ability to score again that same turn.

On a future turn after swapping back: Yes. On a new turn, the per-turn scoring limit resets. You can move a unit to Power Nexus, satisfy "When you hold here," and pay [A][A][A][A] to score 1 point via its ability. The swap-back fully restores Power Nexus to that battlefield spot — it's just that the turn you swapped back is locked out for additional scoring at that location.

question: Does Eye of the Herald spawn where I moved or where I moved from?
answer:
The token is spawned at the destination — where you moved to, not from.

Eye of the Herald reads "here," and the game checks the unit's location when the trigger resolves. At that point the unit is at its new location (the destination), so "here" refers to the battlefield it moved to. This is confirmed across multiple RiftJudge FAQs (#11204, #11375).

question: Is there a limit to how many times I can attack the same battlefield? If I send in a Skuttle, after it dies, can I send in other units to start a new showdown?
answer:
Yes, there's no hard limit. You can initiate as many showdowns at the same battlefield in one turn as you can afford to move units there.

Here's how it plays out with Scuttle Crab:

You move Scuttle Crab to a battlefield you don't control → it becomes Contested, a showdown starts.

During that showdown, Scuttle Crab dies (it's 0 Might, so any damage kills it).

When the showdown closes, you have no units there → the opponent keeps (or re-establishes) control.

Back in Main Phase / Open State, you move another unit in → battlefield becomes Contested again → a new showdown begins.

Repeat as many times as you have ready units and movement phases to spare. Each one is a fresh showdown. The only real limits are movement resources (units cost exhaust to move), timing (Standard Moves only during your Main Phase in Open State, not during an ongoing showdown), and the once-per-battlefield scoring cap (you won't get a second Conquer/Hold point that turn — CR 467).

As FAQ #6149 states: "There can be as many showdowns in a turn as a player can legally enact, limited primarily by movement resources and ready units."

question: How does Teemo's defense ability work on a chain, do I have to choose which unit to target first, or do I just reveal my 5? Where is the window of that chain to react/counter to?
answer:
Yes, you choose the target first, then the opponent can react, then you reveal. Here's the exact order:

Teemo gains Defender designation (during combat setup, or immediately if revealed from Hidden mid-combat per FAQ #8317).

The "When I defend" trigger goes on the Chain as a pending item.

During finalization (while the trigger is still pending), you choose the target — "an enemy unit here." Targets are locked at finalization, not resolution (Rule 352.4.b).

The trigger becomes a Chain Item. Now the opponent gets priority — since they control the newest item on the Chain (Rule 340.4), they can play Reaction-speed spells/abilities. This window opens before any cards are revealed.

If both players pass, the ability resolves — you reveal 5 cards, deal 1 per Hidden card revealed, then recycle.

Key takeaways:

You cannot wait to see what you reveal to then pick a target — the target is chosen in step 3, before you ever see the cards.

The opponent cannot wait until after you reveal to react — their window is in step 4, before resolution.

If they kill or recall Teemo with a Reaction in step 4, the ability still resolves since it's already on the Chain (it just won't deal damage if the target is gone or Teemo's zone changed prevented the reveal).

And no, they can't play Action-speed spells during this window — only Reactions are allowed in a Closed State.

question: When does a combat end?
answer:
Combat ends after the Resolution Step (CR 463), specifically at step 461.7 — when Attacker/Defender designations are removed and all "this combat" effects expire.

The full path is:

Combat Showdown ends when both players pass Focus without playing anything (Rule 348).

That triggers the Combat Damage Step — damage is assigned and dealt (CR 462).

Then the Resolution Step runs: Combat Cleanup (heal all units, recall attackers if defenders remain) → determine combat result → establish control/conquer → then combat officially ends at 461.7.

So a combat effectively ends once the Resolution Step tasks complete, but the showdown that kicks it off only ends when both players consecutively pass Focus with an empty Chain (FAQ #608, #9669).

question: If I hit a unit with 4 might with a Wages of Pain on the Forbidden Waste battlefield and then move in with a unit, can my opponent react with a Hidden Zhonyas to save their card at the battlefield or does it die automatically from the move trigger?
answer:
Yes, your opponent can react with a hidden Zhonya's — but only if they do it before Wages of Pain resolves.

Here's the full sequence:

The 4 Might unit at Forbidding Waste has -2 Might from the battlefield (defending alone), so its effective Might is 2.

Wages of Pain goes on the chain. Your opponent gets a priority window here (Closed State, Reaction timing). They can reveal hidden Zhonya's now — it enters as a gear permanent with its replacement effect active.

Wages resolves, dealing 3 damage. The unit now has 3 damage on 2 Might = lethal.

Cleanup occurs. During cleanup (Rule 320), "Legal Items cannot be executed" — meaning the opponent cannot play Zhonya's from hidden once cleanup has started. The unit would die here.

If Zhonya's was already revealed in step 2, its replacement effect fires in cleanup: "kill this instead. Heal that unit, exhaust it, and recall it" — saving the unit.

If the opponent passes priority and lets Wages resolve without revealing Zhonya's, the unit will die during the subsequent cleanup with no window to save it. There is no "move trigger" that kills it — the lethal damage from Wages is what kills it during cleanup, and the move action happens after that cleanup is complete (per FAQ #11041).

question: Can my opponent reach to me playing a Spinning Axe and attaching it to an Over Zealous Fan with a Gust?
answer:
Yes, your opponent can play Gust in response to your Spinning Axe.

Here's the sequence:

You play Spinning Axe (via Quick-Draw, which gives it [Reaction]) targeting your Overzealous Fan to attach. This puts Spinning Axe on the chain.

The state becomes Closed. Your opponent responds with Gust (also [Reaction]) targeting your Overzealous Fan. Gust goes on the chain on top.

Resolving LIFO: Gust resolves first — your Overzealous Fan (2 Might ≤ 3) is returned to your hand.

Spinning Axe then resolves — it tries to attach to the Fan, but the Fan is no longer on the board, so the attachment instruction is ignored and the Axe enters the battlefield unattached (or is recalled during the next cleanup).

This is the same interaction covered in FAQ #9813 — a Reaction spell like Gust can always be played in response to a chain item, and it will resolve before the item it's responding to.

question: Irelia is exhausted at base. I play en-garde on it and also use Irelia's legend ability to ready her. At the moment, how much might would she be at?
answer:
Irelia starts at printed Might 4, exhausted at your base. Here's the full breakdown:

En Garde targets/chooses Irelia → triggers her ability (+1 from being chosen). Simultaneously, Blade Dancer triggers (choosing a friendly unit) → you exhaust it and pay [A] to ready Irelia.

Blade Dancer resolves — Irelia goes from exhausted to ready → triggers her ability again (+1 from being readied).

Irelia's "chosen" trigger resolves — another +1.

En Garde resolves — gives +1 Might (base effect), and if Irelia is the only unit you control at that location, an additional +1.

Final result:

Alone at base: 4 + 1 (chosen) + 1 (readied) + 2 (En Garde) = 8 Might

Other friendly units also at base: 4 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 7 Might

question: Can I play Grim Apothecary to base and use its effect as a reaction to an opponent attacking a battlefield that I control? Or does it need to be played at that contested battlefield?
answer:
No. You cannot play Grim Apothecary to your base as a reaction to an opponent attacking. To use its Ambush timing, you must play it to a battlefield where you control units.

Why: Ambush grants Reaction timing only conditionally — specifically when playing the unit to a battlefield where you control units (Rule 822.1.b, FAQ #10089). Playing it to your base doesn't meet that condition, so it's a normal Main Phase play only.

What you can do: If the opponent attacks a battlefield where you still have units, you can use Ambush to play Grim Apothecary to that battlefield as a Reaction during the Showdown. Once it enters, its "When you play me" trigger goes on the chain, and you can return a friendly unit (even itself, per FAQ #9746) to your hand — which could save a unit from dying in combat. However, the battlefield must still have at least one of your units there when you finish playing it, or Ambush's permission no longer applies (Rule 822.3).

question: I am playing Darius. I play Cleave. Opponent uses Hard Bargain (non-repeated). Can I pay 1 energy and use Darius Legend Ability to pay Hard Bargain's effect?
answer:
Yes. You can activate Darius's Legend ability during Hard Bargain's resolution to generate the energy you need to pay the [2].

Here's how it works:

Hard Bargain is on the Chain above Cleave. When it resolves, it gives you the option to pay [2] or have Cleave countered. This payment happens during the resolution of Hard Bargain.

Darius's ability (exhaust → [Reaction], [Legion] — [Add] 1 energy) is an activated ability that Adds resources and has Reaction. Per CR 430.3, such abilities can be activated "during the playing or resolution of other spells and abilities, any time that those spells or abilities require resources be paid." And per Rule 430.2, it "immediately finalizes and resolves, even during the resolution of spells and abilities."

Since you've already played Cleave this turn, Darius's condition ("Get the effect if you've played a card this turn") is satisfied.

Sequence: When Hard Bargain asks you to pay [2], you activate Darius (exhaust him, add 1 energy to your Rune Pool), then pay that 1 energy plus 1 more energy from your runes/channeled sources to meet the [2] cost. Cleave is saved from being countered.

Note: Darius only generates 1 energy, so you still need to supply the other 1 energy from your Rune Pool (runes or other sources).

question: When Alpha Strike chooses multiple enemy units, can I choose to deal 0 damage to one of those units?
answer:
No. Each unit you target with Alpha Strike must receive at least 1 damage.

Per Rule 355.14.g, "Valid damage is a positive integer amount, greater than or equal to 1 damage." Since Alpha Strike splits damage and each chosen unit is a target, you cannot assign 0 to one of them — that wouldn't be valid damage. If you target 3 units, you must have at least 3 total damage to split (1 to each).

question: If my opponent is at 7, and he plays Baron Nashor, do the points received from Baron's ability "make a Baron pit and play me to it" give them the final point to win the game? Or would they draw a card if they had not scored all battlefields that turn?
answer:
No, playing Baron Nashor from 7 points does not automatically give them the win. They still must satisfy the Final Point conquer restriction.

The ruling: If they have scored every battlefield in play that turn (including the newly created Baron Pit), they win. If they have not scored every battlefield, they draw a card instead.

Here's how it breaks down in standard 1v1 (Victory Score 8):

Normally there are 2 battlefields. Baron creates a 3rd (Baron Pit).

To win via Conquer at the final point, CR 468.1.b.2 requires they have scored every battlefield that turn — meaning all 3.

Example — they win: Opponent starts at 6 points → holds one battlefield (scores to 7) → conquers the other original battlefield → plays Baron, conquering Baron Pit. They've scored all 3 battlefields this turn (one by hold, two by conquer) — they gain the 8th point and win.

Example — they draw: Opponent starts their turn already at 7 points (e.g., from last turn) → plays Baron, creating and conquering Baron Pit. They've only scored 1 battlefield (Baron Pit) this turn, not the 2 original ones. Per CR 468.1.b.2, they draw a card and stay at 7 points.

Baron's ability doesn't bypass the Final Point rule — it just adds a third target you also need to have scored that turn.

question: If Fiora Peerless has a +1 might buff from Pit Rookie, does that also count towards her might being doubled when she defends or attacks 1 on 1?
answer:
Yes, the +1 Might buff from Pit Rookie counts toward Fiora's doubling.

When Fiora, Peerless's trigger resolves, it doubles her current total Might — not just her base printed value. With a buff counter from Pit Rookie, her Might is 4 (3 base + 1 buff), so the trigger gives her +4, making her 8 Might for that combat.

This is consistent with how all passive Might modifiers work with Fiora. FAQ #10971 directly confirms she doubles total Might including equipment bonuses, and FAQ #11168/FAQ #11471 show the same principle applies to other passive modifiers (like Master Yi or Discipline) — they're already factored in when the trigger resolves, so the doubling includes them.

question: If I played a spell and opponent played Hard Bargain, does it count as I played 1 spell to +1 Might for Ravenbloom?
answer:
No. Ravenbloom Student does not gain +1 Might if the spell you played gets countered by Hard Bargain.

A card is only considered "played" once it resolves (CR 420.4.a–b). If Hard Bargain counters your spell before resolution — whether because you chose not to pay [2] or couldn't — the spell never resolves, so it doesn't count as "played." Ravenbloom Student's trigger condition ("When you play a spell") is not met. This is consistent across all counter effects (Defy, Hard Bargain, etc.) — it doesn't matter how the spell gets countered, only that it didn't resolve.

question: Does Shadows Call trigger if you kill the unit Reaction Speed?
answer:
Yes, you still draw 2. If the unit targeted by Shadow's Call is killed at reaction speed while the spell is on the chain, the spell still resolves — you just miss the "Give it [Temporary]" part.

Here's why: Shadow's Call has two instructions — "Give it [Temporary]" (which requires the targeted unit) and "Draw 2" (which doesn't target anything). Per Rule 359.3.e.11, instructions that can be partially followed are followed as much as possible. The "Give it [Temporary]" instruction fizzles because the target is gone (Rule 359.3.e.7), but "Draw 2" has no target dependency, so it executes normally.

question: To set the circumstance: I play Akshan, mischievous and take my opponent's B.F. Sword on my turn, on their following turn they play an Akshan, mischievous and take that B.F. Sword back—if at this point I then kill their Akshan, mischievous, what happens to their B.F. Sword?
answer:
You regain control of the B.F. Sword.

Here's why: When you played your Akshan first (stealing the sword), you created a control-change effect that lasts "until I leave the board." Your opponent's Akshan created a newer control-change effect that overrode yours via timestamp order. When you kill their Akshan, their effect stops applying. The game recalculates control, and since your Akshan is still on the board, your original control-change effect becomes active again — you take the B.F. Sword back.

(FAQ #8851 and #10776 both directly confirm this result.)

question: Do Reflection Unit tokens have temporary if it doesn't copy?
answer:
No. A Reflection token does not inherently have Temporary.

Per Rule 184.6, a Reflection token is defined as just a "domainless unit token with 0 Might" — no Temporary keyword. Compare that with the Sprite token (184.2), which explicitly does list Temporary as part of its identity.

Temporary on a Reflection token only comes from the specific effect that creates it. Both Mirror Image and Deceiver (LeBlanc) say: play a Reflection token, then make it a copy of a unit and give it Temporary. That's a reflexive trigger that does both things together. If the copy part fails (e.g. no valid target), the Temporary part still resolves — but only because the effect grants it, not because the token has it by default.

question: If Lonely Poro is on a battlefield with Zhonya's Hidden, can I react with Zhonya's Hidden to its death trigger?
answer:
Yes, you can play Zhonya's from hidden in reaction to the Deathknell trigger, but it won't save the Lonely Poro.

When Lonely Poro dies, its Deathknell trigger is added to the chain, putting the game into a Closed state — this opens the window to play Reaction cards (including hidden Zhonya's, which gains Reaction when played from facedown per Rule 811.6). You can absolutely play Zhonya's then.

However, Zhonya's is a replacement effect — it must be active before the death event to replace it (Rule 369.1). By the time the Deathknell trigger is on the chain, the Poro has already died and been sent to trash. Playing Zhonya's now won't retroactively save it. You'll get the Zhonya's onto the board (killing itself since the Poro's death already happened), and the Deathknell will still resolve — you draw 1 as long as the Poro died alone.

question: If I control a bf with Lonely Poro and I hide a Zhonyas there, my opponent attacks with Vex and kills my Poro, can I react to the Deathknell with Zhonyas or my Zhonyas would die before because I don't control units at the battlefield?
answer:
Yes, you can flip Zhonya's in response to the Deathknell trigger — but it won't save the Poro, and the Zhonya's itself is fine.

Here's why each part works:

1. You can react to the Deathknell trigger. When Lonely Poro dies, its Deathknell goes on the chain, entering a Closed State. Your hidden Zhonya's gains Reaction (Rule 811), so you can flip it in response to that trigger on the chain. You have a window.

2. It won't save the Lonely Poro. Zhonya's is a replacement effect ("if a friendly unit would die") — it needs to be active before the death occurs to replace it. The Poro's death already happened by the time its Deathknell trigger hits the chain. Flipping Zhonya's now gets it on the board but can't retroactively undo the kill (FAQ #10998).

3. Your Zhonya's won't "die" from losing the battlefield. While a Combat is ongoing at that battlefield, you don't lose control of it — Rule 187.4.b says control can't change during Combat, and Rule 187.4.c specifically exempts battlefields with an ongoing Combat. And even if you did lose control (e.g. after combat ends), gear isn't killed by losing the battlefield — it stays where it is as your permanent, independent of who controls the location. Unattached gear at a battlefield gets recalled in cleanup (Rule 149.3), but that's a separate process, not a kill.

question: If my opponent uses a Wages of Pain on my 4 might unit at a Forbidding Waste battlefield and then moves a unit onto the battlefield, do I have an opportunity to use flash before my unit dies?
answer:
Yes — you have a window to use Flash before your unit dies.

Here's the timing breakdown:

Wages of Pain goes on the Chain → State becomes Closed. You get priority to play Reaction spells/abilities.

Flash is a [Reaction], so you can play it right now. It goes on the Chain above Wages.

Flash resolves first (LIFO) — you move your unit to Base. It's now safe.

Wages then tries to resolve, but your unit is no longer at the battlefield. The damage instruction can't be executed (illegal target), so it's ignored. (The Gold token is still made as a separate instruction — FAQ #9528.)

If you don't Flash during that window, Wages deals 3 damage. Your 4-Might unit at Forbidding Waste alone has effective Might 2 (from the -2 penalty), so 3 damage = lethal. It dies in the ensuing Cleanup before your opponent can move a unit in (FAQ #11041).

So the only window to save your unit is while Wages of Pain is on the Chain. Once it resolves and Cleanup starts, there's no further opportunity to react.

question: Can you play Starcrossed when I don't have a unit?
answer:
No. You cannot play Star-Crossed unless you control a friendly unit on the board.

The spell reads "Return a friendly unit and an enemy unit to their owners' hands." Both are mandatory targets — there is no "up to" language. At the time you announce the spell and place it on the chain, you must have a friendly unit to target. If you don't control any unit, the targeting requirement can't be met and the spell can't be played.

question: At what point do you get the point for conquering? Is it after combat resolves?
answer:
You get the point immediately when you Establish Control after a Showdown or Combat resolves — it's a game action, not a triggered ability on the Chain.

Here's the precise sequence (CR 463.5, 466.1, 468, and FAQ #8622/#6175):

The Showdown (Combat or Non-Combat) resolves.

Establish Control — the player with units remaining takes control of the battlefield. Contested is cleared.

If that player has not already scored this battlefield this turn, this constitutes a Conquer — and they gain the point immediately (CR 468).

Then, any "when I conquer" triggered abilities (from units or the battlefield itself) are placed on the Chain as Pending Items.

So: point first, triggers second. The point is not a triggered effect — it happens instantly as part of the Conquer, before anyone gets priority to react.

question: Can you use a reaction at any point on your turn or can a reaction be only played in response to your opponent playing an action?
answer:
Yes, you can play Reaction cards on your turn whenever you have priority — they don't need something to respond to.

Reaction grants all the permissions of Action (Rule 813.1.b), meaning it can be played during Open States on your turn like any regular spell. The Reaction keyword additionally lets you play it during Closed States (when a chain exists) on any player's turn (Rule 813.1.c.1).

So on your turn, you can:

Play a Reaction to start a chain with an empty stack, just like an Action spell.

Play additional Reactions in response to something already on the chain.

Play a Reaction during a Showdown Open State (when you have Focus/Priority).

The only restriction is that during your opponent's turn, you generally need a trigger (a spell, ability, or Showdown) to gain priority and play a Reaction — you can't just fire one off randomly. But on your own turn, treat them as fully functional spells you can play at any appropriate timing window.

question: Does Imperial Decree kill units on the Frozen Fortress battlefield during my turn when I play it and there are enemy units there?
answer:
No, playing Imperial Decree during your Main Phase will not kill units already damaged by Frozen Fortress that turn.

Frozen Fortress deals its 1 damage at the start of the Beginning Phase — before your Main Phase. Imperial Decree only triggers on damage taken after it resolves. It does not look back at damage events that already happened earlier in the turn (FAQ #11279, #10843).

However, if you play Imperial Decree on your turn and it remains active until the next Beginning Phase (including your opponent's), then when Frozen Fortress deals 1 damage at that time, Imperial Decree will trigger and kill those damaged units (FAQ #10596).

question: Does using the spell Challenge count as combat?
answer:
No, using Challenge does not count as combat.

Challenge is a spell — it causes two units to deal damage to each other equal to their Might, but this is a non-combat interaction (FAQ #11387, #8835). Combat in Riftbound is a specific game phase that only occurs when a battlefield is Contested and units controlled by opposing players are present, triggering the structured Showdown → Combat Damage → Combat Cleanup sequence (CR 456–460). Challenge bypasses all of that entirely.

This matters for a few things: a stunned unit can deal damage through Challenge (stun only blocks combat damage, FAQ #3841), Challenge won't trigger "when I win a combat" effects like Draven, Audacious (FAQ #8835), and the damage dealt persists on those units until either any combat resolves (which heals all units) or the turn ends (FAQ #7781).

question: If I play Rengar, Trophy Hunter as a reaction when my opponent moves a unit into a battlefield, do Assault or Shield abilities still trigger?
answer:
Assault and Shield are both passive abilities (not triggered abilities) — they don't "trigger" at all. They apply continuously while their conditions are met. But the timing matters here.

During the non-combat showdown (while the chain is resolving your Rengar play and before combat begins): Neither applies. Combat hasn't started yet. Assault requires being "an attacker during Combat" (Rule 807.1.d) and Shield requires being "a defender during Combat" (Rule 814.1.d). During the initial non-combat showdown, the Attacker/Defender designations exist (FAQ #10937), but no combat is ongoing, so the keyword conditions aren't satisfied.

Once combat officially begins (after the chain empties and both players pass focus): Both apply. The opponent's unit retains the Attacker designation (CR 461.2.b) — if it has Assault, it gets +X Might. Rengar retains the Defender designation — if he had Shield (he doesn't, but the principle stands for any defending unit), he'd get +X Might.

In short: Assault and Shield are dormant during the non-combat showdown phase, but kick in as soon as combat starts and the designations carry over.

question: If I am defending with a Fiora Peerless and my enemy attacks with 2 units but Starcross one of them away, does my Fiora Peerless trigger at any point?
answer:
No, Fiora's ability does not trigger.

Fiora's "When I attack or defend one on one" checks the one-on-one condition only at the exact moment she gains the Defender designation — when combat first begins. At that point, there were 2 enemy attackers, so the condition wasn't met, and the trigger never goes on the chain. (Rule 383.4.f.2.b: if the trigger condition contains other requirements and they aren't fulfilled when the unit gains the Defender designation, it won't trigger.)

Removing one attacker later with Star-Crossed doesn't help — Attack/Defend triggers are checked once per combat (Rule 383.4.f.2.a). Fiora already missed her window.

question: There is a showdown on the battlefield Altar of Blood. At the end of this showdown, units from each side are about to die from damages. Which player chooses first to pay the 3 power cost to save their unit?
answer:
Ruling: The turn player chooses first to pay for their units, then the other player in turn order.

Here's why: At the end of combat, all units with lethal damage die simultaneously during the Cleanup (CR 323.4). Altar of Blood creates a replacement effect for each dying unit — "its controller may pay [A][A][A] to heal it, exhaust it, and recall it instead." Each unit's death is a separate event, and each player decides for their own units.

Per Rule 373.1, when replacement effects from different controllers apply to simultaneous events, they execute in turn order. So the turn player makes their pay/decline decisions first for their dying units, followed by the other player.

question: When Mageseeker is on my battlefield, can enemy LeBlanc still play a Reflection token from Holding?
answer:
No, the enemy LeBlanc player cannot play a Reflection token to a battlefield while Mageseeker Warden is on your battlefield.

Here's why: Mageseeker Warden's passive ability says "opponents can only play units to their base." A Reflection token is a unit token (Rule 182.1.d), and the Deceiver legend's ability instructs you to "play a ready Reflection unit token there" — meaning the battlefield where you conquered or held. Because the Mageseeker restriction prevents opponents from playing units to any battlefield, that instruction can't be followed. Per the "do all you can" principle, the impossible instruction is ignored — the token is never created. The Deceiver's ability still goes on the chain and its cost is paid, but the play instruction fails and the copy effect that follows it (which depends on the token existing) also fails.

question: Does revealing Tide Turner and swapping a unit from one battlefield to another make Bellows Breath targeting fizzle?
answer:
No, revealing Tideturner and swapping a unit does not make Bellows Breath fizzle.

Bellows Breath targets "up to three units at the same location" — this is a group targeting restriction (Rule 355.11). When its targets move before resolution, the spell does not fizzle. Instead, per Rule 355.11.b and FAQ #9352/#781, the spell's controller chooses a subset of the original targets that are still at the same location, and deals damage to those.

Here's how it plays out:

Tideturner's trigger resolves first (newest chain item). It swaps your unit from Battlefield B with Tideturner from Battlefield A. Your original unit is now at A, and Tideturner is at B.

Bellows Breath then resolves. Its original targets are now at different locations. The Bellows Breath controller picks one location where some original targets are present and deals 1 damage only to those. For example, if Bellows Breath targeted units X, Y, Z at Battlefield B and Tideturner swapped X to A, the controller can deal 1 damage to Y and Z at B (skipping X), or deal 1 damage to X at A (skipping Y and Z) — but cannot split across locations.

If Bellows Breath targeted only that one swapped unit, the spell tracks it to its new location per FAQ #9062 and still deals damage — it does not fizzle.

Either way, the newly arrived Tideturner was never a target of Bellows Breath, so it takes no damage from it.

question: How does Defy work on a repeated spell? For example, Bellow's Breath, repeated. Do I Defy only the one rep or both entirely?
answer:
The FAQ already in the context covers this thoroughly. Here's the ruling:

You Defy the entire spell — both the initial effect and the repeat — in one go.

Repeat doesn't create a second spell on the chain. When you pay the Repeat cost, you're modifying the single spell to execute its instructions twice upon resolution. It's still one spell object. If Defy counters that spell, the whole thing is countered — both the initial execution and the repeated one.

Key points:

Defy checks the printed (base) cost — Bellows Breath costs 1E / 1P. Paying the Repeat cost doesn't change that, so Defy can target it regardless.

Repeat is an additional cost paid during casting, before the spell is finalized on the chain. You can't wait to see if your opponent Defies before deciding to Repeat (Rule 746.1.d; FAQ #256, #3189).

Countering doesn't refund costs — the 1C you paid for Repeat is lost along with the base cost (Rule 412.1.c).

So if you Defy a Repeated Bellows Breath, the spell is removed from the chain and placed in the trash. No damage is dealt at all — neither instance resolves.

question: When I play Switcheroo and my Unit has total 5 Might with Shield 2 included, my Enemy has 5 Might in total as well with an equip (Hextech Gauntlet). How does it work?
answer:
Since both units have the same current Might (5 each), Switcheroo's swap is effectively a no-op — it applies +0 to both and nothing changes during combat.

Here's the breakdown:

Your unit: base 3 + Shield 2 = 5 total

Enemy unit: base 2 + Hextech Gauntlets (+3) = 5 total

Switcheroo snapshots the current Might (5 and 5), calculates a difference of 0, and applies +0 to each. Shield stays on your unit, Gauntlets stay on the enemy unit — passives and equipment don't transfer (FAQ #341, #645).

After combat ends, Shield falls off (it only works while defending), so your unit drops to base 3. The enemy's Gauntlets remain attached, so they stay at 5. If your unit were not in combat when Switcheroo was played, Shield wouldn't be active at all, and the values would still be 5 and 5 (from different sources), so the result is the same.

If the Might values had been different (e.g., your unit at 7 with Shield vs. enemy at 5 with Gauntlets), the swap would apply a -2/+2 modifier, and after combat your unit would lose Shield and end at base 3 + (-2) = 1, while the enemy would stay at base 2 + Gauntlets 3 + (+2) = 7.

question: Can Elder Dragon target an enemy base? Or only battlefield?
answer:
Yes — an enemy Base is a location, so Elder Dragon can target enemy units there.

Per Rule 107.1.b, each Base is a Location. Elder Dragon's play effect says "choose up to one enemy unit at each location" — which covers both battlefields and bases (and every other location on the board). So when you play Elder Dragon, you can choose up to one enemy unit at your opponent's Base, plus up to one at each battlefield, plus up to one at your own Base (if an enemy unit is there).

question: Can Hunt keyword active when my unit died in cleanup phase?
answer:
No. Hunt does not trigger when your unit dies.

Hunt is defined as "When I Conquer or Hold, my controller gains X XP" (Rule 823.1.c.1). It triggers on establishing control of a battlefield, not on death. Dying during cleanup is a Kill event, not a Conquer or Hold event — that's what Deathknell is for.

The only connection between Hunt and cleanup is incidental: if your unit with Hunt successfully conquered a battlefield earlier in the same turn, the Hunt trigger would already be on the chain or have resolved — its death during a later cleanup does not prevent that trigger from resolving. But the death itself does not activate Hunt.

question: If a Karthus dead with temporary and a Soaring Scout die with temporary, what passes?
answer:
If Karthus, Eternal dies (whether from Temporary or any other cause) at the same time as another unit with Deathknell, his passive still applies — that unit's Deathknell triggers an additional time.

This is because Karthus's ability ("Your [Deathknell] effects trigger an additional time") is a passive ability, not a triggered one. Per FAQs #10742, #9317, and #9711, passive abilities remain active at the exact moment of death — they don't need to "survive" to evaluate their trigger condition. So when the simultaneous-death event creates Deathknell triggers (Rule 808.1.d.2), Karthus is still on the board and his passive doubles those triggers.

If instead you return Karthus to hand before the Temporary kill resolves (responding to the Temporary trigger while it's on the chain), his passive is no longer active on the board when Deathknell triggers process — so no bonus in that case (FAQ #10779).

I noticed multiple unrelated questions. I've answered the first one — please ask the others in separate messages so I can give each one proper attention.

question: Units resolve instantly correct? So can you still react to Brynhir?
answer:
Yes, you're right — units resolve instantly when finalized (Rule 337.1.c). So no, you cannot react to Brynhir herself entering the battlefield. There's no window between her being finalized and her being on the board.

However, you can react to her "When you play me" triggered ability, which is a separate chain item. After Brynhir lands, that trigger goes on the chain as a Pending item, and both players get a Reaction window before it resolves (FEPR process). If you have a Reaction-speed response (like killing her or bouncing her), you play it here. Once the trigger resolves, opponents can't play cards for the rest of the turn — even if Brynhir has been removed in the meantime.

question: If my Ruined Rex dies and my opponent only has a single unit on board which has Deflect, can I choose to not target that unit and decline triggering Ruined Rex's Deathknell ability?
answer:
No, you can't choose to skip triggering the Deathknell or refuse to target the unit. Here's how it actually plays out:

Ruined Rex's Deathknell is mandatory — there's no "may" in its text, so it triggers automatically when he dies (Rule 808.1, FAQ #10066).

Since the opponent's unit is the only valid enemy target, you must target it when the trigger finalizes on the Chain (FAQ #10922). You can't opt out of targeting.

However, because the unit has Deflect, the ability incurs an additional cost of [A]. For triggered abilities only, CR 405.2 lets you decline to pay that cost. If you do, the ability is removed from the Chain and never resolves — no damage is dealt.

So you can't avoid triggering or targeting, but you can effectively stop the effect by refusing the Deflect cost.

question: If mechs are created from Ferrous Forerunner dying, and then Rek'Sai is played after they appear at base, do the mechs get Accelerate?
answer: No, the Mechs do not get Accelerate. Rek'Sai, Breacher's ability — "Friendly units played from anywhere other than a player's hand have [Accelerate]" — is a static ability that applies as those units are being played. The two Mech tokens from Ferrous Forerunner's Deathknell were already played, resolved, and are sitting on your base before Rek'Sai even enters the board. Accelerate only modifies how a unit enters play ("As you play me, you may pay..."); it cannot be granted retroactively to units already on the battlefield. No rule or FAQ supports a "catch-up" application here.

question: Deceiver when I conquer or hold from Leblanc can it be used on a unit on base?
answer:
No, you cannot. The Reflection token and its copy effect are both restricted to the battlefield you conquered or held.

The Deceiver ability reads: "play a ready Reflection unit token there. Then do this: It becomes a copy of another unit there." Both uses of "there" refer to the battlefield where the conquer or hold occurred (confirmed in FAQ #11091). The token is placed at that battlefield, and the copy effect can only target another unit at that same battlefield — not a unit at your base or anywhere else.

If there are no other units at that battlefield when the copy resolves, the token simply remains a 0 [M] Reflection (and gains Temporary).

question: Can Hidden Blade be used when we are distributing the damage on the battlefield?
answer:
No — Hidden Blade cannot be used while combat damage is being assigned/distributed on the battlefield.

Here's why: Once the Showdown closes (both players pass Focus), you enter the Combat Damage Step. The game skips FEPR during this step (CR 462.3), meaning there is no priority window to play any spells — including Hidden Blade — while damage is being assigned or dealt. Hidden Blade must be played during the Showdown while you have Focus and the Chain is open.

If you want to use Hidden Blade to kill a unit before it deals or receives combat damage, play it during the Showdown (before both players pass). Once the damage assignment process begins, it's too late to intervene.

question: When I play a Lucian and I have a Shepherd on the board, can I equip that gear even if I don't have XP?
answer:
No. You cannot equip Shepherd's Heirloom via Weaponmaster if you have 0 XP.

Shepherd's Heirloom's Equip cost is "Spend 1 XP" — there is no [A] (Power) cost to reduce. Per Rule 821.1.c.3, Weaponmaster only reduces the [A] portion of the Equip cost; costs that aren't [A] must still be paid in full. And per Rule 821.1.c.5, if the cost can't be paid, the equipment stays where it is.

Since you have no XP, you can't spend 1 XP, so the Equip cost can't be paid.

That said, if you play Shepherd's Heirloom first (costing 2 Energy), its "When you play this, gain 1 XP" trigger gives you 1 XP. Then when you play Lucian, Merciless, you'd have that 1 XP to spend on Weaponmaster's Equip — the timing works fine for that sequence. But with 0 XP at the moment Weaponmaster resolves, the equip fails.

question: Is buff a keyword or a limited action?
answer:
Buff is a Limited Action — not a keyword.

Under CR 427, "Buff" is defined as an action (Buffing) that places a Buff counter on a unit. CR 427.2 explicitly states: "Buffing is a Limited Action" — it can only be done when a game effect directs you to. It is not listed in the Keywords reference, nor is it a Permissive, Passive, Triggered, or Dependent keyword.

Buffs themselves are objects (counters) placed on units, each giving +1 Might (CR 701–703), but the act of placing one is an action, not a keyword.

question: If I use Possession on an enemy unit with gears attached to it, do I take control of the unit with the gears too?
answer:
No. You take control of the unit itself, but you do not gain control of the attached Gear.

The Possession spell targets a unit — only the top-most card changes control. The equipped Gear remains attached to that unit, and the original owner retains control of the Gear itself. While the Gear stays attached, you benefit from its effect text (e.g. stat boosts), but you cannot activate its abilities — including Equip to move it — because you don't control the gear.

If the possessed unit later dies or leaves the battlefield, the Gear detaches and is Recalled to the original owner's Base during the next Cleanup. (Per RiftJudge FAQ #10699 and #5310.)

question: What is the exact rule that says a showdown cannot end while there are items on a chain?
answer:
There isn't a single standalone sentence that says "a showdown cannot end while items are on a chain" — instead, the prohibition is structural across several rules. Here are the two clearest pathways:

Path 1 — State-based (Rules 310.4, 313.1, and 347.3):

When a Chain exists during a Showdown, the turn is in a Showdown Closed state (Rule 310.4).

A player can only Pass (the action that leads to ending the showdown) when they have Focus during a Showdown Open state (Rule 313.1: "Focus is the permission to take appropriately timed Discretionary Actions when the turn is in a Showdown Open State").

The Showdown ends when all players Pass in sequence (Rule 347.3.a).

So while items are on the Chain, the state is Closed — no one can Pass to end it. The Chain must empty first (Rule 340.2 / Rule 346), returning to Showdown Open, before Pass is even an option.

Path 2 — Cleanup lockout (Rules 321 and 347.3.a.1):

Ending a Showdown performs a Cleanup (Rule 347.3.a.1).

Rule 321 states: "while Chain Items are Resolving, a Cleanup cannot occur."

If a Cleanup would be needed but Chain Items are resolving, the Cleanup becomes an Outstanding Task (Rule 321.1) — it's deferred until the Chain empties.

Bottom line: The mechanism is that the chain must fully resolve to empty before the state opens, Focus can be exercised to Pass, and the showdown-ending sequence can begin.

question: Can Not So Fast counter Mirror Image?
answer:
Yes, but only if your opponent chooses one of your units as the target.

Not So Fast counters an enemy spell or ability that chooses a friendly unit or gear. When your opponent plays Mirror Image targeting your unit, it's an enemy spell and the chosen unit is friendly to you — both conditions are met. If they target their own unit instead, you cannot use Not So Fast, because that unit is an enemy from your perspective.

(FAQ #10501)

question: If I have 2 Glasc Mixologist die at the same time and Deathknell trigger go on chain, the first trigger bring back Karthus, does the second trigger will be affected by Karthus ability?
answer:
No. The second Deathknell trigger will still resolve only once, unaffected by Karthus.

When both Glasc Mixologists die simultaneously, the game checks the board state at that exact moment. Since Karthus, Eternal isn't on the battlefield yet, each Mixologist's Deathknell triggers only once (the base trigger). Those triggers become pending items and the number of resolutions is locked in (Rule 808.1.d.2, FAQ #9606).
