question: In a 2v2, if my teammate Ride the Winds my unit to a battlefield during our opponents' turn for our final point, will we win?
answer:
No, you will not win. You'll draw a card instead of gaining the winning point.

Here's why: Ride the Wind is an [Action] spell, so on the opponent's turn it can only be played during a showdown (per its timing restriction). But more importantly, when you're at 10 points in 2v2 (1 away from 11), the final point via Conquer requires you to have scored every battlefield that turn (CR 468.1.b.2, adjusted by 484.8.f.1 — excepting those your ally controlled at the Beginning Phase). Since this is the opponent's turn, you haven't scored any battlefield this turn. You can't satisfy "scored every battlefield this turn," so you don't gain the point — you just draw a card.

You can still score a regular point via Ride the Wind on an opponent's turn (FAQ #572), and if you were at 9 or fewer points this would work fine. But for the final point, the conquer restriction blocks the win.

question: Playing as Lux legend, if I play Falling Comet to a battlefield and the opponent plays Retreat to return the unit to their hand before Falling Comet resolves, do I still get to draw 1 for the legend? Or since the spell doesn't resolve, I don't draw?
answer:
Yes, you still draw a card.

When your opponent plays Retreat in response, the targeted unit returns to hand and is no longer a legal target. Falling Comet still resolves — it just has no effect on that illegal target (Rule 359.3.e.1, 359.3.e.6). A spell that resolves to no effect is still considered played (Rule 359.3.e.10), which is what Lux's Legend checks for.

This is different from a spell being countered (e.g. by Wind Wall), which prevents resolution entirely and would deny the draw — but Retreat doesn't counter, it just removes the target. The spell still goes through the full resolution process, so Lux triggers and you draw 1.

question: If I conquer with Kennan and can give a spell flow, can I give drag under flow with cost 3 energy and 1 power or is it printed cost of 5 energy 1 power?
answer:
No — it checks the printed cost of 5 Energy.

Kai'Sa, Evolutionary's trigger says "with Energy cost less than your points" — and per Rule 131.4, effects that determine a card's cost for any purpose always use its printed cost, even if that cost would be reduced when played. Drag Under's printed Energy cost is 5, not 3. The self-discount ("I cost [2] less from anywhere other than your hand") only applies during the playing process, after the eligibility check is done.

So unless you have 6 or more points, Drag Under cannot be chosen by Kai'Sa's conquer trigger. This is the same logic as Fizz, Trickster not working with Drag Under (FAQ #7430), and Kai'Sa not being able to play Sky Splitter based on its reduced cost (FAQ #3520).

If you do have 6+ points and play it via Kai'Sa, you ignore the 5 Energy cost but still pay the 1 Power cost (per the parenthetical on Kai'Sa's card).

question: Can I play green Janna as a reaction for attacking with my unit on base and sent to battlefield?
answer:
Yes, you can play Janna, Savior as a Reaction during your attack — but she must be placed at a location you already control, not the battlefield you're attacking.

Here's how it works:

You move your unit from base to an occupied battlefield. That applies Contested and starts a Combat Showdown.

As the Attacker, you gain Focus in the Showdown Open state.

Janna has [Reaction] — she can be played at any time, including during a Showdown.

Placement restriction: When you move into an occupied battlefield, you do not control it (it's contested). Units must be played to a battlefield you control or your base. So Janna goes to your base or a different battlefield you already control — not the one you're attacking.

Why you might want to: If the enemy has a unit at that contested battlefield and you'd like to move it away, Janna's trigger can't reach it from a different location (her ability says "here"). But you could still play her to your base to set up for future turns or to use her healing on units elsewhere.

Refs: FAQ #11160; Combat reference §Attacker/Defender; CR 459.2

question: Does the battlefield conquer effect have priority over other "When I conquer" effects?
answer:
No — a battlefield's conquer effect does not have priority over other "When I conquer" effects.

All "When you conquer" triggers (from units, battlefields, or other sources) trigger simultaneously when you conquer. Since they trigger at the same time, the player who controls them chooses the order they're placed on the Chain (Rule 383.3.d). They then resolve last-in-first-out as usual.

So you get to sequence them however you want — no inherent priority between a battlefield's and a unit's conquer effect.

question: If there's Abandoned Hall and they use Flash on their unit, does the unit still get +1 might?
answer:
No. The unit will not get the +1 Might from Abandoned Hall.

Here's why: Flash resolves first, moving the unit from Abandoned Hall to your base. Only after Flash finishes resolving does Abandoned Hall's "when a player plays a spell" trigger go on the chain. When that trigger resolves, it asks you to give +1 Might to "a unit you control here" — but your unit is no longer at Abandoned Hall, so it's not a valid target. (This is directly covered by FAQ #11451.)

question: When you have a unit with 2 extra might cast on it and then you play Thrill of the Hunt, does that unit still have the 2 extra might when you play it to a battlefield?
answer:
No, the unit does not keep the +2 extra Might.

When Thrill of the Hunt banishes the unit and then plays it to a battlefield, the unit leaves the board entirely. Per CR 705, all buffs and modifiers are removed when a unit leaves play. The unit then enters as a new game object — it's treated as a fresh copy of the card, carrying only its printed base Might (plus any permanent modifiers like gear might bonuses). Any temporary +2 Might from a spell effect is gone for good. (RiftJudge FAQ #9870 and #11336 confirm this.)

question: When Flame Chompers die, can I pay a Fury Rune to play it?
answer:
No. Flame Chompers' ability triggers only on discard (hand → trash), not on being Killed (board → trash). Those are different game actions with different trigger conditions.

The card reads: "When you discard me, you may pay fury rune (power) to play me." Being destroyed in combat, removed by a Kill effect, or any other form of death from the board does not satisfy "discard" — Discard specifically means moving a card from hand to trash. You would need a separate recursion effect (like Unlicensed Armory or similar) to bring Flame Chompers back from the trash after it's Killed.

question: If a player's "on attack" trigger kills an enemy unit at a battlefield with deathknell, does the deathknell effect happen before you move into the main part of a showdown?
answer:
Yes — the Deathknell resolves during the Combat Showdown Step, before combat damage is dealt.

Here's why: An "on attack" trigger fires during Step 1 of Combat (the Combat Showdown Step, CR 461). When that trigger resolves and kills a unit with Deathknell, the Deathknell trigger becomes a Pending Item on the chain (CR 429.1.a.1.b). Since the chain is still active within the Showdown Step, the Deathknell must go through normal FEPR — Finalize, get placed on the chain, and resolve — before the Showdown can close.

The Showdown cannot close while chain items exist (Rule 348). Only after the chain empties and all players pass does the Showdown close, and only then do you proceed to the Combat Damage Step (Rule 348.1).

This is distinct from Deathknell caused by combat damage itself — that Deathknell happens during Combat Cleanup (after damage), in a separate sequence. But a Deathknell triggered by an "on attack" kill resolves right then and there during the Showdown Step, well before anyone assigns combat damage.

Bottom line: The Deathknell resolves fully during the Combat Showdown Step. The unit is dead and its effect happens before combat damage is even calculated.

question: Can I Smoke Screen my opponent's unit that is the target of Baited Hook before it is killed?
answer:
Yes, you can.

Smoke Screen has [Reaction], so you can play it in response to Baited Hook's activation while the ability is on the Chain (Closed State). It resolves first (LIFO) and reduces the targeted unit's Might before Baited Hook kills it.

What happens: Baited Hook checks the unit's current Might at the moment it is killed (FAQ #2156, FAQ #8885). Since Smoke Screen reduces that value — to a minimum of 1 — the opponent's search threshold becomes "Might up to 1 more than" that reduced value. If you drop a 4-Might unit to 1, they can only fetch a unit of Might 2 or less instead of 5 or less.

Important: The unit must still be a legal target for Smoke Screen at the time you play it — it needs to be on the board and meet the "unit" targeting requirements. Baited Hook's target is still on the board when the Chain is open for Reactions, so that's satisfied.

question: A hypothetical unit has "When you play your first card each turn, if I'm at a battlefield, your next card costs [2][Rune][Rune] less." If I play this card to a battlefield, does my next card get the discount? Assuming no other cards have been played this turn.
answer:
Yes. Your next card does get the discount.

Here's why. The trigger condition ("When you play your first card each turn") is evaluated after the inciting event — playing the card — has been fully processed (Rule 383.2.c). By that point, the unit has been finalized and has entered the board. So when the conditional "if I'm at a battlefield" is checked (Rule 383.3.e), the unit is already at the battlefield, and the trigger goes on the Chain. Rule 383.2.c.1 confirms this: a Game Object whose ability is active in a zone can evaluate its trigger if it enters that zone at the same time its condition is met.

question: How does a ready gold token work? Do you get both energy and fulfill a power requirement when it is rested and killed?
answer:
No, a Gold gear token only adds Power — not Energy — when you exhaust and kill it.

A Gold gear token is defined in Rule 184.5 as having the ability: [Reaction][>] Kill this, [E]: [Add] [A]. That breaks down as: exhaust it + kill it → add 1 Universal Power to your Rune Pool. It does not generate Energy, and it does not fulfill any Energy requirement.

You can activate this ability during an Open State (Main Phase), or during the Pay Costs step of playing a card or ability (thanks to the Reaction tag — see CR 430.3). Once you pay the cost (exhaust + kill the token), the Power is added immediately, and you can spend it on any Power cost of any domain.

The only exception is if you also control Chem-Baroness Renata with her legend ability active (within 3 points of Victory Score), in which case Gold adds both 1 Energy and 1 Power per FAQ #9476.

question: If you ride the wind from one abandoned hall to another abandoned hall does your unit get any plus might?
answer:
Yes — your unit gets +1 [S] from the destination Abandoned Hall, but not from the origin one.

Here's the timeline:

Ride the Wind resolves — the unit leaves Abandoned Hall A and arrives at Abandoned Hall B, readying along the way.

Only after the spell finishes resolving do both Abandoned Halls' "When a player plays a spell" triggers go on the chain (per FAQ #11430 and #10497).

Abandoned Hall A's trigger resolves — it asks you to give +1 [S] to "a unit you control here." Your unit is no longer at Hall A, so it's not a valid target. No buff from Hall A.

Abandoned Hall B's trigger resolves — your unit is there, so it's a valid target. You may give it +1 [S] this turn.

So you get exactly one +1 [S] — from the battlefield you arrived at.

question: If a card has an attack trigger, can I move the unit into the showdown, then use a reaction spell to move it out while still keeping the attack trigger?
answer:
Yes, the trigger still resolves — but parts of it may do nothing depending on what it says.

Once a "when I attack" trigger is on the chain, it's an independent game object. Moving the unit away doesn't remove the trigger. However, whether the effect actually works depends on what the trigger says.

Rule 359.3.f.2 gives your exact scenario with an example: Yasuo, Remorseful attacks, his trigger goes on the chain, and an opponent moves him back to base with Fight or Flight in reaction. The ruling: "When the attack trigger resolves, 'here' is no longer the battlefield where combat is ongoing and the attack trigger mistargets." The trigger is on the chain and resolving, but the instruction referencing "here" can't find a valid location, so that instruction does nothing.

Two categories:

No "here" / location reference — e.g., "When I attack, draw a card" or "When I attack, give other friendly units +1 Might this turn." These resolve fully regardless of where the unit went. The trigger is already on the chain and the instructions don't depend on the unit's presence.

Uses "here" or a location-dependent phrase — e.g., "When I attack, deal 2 to an enemy unit here." The trigger resolves, but the "here" reference fails because the unit is no longer at that battlefield. That instruction is ignored (Rule 359.3.f.2—Yasuo example). Other independent instructions on the same trigger would still work.

One more nuance: Moving the unit to base (board zone) means effects that check "my Might" still work (the unit exists and has Might). Moving it to a non-board zone (hand, trash) makes characteristics return null — so "my Might" would also fail (Rule 359.3.e.12).

question: If I ride the wind into abandoned hall do I get plus might from Ride the Wind resolving?
answer:
Yes. When you play Ride the Wind to move a unit to Abandoned Hall, the unit does get +1 Might from Abandoned Hall's triggered ability.

Here's the timing in order:

Ride the Wind resolves — your unit moves to Abandoned Hall and is readied.

Only after the spell fully resolves does Abandoned Hall's "When a player plays a spell" trigger check in. Since your unit arrived during step 1, it's already at Abandoned Hall and is a valid target for the buff.

The trigger goes on the chain and resolves, giving the unit +1 Might.

The key insight: Abandoned Hall's trigger fires after the spell finishes resolving, not while it's still on the chain. So the unit is already there to receive the bonus.

question: In a 4-player free for all game, would Elder Dragon hit every player's base and all 3 battlefields?
answer:
Yes. Elder Dragon's play effect targets "up to one enemy unit at each location," and in a 4-player FFA (FFA4/War, CR 485), there are 7 locations on the board: 4 player Bases (each a Location per Rule 107.1.b) and 3 Battlefields (each a Location per Rule 107.2.b).

The ability creates a separate targeting restriction for each of those 7 locations. At your own Base, any units there are friendly, so you won't choose anything there. But at each of your 3 opponents' Bases and at all 3 Battlefields, you can choose up to one enemy unit and deal 1 damage to it — for a maximum of 6 targets.

question: Can I play Thrill of the Hunt in opponent turn and conquer a battlefield that I am standing on?
answer:
Yes, you can. On your opponent's turn, play Thrill of the Hunt (a [Reaction]) to banish a friendly unit and play it to any battlefield you don't control. When it arrives, the battlefield becomes Contested, triggering a Non-Combat Showdown. If you win that showdown — meaning your unit is the only one left — you establish control and Conquer, scoring a point (CR 344.2, 348.2, 466.1).

A few important limits:

Once per battlefield per turn. You can only score from that battlefield once (CR 467). If you already scored it this turn, you won't get a second point.

Winning Point restriction. If this would be your final point to win (e.g., from 7 to 8 in standard 1v1), you must have scored every other battlefield this same turn to gain the point via Conquer. Otherwise you draw a card instead (CR 468.1.b.2, FAQ #11423).

No win on opponent's turn. Even if you hit the victory score, the game only checks for a winner during a cleanup — the turn still belongs to your opponent, so the game won't end until that cleanup occurs (Rule 323.1).

question: If I have a Gear Svellsongur attached to the Ornn, I will have Deflect 4, but if someone targets with a spell my Gear, do they have to pay Deflect 2?
answer:
No, they do not have to pay any Deflect when targeting Svellsongur directly.

When a spell targets the gear (Svellsongur) rather than the unit (Ornn), Deflect doesn't apply. Here's why:

Deflect is on the unit, not the gear. Ornn has Deflect 4, but that protection belongs to him. Svellsongur is a separate game object — targeting the gear is not the same as targeting Ornn (FAQ #734, #9176).

The gear's own printed rules text is inactive while attached (Rules 718.2, 135.4). Even if Svellsongur somehow had Deflect printed on it, that text would be inactive while attached. And its effect text (the copying ability) grants Deflect to the unit, not to the equipment card itself (FAQ #7465).

So: targeting your Svellsongur with something like Salvage or Detonate costs zero extra Power. Only spells or abilities that choose Ornn himself have to pay the Deflect 4.

question: Does Vi Hotheaded equipped with Svellsungur have 6 or 12 might after paying 2 energy and 1 power?
answer:
Ruling: 6 Might.

Svellsongur gives Vi two separate instances of her activated ability ([2] [C] : Double my Might this turn.), but each instance requires its own cost payment. Paying [2] [C] once only activates one of those two instances, so Vi's Might doubles once: from 3 to 6 (CR 433.1).

To reach 12, you would need to pay [2] [C] a second time for the Svellsongur-granted copy — for a total of [4] [C][C]. Each activation is independent and you can activate both in sequence as long as you can pay each cost (FAQ #10207).

question: If I have two tanks at the same battlefield and my opponent attacks, who decides which tank unit takes damage first?
answer: The attacker (the opponent) decides which of your two tanks takes damage first. Since both have Tank, they share the same damage-assignment priority, so the attacker can choose the order they assign lethal damage to them (CR 815.1.c.2, 462.2.c.6).

question: If a Brutalizer is equipped and then detached, does the +2 persist on the unit?
answer:
No, the unit does not keep the +2 bonus when Brutalizer detaches.

As confirmed by FAQ #8582, when Brutalizer leaves the unit, all bonuses it provided (both the base +1 Might and the conditional +2) are lost immediately. Per Rule 136.3.a, a Might Bonus applies only while the card is Attached and stops applying as soon as it's no longer Attached. The same logic applies to Brutalizer's conditional effect — it's tied to the equipment being attached, not a lingering buff.

question: If Ruined Rex dies in a combat showdown and deals 4 damage to a unit on another battlefield as that showdown resolves, does that damage heal?
answer:
No, the 4 damage from Ruined Rex's Deathknell does not immediately heal.

Here's why: the Combat Cleanup's "Heal all Units" step (CR 463.1.a.1) happens before the pending Deathknell trigger resolves — not after. As established in RiftJudge FAQs #10018, #10182, and #10410, the sequence is:

Combat Damage Step — damage is dealt, Ruined Rex dies and its Deathknell becomes pending on the chain.

Units with lethal damage are moved to trash.

Heal all Units — everything on the board has its damage cleared.

Deathknell resolves — dealing 4 damage to your chosen enemy unit.

Since step 4 happens after step 3, the 4 damage lands on a freshly healed board. There's no second healing wave unless another Combat Cleanup starts at that unit's battlefield, or the turn ends. So that 4 damage stays marked on the target until the end of the turn (Rule 143.3.b).

question: If I use Discipline, does it stay in effect at the end of my turn when Glowstone deals 5 damage to my units?
answer:
I couldn't find "Glowstone" in the card database — it doesn't appear in my current index. But I can answer the general timing question about Discipline and end-of-turn damage.

Discipline's +2 Might lasts the entire turn, including into the Ending Phase. The buff expires during the Expiration Step of your turn's Ending Phase (Rule 317.2.d — all "this turn" effects expire simultaneously). Healing also occurs in that same step (317.2.c), before the buffs expire.

So if Glowstone deals its 5 damage during the Ending Step (317.1 — "at the end of the turn" timing) or during the Expiration Step before the "this turn" effects expire, then your unit would still have the +2 Might from Discipline when the damage is dealt, potentially surviving a hit it otherwise wouldn't.

If you can share Glowstone's exact card text, I can pinpoint the exact timing and ruling. It's likely a Location or an effect with a specific trigger phrase like "At the end of your turn" or "During your Ending Phase" — the exact wording determines the ordering.

question: Does Convergent Mutation buff units for more than one turn?
answer:
No. Convergent Mutation's buff only lasts until the end of the turn it was played — not multiple turns.

The card was errata'd to add "This turn" to its text (October 2025 patch). The original printing was missing that duration, but the errata overrides it for competitive play. The effect expires when the turn ends, and the unit returns to its base Might.

question: If I have Spellsinger and Guardian Angel attached to my Sand Soldier, and the Soldier dies, what equipment will be destroyed?
answer:
Only Guardian Angel is destroyed. Svellsongur stays attached and returns to base with the soldier.

Here's the breakdown:

The death event triggers the replacement effect. Guardian Angel reads: "If I would die, kill Guardian Angel instead. Heal me, exhaust me, and recall me." The "I" here refers to the equipped unit (the Sand Soldier). When the soldier would die, Guardian Angel replaces that event — Guardian Angel itself is killed, and the soldier is healed, exhausted, and recalled to base.

Svellsongur copies the unit's text, not other gear's text. Svellsongur says: "Copy that unit's text to this Equipment's effect text." A Sand Soldier token has no rules text (it's just 2 Might with the Shurima tag per Rule 184.3), so Svellsongur gains nothing from it. It has no triggered ability of its own to fire.

The soldier never "dies." Because Guardian Angel's replacement effect prevents the death (Rule 370.1), the soldier stays on the board and merely moves to base. Per FAQ #9097, #8298, and #5370, when a unit is saved by Guardian Angel, all other equipment remains attached. Svellsongur stays equipped and recalls to base with the soldier.

Result: Guardian Angel → killed (trash). Svellsongur → still attached to the soldier at base.

question: If I have Yone in base and play Blade of the Ruined King, must I still kill a unit to attach? If there is no unit, I cannot attach it?
answer:
Yes, you must still kill a friendly unit to attach it, and if you have no other friendly unit besides Yone, you cannot attach it.

Here's the breakdown. Playing Blade of the Ruined King (putting the Gear card on your board from hand) does not require any kill — the Gear simply enters play normally.

The Equip ability is a separate activated ability. Its cost is [C] plus "Kill a friendly unit." That kill is a mandatory part of the cost — Weaponmaster reduces the power cost by [A], but does not bypass non-resource costs like the kill (FAQ #5147).

Per FAQ #1747, you cannot kill the same unit you're equipping. You need at least two friendly units: one to kill for the cost, and a different one to receive the equipment. If Yone is your only unit on the board, you have no legal way to pay the Equip cost, so the ability cannot be activated.

question: If your first card played is Darius Trifarian then you play a spell, does Darius immediately trigger before any player gets priority?
answer:
No. Darius does not trigger until the spell (your second card) has fully resolved — not when the spell is placed on the chain.

Per CR 420.4.a, "when you play" triggers happen after the card resolves, not when it enters the chain. So the sequence is:

You play the spell — it goes on the chain.

Players pass priority; the spell resolves.

After resolution, Darius sees that the second card was played. His mandatory trigger goes on the chain.

Players get priority to respond to Darius's trigger.

If the spell is countered, it was never "played" (CR 420.4.b), and Darius won't trigger at all. (FAQ #2630 covers this exact timing with Challenge — Darius's +2 always comes after the spell resolves.)

question: If an opponent captures a BF with Irelia and then charms my unit but I win the combat, will I conquer since I was the attacker?
answer:
Yes, you conquer. When your opponent charms your unit to a battlefield they control, your unit applies Contested status — making you the attacker. If you win the combat, you establish control and score a conquering point (CR 466.1, CR 461.2.b.1).

Key details:

You are the attacker even though your opponent moved your unit and controls the battlefield. The unit that applied Contested determines who the attacker is (CR 461.2.b.1; FAQ #590, #1092, #8296).

Each player can score once per battlefield per turn — so even if the opponent already scored from that battlefield earlier this turn (by conquering with Irelia), that doesn't block you. Your scoring limit is separate (CR 467; FAQ #5834).

However, if you already scored that same battlefield earlier this turn (e.g. from a previous Hold or Conquer), then you cannot conquer it again — the once-per-turn limit applies to you (CR 467).

question: Can I move units from different battlefields with Emperors Divide?
answer:
No. Emperor's Divide can only move units from a single battlefield. The card text says "at a battlefield" (singular), so you must choose one battlefield and move units only from that location.

If it were intended to affect multiple battlefields, it would use plural wording like "at battlefields." Units moved by Emperor's Divide retain their current state (Ready or Exhausted) when they arrive at your base.

question: Gearhead Svellsongur, does it give extra might per gear or not?
answer:
No, Svellsongur does not give extra Might per gear on Gearhead. Here's why:

Svellsongur copies Gearhead's printed ability ("Each Equipment attached to me gives double its base Might bonus") onto itself. This creates two instances of the same doubling effect on Gearhead — but they don't stack multiplicatively. Both look at the same base values and apply the same doubling, so the result is the same as having just one copy (FAQ #8493).

Additionally, Svellsongur has a base Might bonus of +0, so doubling it contributes nothing (FAQ #8493).

Example: Gearhead (base 3 Might) with one Doran's Shield (+1) ends at 5 Might — whether Svellsongur is attached or not. With two +1 Equipment (say Doran's Shield and another), you'd get 3 + 1×2 + 1×2 = 7 Might — but that's still just Gearhead's own doubling applying to each gear once. Svellsongur just duplicates Gearhead's already-present effect, not amplifying it further.

question: If the only defending unit is killed during a move trigger from the attacker, is the pending showdown still a combat showdown?
answer:
No. If the defending unit is killed during the move trigger before Cleanup, the outcome is a non-combat showdown, not a combat showdown.

Here's why: when a move makes a battlefield contested, the contested status is applied immediately (CR 447). But Combat isn't staged until the next Cleanup (CR 323.8), which happens after the entire chain resolves. By that point the defending unit is already in the trash. Since CR 323.8 only stages a Combat at battlefields that "have Units present controlled by opposing players," and the defender's unit is gone, no Combat is staged — only a Showdown is staged (CR 323.7). So when the turn player later initiates that showdown (CR 323.10), it opens as a non-combat showdown, not a combat showdown.

question: Blue Sentinel with Svellsongur, does it give an additional trigger of hold effects?
answer:
Yes — with Svellsongur attached, Blue Sentinel gives two additional triggers of each hold effect (total 3), and you'll have two separate "When I hold" abilities, each triggering 3 times.

Here's how it works:

Svellsongur copies Blue Sentinel's printed text to its own Effect Text. Per Rule 718.3 (and 136.2.c), that Effect Text is appended to Blue Sentinel's Rules Text while attached. So Blue Sentinel effectively has two instances of both its passive and its "When I hold" ability.

Two passives stack additively. Each instance of "Your hold effects for holding here trigger an additional time" is a separate modification. So each hold effect triggers 1 (base) + 1 (first passive) + 1 (second passive) = 3 times instead of the usual 2 with just one Blue Sentinel.

Two separate "When I hold" abilities. The original printed one and the copy from Svellsongur are two distinct triggered abilities. Each is a hold effect, so each triggers 3 times due to the dual passive. That's 6 total [Add] [A] triggers — you'll add 6 Power at the start of your next Main Phase.

Same applies to any other hold effect at that battlefield (e.g., Grove of the God-Willow's "draw 1" triggers 3 times, drawing 3 cards).

question: I attack with Vex, Apathetic and Showdown stats. They react to my Showdown with Rengar AMBUSH. Is Rengar Stun or not?
answer:
Yes, Rengar gets stunned.

When your opponent plays Rengar via Ambush to Vex's battlefield, Vex's ability triggers immediately — "When an opponent plays a unit while I'm at a battlefield, [Stun] it." Ambush doesn't bypass this; playing a unit is still playing a unit (FAQ #9735, #10932). Vex's stun goes on the chain and resolves, stunning Rengar before combat happens.

Per CR 424.1.b, a stunned Rengar won't contribute his Might to damage during combat, so Vex will deal 4 damage to Rengar while taking 0 in return.

question: A player uses Bellows Breath, if I use Smoke and Mirrors in reaction to move a unit away from the location that was targeted with Bellows, how does this resolve?
answer:
Yes, you can use Smoke and Mirrors as a Reaction from Hidden to respond to Bellows Breath on the chain. Here's how it resolves:

When you reveal Smoke and Mirrors from Hidden (gaining Reaction per Rule 811/737), you swap two of your units at different locations — e.g., moving the targeted unit away from the battlefield Bellows Breath chose.

On resolution, Bellows Breath does not fizzle. The "same location" requirement is a targeting restriction for playing the spell, not for resolution (FAQ #7422, #9018). Instead, you choose one location among those where your originally targeted units are now present, and deal 1 damage only to the targeted units at that chosen location.

So if the moved unit ends up alone at your Base and the other targeted units remain at the battlefield, the Bellows Breath player can choose either location — damaging just the unit(s) there. Units not originally targeted (like the unit swapped in by Smoke and Mirrors) take no damage.

question: If I target Vex Apathetic with the spell Falling Star, do I need to pay the deflect cost for both instances of damage?
answer:
Yes, you must pay the Deflect cost twice.

Falling Star has two separate instances of "Deal 3 to a unit," and each instance chooses (targets) a unit. Vex, Apathetic has Deflect (Deflect 1), and per Rule 809.1.c, Deflect imposes an additional cost "for each time they choose me." If you target Vex with both instances, that's two times chosen, so you pay 1 Power twice — totaling 2 Power in Deflect costs on top of Falling Star's base cost of 2 Energy and 2 Power.

question: If the enemy chooses a 5 might unit with sacrifice, can I use star cross on it first?
answer:
No. The 5-Might unit is killed as an additional cost while your opponent plays Sacrifice, before you get priority to respond. You cannot "Star-Cross it first" to save it.

Here's the sequence:

Your opponent plays Sacrifice — during Step 4 (paying costs), they kill their friendly Mighty unit. This happens before Sacrifice is finalized on the chain.

Sacrifice is finalized and added to the chain.

Only now do you get a window to play Star-Crossed as a Reaction.

At that point, the Mighty unit is already in the trash, not on the board. Star-Crossed targets units on the board (Rule 355.9.a.1), so you cannot target the sacrificed unit. You'd need a different enemy unit still on the board to even play Star-Crossed (it requires both a friendly and an enemy target — FAQ #10191).

Even if you could target it, the unit is already dead — Star-Crossed returning it to hand wouldn't undo Sacrifice's cost payment. The FAQ on Sacrifice + Star-Crossed (FAQ #10993, #10982) confirms: the cost is paid during finalization, so returning the unit later doesn't stop Sacrifice from resolving.

question: If Pyke, Returned with Backline gets targeted by Block, which assigns him Tank as well, does he have Tank or Backline, and when should he be targeted?
answer:
The attacker (opponent assigning damage) chooses whether to treat Pyke as first or last.

Pyke, Returned naturally has Backline (must be assigned damage last). Giving him Tank via Block creates an exclusionary conflict — he can't be both first and last. Per CR 462.2.c.7 (and FAQs 11355, 7737), the player assigning combat damage picks one of the two keywords to apply when assigning damage to Pyke. They can choose to treat him as Tank (damage him before other non-Tank defenders) or Backline (damage him after other non-Backline defenders), but not both.

question: If I have Switcheroo at Trifarrian War Camp, and I switch Irelia with another unit, how does it work? How does it work with the buff from Battlefield and also the Choose Me?
answer:
Here's how it all works.

Yes, playing Switcheroo on Irelia triggers her +1 Might. Switcheroo chooses/targets two units (CR 434), and Irelia, Fervent's ability says "When you choose or ready me, give me +1 Might this turn." So she gets +1 from being chosen.

You control the order on the chain. Since you control both Switcheroo and Irelia's trigger, you decide which goes on the chain first. The last item you place resolves first (LIFO). If you put Irelia's trigger on top, it resolves first (she gains +1 Might), then Switcheroo resolves using the updated Might values.

How the numbers work with Trifarian War Camp: The battlefield gives +1 Might as a continuous effect on all units there. When Switcheroo resolves, it calculates the difference between the two units' current Might (which already includes the battlefield's +1 and Irelia's +1 from being chosen if that resolved). Then it applies a -X modifier to the higher-Might unit and a +X modifier to the lower one for the turn. All continuous effects (battlefield, Irelia's trigger, Switcheroo's modifier) keep applying on top of each other through layers.

Example: Irelia (4 base) and a 3-Might unit, both at War Camp (+1 each). You choose the order so Irelia's trigger resolves first (+1). At Switcheroo resolution: Irelia = 6, other = 4. Difference = 2. Irelia gets -2, other gets +2. Final: Irelia = 4 + 1 (camp) + 1 (chosen) − 2 (swap) = 4 Might. Other = 3 + 1 (camp) + 2 (swap) = 6 Might. The continuous effects mean neither unit gets "locked" to a number — if either later leaves the camp or gains more Might, the modifier adjusts on top (FAQ #9775, FAQ #8531).

question: Does Turn to Dust on an equipped unit still kill the gear that is equipped the following turn?
answer:
Yes. A gear hit with Turn to Dust while attached will be killed during your next Beginning Phase.

Here's the key distinction: when a gear is attached, its printed rules text becomes inactive (Rules 135.4, 718.2). However, Turn to Dust grants the [Temporary] keyword — and granted rules text remains active while attached. The granted [Temporary] triggers normally in your next Beginning Phase, killing the gear and detaching it from your unit. Any stat bonuses or effects the gear was providing cease immediately at that point.

question: When I have a Ravenbloom Student on a battlefield and play a hidden card on the battlefield, does she get a buff or only when the hidden spell gets "played" as in revealed?
answer:
Ravenbloom Student gets +1 Might only when you play the hidden spell — that is, when you flip it up from facedown and resolve it on a later turn. Hiding it initially (paying [A] to put it facedown) is a separate action — it does not count as playing the spell and does not trigger Ravenbloom Student.

To be precise:

Hiding a spell (placing it facedown at a Battlefield) — does not trigger Ravenbloom Student.

Playing from hidden (flipping it up on a future turn, resolving its effect) — does trigger Ravenbloom Student, since playing a card from hidden still counts as playing it (FAQ #1301, #3691).

question: Does Unyielding Spirit prevent death from Imperial Decree?
answer:
No, Unyielding Spirit does not prevent death from Imperial Decree.

Imperial Decree creates a triggered ability that kills a unit when that unit takes damage. Unyielding Spirit prevents damage from spells and abilities — but the kill from Imperial Decree is a separate instruction (a Kill effect, not a damage effect) and is not prevented.

Even if Unyielding Spirit blocks the damage itself, the Imperial Decree trigger still fires and kills the unit. The "Kill" action is mechanically distinct from "Damage" in Riftbound, so damage prevention effects don't interfere with it.

question: Can Tideturner switch locations with a unit at Vilemaw's Lair?
answer:
No — you cannot swap a unit out of Vilemaw's Lair via Tideturner if Tideturner was played to base.

Tideturner's "When you play me" ability uses the word "move." Vilemaw's Lair says "Units can't move from here to base." Since a "can't" restriction beats a "can" effect, the targeted unit in the Lair cannot move to base.

Here's what happens:

Tideturner is played to base and targets a unit in Vilemaw's Lair.

Tideturner successfully moves to the Lair.

The targeted unit cannot move to base — it stays in Vilemaw's Lair.

The swap partially resolves: Tideturner ends up in the Lair alongside the other unit. (FAQ #7241, #8637)

One exception: If Tideturner's original location is a different battlefield (not your base), the swap completes fully — Vilemaw's Lair only blocks movement to base, not to another battlefield. (FAQ #11402)

question: Can I keep my opponent's battlefield a Brush if I conquer it?
answer:
Yes, you can. When you conquer a Brush token battlefield, you become its controller. The Brush's ability says "When you score here, you may replace this with the battlefield it replaced" — and "you" refers to the battlefield's controller (Rule 187.6.c). Since you now control it, the choice is yours. You may simply choose not to replace it, and the Brush token stays in play under your control.

The Brush token doesn't automatically revert or expire. It stays until its controller chooses to swap it back upon scoring, or until a game effect removes it (FAQ #8747). Conquering it doesn't force a swap — that's entirely your decision as the new controller.

question: Can I play Tideturner on the same battlefield as Hwei and choose him and it will count as him moving?
answer:
No. Tideturner's ability says "choose a unit you control at another location." If Hwei is on the same battlefield as Tideturner, he's at the same location — that choice is illegal, so you cannot pick him.

Even setting that restriction aside, the swap would be a pointless same-location exchange (both would end up on the same battlefield they started on), which wouldn't constitute a meaningful zone-change move for Hwei's trigger.

If you want to move Hwei with Tideturner, you'd need to play Tideturner from hidden at a different battlefield (e.g., Battlefield B) and target Hwei at Battlefield A — that would swap them between locations and trigger Hwei's "When I move" ability.

question: On my turn I attack a BF, opponent plays Hidden Hostile Takeover. After Hidden Hostile Takeover resolves, they attempt to sacrifice my unit on an open showdown. Is this legal?
answer:
Yes, this is legal.

After Hostile Takeover resolves and the chain empties, the Showdown goes to Open State. Since the chain was opened by a played card (not a trigger or Add ability), Focus passes to the next player — your opponent — per Rule 346. With Focus in Showdown Open, they can play a card with [Action] or [Reaction] timing (such as Hidden Blade, which has Action) to kill the unit they now control.

This is directly supported by FAQ #8808 and #9563 — you can Hidden Blade a unit you took over with Hostile Takeover, and since you control the unit when the kill resolves, any "controller draws" effects (like Hidden Blade's draw 2) benefit you. The same principle applies to any similar kill/sacrifice effect with proper Showdown timing.

question: Can I conquer the same bf twice in a turn if I conquered it, then the opponent conquered the same bf and then I conquered again?
answer:
No. Once you've scored a battlefield (by conquering it), you cannot conquer it again in the same turn — even if the opponent takes it and you take it back.

Why: Each player may only score each battlefield once per turn, by either method (Hold or Conquer) — CR 467. Your first conquer already used up your scoring opportunity for that battlefield this turn. When you later regain control, you take control but do not score again, so it doesn't count as a conquer and won't trigger conquer abilities.

Your opponent can score it when they take it, since they're a different player and haven't scored it yet (FAQ 244). But your second reclaim is just a control change, not a conquer.

question: If an opponent plays hidden blade from hand, and i react with a hidden tidehunter, does it save my unit being targetted?
answer:
To determine the outcome of this interaction, we must look at how the chain resolves and how targeting works in Riftbound.

The Chain Sequence

Opponent plays Hidden Blade: This is a spell that targets a unit at a battlefield. It goes on the chain. You are the current defender, and the state is now CLOSED (a chain exists).

You react with Tideturner: Since Tideturner has the Hidden keyword, it gains [Reaction] when played from facedown, allowing you to play it during a CLOSED state. It goes on top of the chain.

Chain Resolution (LIFO - Last-In, First-Out):

Tideturner's ability resolves first: When Tideturner enters play, its triggered ability goes on the chain. It allows you to move Tideturner to the location of a friendly unit you control elsewhere and move that unit to Tideturner's original location (swapping their positions).

Hidden Blade resolves last: After the swap is complete, Hidden Blade attempts to resolve.

Does this save your unit?

Yes, it can.

According to Rule 359.3.e.9, when a spell targets a unit at a battlefield, if that unit is moved to a different battlefield (or its base) before the spell resolves, the spell is still targeting that unit. However, Hidden Blade specifies "Kill a unit at a battlefield."

If your unit was at a battlefield and you swap it with Tideturner (who is also at a battlefield), your unit is now at a new location. As long as it is still at a battlefield, it remains a legal target for Hidden Blade, and the spell will successfully kill it.

However, if your unit was at a battlefield and you swap it with Tideturner (who was at a battlefield) and the move results in your original unit ending up in your base (a non-battlefield zone), the target is no longer at a battlefield. Hidden Blade's instruction to "Kill a unit at a battlefield" cannot be followed for that target, and it will fail to kill your unit (see Rule 359.3.e.9 and Rule 359.3.e.10).

Summary: Swapping your targeted unit to a battlefield location saves it only if the spell's specific targeting requirements (in this case, "at a battlefield") are no longer met when the spell attempts to resolve. If you swap it to a non-battlefield zone (like your base), it is safe.

question: My opponent has a 1M recruit unit at battlefield A (no other units) with a facedown (hidden) hidden blade. I play Shuriken Flip targeting that recruit at Battlefield A and target one of my units to move to Battlefield A, is there a window in which the opponent can hidden blade my unit that moves into Battlefield A with shuriken flip, or is the hidden card discarded in a cleanup before there's a chance to do so?
answer:
If you target the single 1Might recruit unit at Battlefield A and then move your unit to the same Battlefield A, you will get a cleanup at the end of Shuriken Flip resolution.
316.8.b: A Showdown is marked as Staged at a Battlefield in the cleanup after the Contested status is applied to that Battlefield.

So we have to check cleanup order of outstanding tasks.
323.6: 4. Players lose control of any controlled Battlefields without their Units occupying them if the turn is in an Open State and there is no Showdown or Combat ongoing there.
323.7: 5. Recall ... . Remove all Hidden cards from all Battlefields that are not controlled by the same player and place them in their owner's Trash.
323.8: 6. Mark a Showdown as Staged at each Battlefield that Contested was applied to.

Step 4 control is lost; step 5 hidden go to trash; step 6 Showdown is staged.

The order is which outstanding tasks are handled during a cleanup would invalidate 190.4.b as reason to keep hiddens in play. As a Combat or Showdown is staged after control is lost.
190.4.b: While a Combat or Showdown is ongoing at a Battlefield, Control of that Battlefield cannot change until instructed by steps of the Combat or Showdown.

So while Shuriken Flip is resolving, the Hidden Blade can not be played at reaction speed since you can not interrupt the resolution of Shuriken Flip. And after Shuriken Flip has resolved we go through a cleanup which will remove the hidden card. So there is no window to react with a hidden Hidden Blade targeting the unit you move in with Shuriken Flip.

But if there would be another trigger on the chain (for instance if your unit would have a 'When I move trigger') the game would be in a closed state and control would not be lost.
190.4.c: If a player has no Units at a Battlefield and the turn is in an Open state, they lose Control of that Battlefield in the following cleanup unless there is a Combat or Showdown ongoing there.
321: Similarly, while Chain Items are Resolving, a Cleanup cannot occur.

question: If i play fizz to my base and as part of the ability play the spell bushwhack from my trash. Does the effect of Bushwhack work retroactively reading my fizz or does it only effect units after its played?
answer:
To determine how Bushwhack interacts with Fizz, Trickster, it is important to note that the effect of Bushwhack is not retroactive; it applies to the game state at the moment the spell resolves.

Because the spell enters the chain as a new item and resolves after Fizz has already entered the battlefield, Fizz is fully present on the board when Bushwhack's effect executes. Any friendly unit on the board at that time (including Fizz) will not be affected by Bushwhack.
Step-by-Step Sequence

Play Fizz: You play Fizz from your hand. He enters the chain as a pending item.
Fizz Finalizes: Fizz enters the battlefield (your base).
WYPM Trigger: Fizz's "When you play me" (WYPM) ability triggers and is placed on the chain.
Targeting/Choice: You choose Bushwhack from your trash to play.
Chain Resolution: The chain resolves (LIFO - Last-In, First-Out). Fizz's WYPM ability resolves, and you play Bushwhack from your trash (paying its Power cost).
Bushwhack Finalizes: The spell enters the chain as its own, new item.
Bushwhack Resolves: When the chain reaches Bushwhack, the spell executes:
Effect: "Friendly units enter ready this turn."
Any units you already control on the board are not affected by this effect. As they do not 'enter' the board.
Gold Gear: You then play the Gold gear token exhausted.

Why it does not work

The instructions on Bushwhack do not "look back" at when Fizz was played; they simply allow friendly units played that turn and after Bushwhack resolved, to enter in a ready state.

This interaction is consistent with how triggered abilities and spell resolutions function in Riftbound. As established in the Fizz, Trickster FAQ, playing a spell through Fizz's ability makes that spell a new, separate item on the chain, allowing it to interact with the board state created by Fizz’s entry.

Brynhir is a unit so it immediately resolves, it does not linger on the chain.

If you pass, priority goes to your opponent.

question: if I swap a unit using green Azir's ability and he grabs Pendulum Blade off of them during resolution, does he get the addition +2 from the blade or does his move resolve first
answer:
The ability of Azir, Ascendant resolves as a sequence of instructions executed in the order written, per Rule 157.1:

question: Does might go to minus? In that case if I use a combat trick on a unit how does it go?
answer:
Yes, Might can go negative.

Here's how it works:

A unit's Might can be reduced below 0. The game tracks the actual value (including negatives) for calculation purposes. But whenever the game checks its Might — such as for combat damage, or for effects that reference "Might" — any negative value is treated as 0 (CR 143.2.c).

How combat tricks work with a negative unit:

Say you have a 3 Might unit that gets hit with a -4 effect. Its current Might is -1. For combat, it contributes 0 damage, and if it takes even 1 damage it will die (since 0 Might with any nonzero damage = dead).

Now you respond with a combat trick that gives it +2 Might. The calculation uses the unit's current actual value (-1), not the 0 placeholder:

-1 (current) + 2 = 1 Might

So the unit ends up at 1 Might. It doesn't snap back to a higher value — the buff applies on top of whatever negative value it's sitting at (FAQ #9535). If it was at -3 and you gave it +2, it'd be at -1, still treated as 0 for combat but now only needing +1 more to become positive.

question: When Akali moves and deals 1 damage, and then moves back dealing 1 more damage before triggering showdown, does the unit defending heal damage?
answer:
No, the defending unit does not heal. But this has several conditions that must be true for this to happen.

This is best explained with an example:

Opponent controls Battlefield A with one 4 Might unit. I have Akali Deadly Weapon - NOT empowered in base.

I move my Akali to BF A → 'When I move' triggers and creates a chain. A Combat Showdown will be staged at the next possible moment, but not yet as there is an active chain. As a reaction to my own Akali's 'When I move' trigger I play Flash, target my Akali and move her back to base. Nothing else gets played by either player. So we resolve the existing chain.

Flash resolves → Akali moves back to base → NEW Akali 'When I move' trigger gets added to the chain on top of the old one. New 'when I move' trigger resolves dealing 1 damage to the opposing 4Might unit at BF A. Old 'when I move' trigger resolves dealing 1 damage to the opposing 4Might unit at BF A.

Rule 190.3.b.1: If a player who applied Contested status to a Battlefield controls no Units there and there is no ongoing Showdown or Combat at that Battlefield, then Contested status is removed in the following Cleanup.

So no contested status, no combat showdown and no healing for the opposing unit.

There is no healing event between the two Standard Moves, even though a Cleanup occurs after each move — Cleanup stages combats and checks lethal damage, but does not heal units.

This only works with reaction speed of course. Using the Akali Legend ability cannot reproduce this effect as a Combat Showdown will have started and healing will occur at the end of it: The move trigger from Akali - Deadly Weapon would go on the chain. Assuming no reactions are played it would resolve and deal 1 (or 2 if empowered) damage to a unit there. Upon that resolution though a combat showdown would start. If you then used focus to activate the Rogue Assassin Legend at Action speed, you could move Akali - Deadly Weapon out of the battlefield and inflict another 1 (or 2) damage. However, since a combat showdown was initiated it would need to clean up, meaning any damage taken would be healed AFTER the Akali move trigger resolved. If the damage dealt is enough to kill a unit it would die. If not they would return to full health. As per the rules of the Combat Special Cleanup.

Why: Doubling (CR 433) means increasing Might by an amount equal to its current value. If Fiora is at −1 Might, doubling would try to increase by −1 (a negative amount). question: If I play cleave on my 2 might unit and then goes in and conquer a contested battlefield, can I then react to my legend, Vi’s conquer effect with death grip to still be able to get the +3 might from the cleave transferred?
answer:
Yes, the +3 from Cleave does transfer.

Here's the timing sequence that makes it work:

Your 2 Might unit fights and wins combat as the Attacker — Cleave's Assault gives it +3 (now effectively 5 Might).

Combat Cleanup → Determine Combat Result → Establish Control (CR 468.5) → Conquer happens. The unit still has the Attacker designation at this point.

The conquer triggers (including your Legend's) go on the chain as Pending Items.

Before those triggers resolve, you play Deathgrip with [Reaction] in the Closed State.

Deathgrip resolves — still before CR 468.7 (Combat ends / remove designations) — so the unit is still an Attacker, Assault still applies, and its Might is 5 (2 base + 3 Assault).

Deathgrip kills the unit and transfers +5 Might to another friendly unit. You also draw 1.

Per CR 468.5→466.6→466.7, the chain items from establishing control (conquer triggers) resolve before Attacker/Defender designations are removed. Assault is a passive ability that applies as long as the unit has the Attacker designation (FAQ #2998, Rule 807), and that designation is still present when Deathgrip does its check.

Key distinction: This works specifically because the conquer happens during the Resolution Step of Combat. If this were a Non-Combat Showdown (moving to an empty battlefield), there are no Attacker/Defender designations at all — Assault would never be active, and you'd only transfer 2 Might (FAQ #3037).

question: If the first spell got defied, can I still use Crumble Sand to counter the second spell they played?
answer:
Yes, you can.

Crumbling Sands checks whether an opponent has played "another spell" this turn as a condition — not a triggered ability. Per CR 420.4.b, non-triggered abilities that check whether cards were played care about Finalization, not whether the spell resolved or was countered. A countered spell was still finalized on the chain before being removed, so it counts.

In your scenario:

• Opponent's spell was finalized on the chain when played. You Defy this spell.
• When you later play Crumbling Sands targeting their second spell, your opponents first spell counts as "another spell" the opponent played this turn.
• The condition is satisfied, so you can counter the second spell.

Common point of confusion: CR 426.1.b says a countered spell isn't considered played for abilities that trigger on cards being played (e.g., Abandoned Hall, Ravenbloom Student). But Crumbling Sands isn't a trigger — it's a conditional cost/restriction on a Reaction spell, so it falls under 419.4.b instead.

question: If I have Siphoning Strike and it gets Rebuttal, when Mel makes a new decision will she do 4 DMG or 7 DMG based on her rune?
answer:
It depends on how many runes Mel's controller has at resolution — not a choice she makes, and not based on the original Nasus player's runes.

When Rebuttal resolves and the [A] is paid, control of Siphoning Strike changes to the Mel player, and she "may make new choices" — but those choices are limited to locations, modes, destinations, and targets (Rule 752.1). The 4-vs-7 damage check is not a finalization choice; it's a condition evaluated when the spell resolves, and "you" in the spell text now refers to its new controller. So: if Mel controls 7+ runes when it resolves, it deals 7; otherwise 4. She does pick a new target for it (a unit at a battlefield), but the damage number is automatic.

question: if opp play Rampage and didnt pay the additional cost, can I use rebuttal to make a new choice and pay the additional cost for the card?
answer:
No — Rebuttal cannot let you pay Rampage's optional additional cost.

"Make new choices" effects only let you remake finalization choices: locations, modes, destinations, and targets. Choices made "as you play this" — including Optional Additional Costs like Rampage's [C] — are explicitly excluded (Rule 752.2). The spell was already played and its costs already paid, and any cost that would be incurred by remade choices is ignored (Rule 755). Rampage will resolve under your control, but since [C] was never paid, the +2 Shield clause won't execute.

question: If i use shady spectacles to turn a recruit into a copy of illaoi does this recruit still count as a token unit or just a ''token''?
answer:
Yes — it stays a token unit. Copy effects only change "copyable traits" (Might, rules text, tags); they can't touch a game object's fundamental identity as a token (Rule 185.1.a: "Token Game Objects cannot lose their token nature by any means").

So the Recruit is still a token and still a unit — it's not downgraded to "just a token." It still counts for things that care about token units (e.g., Illaoi's own "+1 power for each token unit you control"), and if it ever leaves the board it will cease to exist like any token. Being a copy of Illaoi only affects its stats and rules text (Rule 185.1, FAQ #11371).

question: If I mark 1 damage on an Irelia with a Guardian Angel on it then I play Elder Dragon, does she die, proc Guardian Angel and die again?
answer:
Yes - but only if you also choose Irelia with the 'When you play me' triggered ability from Elder Dragon.

Here's how it works: Elder Dragon's passive makes any non-zero amount of your damage lethal for enemy units (Rule 142.4.c), so Irelia's 1 marked damage is already lethal once Elder Dragon enters. A cleanup is inserted and Elder Dragon's 'When you play me' ability becomes a pending item on the chain. The WYPM ability has to wait for the cleanup to finish before finalizing on the chain. During this cleanup Irelia dies but her death gets replaced by the attached Guardian Angel. Irelia is healed, exhausted and recalled to base (rule 369.1). After this cleanup Elder Dragon's play effect can finalize on the chain and Irelia can be chosen as one of the possible targets. After Elder Dragon's WYPM ability is resolved another cleanup occurs and if Irelia was a target and did receive damage she would again be marked with lethal damage and be killed.

Guardian Angel is a one-time replacement effect that intercepts that death, killing itself and healing/exhausting/recalling Irelia.

question: can you give me the order of all the (possible) steps in a combat, attack / defend trigger, start / end of combat trigger, assualt shield etc
answer:
Here's the full combat walkthrough, in order (CR 465–468):

Before combat opens: After a move/effect puts units at a battlefield, Cleanup stages a Showdown (if Contested) and then a Combat if opposing units are present. If multiple combats are staged, the Turn Player picks which to resolve first (461.1).

Step 1 — Combat Showdown (464):

Start-of-combat / showdown effects happen now (464.2.b) — these are triggers, they go on the Chain like any other.

Attacker/Defender are established: Attacker = the player whose unit applied Contested; units gain the matching designation (464.2.c). This is when Assault and Shield turn on — they're passive abilities that apply as long as the unit holds the designation, no Chain involved (807, 814).

Attacker gains Focus (464.2.d).

Attack/Defend triggers (and any other simultaneous triggers) go on the initial Chain: Attacker's triggers first, then other players in turn order, then Defender's triggers last (464.2.e). Because Chains resolve LIFO, defend triggers resolve before attack triggers. Attack and Defend triggers only fire the first time a unit gains that designation in a combat (383.4.e–f). Reactions can be added to this Chain.

The Showdown continues Open — Action/Reaction play alternates with Focus until all players pass, then the Showdown Closes (348).

Step 2 — Combat Damage (465) — only if both sides still have units:

Sum Might of Attackers and Defenders using current Might (Assault/Shield bonuses included). Attacker assigns lethal damage first, then Defender (465.2.c). Tank forces a unit to be assigned lethal first; Backline last.

Once all damage is assigned, it's dealt simultaneously; triggers from deaths resolve after.

Step 3 — Resolution (466):

Combat Cleanup: heal all units in play (not just combatants), then recall Attackers still present if Defenders remain (466.1).

Determine combat result — win/lose/"No Result" (No Result can re-stage Combat) (466.3).

If no Showdown/Combat is staged, the player with units Establishes Control → clears Contested → Conquer if not yet scored there this turn (466.5).

Combat ends: Attacker/Defender designations are removed, "end of combat"/"combat ends" effects happen, and all "this combat" effects expire simultaneously (466.7).

Key nuance: non-Combat Showdowns (conquering an empty battlefield) skip Step 2 and the Combat Cleanup entirely — no damage, no healing, straight to Establish Control.

question: if you play astral heron for your first card to a battlefield. can its card cost reduction be used for hiding a card?
answer:
No. Astral Heron's reduction only applies to playing a card, and hiding is not playing a card.

Hiding is a separate Discretionary Action — Rule 811.1.c.1 explicitly states "Hide is not a subset of Play," and hiding doesn't even open a chain. Astral Heron's discount applies to "your next card" during the cost-determination steps of playing a card (Rule 356); the [A] you pay to hide is a cost of the Hide action, not a card cost, so no card cost reduction touches it.

It also wouldn't matter if it could: playing a card from Hidden costs [0] (base costs ignored), so there'd be nothing to reduce. The only card-play cost Astral Heron would meaningfully discount is a card played normally from hand.

question: if i have astral heron and the discount is applied. can i play bellows breath repeat and have the 2 energy 2 power fully reduced? does it work with the repeat cost?
answer:
Yes. Astral Heron's discount ([2][A][A]) reduces the Energy and Power components of your next card's total cost — including the Repeat additional cost — so Bellows Breath (1E + 1P base, plus 1E + 1C Repeat) ends up costing 0 total.

Key points:

Repeat's cost is an additional cost added during cost determination, and discounts can reduce additional costs all the way to 0 (Rule 356.4.f).

Since you chose to pay the Repeat cost, it's considered "paid" even at 0, so Bellows Breath still executes twice (Rule 356.4.f.1).

The discount is applied once to the combined cost (base + Repeat), not twice (FAQ #629). You only get one discounted card, so don't expect the Heron to also discount a second spell that turn.

question: If my opponent decide to play a flow card, can i react with disposable order and recycle it before he plays it ? Can i do the same with fizz ?
answer:
No for a Flow card, yes for Fizz.

Flow: Once your opponent announces they're playing a spell with Flow, the very first step of the process of play moves it from the trash to the Chain — there is no priority window before that happens (Rule 354.1). Once it's on the Chain, it's no longer in the trash, and Disposal Order can only choose cards from opponents' trashes, so you can't recycle it. Your only window is to respond to the spell itself (e.g., counter it) while it's on the Chain.

Fizz: Yes. Fizz's "When you play me" ability is a separate trigger that targets a spell still sitting in the trash. You can respond to that trigger with Disposal Order (it has [Reaction]), recycle the targeted spell, and when Fizz's ability resolves the target is gone — so the spell is not played at all (FAQ #11060). Just note you have to wait until the trigger is actually on the Chain; you can't preempt the trigger itself.

The spell is still legal to play, but on resolution the movement instruction can't be followed and is ignored (per the "can't beats can" rule, Rule 356.3.e.6). The spell resolves with no effect on those units. This applies to any spell or ability trying to move units from the Lair to base — the restriction only blocks moves to base, so moving them to another battlefield (e.g., via ganking) remains legal.

question: what is the rule about sideboard size? what amount? up to or must be?
answer:

Sideboarding is done 1-for-1 with Main Deck cards between games (403.4), your Main Deck stays exactly 40 (402.1), and copy limits apply across the Main Deck + sideboard combined (403.3). Note: older FAQs reference an 8-card limit from an earlier rules version — the current rules allow up to 10. In limited formats (sealed/draft), the sideboard is instead everything in your card pool not used in your starting configuration (602.4.a.7).

question: if i use retreat and it resolves. does the combat end right away or can the opponent still use an action as if it was still ongoing?
answer:

That player gets to play spells/abilities with Action or Reaction if they want — Retreating your last unit doesn't skip that. Combat only closes when both players pass Focus in succession without starting a chain, even if no units remain at the battlefield (FAQ #1229, #976).

question: if i use bellows breath on 2 units at a battlefield. and they use emperor's divide. now they're at different locations. how is it decided which still get hit?
answer:
You decide. The "same location" requirement is a targeting restriction when Bellows Breath is cast, not a resolution requirement — so the spell doesn't fizzle when Emperor's Divide scatters them.

On resolution, you (the spell's controller) choose one location where your originally targeted units currently are. All originally targeted units at that chosen location take 1 damage; any at other locations are unaffected. You can't split damage across locations, and you can't pick new targets — only units you originally chose.

One practical note: in 1v1, Emperor's Divide sends both units to their controller's base, so they'll both usually end up at the same location and both get hit. "Different locations" only matters if the two units have different controllers (e.g., 2v2, where each moves to its own owner's base) — then you pick one to hit. (Rule 355.11.b; FAQ #7422)

question: If I have Poro at base alone and use Baited Hook and get a new unit, does Poro get its +1 draw? What's the order?

question: Can you explain the difference between focus and priority, and lets say im a showdown if i play an action technically i still have to pass focus after that right
answer:
They're different layers: Focus is "who may start a chain in a Showdown Open State," Priority is "who may act right now" (including playing Reactions on an existing chain).

Focus is a "home base" tracking tool — it's what lets you play an Action when the chain is empty. Priority is the singular exclusive right to take any discretionary action at this instant, and it bounces around as players react, pass, and resolve (Rule 312–313). They come as a bundle — gaining Focus also grants Priority (313.2) — but you can pass Priority and still keep Focus (313.3).

Yes, in effect — but you don't "pass" it manually. When you play an Action in a Showdown, you keep Focus for the entire chain. You pass Priority (often to your opponent, then back) to let the chain resolve. The moment the last item resolves and the state returns to Open, Focus automatically passes to the next player in turn order (Rule 346, 347.1.b). So you can't start a second chain back-to-back — the opponent gets first crack. The only "manual" pass of Focus is the Pass action with an empty chain, which is what eventually closes the Showdown (347.2).

One caveat: passing priority isn't a one-way door — after you pass, your opponent gets priority, but if they play something, priority comes back to you to respond, and so on until both players pass in sequence (Rule 339).

question: If I rebuttal a Star-Crossed, can I select two enemy units? And then it tries to do as many as it can and will only return one?
answer:
When you play Rebuttal and pay the [A], you can choose any number of targets or modes to make new choices for. The rest remain the same.

If you are remaking choices in this way, any choices you choose NOT to remake must be legal choices. You can't choose to have some but not all choices be legal choices. Of course, you can always choose not to make new choices. In that case, any of the current choices will remain in their current state, whether that state is illegal or not.

For Star-Crossed + Rebuttal:

You can target the same units that were previously targeted, and in some cases you will need to. These are new friendly and enemy units so they are not the same as before. For example, if you Rebuttal a Star-Crossed, pay the A and do not change targeting, Star-Crossed will mistarget both units when it resolves as they no longer meet the enemy and friendly unit targeting requirements.

Additionally, if you remake any choices, you need to remake all currently illegal choices. You can't choose to retarget one part of Star-Crossed and not the other to get only part of it to mistarget.

question: If you have the gear which gives 1 might when you attack or defend alone, and you have a sprite at base and a unit which creates a sprite in the location it moves from. Let's say you have that unit defending. Reveal a tide turner to move it to base and move the sprite to the battlefield. But that also means a new sprite is added when it is moved — does one sprite get the solo attack buff before the second sprite is generated by the move?
answer:
Yes — if the Sprite is the only unit at the battlefield when it arrives, it gets the Mask of Foresight +1 before Lillia's move-trigger Sprite is ever created.

The "alone" condition is checked the moment the Sprite gains its Defender designation (in the Cleanup after the swap resolves, per the "units arriving later gain designation" rule). At that point Lillia has already left and her "when I move" trigger is only pending on the Chain — the second Sprite isn't on the board yet. So the Sprite is alone, Mask triggers, and that trigger is locked in; the second Sprite appearing when Lillia's trigger resolves later does not remove the buff (FAQ 11212/10888, 10067).

Two caveats:

If Lillia is still present when the Sprite arrives, the Sprite is not "alone" and Mask does not trigger at all (FAQ 6385). Shouldn't be a problem if it's a single movement "swap", but if it's two separate movements take it into consideration.

Tideturner's ability swaps itself with one friendly unit at another location — for that to happen it'd need to be revealed from hidden on another battlefield, move Lillia there and itself to the active combat, gaining the bonus. For the swap you mention to happen, something like Smoke and Mirrors would be necessary.

question:
I control a unit at a battlefield.
I play Flurry of Feathers, intending to add units to that same battlefield.
My opponent reacts with Gust.
What happens with the bird tokens?
answer:
The bird tokens still get played to that battlefield — Gust doesn't stop them.

Gust resolves first and returns your unit to hand, leaving you with no units there. But control of a battlefield can't be lost while there's an item on the chain (Rule 190.4.c, clarified in the 2026-03-30 patch), and a Cleanup can't occur during chain resolution (Rule 321). Since Flurry of Feathers is still on the chain when it resolves, you still control that battlefield, so it remains a legal location for the four Bird tokens — tokens follow the normal "play to your base or a battlefield you control" rule (FAQ #10013).

Once the birds enter, you have units there again and keep control. Note Gust could only have targeted your 3-or-less Might unit anyway — the birds didn't exist yet when Gust was played. If your opponent instead waited until after Flurry resolved, Gust could then hit a 1-Might Bird, and a token bounced to hand would cease to exist.

question: Can i react to my own faefolk trigger targetting vex apathatic ambush rengar in without getting stunned?
answer:
Yes — play Rengar as a Reaction to your own Faefolk trigger (before it resolves), and Vex will not stun him.

Vex, Apathetic's ability only fires when an opponent plays a unit while Vex is at that battlefield. Faefolk's trigger is still on the Chain when you play Rengar, so Vex is still at her old location — Rengar enters before she arrives, the trigger condition is never met, and no stun happens (Rule 383.2.c). This is the same window FAQ #11573 describes: your own Faefolk trigger puts you in a Closed State with priority, and you can jump in before the pulled unit lands.

Note the contrast with FAQ #10932/#9735: those Ambush units were played after the pull resolved, with Vex already on the battlefield — that's when she stuns. Also check your Rengar's permissions: Rengar, Pouncing can come in via "a battlefield you're attacking" (your Faefolk move made you the attacker), but Rengar, Trophy Hunter's Ambush needs enemy units already at that battlefield — if it's empty, he can't legally be played there at all.

answer:

The reason: when you play Rengar, Faefolk's trigger hasn't resolved yet, so Vex is still at its current battlefield. Chain order doesn't save you: Vex's trigger goes on top of Faefolk's, resolves first, stuns Rengar (and locks him from moving this turn), and then Faefolk pulls Vex over.

One caveat: if Vex happens to be at a Base (not a battlefield) when Rengar enters, the stun won't trigger — but in the typical setup where Vex is at a battlefield, Rengar comes in stunned and contributes no Might in the ensuing combat (CR 424.1.b).

question: Can you still play defy with Empowered blue Mel out
answer:
Yes, you can still play Defy — but it won't actually counter anything. A spell that "can't be countered" (from an Empowered Mel, Newly Awakened) is still a legal target for Defy, since it's a spell on the chain with the right cost; "can't be countered" is a prevention on the counter action, not a targeting restriction. On resolution, the counter instruction is negated (Rule 358.3.a, Rule 54 "can't beats can"), so Defy goes to trash and does nothing, and the protected spell resolves normally.

Note this only applies to spells controlled by Mel's controller while Mel is Empowered. If Mel isn't Empowered — or if the spell belongs to a different player — Defy counters as usual.

question: Does a defy that does nothing because of empowered blue Mel still count for abandon hall?
answer:
Yes. Defy resolves normally (it isn't itself countered), so it counts as a played spell for Abandoned Hall even though its counter instruction did nothing.

Mel, Newly Awakened's Empowered ability ("Your spells and abilities can't be countered") only stops the counter from succeeding — Defy's instruction is simply ignored on resolution. A spell that resolves with no effect is still considered played (Rule 359.3.e.10). The "not considered played" rule (425.1.b) applies only to spells that are actually countered, which isn't the case here. So once Defy finishes resolving, Abandoned Hall's "when a player plays a spell" trigger fires, and the Defy's controller may give one of their units there +1.

question: If I conquer a Minefield and trigger my Ivern legend, will I still have to burn 2?
answer:

Both go on the Chain as independent triggered abilities, and once Minefield's trigger is on the Chain it resolves regardless of whether Minefield is still in play (FAQ #9525 / #10867). You choose the order both triggers are placed on the Chain (Rule 383.3.d), but either way Minefield's burn 2 still happens.

question: Can I play not so fast on a green Janna reaction?
answer:
Yes — you can play Not So Fast to counter Janna, Savior's "When you play me" trigger, provided her controller chose one of your units to move to base.

Janna's trigger is a triggered ability (not a spell), and it goes on the Chain as a Closed state. Not So Fast has [Reaction], so you can respond. From your perspective, the unit Janna's ability targets is a "friendly unit," and the ability is an enemy ability — exactly what Not So Fast counters. This works the same way as countering Blitzcrank's play trigger (FAQ #10845).

Two limits: Not So Fast can't target Janna herself (she's a unit and finalizes immediately — only her trigger is on the Chain), and if her controller chooses zero units to move ("up to one"), the ability doesn't choose a friendly unit, so Not So Fast has no legal target.

question: if leblanc uses mirror image on my unite and i react with retreat to remove my unit, does she still get a 0 might reflection which they can play and conq with?
answer:
Yes. Retreat resolves first and puts your unit in your hand, so when Mirror Image resolves the "becomes a copy" instruction simply fails (Rule 359.3.e.6 — instructions that can't be followed are ignored), but the token is still played to LeBlanc's base as a 0 [M] Reflection with Temporary (FAQ #9729, #11492).

And yes, that token can still be used to conquer: it enters ready, so its controller can Standard Move it from base to a battlefield during their Main Phase, and a unit doesn't need Might to conquer an empty battlefield (CR 144, 187.3, 448). Just be aware it has Temporary — it's killed at the start of its controller's next Beginning Phase, before scoring — so it has to be used that same turn, and conquering with it only scores that battlefield (Final Point still requires scoring every other battlefield that turn).

question: If I have a spell cost reduction (like empowered Applied Researchers), do spells that originally costed 4 energy still qualify for Jhin legend's ability to be banished, or do I have to actually spend the 4 energy?
answer:
No — you have to actually spend 4 or more energy.

Virtuoso's ability reads "When you play a spell, if you spent [4] or more, you may banish it." That condition checks the energy you actually paid during finalization (Rule 357), not the printed cost. With empowered Applied Researchers reducing your spells' Energy cost by 1 (minimum 1), a 4-cost spell only costs you 3, so you spent 3 — Virtuoso doesn't trigger and you can't banish it.

This is the opposite of effects that reference a spell's cost (like Lux or Defy), which use the printed cost regardless of discounts (CR 206). "Spent" is specifically about real payment — which is also why paying a Repeat cost counts toward Jhin's 4-energy threshold, and why Hard Bargain payments don't (FAQ #10012, #10606).

So: 4-cost spell under Applied Researchers → spends 3 → no banish. A 5-cost spell reduced to 4 → spends 4 → banish works.
